          {
            "title": "Description",
            "content": "A digital BP monitor that facilitates daily BP regimen in homecare setting."
          },
          {
            "title": "Uses",
            "content": "Used to measure BP and pulse rate of adults."
          },
          {
            "title": "Direction",
            "content": "Select the correct cuff size. Wrap the cuff around bare upper arm (preferably left arm), about 1-2 cm above the inside of the elbow. Press the start button. Squeeze the rubber bulb until the up mark disappears, then, the automatic exhaust mechanism will gradually reduce pressure in the cuff until the heart mark is displayed, along with the current pressure reading. Remain still during measurement. Once the measurement is complete, the down mark is displayed. Press the exhaust valve, then, remove the cuff from the arm. Press the start button to turn off. See instruction manual for complete instructions for use."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "History of mastectomy. History of severe circulatory deficit in the arm. Childn. Pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Avoid extreme temperature, humidity, direct sunlight, shock, or dust. Never use alcohol, benzene, thinner, or other harsh chemicals when cleaning. Avoid tightly folding the cuff or storing the hose tightly twisted for long periods. Device and cuff are not water-resistant. Do not use closely to televisions, microwave ovens, cellular telephones, X-ray or other devices with strong electrical fields. Keep a minimum distance of 30 cm from wireless communication devices. Do not use near flammable gases and highly concentrated oxygen environments. Using too frequently may cause prolonged impairment of blood circulation. Patients who had mastectomy. Allow the device to adapt for about 1 hr to surrounding environment before use.",

        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/0EgQOZSs4984DmB7RDrVF6UfWzwBPt3JLFETP0mhqsEjO28SM9.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/MNv5ncq9xq0rWSwBdvW1O2xA2rbtWgQjFD7JmhnJnWO2C1dOD8.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/VIgBqjauEtE9dJqSjNRmaadcjAfzvsKbvML98NKiZwH6SLnFqQ.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Apixaban",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Anticoagulants"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Prevention of venous thromboembolic events (VTE) in adults who have undergone elective hip or knee replacement surgery. Reduction of risk of stroke, systemic embolism, and death in patients with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF), with one or more risk factors, including patients unsuitable for warfarin. Treatment of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE). Prevention of recurrent DVT and PE."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Prevention of VTE</b> - <b>Elective hip or knee replacement surgery:</b> 2.5 mg twice daily, initial dose should be taken 12-24 hrs after surgery. Recommended duration of treatment - Hip replacement surgery: 32-38 days; Knee replacement surgery: 10-14 days. <b>Prevention of stroke and systemic embolism</b> - <b>NVAF:</b> 5 mg twice daily. In patients with at least 2 of the following characteristics: age &ge;80 yrs, BW &le;60 kg, or serum creatinine &ge;1.5 mg/dL (133 micromole/L): 2.5 mg twice daily. <b>Treatment of DVT and PE:</b> 10 mg twice daily for 7 days, followed by 5 mg twice daily. <b>Prevention of recurrent DVT and PE:</b> 2.5 mg twice daily after at least 6 months of treatment for DVT or PE. Patients who may require cardioversion but not previously treated with anticoagulants: 5 doses of apixaban 5 mg twice daily before cardioversion. If cardioversion is required before 5 doses of apixaban can be administered, give 10 mg loading dose then 5 mg twice daily. Give loading dose at least 2 hrs before cardioversion. Tabs may be crushed and suspended in a suitable liquid for patients unable to swallow or through nasogastric tube."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Clinically significant active bleeding."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Increased risk of hemorrhage e.g. congenital or acquired bleeding disorders, active ulcerative GI disease, bacterial endocarditis, thrombocytopenia, platelet disorders, history of hemorrhagic stroke, severe uncontrolled HTN, and recent brain, spinal, or ophthalmological surgery. Patients with hepatic disease associated with coagulopathy and bleeding risk; renal impairment (CrCl < 15 mL/min), and undergoing dialysis, hepatic impairment. Concomitant use with strong CYP3A4 and P-gp inhibitors and inducers, and antiplatelet agents. Monitor for signs and symptoms of neurological impairment when neuraxial or spinal/epidural anesthesia is employed. Patients undergoing hip fracture surgery; with prosthetic heart valves, and antiphospholipid syndrome. Not recommended as alternative to unfractionated heparin for initial treatment of PE in hemodynamically unstable patients. Childn < 18 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Anemia, hemorrhage, nausea, contusion. Epistaxis, eye and GI hemorrhage. Hematoma, gingival bleeding, hematuria, menorrhagia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "CYP3A4 and P-gp inhibitors and inducers, other anticoagulants, platelet inhibitors, and NSAIDs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 2.5 mg, 5 mg."
          }
        ],

  {

    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 702,
        "brand_name": "Abilify",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/WjVjFGhC3fRWNIf5XgXJbvq0f55Iyd6lPJxFrgsoMo7oRBFTOb.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/DCRZXh0GW7fmJycTXYE3ebbs6985tPhtYzFm1WGLvzyO6TZell.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/KGwavPPCQSdS7N7K1it2njLSzXUaEDcyEi0QGWEKta9ci1rBLK.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Aripiprazole",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Atypical Antipsychotics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of schizophrenia. Acute treatment of manic and mixed episodes associated with bipolar disorder and maintenance therapy for bipolar I disorder, both as monotherapy and as adjunct to lithium or valproate. Adjunctive treatment of major depressive disorder (MDD). Treatment of irritability associated with autistic disorder, Tourette’s disorder. Special considerations in treating childn with schizophrenia, bipolar I disorder, and irritability associated with autistic disorder."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Schizophrenia</b> - <b>Adults:</b> 10 or 15 mg/day once daily. Dose range 10-30 mg/day. <b>Adolescents:</b> 10 mg/day, initially 2 mg/day, titrate to 5 mg/day after 2 days and then 10 mg/day after 2 additional days. Adjust dose further by 5 mg increments up to max 30 mg/day. <b>Bipolar I disorder</b> - <b>Adults</b> - Monotherapy: 15 mg once daily. Adjunctive treatment with lithium or valproate: 10-15 mg once daily. Adjust dose further by 5 mg increments up to max 30 mg/day. <b>Childn 10-17 yrs:</b> Initially 2 mg/day, titrate to 5 mg/day after 2 days and then 10 mg/day after 2 additional days. <b>Adjunctive treatment of MDD</b> - <b>Adults:</b> Initially 2-5 mg/day. Dose range 2-15 mg/day. Adjust dose gradually up to 5 mg/day at intervals of not < 1 week. <b>Irritability associated with autistic disorder</b> - <b>Childn 6-17 yrs:</b> 5-15 mg/day. Initially 2 mg/day, increase to 5 mg/day and then 10 or 15 mg/day. Adjust dose gradually up to 5 mg/day at intervals of not < 1 week. <b>Tourette’s disorder</b> - <b>Childn 6-18 yrs:</b> 5-20 mg/day; Patients weighing < 50 kg: Initially 2 mg/day, then 5 mg/day after 2 days. May be increased to 10 mg/day; &ge;50 kg: Initially 2 mg/day for 2 days, increased to 5 mg/day for 5 days, then 10 mg/day on day 8. Adjust dose gradually by 5 mg/day increments at intervals of not < 1 week. Max: 20 mg/day. <b>Poor CYP2D6 metabolizers, patients taking concomitant CYP3A4 or CYP2D6 inhibitors or CYP3A4 inducers:</b> Adjust dose except when used as adjunctive treatment of MDD."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Oral soln is not approved for MDD. Patients with dementia-related psychosis; worsening and/or emergence of suicidal ideation and behavior. NMS, tardive dyskinesia, hyperglycemia, DM, dyslipidemia, weight gain, compulsive behaviors, orthostatic hypotension, fall-related injury, leukopenia, neutropenia, and agranulocytosis. Patients with history of seizures, at risk for aspiration. Disruption of body temp regulation. Patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, the Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption. May impair ability to drive or operate machines. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category C.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nausea, vomiting, headache, constipation, dizziness, akathisia, anxiety, insomnia, and restlessness. Somnolence, extrapyramidal disorder, fatigue, increased appetite, nasopharyngitis, and weight increased."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. itraconazole, clarithromycin) or strong CYP2D6 inhibitors (e.g. quinidine, fluoxetine, paroxetine), strong CYP3A4 inducers (e.g. carbamazepine, rifampin), antihypertensive drugs, benzodiazepines e.g. lorazepam."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 5 mg (P163.36), 10 mg (P238.21), 15 mg  (P238.21)."
          }
        ],
        "company": {
          "id": 105,
          "name": "Otsuka (Philippines) Pharmaceutical, Inc."
        },

          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Atypical Antipsychotics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Acute and maintenance treatment of schizophrenia in adult patients stabilized with oral aripiprazole."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "IM only. 400 mg monthly (no sooner than 26 days after the previous injection). <b>Patients who have never taken aripiprazole:</b> Establish tolerability with oral aripiprazole prior to initiating treatment with Abilify Maintena. Starting dose (for one of the regimen) - Regimen 1: Administer 1 Abilify Maintena injection, then continue with oral aripiprazole (10-20 mg) for 14 consecutive days to achieve therapeutic concentrations during initiation of therapy. Regimen 2: Administer 2 separate injections of 400 mg at separate sites, along with one 20 mg oral aripiprazole. <b>Patients already stable on another oral antipsychotic (known to tolerate aripiprazole):</b> After 1<sup>st</sup> Abilify Maintena injection, continue with antipsychotic for 14 consecutive days. Consider reducing dosage to 300 mg once monthly if there are adverse reactions with the 400 mg dosage. <b>Poor CYP2D6 metabolizers, patients taking concomitant CYP3A4 or CYP2D6 inhibitors or CYP3A4 inducers:</b> Adjust dose."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Elderly with dementia-related psychosis. Neonates. Lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Cerebrovascular adverse reactions, NMS, tardive dyskinesia, metabolic changes (hyperglycemia or DM, dyslipidemia, and weight gain), pathological gambling and other compulsive behaviors, orthostatic hypotension, leukopenia, neutropenia and agranulocytosis, seizures, potential for cognitive and motor impairment, body temp regulation and dysphagia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Ketoconazole, paroxetine, fluoxetine, carbamazepine, antihypertensive drugs, lorazepam."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Lyophilized powder for extended-release suspension for injection in pre-filled dual chamber syringe (IM) 300 mg (P6,938.39), 400 mg (P6,938.39)."
          }

        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Abiraterone acetate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Hormones and Antagonists in Chemotherapy"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "In combination with prednisone or prednisolone, treatment of newly diagnosed high risk metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC) in adult men with androgen deprivation therapy (ADT); metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) in adult men who are asymptomatic or mildly symptomatic after failure of ADT in whom chemotherapy is not yet clinically indicated, or in adult men whose disease has progressed on or after a docetaxel-based chemotherapy regimen."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "4 tabs (1000 mg) once daily swallowed whole with water, without meals. <b>Prednisone or prednisolone dose in combination - mHSPC:</b> 5 mg daily; <b>mCRPC:</b> 10 mg daily. Continue medical castration with luteinizing hormone-releasing hormone (LHRH) analogue during treatment if not surgically castrated. <b>Re-treatment following return of liver function to baseline:</b> Reduced dose of 500 mg once daily.  See complete product insert for dose modifications during toxicity. Taken at least 2 hrs after eating and no food at least 1 hr after administration."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Severe hepatic impairment. Concomitant use with prednisone or prednisolone in combination with Ra-223 dichloride. Women of childbearing potential. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Maintain potassium level at &ge;4 mM in patients with pre-existing or have developed hypokalemia during treatment. Patients with moderate hepatic or severe renal impairment; underlying medical conditions who might be compromised by an increase in BP, hypokalemia, or fluid retention, severe or unstable angina pectoris, recent MI or ventricular arrhythmia; history of CV disease; active or symptomatic viral hepatitis; previously treated with ketoconazole; galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, glucose-galactose malabsorption; on a controlled sodium diet. HTN, hypokalemia and fluid retention; QT prolongation; adrenocortical insufficiency on corticosteroid withdrawal; decreased bone density, hyperglycemia; anemia, sexual dysfunction; myopathy. Concomitant use with corticosteroids, cytotoxic chemotherapy, drugs associated with myopathy/rhabdomyolysis, strong CYP3A4 inducers. Measure serum transaminases prior to therapy, every 2 weeks for the 1<sup>st</sup> 3 months, and monthly thereafter; minimum of every 2 weeks for 3 months and monthly for re-treatment. Monitor BP, serum potassium, and fluid retention monthly; if with significant risk for CHF, every 2 weeks for 1<sup>st</sup> 3 months and monthly thereafter. Assess cardiac functions (e.g. ECG) before treating patients with significant risk for CHF. Withhold treatment when Grade &ge;3 toxicities or hepatotoxicity (ALT or AST >5x ULN) occur or recur. Affect fertility. Childn. Use contraception.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "UTI; hypokalemia; HTN; diarrhea; increased ALT an/or AST; peripheral edema. Sepsis; hypertriglyceridemia; cardiac failure (including CHF, left ventricular dysfunction, decreased ejection fraction), angina pectoris, atrial fibrillation, tachycardia; dyspepsia; rash; hematuria; fractures except pathological fractures."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Strong CYP3A4 inducers (e.g. phenytoin, carbamazepine, rifampicin, rifabutin, rifapentine, phenobarbital, St. John’s Wort) and inhibitors (e.g. ketoconazole); CYP2D6-metabolized drugs (e.g. dextromethorphan, metoprolol, propranolol, desipramine, venlafaxine, haloperidol, risperidone, propafenone, flecainide, codeine, oxycodone, tramadol); pioglitazone; drugs eliminated by OATP1B1, QT-prolonging drugs (e.g. class IA or III antiarrhythmics, methadone, moxifloxacin, antipsychotics); spironolactone."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 250 mg x 120s (P50,000.00)."
          }
        ],

          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/pncpYNnjkKTHU3jVrhqU5ywlJWKLU6BgQimFKNGc9HuYff22Fk.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Testosterone",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Androgens"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Replacement therapy for male adults with hypogonadism when testosterone deficiency has been clinically and biologically confirmed."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Prime the canister pump before the 1<sup>st</sup> dose; discard the 1<sup>st</sup> 3 pumps. Apply 2 pumps once daily on clean, dry, and healthy skin on the right and left shoulder and upper arms, at approx same time each day preferably in the morning. Spread in a thin layer and let dry for at least 3-5 mins before covering the application site with clothing. Dose can be adjusted in increments of 1 pump (20.25 mg testosterone or 1.25 g gel) based on patient’s response. Max 4 pumps/day. Take a shower or wash hands and the application site thoroughly with soap and water to remove any residue before any anticipated contact with another person’s skin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with confirmed or suspected prostate cancer or breast carcinoma."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Intended for use by men only. Not indicated for male sterility or impotence. Should not be applied to the genitals. Perform a thorough examination to rule out any risk of preexisting prostate cancer before initiating treatment. Regular monitoring of prostate and breasts should be done using the recommended methods (rectal examination and PSA-prostate-specific antigen assay) at least once a yr; twice a yr in elderly patients and patients at risk. May accelerate progression of subclinical prostate cancer or BPH. Patients with cancer with risk of hypercalcemia (and associated hypercalciuria related to bone metastases; severe heart, liver, or kidney failure; IHD; HTN; thrombophilia or with risk factors for VTE; epilepsy, migraine; obesity, chronic respiratory disease. Irritability, nervousness, weight gain, prolonged or frequent erections; spermatogenesis suppression; gynecomastia. Risk of inadvertent testosterone transfer. May induce a positive reaction to tests performed during anti-doping controls. Contains alcohol; may cause burning sensation on damaged skin. May interfere with laboratory tests for thyroid hormones. Female patients. Male childn < 18 yrs. Elderly >65 yrs.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Emotional symptoms (e.g. mood swings, affective disorders, anger, aggression, impatience, insomnia, abnormal dreams, increased libido); skin reactions (e.g. acne, alopecia, skin dryness or lesions, contact dermatitis, hair color changes, rash, hypersensitivity, pruritus); increased PSA, Hgb, or Hct."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Oral anticoagulants, ACTH or corticosteroids, antidiabetics. Positive reaction to anti-doping controls."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Transdermal gel 16.2 mg/g x 88 g (approx 60 doses) (P2,588.75)."
          }
        ],

        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/xYat6GtbKgsC1CydkIrWJNMZrWsVzkiOhH9FlsKq6DMRuYgyKw.jpg",

          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/4AQ6d1qMLEki1Fc15PQojsLgfrQjzopc1iA0fmy5BDBzgiy83f.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Biperiden HCl",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Antiparkinsonism"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Symptomatic treatment of parkinsonism, including the alleviation of the extrapyramidal syndrome (EPS) induced by drugs e.g. phenothiazines."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Initially 1 mg twice daily, gradually increased over several days according to the needs of patient. Usual optimum maintenance dosage varies from 3-12 mg daily in divided doses. <b>Idiopathic parkinsonism:</b> 2 mg 3-4x daily increased according to the needs of patient to max 16 mg in 24 hrs. <b>Drug-induced EPS:</b> 2 mg once to thrice daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category C.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Choreic movements (with carbidopa/levodopa), sleep disorder, drowsiness, euphoria or disorientation, agitation. Blurred vision, dry mouth, constipation. Decrease in urinary flow, postural hypotension, bradycardia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Other anticholinergic psychotropic drugs, antihistamines, antiparkinsonian drugs and antispasmodics, quinidine, levodopa, metoclopramide, alcohol."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 2 mg (P15.00)."
          }
        ],

  {
    "id": 4747,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 4747,
        "brand_name": "Apiklot",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/Rfoy8F1ZQqUQ3CAxIwdWrESyJLSqoWvxZ5ni1eqVZCVnZKVDh4.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/DK9hfpPMhtivHtfKJ3YBz137AuX1ApN3tnpZarlgFs9NJqHIUR.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/zUyzG6nJwmLHsXSdeinZ7FZJYKsB8LOUzDoBSFUN8OtJLBKEb0.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Apixaban",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Anticoagulants"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Prevention of venous thromboembolic events (VTE) in adult patients who have undergone elective hip or knee replacement surgery.  Prevention of stroke and systemic embolism in adult patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF), with one or more risk factors, e.g. prior stroke or transient ischemic attack (TIA), age  &ge;75 yrs, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, symptomatic heart failure (NYHA Class &ge; II). Treatment of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE), and prevention of recurrent DVT and PE in adults."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Prevention of VTE-</b> elective hip or knee replacement surgery: 2.5 mg twice daily, initial dose should be taken 12-24 hrs after surgery. Recommendation duration of treatment - Hip replacement surgery: 32-38 days; Knee replacement surgery: 10-14 days. <b>Prevention of stroke and systemic embolism - NVAF:</b> 5 mg twice daily. In patients with at least 2 of the following characteristics: &ge;80 years, BW &le;60 kg, or serum creatinine &ge;1.5 mg/dL (133 micromole/L): 2.5 mg twice daily. <b>Treatment of DVT and PE:</b> 10 mg twice daily for 7 days followed by 5 mg twice daily. <b>Prevention of recurrent DVT and PE:</b> 2.5 mg twice daily after at least 6 months for DVT and PE. Patients who may require cardioversion but have not previously been treated with anticoagulants: 5 doses of apixaban 5 mg twice daily before cardioversion. If cardioversion is required before 5 doses of apixaban can be administered a 10 mg loading dose then 5 mg twice daily. The loading dose should be given at least 2 hrs before cardioversion."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Active pathological bleeding."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Increased risk of stroke. Concomitant use of antiplatelet agents, anticoagulants, heparin, thrombolytic agents selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, serotonin norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors, and NSAIDs may increase the risk of bleeding.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Anemia, hemorrhage, hematoma, epistaxis, nausea, GI hemorrhage, rectal hemorrhage, gingival bleeding, gamma-glutamyltranserase increased, hematuria, confusion. Prevention of stroke and systemic embolism in adult patients with NVAF, one more risk factor: Eye hemorrhage, hypotension. Treatment of DVT and PE, and prevention of recurrent DVT and PE: Mouth hemorrhage, alanine aminotransferase increased, skin rash, abdominal vaginal hemorrhage, urogenital hemorrhage."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 2.5 mg, 5 mg."
          }
        ],

            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Prevention of episodes of angina pectoris. Adjuvant treatment of visual disorders of circulatory origin; vertigo and tinnitus."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "1 tab in the morning and evening. Take with food."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Parkinson's disease, Parkinsonian symptoms, tremors, restless leg syndrome, and other movement-related disorders. Severe renal impairment (CrCl < 30 mL/min). Pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not a curative treatment for angina pectoris, initial treatment for unstable angina pectoris or MI, or in the pre-hospital phase or during first days of hospitalization. Patients with moderate renal impairment. May aggravate or cause symptoms similar to Parkinson’s disease; falls following drop in BP and balance loss, particularly in patients on antihypertensives. Reevaluate coronaropathy and consider treatment adaptation in the event of angina attack. Discontinue if Parkinsonian symptoms, restless leg syndrome, tremors, gait instability occur. Elderly >75 yrs. Lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Dizziness, headache, abdominal pain, diarrhea, dyspepsia, nausea, vomiting, rash, pruritus, urticaria, asthenia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "MAOIs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Modified release tablet 35 mg (P9.00)."
          }

        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Amiodarone HCl",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Antiarrhythmics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Control of ventricular and supraventricular arrhythmias, including arrhythmias associated with Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome. Prevention of arrhythmias in patients with myocardial infarction or heart failure."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Initial dose:</b> 200 mg thrice daily for a week, then 200 mg twice daily for a week, and then a usual maintenance dosage of 200 mg or less daily, according to patient's response."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Patients with bradycardia, SA block, AV block, or other severe conduction disorders (unless patient has a pacemaker), severe hypotension, or severe respiratory failure. Lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with heart failure. Electrolyte disorders should be corrected before starting treatment. Avoid in patients with iodine sensitivity, or evidence or history of thyroid disorders. Avoid exposure to sunlight. Monitor thyroid function regularly.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Severe bradycardia, sinus arrest, and conduction disturbances; benign intracranial HTN, hemolytic or aplastic anemia, peripheral neuropathy, paresthesia, myopathy, ataxia, tremor, nausea, vomiting, metallic taste, nightmares, headaches, sleeplessness, fatigue, and epididymitis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Beta-blockers or CCBs, and with other anti-arrhythmic drugs. Arrhythmogenic drugs (e.g. phenothiazine). Antipsychotics, tricyclic antidepressants, halofantrine, and terfenadine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 200 mg (P48.53)."

        "id": 4858,

        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,

          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Tranexamic acid",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Hemostatics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "For short term use for hemorrhage or risk hemorrhage in those with increase fibrinolysis or fibrinogenolysis; Local fibrinolysis may occur in condition such as prostate and bladder surgery, menorrhagia, nosebleed, cervical conization, traumatic hyphema, dental extraction in hemophilia patients, hereditary angioneurotic edema."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults:</b> Local fibrinolysis – 15-25 mg/kg BW 2-3x daily; Prostatectomy: Start pre- or post-operative with injectable form, followed by 2 tabs 2-3x daily. Menorrhagia: 2-3 tabs daily for 4 days. Max dose 4 g; Epistaxis: 2 tabs 3x daily for 7 days; Cervix conization: 3 tabs 3x daily; Traumatic hyphema: 2-3 tabs 3x daily; Hemophilia: For dental extraction management, 2-3 tabs every 8 hrs; Hereditary angioneurotic edema: 2-3 tabs 2-3x daily. <b>Childn:</b> 25 mg/kg/dose BW. <b>Renal impairment – Serum creatinine</b> 120-249 &mu;mol/L: 15 mg/kg BW 2x daily; 250-500 &mu;mol/L: 15 mg/kg BW daily."
          },
          {

        "content": "Tetanus and diphtheria toxoids adsorbed and combined with component acellular pertussis vaccine",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "DPT & Tetanus Vaccines"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Active booster immunization for prevention of tetanus, diphtheria, and pertussis in patients &ge;4 yrs. Passive protection against pertussis in early infancy following maternal immunization during pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "0.5 mL IM as a single inj preferably into the deltoid muscle. Re-dosing can be used to boost immunity to diphtheria, tetanus, and pertussis at 5- to 10-yr intervals. The immunization schedule with Adacel should follow local recommendations. Adacel may be administered to pregnant women during the  3<sup>rd</sup> trimester to provide passive protection of infants against pertussis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Encephalopathy within 7 days of administration of a previous dose of any vaccine containing pertussis antigens not attributable to another identifiable cause. Progressive neurological disorders, uncontrolled epilepsy or progressive encephalopathy. Febrile/acute illness. Avoid fractional doses <0.5 mL."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Avoid IV, intradermal, and buttocks administration. Hemophilia, thrombocytopenia, patients on anticoagulant therapy. Syncope. May be administered concomitantly with other inactivated and live vaccines at different sites. Do not mix with other parenterals in the same syringe. Childn < 4 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Pain and swelling at the inj site, tiredness, chills, fever, headache, muscle weakness, sore/swollen joints, nausea, diarrhea, and vomiting. Usually transient and of mild to moderate intensity. Anaphylactic reactions."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Immunosuppressive treatments."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Suspension for injection (IM) 0.5 mL."

  {
    "id": 3018,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 3018,
        "brand_name": "Adcetris",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/IomRvgMLnpkbmw5aqPecihseHKIEByEA2d8Gy6UiUWvwc7hJta.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/GxPFypNzQGyyNKU8500b2rnpGc0J8u9ijjLWLqcCDr2Y1e5im7.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/wKPj68YzYRePzbpmjBVcjQppgHTqpRgjPUCNArsonNzpOeXgn0.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Brentuximab vedotin",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Monoclonal Antibodies, Antineoplastic"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of adults with: (1) previously untreated CD30+ Stage IV Hodgkin lymphoma (HL) in combination with doxorubicin, vinblastine, and dacarbazine (AVD); (2) CD30+ HL at increased risk of relapse or progression following autologous stem cell transplant (ASCT); (3) relapsed or refractory CD30+ HL following ASCT or at least 2 prior therapies when ASCT or multi-agent chemotherapy is not a treatment option; (4) previously untreated systemic anaplastic large cell lymphoma (sALCL) or other CD30-expressing peripheral T-cell lymphomas (PTCL), including angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma and PTCL not otherwise specified, in combination with cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, and prednisone (CHP); (5) relapsed or refractory sALCL; (6) CD30+ cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (CTCL) after at least 1 prior systemic therapy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Previously untreated HL:</b> 1.2 mg/kg IV infusion over 30 mins on days 1 and 15 of each 28-day cycle for 6 cycles, in combination with AVD. <b>HL at increased risk of relapse or progression:</b> Following recovery from ASCT, 1.8 mg/kg IV infusion over 30 mins every 3 weeks up to 16 cycles. <b>Relapsed or refractory HL or sALCL, retreatment with brentuximab:</b> 1.8 mg/kg IV infusion over 30 mins every 3 weeks. Patients who achieve stable disease or better should receive 8-16 cycles. <b>Previously untreated sALCL or other CD30-expressing PTCL:</b> 1.8 mg/kg IV infusion over 30 mins every 3 weeks for 6-8 cycles in combination with CHP chemotherapy. <b>CTCL:</b> 1.8 mg/kg IV infusion over 30 mins every 3 weeks up to 16 cycles. If neutropenia or neuropathy develops or worsens: Modify dosage. <b>Hepatic or severe renal impairment -</b> Patients receiving brentuximab vedotin (BV) monotherapy: 1.2 mg/kg IV infusion over 30 mins every 3 weeks. <b>Mild hepatic impairment -</b> Patients receiving BV-AVD: 0.9 mg/kg IV infusion over 30 mins every 3 weeks; BV-CHP: 1.2 mg/kg IV infusion over 30 mins every 3 weeks."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Concomitant use with bleomycin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Monitor CBC prior to administration of each dose. Patients should be monitored during and after infusion. Do not administer IV push/bolus. JCV reactivation resulting in PML. Acute pancreatitis, pulmonary toxicity (e.g. pneumonitis, ILD, ARDS), serious and opportunistic infections, immediate and delayed IRR, peripheral neuropathy, Grade 3 or 4 anemia, thrombocytopenia, prolonged Grade 3 or 4 neutropenia, febrile neutropenia, SCARs, GI complications, hyperglycemia, infusion site extravasation. Patients with renal/hepatic impairment and those at risk of TLS (e.g. with rapidly proliferating tumors and high tumor burden). Hepatotoxicity. Patients on a controlled sodium diet. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn < 18 yrs. Testicular toxicity and may alter male fertility. Women of childbearing potential. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Infections, URTI, cough, dyspnea, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation, abdominal pain, rash, pruritus, arthralgia, myalgia, fatigue, pyrexia, infusion-related reactions, weight decrease; neutropenia, peripheral neuropathy. Herpes zoster, herpes simplex, oral candidiasis, pneumonia, anemia, thrombocytopenia, hyperglycemia, dizziness, AST/ALT increase, alopecia, back pain, chills."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Bleomycin, CYP3A4 inducers (e.g. rifampicin) and inhibitors (e.g. ketoconazole)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Powder for concentrate for solution for IV infusion 50 mg (P122,962.00)."
          }
        ],

          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/TcgykcR8LPnO4i7JqESOvQRaRtwm5hSN3Fzx9wLVGzMLQjVAK5.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Apixaban",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Anticoagulants"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Prevention of venous thromboembolic events (VTE) in adult patients who have undergone elective hip or knee replacement surgery. Treatment of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE); prevention of recurrent DVT and PE. Reduce the risk of stroke, systemic embolism, and death in patients with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation with one or more risk factors."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Prevention of VTE – Elective hip or knee replacement surgery:</b> 2.5 mg twice daily, taken 12-24 hrs after surgery. Duration of treatment for patients undergoing hip replacement surgery: 32 to 38 days; knee replacement surgery: 10-14 days. <b>Prevention of stroke and systemic embolism – NVAF:</b> 5 mg twice daily. In patients with at least 2 of the following characteristics: age &ge;80 yrs, BW &le;60 kg, or serum creatinine &ge;1.5 mg/dL (133 micromole/L): 2.5 mg twice daily. <b>Treatment of DVT and PE:</b> 10 mg twice daily for 7 days, followed by 5 mg twice daily. <b>Prevention of recurrent DVT and PE:</b> 2.5 mg twice daily after at least 6 months of treatment for DVT or PE. <b>Cardioversion</b> - For patients initiating treatment with apixaban: 5 single doses of 5 mg twice daily before cardioversion. Dose reduction to 2.5 mg twice daily. If cardioversion is required before 5 doses of apixaban can be administered, give 10 mg loading dose then 5 mg twice daily. Dose reduction to 5 mg loading dose followed by 2.5 mg twice. Loading dose to be given at least 2 hrs before cardioversion."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Increased risk of hemorrhage, bleeding. Discontinue prior to elective surgery or invasive procedures places patients at an increased risk of thrombosis. Renal Impairment (CrCl < 15 mL/min) or undergoing dialysis; mild or moderate hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh A or B). Post-op use of indwelling epidural catheters or concomitant use of medicinal products affecting homeostasis. Risk of developing an epidural or spinal hematoma which can result in long-term or permanent paralysis. Childn < 18 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Anemia, hemorrhage, contusion, epistaxis, hematuria, hematoma, gingival bleeding, menorrhagia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Anticoagulants. Strong CYP3A4 and P-gp inhibitors (e.g. ketoconazole), inducers (e.g. rifampin, phenytoin, carbamazepine, or St. John’s wort), and HIV protease inhibitors (e.g. ritonavir). Platelet aggregation inhibitors or other antithrombotic agents and NSAIDs including aspirin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 2.5 mg, 5 mg."
          }
        ],

            "content": "<b>Cap:</b> Patients with gallbladder disease, diabetes, predisposition to gout, renal impairment. May cause GI irritation, abdominal pain with nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or constipation. Avoid in patients with severe peptic ulcer, enteritis, or ulcerative colitis. Avoid iron for more than 6 months. May impair ability to drive or operate machines. Long-term therapy. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Numbness, hypersensitivity reactions, flatulence, diarrhea/constipation, vomiting, abdominal pain, black stool discoloration, bright yellow urine, drowsiness, mouth dryness and jitteriness. Cap: Irritability, vomiting, loss of appetite, skin changes, hypercalcemia, hypercalciuria."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Alcohol. Neomycin, fluorouracil, anticonvulsants, levodopa, altretamine, aspirin, PPIs, H2-receptor antagonists, colchicine, chloramphenicol, antacids, penicillamine, tetracycline, cefdinir, methyldopa, quinolone antibiotics, levothyroxine, barbiturates, hypnotics, narcotics, analgesics, sedatives, tranquilizers. Coffee, tea, red wine. <b>Cap:</b> Contraceptive pills, warfarin, cholestyramine, paraffin oil, paricalcitol, calcipotriene, doxercalciferol, mineral oil, orlistat, colesevelam, colestipol, thiazide diuretics."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Syrup 60 mL (P222.37), 120 mL (P438.32). Capsule (P17.58) (Rx)."
          }

        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Inhaled Corticosteroids"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Regular treatment of asthma where use of a combination product (long-acting beta-2-agonist and inhaled corticosteroid) is appropriate. Patients not adequately controlled with inhaled corticosteroids and 'as needed' inhaled short acting beta-2 agonist. Patients already adequately controlled on both inhaled corticosteroid and long-acting beta-2-agonist."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adult and adolescents (12 years and older)</b>: 2 inhalations twice daily. <b>Children (4 years and older)</b>: 2 inhalations of 25 mcg salmeterol and 50 mcg fluticasone propionate twice daily. Maximum: 100 mcg twice daily. No need to adjust the dose in elderly patients or in those with renal impairment."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Should not be used to treat acute asthma symptoms for which a fast and short acting bronchodilator is required. Pulmonary tuberculosis, paradoxical bronchospasm, cushing's syndrome, cushingold features, adrenal suppression, decrease in bone mineral density, cataract and glaucoma. Children and adolescents < 16 years. The height of children receiving prolonged treatment with inhaled corticosteroid is regularly monitored. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Candidiasis of the mouth and throat, pneumonia and bronchitis. Hypokalemia, headache, nasopharyngitis, hoarseness/dysphonia and sinusitis. Contusions, traumatic fractures, arthralgia and myalgia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Ritonavir, ketoconazole and other potent CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. itraconazole, telithromycin). Erythromycin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Metered Dose Inhaler 25 mcg/125 mcg per actuation (P394.52), 25 mcg/250 mcg per actuation (P553.84)."
          }
        ],

            "content": "Statins"
          },
          {

            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Reduce LDL-C, apolipoprotein B and triglycerides; and to increase HDL-C in the treatment of hyperlipidemias, including hypercholesterolemia and combined hyperlipidemia, hypertriglyceridemia and dysbetalipoproteinemia. Adjunctive therapy in patients with homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia who have some LDL-receptor function."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Initially 10-20 mg daily, may be adjusted to a max of 80 mg daily at 4-week interval."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Active liver disease or unexplained persistent serum aminotransferase elevations. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Severe renal impairment, risk of rhabdomyolysis. Discontinue use if creatinine phosphokinase increases significantly or if myopathy is diagnosed. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category X.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "GI disturbances."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",

          },
          {

  {
    "id": 1613,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 1613,
        "brand_name": "Amlife",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Losartan potassium, amlodipine besilate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Angiotensin II Receptor Blockers"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Hypertension (HTN)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Individualized dosing. <b>Usual dose:</b> 1 tab daily Losartan 50 mg + Amlodipine 5 mg fixed-dose combination (FDC). <b>Uncontrolled BP after 1-2 weeks of treatment:</b> 1 tab/day Losartan 100 mg + Amlodipine 5 mg FDC or 1 tab/day Losartan 100 mg + Amlodipine 10 mg FDC."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Severe hepatic impairment, shock, severe hypotension, high-grade aortic stenosis, and unstable heart failure after MI. Concomitant use with aliskiren in patients with DM or renal impairment (GFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>). Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Fetal toxicity. Hypotension, electrolyte imbalance. Patients with renal and hepatic impairment, primary hyperaldosteronism, ischemic CV and cerebrovascular disease, heart failure, aortic and mitral valve stenosis, obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, angioedema. May impair ability to drive and operate machines. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category C (1<sup>st</sup> trimester) and D (2<sup>nd</sup> and 3<sup>rd</sup> trimester).",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Somnolence, dizziness, headache, palpitations, flushing, abdominal pain, nausea, ankle swelling, edema, and fatigue."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "<b>Losartan:</b> Lithium, potassium-sparing diuretics, potassium supplements or salt substitutes containing potassium, NSAIDs (i.e. selective COX-2 inhibitors), ARBs and ACE inhibitors, tricyclic antidepressants, antipsychotics, baclofene, amifostine, rifampicin, and fluconazole. <b>Amlodipine:</b> Grapefruit juice, simvastatin, immunosuppressants, CYP3A4 inhibitors and inducers."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 50 mg/5 mg (P23.93), 100 mg/5 mg (P29.85), 100 mg/10 mg (P34.15)."
          }
        ],

            "content": "Monotherapy for the 1<sup>st</sup> treatment of mild to moderate hypertension (HTN).           {

            "content": "<b>Adults – HTN, angina</b>: Initially 5 mg once daily, may be increased to max 10 mg. <b>Small, fragile or elderly patients and patients with hepatic insufficiency</b>: 2.5 mg once daily."

            "content": "<b>HTN</b>: 50 mg once daily, may be increased to 100 mg daily as a single dose or in 2 divided doses. <b>In elderly >75 yrs, patients with moderate or severe renal impairment (CrCl < 20 mL/min) or intravascular fluid depletion:</b> 25 mg once daily.           },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with renal artery stenosis, renal impairment and hepatic impairment, vol depletion.           "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/WVYh1uvxBUPtd8ZqTrYlJVYNFq2jZRtrVxfYbxmnpmY4SL4Dcu.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/QfwQGecuZsMUeJ60G2G2RMj5MhfBoids8teaszT552wbLMEwff.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/uWSaVdoWIibR1wNX1HfAVf8AqSITK4iiOtF4c5ELqEuucxgtDC.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Valsartan, amlodipine besilate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Angiotensin II Receptor Blockers"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of essential hypertension. For patients whose BP is not adequately controlled on valsartan or amlodipine monotherapy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "1 tab daily. Patients with mild to moderate hepatic impairment without cholestasis: Max 80 mg valsartan."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to valsartan, amlodipine or dihydropyridine derivatives. Severe hepatic impairment. Severe renal impairment (GFR &lt;30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>) and patients undergoing dialysis. Biliary cirrhosis or cholestasis. Pregnancy (2<sup>nd</sup> and 3<sup>rd</sup> trimesters)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Sodium- and/or vol-depleted patients. Concomitant use of products containing potassium. Frequent monitoring of potassium levels. Patients with bilateral renal artery stenosis or stenosis to a solitary kidney; recent kidney transplantation; hepatic impairment or biliary obstructive disorders; primary hyperaldosteronism; severe heart failure; aortic or mitral valve stenosis or obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Elderly &ge;65 yrs. Childn and adolescents &lt;18 yrs. Pregnancy (1<sup>st</sup> trimester) and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nasopharyngitis, influenza; headache; edema; pitting, facial, and peripheral edema; fatigue, flushing, asthenia, hot flush; vomiting."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "<b>Valsartan</b>: Lithium; potassium-sparing diuretics, potassium supplements, salt substitutes containing potassium and other substances that may increase potassium levels; NSAIDs including selective COX inhibitors, aspirin and non-selective NSAIDs; TCAs, alpha-blockers for treatment of BPH. <b>Amlodipine</b>: CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. ketoconazole, itraconazole, ritonavir); CYP3A4 inducers (e.g. carbamazepine, phenobarbital, phenytoin, fosphenytoin, primidone, rifampicin, St. John’s wort)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 80 mg/5 mg (P33.00), 160 mg/5 mg (P42.85), 160 mg/10 mg (P42.85)."
          }
        ],

    "id": 2989,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 2989,
        "brand_name": "Amoclav",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/Y41LMWToxHEUkE0g8HcKSKpzrHmzYX7wMeA3iCaR26xIeLHj6N.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/VrAHBgQBcziD6l5szCSAB1bb8mVTTsVMDDpBUlUEmgn2shjcoN.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/K0gySLD3KmxmZEIubbwOdtmaQbl1JjkYgNJDcMzKPmNrM3Yr4F.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Co-amoxiclav",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Penicillins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of upper respiratory tract infections (URTI) e.g. tonsillitis, sinusitis, otitis media; lower respiratory tract infections (LRTI) e.g. acute and chronic bronchitis, pneumonia, lung abscess; cystitis, urethritis, pyelonephritis, female genital infections, septic abortion, pelvic or puerperal sepsis, intraabdominal sepsis, furuncle and abcess, cellulitis, wound infections, osteomyelitis, dentoalveolar abscess, septicemia, peritonitis, and post-op infections caused by susceptible microorganisms."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "All doses taken before meals. Treatment duration: Max 14 days. <b>Adults and childn >12 yrs - Mild to moderate infections:</b> 375 mg tab every 8 hrs or 625 mg tab every 12 hrs; <b>Dental infections:</b> 375 mg tab every 8 hrs for 5 days; <b>Severe infections (including chronic and recurrent urinary tract infections and LRTI):</b> 625 mg tab every 8 hrs or 1 g tab every 12 hrs. <b>Renal impairment -</b> CrCl 10-30 mL/min: 375 mg or 625 mg tab every 12 hrs; < 10 mL/min: 375 mg tab every 12 hrs. Hemodialysis: 375 mg or 625 mg tab every 24 hrs, with an additional dose both during and at the end of dialysis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. History of co-amoxiclav or penicillin-associated cholestatic jaundice or hepatic impairment; glandular fever or lymphatic lymphoma."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with renal and hepatic impairment; infectious mononucleosis. CDAD; hepatic dysfunction including hepatitis and cholestatic jaundice. Overgrowth of nonsusceptible organisms including fungi during prolonged use. Maintain adequate fluid intake and urinary output. Evaluate renal, hepatic, and hematopoietic status periodically during prolonged therapy. Concomitant use with anticoagulants. May impair ability to drive or operate machines. Childn < 40 kg. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category B.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Diarrhea, nausea, vomiting."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Probenecid, allopurinol, methotrexate, oral contraceptives, oral anticoagulants (e.g. acenocoumarol, warfarin), disulfiram, mycophenolate mofetil. False positive reaction in Clinitest, Benedict’s soln, Coombs’ test."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 625 mg (P53.50), 1 g (P75.25)."
          }
        ],
        "company": {

        },

          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/Oju7zgrUm2rtyY9xIQRjbPsio1jUFEnTRXMpnYC6Al0AjfztOA.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/dDAdYuna4ZTJR2uh8qkGmY56yvtFkEIXOZf08DOUI33l1NYlSV.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Co-amoxiclav",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Penicillins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "<b>Susp 156.25 mg and 312.5 mg:</b> Treatment of acute bacterial sinusitis, otitis media, and exacerbations of chronic bronchitis; community-acquired pneumonia; cystitis; pyelonephritis; skin and soft tissue infections; bone and joint infections. <b>Susp 228.5 mg and 457 mg:</b> Short-term treatment of upper and lower respiratory tract infections (URTI and LRTI); genitourinary tract (GUT) and abdominal; skin and skin structure; bone and joint; and dental infections."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Susp 156.25 mg and 312.5 mg - Adults and childn &ge;40 kg:</b> 500 mg/125 mg thrice daily; <b>Childn < 40 kg:</b> 20 mg/5 mg/kg/day in 3 divided doses. <b>Renal impairment -</b> Adults and childn &ge;40 kg: CrCl 10-30 mL/min: 500 mg/125 mg twice daily; < 10 mL/min or on hemodialysis: 500 mg/125 mg once daily. Additional 500 mg/125 mg both during and at the end of dialysis; Childn < 40 kg: CrCl 10-30 mL/min: 15 mg/3.75 mg/kg twice daily; < 10 mL/min or on hemodialysis: 15 mg/3.75 mg/kg once daily. Additional 15 mg/3.75 mg/kg both during and at the end of dialysis. <b>Susp 228.5 mg - Childn 6-12 yrs with 18-40 kg BW:</b> Mild to moderate: 5-10 mL; Severe: 10-20 mL; <b>1-6 yrs with 10-18 kg BW:</b> Mild to moderate: 2.5-5 mL; Severe: 5-10 mL; <b>< 1 yr with < 10 kg BW:</b> Mild, moderate, and severe: 2.5 mL. All given in divided doses every 12 hrs; <b>Renal impairment (Childn up to 12 yrs) -</b> CrCl 10-30 mL/min: 15 mg/kg every 12 hrs; < 10 mL/min or on hemodialysis: 15 mg/kg once daily. Additional 15 mg/kg both during and at the end of dialysis. <b>Susp 457 mg - Childn 6-12 yrs with 18-40 kg BW:</b> Mild to moderate: 2.5-5 mL; Severe: 5-10 mL; <b>1-6 yrs with 10-18 kg:</b> Mild to moderate: 2.5 mL; Severe: 2.5-5 mL. All given in divided doses every 12 hrs; <b>Renal impairment (Childn up to 12 yrs) -</b> CrCl 10-30 mL/min: 15 mg/kg every 12 hrs; < 10 mL/min or on hemodialysis: 15 mg/kg once daily. Additional 15 mg/kg both during and at the end of dialysis. Shake well. All doses taken before meals."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. History of amoxicillin/clavulanic acid-associated jaundice/hepatic impairment. Possible cross-sensitivity with other beta-lactam antibiotics. Suspected infectious mononucleosis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "History of penicillin hypersensitivity or atopic individuals. Overgrowth of non-susceptible organisms (prolonged use). Hepatic dysfunctions. Antibiotic-associated colitis. <i>Clostridium difficile</i>-associated diseases. Concomitant use of anticoagulants. Periodic assessment of organ system functions during prolonged therapy. Maintain adequate hydration. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation. <b>Susp 156.25 mg and 312.5 mg:</b> Convulsions in patients with impaired renal function or those receiving high doses. Feverish generalized erythema associated with pustula.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, mucocutaneous candidosis, overgrowth of non-susceptible organisms."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Oral anticoagulants, methotrexate, probenecid, mycophenolate mofetil. <b>Susp 228.5 mg and 457 mg:</b> Allopurinol, oral contraceptives, disulfiram. False positive reactions (e.g. Clinitest, Benedict’s Soln). Possible false positive Coomb’s test."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Powder for suspension 228.5 mg/5 mL x 70 mL (P397.00); 312.5 mg/5 mL x 60 mL (P267.50); 457 mg/5 mL x 35 mL (P297.00), 70 mL (P470.25); 642.9 mg/5 mL x 100 mL (P513.25)."
          }
        ],

            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Secretolytic therapy in acute and chronic bronchopulmonary diseases accompanied by impaired formation and transport of mucus."

            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Adults and adolescents from 14 yrs: &frac12; effervescent tab twice daily or 1 effervescent tab once daily. Dissolve effervescent tab in a glass of water and take after meals. Do not take more than 4-5 days without medical advice."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Active peptic ulceration. Do not use 600 mg in childn &lt;14 yrs. Childn &lt;2 yrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with bronchial asthma, history of ulcers particularly if additional drugs are taken that are known to irritate the mucous membranes.           },

          },
          {

            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Advanced aortic stenosis, severe liver failure and known history of shock. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {

          {

          },
          {

            "content": "Treatment of hypertension (HTN)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "1 tab of 5 mg/12.5 mg once daily. Dose may be increased to 1 tab amlodipine 10 mg + HCTZ 12.5 mg once daily depending on the individual patient’s response."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Severe hypotension, shock, obstruction of outflow tract of left ventricle (e.g. high-grade aortic stenosis), unstable heart failure after MI, and anuria."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "May worsen angina, acute MI, and SLE. May cause symptomatic hypotension, hypercalcemia, idiosyncratic reaction, and non-melanoma skin cancer. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category C",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [

                  "title": "C",

                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Blood and lymphatic system, immune system, psychiatric, nervous, eye, ear and labyrinth, cardiac, vascular, respiratory, thoracic and mediastinal, GI, hepatobiliary, skin and subcutaneous tissue, musculoskeletal and connective tissue, renal and urinary, breast and reproductive system disorders. Asthenia. <b>Amlodipine:</b> Chest pain, edema, fatigue, hot flushes, malaise, pain, rigors. Weight increase/decrease. <b>HCTZ:</b> Fever and weakness. Increased total cholesterol, LDL-C, VLDL-C, and triglycerides."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Grapefruit juice, simvastatin, strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors, macrolides, immunosuppressants, and mechanistic target of rapamycin inhibitors. Amantadine, aminoglycoside antibiotics, diazoxide, calcium salts, vit D supplements, carbamazepine, cardiac glycosides, cholestyramine and colestipol resins, corticosteroids, ciclosporin, lithium, pressor amines, NSAIDS (i.e. COX-2 inhibitors), skeletal muscle relaxants, SSRIs, topiramate, and iodinated contrast media. Anticholinergic, antidiabetic, antigout, cytotoxic, and other antihypertensive agents."

          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Symptomatic treatment of mild, moderate, and severe Alzheimer’s disease; vascular dementia (dementia associated with cerebrovascular disease); dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults and elderly</b>: Initially, 5 mg once a day in the evening, before bedtime. The dose 5 mg/day should be maintained for at least 1 month for earlier assessment of clinical response and for steady-state concentrations of donepezil to be achieved. Dose can be increased to 10 mg once a day after a 4-6 weeks clinical assessment in patients who tolerated treatment at 5 mg/day. <b>Patients with DLB</b>: Dose may be decreased to 5 mg depending on the symptoms of the patient. Tab should be placed on the tongue and allowed to disintegrate before swallowing with or without water."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to donepezil or to piperidine derivatives."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients receiving anesthesia and NSAIDs.  Bradycardia. GI bleeding, ulcer, convulsions. History of asthma or obstructive pulmonary disease. Hepatic Impairment. Bladder outflow obstruction, generalized convulsions. Minor to moderate influence on the ability to drive and use machines. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Diarrhea, muscle cramps, fatigue, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, headache, pain, accident, common cold, abdominal disturbance, dizziness, syncope, bradycardia, SA and AV block, aggression, fall, UTI, nasopharyngitis, agitation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "CYP3A4 inhibitors e.g. ketoconazole, itraconazole, erythromycin. CYP2D6 inhibitors e.g. quinidine, fluoxetine.           },
          {
