          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/KDu45CV2sh5ZS1usAxY29ZPHVFT2I2UfwcPpeW87QAdE6aRE11.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/kmbWI8MPOcvXUlO0DaP8yalPU3gRpjfOEqxWnblwq8ZEbgHavB.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Aripiprazole",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Atypical Antipsychotics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of schizophrenia in adults and adolescents &ge;15 yrs; moderate to severe manic episodes in bipolar I disorder in adolescents &ge;13 yrs. Prevention of new manic episodes in adults with predominantly manic episodes."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults - Schizophrenia:</b> Initially 10 mg/day or 15 mg/day. Maintenance: 15 mg once daily. Max 30 mg daily. <b>Manic episodes in bipolar I disorder:</b> Initially 15 mg once daily. Max 30 mg. <b>Childn - Schizophrenia:</b> Initially 2 mg for 2 days, titrated to 5 mg for 2 additional days to reach 10 mg once daily. Subsequent doses may be increased in 5 mg increments. Max 30 mg daily. <b>Manic episodes in bipolar I disorder:</b> Initially 2 mg for 2 days, titrated to 5 mg for 2 additional days to reach 10 mg once daily for max 12 weeks. Place the tab on the tongue. Alternatively, tab may be dispersed in water."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not indicated for treatment of dementia-related psychosis. Patients with CV disease, cerebrovascular disease, predisposition to hypotension or HTN, family history of QT prolongation or DM, history of seizure disorder, aspiration pneumonia, phenylketonuria. Suicidal behavior, VTE, hyperglycemia, weight gain, dysphagia, increased and uncontrollable urges, somnolence, postural hypotension, motor and sensory instability. Consider dose reduction or discontinuation if tardive dyskinesia or symptoms of other EPS occur. Discontinue if NMS occurs. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Elderly &ge;65 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Akathisia, nausea, DM, insomnia, anxiety, restlessness, EPS disorder, tremor, headache, sedation, somnolence, dizziness, blurred vision, constipation, dyspepsia, salivary hypersecretion, vomiting, fatigue."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole, itraconazole, HIV protease inhibitors, diltiazem) and inducers (e.g., carbamazepine, rifampicin, rifabutin, phenytoin, phenobarbital, primidone, efavirenz, nevirapine, St John’s Wort), CYP2D6 inhibitors (e.g., quinidine, fluoxetine, paroxetine, escitalopram), SSRI, SNRI, antihypertensives, CNS drugs, QT prolonging drugs, drugs-induced electrolyte imbalance. Alcohol."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Orodispersible tablet 10 mg."
          }
        ],

        "content": "Montelukast sodium",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Leukotriene Receptor Antagonists (LTRA)"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of asthma as add-on therapy in childn with mild to moderate persistent asthma inadequately controlled with inhaled corticosteroids and short-acting beta-agonists. As alternative treatment to low-dose inhaled corticosteroids in patients who do not have a recent history of serious asthma attacks and are not capable of using inhaled corticosteroids. As prophylaxis for exercise-induced asthma."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Childn 6-14 yrs:</b> 5 mg chewable tab; <b>2-5 yrs:</b> 4 mg chewable tab. Doses are administered once daily in the evening, taken 1 hr before or 2 hrs after food."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with asthma exacerbations after exercise should continue using their usual regimen of inhaled beta-agonists as prophylaxis and have a short-acting inhaled beta-agonist available to the rescue. Patients on therapy may present with systemic eosinophilia. Do not abruptly substitute montelukast for inhaled or oral corticosteroids. Not used in the treatment of acute asthma attacks. Not recommended as monotherapy in patients with moderate persistent asthma. Evaluate patients for asthma control periodically. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category B.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "URTI, diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, increased ALT and AST, rash, pyrexia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Hepatic enzyme inducers e.g. phenytoin, phenobarbital, and rifampicin. Aspirin, NSAIDs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Chewable tablet 4 mg (P14.50), 5 mg (P21.43)."
          }
        ],
        "company": {

        "content": "Venlafaxine HCl",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Tricyclics; Norepinephrine- Reuptake Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of major depressive disorder (MDD), generalized anxiety disorder (GAD), social anxiety disorder (SAD), and panic disorder with or without agoraphobia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>MDD, GAD:</b> Initially 75 mg, may be increased up to max 225 mg/day. Some may start at 37.5 mg for 4-7 days, then increase to 75 mg. Dose increases should be in increments of up to 75 mg/day at intervals of not < 4 days. <b>SAD:</b> 75 mg. <b>Panic disorder:</b> Initially 37.5 mg for 7 days, increased to 75 mg the following week and may be increased up to max 225 mg/day. Dose increases should be in increments of up to 75 mg/day at intervals of not < 7 days. <b>Mild to moderate hepatic impairment:</b> Reduce dose by 50%. <b>Renal impairment:</b> Reduce total daily dose by 25-50%. All taken as a single dose with meals either in the morning or evening at approx same time each day. Swallow whole; do not divide/crush/chew/place in water. Cap may be opened carefully and sprinkled on a spoonful of applesauce, then swallowed immediately followed by a glass of water."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Concomitant use with MAOIs (e.g. linezolid, IV methylene blue) or use within 7-14 days of treatment discontinuation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Avoid abrupt withdrawal. Suicide risk and suicidal ideation/behavior or unusual change in behavior. Screen for bipolar disorder; not for treatment of bipolar depression. Patients with history of mania/hypomania, MI, unstable heart disease, hyperthyroidism, heart failure, renal impairment, liver cirrhosis, HTN. Concomitant use with other serotonergic drugs (triptans, TCAs, fentanyl, lithium, tramadol, tryptophan, buspirone, St. John’s Wort). Worsening of symptoms of MDD. Serotonin syndrome, angle-closure glaucoma, sustained HTN; insomnia, nervousness; weight changes; hyponatremia risk in elderly, diuretic use and volume depletion; abnormal bleeding; ILD, eosinophilic pneumonia. Monitor BP regularly. Gradual withdrawal upon discontinuation. Childn. Elderly with hepatic impairment. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Sexual function abnormalities (e.g. abnormal ejaculation, impotence), GI disturbances (e.g. nausea, dry mouth, anorexia, constipation), CNS complaints (e.g. dizziness, somnolence, abnormal dreams, decreased libido, nervousness, insomnia, tremor), abnormal vision, sweating, asthenia, yawning. Chest and neck pain, chills, fever; migraine, tachycardia; increased appetite; ecchymosis; edema, weight gain; amnesia, confusion, depersonalization, hypesthesia, abnormal thinking, trismus, vertigo; increased cough, dyspnea; pruritus; accommodation abnormality, mydriasis, taste perversion; albuminuria, impaired urination."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Cimetidine, haloperidol; NSAIDs, aspirin, warfarin; drugs metabolized by CYP2D6; metoprolol; CNS active drugs; triptans; QT-prolonging drugs. False positive urine immunoassay screening tests for phencyclidine and amphetamine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Sustained-release capsule 75 mg (P28.00), 150 mg (P33.00)."
          }
        ],

          },

        "content": "Aripiprazole",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Atypical Antipsychotics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of schizoprenia in adults and in adolescents &ge;15 yrs; moderate to severe manic episodes in bipolar I disorder and for the prevention of a new manic episode in adults who experienced predominantly manic episodes responded to aripiprazole treatment; up to 12 weeks of moderate to severe manic episodes in bipolar I disorder in adolescents &ge;13 yrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Schizophrenia</b> - Starting dose: 10 or 15 mg/day. Maintenance: 15 mg once a day. Max: 30 mg daily. <b>Bipolar I disorder</b> - Starting dose: 15 mg once daily. Max: 30 mg daily. <b>Schizophrenia in adolescents &ge;15 yrs</b>: 10 mg/day. Initiated at 2 mg (using aripiprazole oral soln 1 mg/mL) for 2 days. Titrate to 5 mg for 2 additional days to reach the recommended daily dose of 10 mg. Increase in 5 mg increments without exceeding the max daily dose 30 mg. <b>Manic episodes in Bipolar I disorder in adolescents &ge;13 yrs</b>: 10 mg once a day.  Initiated at 2 mg (using aripiprazole oral soln 1 mg/mL) for 2 days. Titrate to 5 mg for 2 additional days to reach the recommended daily dose of 10 mg. Tab should be placed on the tongue, where it will rapidly disperse in saliva. Can be taken with or without liquid."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Close supervision for high-risk suicidal patients. Patients with known CV or cerebrovascular disease, predisposition to hypotension or HTN, VTE, hyperglycemia, or seizures. Dose-reduction or discontinuation if signs and symptoms of tardive dyskinesia appear. Do not give to patients with dementia-related psychosis. Monitor regularly for worsening of glucose control for patients with DM. May cause weight gain. Patients at risk for aspiration pneumonia. Patients may experience increased urges, particularly for gambling, and the inability to control urges, other urges: increased sexual urges, compulsive shopping, binge or compulsive eating, and other impulsive and compulsive behaviors. Patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, total lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. ADHD comorbidity.  May cause somnolence, postural hypotension, motor and sensory instability. Coadministration with drugs known to cause QT prolongation or electrolyte imbalance. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "DM, Insomnia, anxiety, restlessness, akathisia, extrapyramidal disorder, tremor, headache, sedation, somnolence, dizziness, blurred vision."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "H2-antagonists, antihypertensives, other CNS drugs, alcohol. Quinidine and other CYP2D6 inhibitors, ketoconazole and other CYP3A4 inhibitors, carbamazepine and other CYP3A4 inducers."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Orally disintegrating tablet 10 mg, 15 mg."
          }

          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/4JdBH7e7XsRM2AzZNBQ5xHaaj1qIeMV9OEGmxrDQI88lZQAHky.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/pMbO51j6sImy0z13TpkWakdFPE2sc04uT0D5ZqgDWvBGhKl9qK.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Etoricoxib",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "COX-2 Specific Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "For symptomatic relief of osteoarthritis (OA), rheumatoid arthritis (RA), ankylosing spondylitis, and the pain and signs of inflammation associated with acute gouty arthritis, and treatment of moderate pain associated with dental surgery in adults and adolescents &gt;16 yrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Acute gouty arthritis</b>: 120 mg/day for max 8 days. <b>OA</b>: 30-60 mg once daily. Max 60 mg/day. <b>RA, ankylosing spondylitis</b>: 60-90 mg once daily. Max 90 mg/day. <b>Post-op dental surgery pain</b>: 90 mg for max 3 days. <b>Hepatic dysfunction</b> - Mild (Child-Pugh score 5-6): Max 60 mg once daily; Moderate (Child-Pugh score 7-9): Max 30 mg once daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with CrCl &lt;30 mL/min. Active peptic ulceration or active GI bleeding. Severe hepatic dysfunction (serum albumin &lt;25 g/L or Child-Pugh score &gt;10). IBS. CHF (NYHA II-IV). CV disease (e.g. HTN, IHD, and stroke). Childn &lt;16 yrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Upper GI complications e.g. perforations, ulcers, or bleedings. History of GI disease e.g. ulceration and GI bleeding. CV risk factors. Compromised renal perfusion. Fluid retention, edema, and HTN. Liver dysfunction. Dehydration. Exfoliative dermatitis, SJS, and toxic epidermal necrolysis. May mask fever and other signs of inflammation. Co-administration of warfarin or other oral anticoagulants. Patients with galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Women attempting to conceive. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Alveolar osteitis; edema/fluid retention; dizziness, headache; palpitations, arrhythmia, HTN; bronchospasms; abdominal pain, constipation, flatulence, gastritis, heartburn/acid reflux, diarrhea, dyspepsia/epigastric discomfort, nausea, vomiting, esophagitis, oral ulcer, ALT, and AST increased; ecchymosis; asthenia/fatigue, flu-like disease; nephrotoxicity including interstitial nephritis, and nephritic syndrome."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Oral anticoagulants, diuretics, ACE inhibitors, ARBs, aspirin, ciclosporin, tacrolimus, lithium, methotrexate, oral contraceptives, HRT, prednisone/prednisolone, digoxin, other drugs metabolized by sulfotransferases (e.g. oral salbutamol, minoxidil), ketoconazole, voriconazole, and miconazole, rifampicin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 120 mg (P65.00)."
          }
        ],

        },

    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 4234,
        "brand_name": "Acantha",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/HCZilr2pZCHngdWyGl8oXq42u2YXIkNbQSlePYbbZfK3uAAfx1.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/GgcP0r1Xwth4jEgDQliVZlHjPleMwijEspUecRoQ8J6ItL3XlR.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/gh0al9QiBYLfqqs9TS4PZwPM3UqTBb8Cd0b2aRlXnG8qWeBaCB.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Sitagliptin (as phosphate)",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Dipeptidyl Peptidase-4 (DPP-4) Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "For adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus, as monotherapy in patients inadequately controlled by diet and exercise alone and for whom metformin is inappropriate due to contraindications or intolerance; in combination with metformin, a sulfonylurea, or a PPAR-gamma agonist (i.e. thiazolidinedione) when diet and exercise plus the individual agent alone do not provide adequate glycemic control; in combination with metformin and a sulfonylurea or a PPAR-gamma when diet and exercise plus dual therapy with these agents do not provide adequate glycemic control; as add-on to insulin (with or without metformin) when diet and exercise plus stable dose of insulin do not provide adequate glycemic control."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "100 mg once daily. In combination with metformin and/or PPAR-gamma agonist: Maintain dose and administer sitagliptin concomitantly. In combination with sulfonylurea or with insulin: Consider lower dose for sulfonylurea or insulin. Renal impairment - Moderate (CrCl &ge;30-&lt;50 mL/min): 50 mg once daily. Severe (CrCl &lt;30 mL/min) or with ESRD (requiring hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis): 25 mg once daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Do not use in patients with type 1 DM or diabetic ketoacidosis. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patient with history of pancreatitis, heart failure, or history of serious hypersensitivity reaction (e.g. angioedema) with other DPP-4 inhibitors. Risk of hypoglycemia. Patient undergoing periods of stress (e.g. trauma, infection, fever, surgery). Childn &lt;18 yrs.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "CYP3A4 inhibitors. Digoxin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 50 mg (P27.00), 100 mg (P28.00)."
          }
        ],
        "company": {
          "id": 790,
          "name": "Corbridge Group Phils., Inc."
        },

  {
    "id": 4235,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 4235,
        "brand_name": "Acantha Max",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/Bj9udNd2iCemGy4crIwWW6TUaWQQJ5TETiiyCKjyt80XX6ZSoU.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/LZGzuIV7AvPgVGVw7bM7atp0qLfHi4z7SUt82XBDsH39Ky6c2h.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/hAhHkzQJbwCYB4GfaZXfZNrtckMyNkb4m9W4pOhBQumOLs5s2r.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Sitagliptin (as phosphate monohydrate), metformin HCl",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Dipeptidyl Peptidase-4 (DPP-4) Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "For adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus. As an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in patients inadequately controlled on their maximal tolerated dose of metformin alone or those already being treated with the combination of sitagliptin and metformin as separate tabs. As triple combination therapy with a sulfonylurea or a PPAR-gamma agonist (i.e. thiazolidinedione) as adjunct to diet and exercise in patients inadequately controlled on metformin and a sulfonylurea or a PPAR-gamma agonist. In combination with insulin as an adjunct to diet and exercise when stable dose of insulin and metformin alone do not provide adequate glycemic control."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Individualized dosage. To be taken twice daily with meals. Max 100 mg sitagliptin and 2,000 mg metformin daily. <b>Patients not currently treated with metformin:</b> Initially 50 mg sitagliptin and 500 mg metformin twice daily with gradual dose escalation. <b>Patients already treated with metformin:</b> 50 mg twice daily (100 mg total daily dose) and the dose of metformin already being taken. <b>Patients taking metformin 850 mg twice daily:</b> 50 mg sitagliptin and 1 g metformin HCl twice daily. Consider lower doses for insulin or insulin secretagogues when used concomitantly."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "History of serious hypersensitivity reaction to sitagliptin, or metformin. Severe renal impairment (eGFR &lt;30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>). Metabolic acidosis, including diabetic ketoacidosis. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Renal impairment (eGFR 30-&lt;45 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>), hepatic impairment. Discontinue at the time of or before iodinated contrast imaging procedures. Lactic acidosis, pancreatitis, heart failure, acute renal failure, vit B deficiency. Severe joint paint, bullous pemphigoid.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Diarrhea, URTI, headache."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Carbonic anhydrase inhibitors. Ranolazine, vandetanib, dolutegravir, and cimetidine. Alcohol."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 50 mg/1 g (P20.50)."
          }
        ],
        "company": {
          "id": 790,
          "name": "Corbridge Group Phils., Inc."
        },

        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/m20LnDU3u3GdXBHv7T3hqOEEMWxMKzx8xigt9cmWWDJHYIYmOl.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/6GLTMVKp3VVj0RJWRj2OYYrT1wZdSuNmGaQvhwN4cxnNLKwXpc.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/QiVsfJU0nsnDmlPmg0SnzfdpQy8JIJ75LxMvaw35GP64CFuDyj.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Omeprazole",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Proton-Pump Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of aspiration syndromes, dyspepsia, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), peptic-ulcer disease (PUD), and Zollinger-Ellison syndrome."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Oral - GERD</b>: 20 mg once daily for 4 weeks. <b>Dyspepsia</b>: 10-20 mg daily for 2-4 weeks. <b>PUD</b>: 20 mg daily as single dose or 40 mg in severe cases. <b>NSAID-associated ulceration</b>: 20 mg daily. <b>Zollinger-Ellison syndrome</b>: 60 mg once daily. <b>Acid aspiration prophylaxis during general anesthesia</b>: 40 mg in the evening before surgery and a further 40 mg 2-6 hrs before the procedure. Injection – Administer in IV infusion for 20-30 mins. <b>Injection</b> - Oral therapy alternative: 40 mg once daily. <b>Zollinger-Ellison syndrome</b>: Initially 60 mg daily. Higher doses may be required and the dose should be adjusted individually. If dose &gt;60 mg daily, dose should be divided and given twice daily. <b>Impaired hepatic function</b>: 10-20 mg daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Concomitant use with nelfinavir."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with hepatic impairment. Lactation. Concomitant use with atazanavir, reduced absorption of vitamin B<sub>12</sub>. Childn.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Headache, diarrhea, abdominal pain, constipation, nausea and vomiting, flatulence. <b>Oral</b> - skin rashes, pruritus, dizziness, fatigue, arthralgia and myalgia, urticaria, and dry mouth. <b>Inj</b> – Fundic gland polyps (benign)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Ampicillin, iron salts, ketoconazole, anticoagulants (e.g. coumarin, indandione-derivative), diazepam, phenytoin, bone marrow depressants. Nelfinavir, atazanavir. Digoxin. Clopidogrel. Posaconazole, erlotinib, and itraconazole."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Capsule 40 mg (P38.11). Powder for injection 40 mg (P591.36)."
          }
        ],
        "company": {
          "id": 3911,

        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Isotretinoin",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Acne Agents & Cell Stimulants & Proliferants"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Used for severe forms of cystic acne and acne conglobata, especially when the lesions involve the trunk."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults and adolescents</b>: 0.5 to 1 mg/kg BW daily in 2 divided doses for 15-20 weeks. Max 2 mg/kg/day. Maintenance treatment to be adjusted within the range of 0.1 to 1 mg/kg/day. <b>Usual treatment duration</b>: 16 weeks. Take with meals."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Hepatic or renal insufficiency. Hypervitaminosis A. Patients with excessively elevated blood lipid values. Blood donation by patients during and within 1 month of isotretinoin treatment to women of childbearing potential should be avoided. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Concurrent administration of other keratolytic or exfoliative anti-acne agents. Radiation therapy with UV light. Avoid exposure to sun. Monitor liver function. Patients with history of depression; diabetes, obesity, alcoholism, disturbances of lipid metabolism, psychiatric disorders. Dental problems. Avoid dermabrasion and wax epilation during and 5-6 months after treatment. Vision impairment may develop. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Use of androgen progestational contraceptives should be avoided. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category X.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Cheilitis, dryness of the mucosa, pruritus, dermatitis facialis, sweating, reversible alopecia, hirsutism, hyperpigmentation, photosensitivity, muscle and joint pain, depression, headache, visual disturbances, hematuria, proteinuria."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Vitamin A and tetracyclines."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Capsule 10 mg (P50.00)."
          }
        ],

        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Salbutamol",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Sympathomimetic Anti-Asthmatic & COPD Agents"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Prevention and treatment of reversible airway obstruction of all types including bronchial asthma, chronic bronchitis, and emphysema. Used as bronchodilator in the management of reversible airways obstruction, as in asthma and in some patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Syr: Adults:</b> 5-10 mL. Max 80 mL/day. <b>Childn &ge;12 yrs:</b> 5-10 mL to be cautiously increased to max 60 mL/day; <b>6-12 yrs:</b> 5 mL; <b>2-6 yrs:</b> 2.5-5 mL. <b>Elderly:</b> 5 mL to be cautiously adjusted to 20 mL if necessary. All doses to be taken 3-4x daily. <b>MDI: Adults -</b> Immediate relief: 1-2 puffs; Chronic or preventive treatment: 2 puffs 3-4x a day; Relief of effort-induced bronchitis: 2 puffs before starting activity. <b>Childn -</b> Immediate relief or before effort: 1 puff; Chronic or preventive treatment: 1 puff 3-4x a day, may be increased to 2 puffs when necessary. Take at fixed intervals. Complete the treatment. <b>Soln for Inhalation:</b> Adults and childn >12 yrs: 2.5-5 mL 4x daily. In adults, max dose of 40 mg/day for the treatment of severe airway obstruction may be given under strict medical supervision in the hospital. <b>Childn < 12 yrs:</b> 1.25-2.5 mL every 4-6 hrs if needed. Use with a nebulizer and inhale over 5-15 mins. <b>Soln for Nebulization:</b> Initially 2.5 mg, may be increased to 5 mg. May be repeated up to 4x daily. For faster delivery time, this may be used undiluted. If prolonged delivery time is desired, dilution with an equal amount of 0.9% sodium chloride soln may be done. Used with a nebulizer, taken by inhalation over 5-15 mins."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Thyrotoxicosis. Not used for threatened abortion during the 1<sup>st</sup> and 2<sup>nd</sup> trimesters of pregnancy. Syr: Concomitant use of non-selective beta-blockers e.g. propranolol. Pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "HTN, hyperthyroidism or DM, patients with CV diseases (e.g. IHD, tachycardia, occlusive vascular disorders), angina pectoris. Not indicated for the prevention of premature labor associated with toxemia of pregnancy or antepartum hemorrhage. Adjustment of dose and frequency of administration should only be done upon medical advice. <b>Syr:</b> Patients with thyrotoxicosis. Monitor potassium levels in patients taking corticosteroids, diuretics, xanthines, and under digoxin therapy. <b>MDI:</b> Patients with impaired heart and/or vascular system, hyperactivity of the thyroid gland, enlarged prostate, history of spasms. Pregnancy and lactation. <b>Soln for Inhalation:</b> Not to be injected or administered orally, myocardial insufficiency, arrhythmias, susceptibility to QT-interval prolongation, closed-angle glaucoma; undergoing anesthesia with cyclopropane, halothane or other halogenated anesthetics. Monitor plasma potassium concentrations. <b>Soln for Nebulization:</b> Patients with convulsive disorders and hypokalemia. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category C.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Tremor, palpitations, tachycardia, nervous tension, headaches, peripheral vasodilation, and flushing. <b>Syr:</b> Large doses may cause slight tachycardia, tenseness, and peripheral vasodilation. Reversible hypokalemia and hyperglycemia. <b>MDI:</b> Nausea, dizziness, skin rash, and irritation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Beta-blockers, disopyramide, quinidine, phenothiazine or procainamide. Corticosteroids, aminophylline, or xanthines. <b>Syr:</b> Diuretics and digoxin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Syrup 2 mg/5 mL x 60 mL (P82.60). Metered-dose inhaler 100 mcg/actuation x 200 actuations (P332.64). Solution for inhalation 1 mg/mL x 20 mL (P89.88). Solution for nebulization 1 mg/mL x 2.5 mL (P24.92)."
          }
        ],

          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/T27dipTRY6NoWWCWiUUtZaxzfBg1QMb71ebIbg6dqogwCrHmNR.jpg"

            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Sympathomimetic Anti-Asthmatic & COPD Agents"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Relief of bronchospasm associated with reversible obstructive airway diseases (e.g. bronchial asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease). <b>Soln for inhalation:</b> Prevention of bronchospasm; treatment of acute exacerbations of asthma."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Soln for inhalation -</b> Adults and childn >12 yrs: 5 mg (2 nebs); Childn 4-12 yrs: 2.5 mg (1 neb). Used in a nebulizer. <b>Syr -</b> Adults and childn >12 yrs: 5-10 mL; Childn 7-12 yrs: 5 mL; 2-6 yrs: 2.5-5 mL; Elderly and patients sensitive to beta-adrenergic stimulant drugs: Initially 2 mg. All doses taken every 6-8 hrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Certain maternal or fetal conditions (e.g. eclampsia or severe preeclampsia, intrauterine infection and fetal death, antepartum hemorrhage, placenta previa, cord compression, toxemia); threatened abortion."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Paradoxical bronchospasm, deterioration of asthma, hypokalemia; reversible metabolic effects (e.g. increased blood glucose). Patients with CV and convulsive disorders, hyperthyroidism, DM, and those unusually responsive to sympathomimetic amines. Pregnancy and lactation. <b>Soln for inhalation:</b> Excessive use of sympathomimetic oral inhalations. Patients with acute severe asthma where concomitant therapy with steroids, xanthine derivatives, or diuretics, and by hypoxia may result in hypokalemia. Monitor potassium concentration.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Conjunctivitis. Immune system; metabolism and nutrition; psychiatric and nervous system; eye; cardiac and vascular; respiratory, thoracic, and mediastinal; GI; musculoskeletal and connective tissue disorders. Increased sweating."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Sympathomimetic agents, beta-blockers, nonpotassium-sparing diuretics (e.g. loop or thiazide diuretics), digoxin, MAOIs, TCAs. <b>Soln for inhalation:</b> Nebulized anticholinergic drugs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Solution for inhalation 1 mg/mL x 2.5 mL (P36.00). Syrup 2 mg/5 mL x 60 mL (P156.25)."
          }

        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Alteplase",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Thrombolytic/Fibrinolytic Agents"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Thrombolytic treatment in acute myocardial infarction (MI), acute massive pulmonary embolism (PE)  with hemodynamic instability, and acute ischemic stroke."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Given as early as possible after symptom onset. <b>Acute MI - 90-min accelerated dose regimen (started within 6 hrs after symptom onset) - &ge;65 kg BW:</b> 15 mg IV bolus, followed by 50 mg IV infusion for 1<sup>st</sup> 30 mins, then 35 mg IV infusion for 60 mins, until max total dose of 100 mg; <b>< 65 kg:</b> 15 mg IV  bolus, followed by 0.75 mg/kg IV infusion for 1<sup>st</sup> 30 mins, then 0.5 mg/kg IV infusion for 60 mins. <b>3-hr  dose regimen (started between 6-12 hrs after symptom onset) - >65 kg:</b> 10 mg IV bolus, followed by  50 mg IV infusion for 1<sup>st</sup> hr, then 40 mg IV infusion for 60 mins, until max total dose of 100 mg; <b>< 65 kg:</b> 10  mg IV bolus followed by up to max total dose of 1.5 mg/kg IV infusion for 3 hrs. <b>Acute massive PE - &ge;65 kg BW:</b> 10 mg IV bolus for 1-2 mins, followed by 90 mg IV infusion for 2 hrs, until max total dose of 100 mg; <b>< 65 kg:</b> 10 mg IV bolus for 1-2 mins, followed by up to max total dose of 1.5 mg/kg IV infusion for 2 hrs; <b>Adjunctive therapy:</b> After therapy, initiate heparin therapy when aPTT values are < 2x ULN. Adjust infusion to maintain aPTT between 50-70 secs (1.5-2.5 fold of reference value). <b>Acute ischemic stroke (started within 4.5 hrs of symptom onset):</b> 0.9 mg/kg (max 90 mg) IV infusion for 60 mins with 10% of total dose as IV bolus, followed by remainder of total dose as IV infusion for 60 mins; treatment effect is time-dependent; <b>Adjunctive therapy:</b> Max 10,000 IU/day SC if heparin is required for other indications (e.g. prevention of DVT). See product insert for dosing table for acute MI and instructions for reconstitution."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients at high risk for hemorrhage. <b>Acute MI and acute massive PE:</b> Hemorrhagic stroke or stroke of unknown origin; ischemic stroke or TIA in last 6 months, except current acute ischemic stroke within 4.5 hrs. <b>Acute ischemic stroke:</b> Symptoms of ischemic attack began >4.5 hrs prior infusion start or when time of symptom onset is unknown; symptoms of acute ischemic stroke that were either rapidly improving or only minor prior start of infusion; severe stroke as assessed clinically  (e.g. NIHSS >25) or by imaging techniques; seizure at onset of stroke; history of stroke or serious head trauma within 3 months; combination of previous stroke and DM; administration of heparin within 48 hrs prior onset of stroke with elevated aPTT; platelet count of < 100,000/mm<sup>3</sup>; SBP >185 mmHg or DBP >110  mmHg, or aggressive management (IV) necessary to reduce BP; blood glucose < 50 mg/dL or >400  mg/dL; childn < 16 yrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with acute ischemic stroke, pre-treated with aspirin; extensive infarctions. May induce bleeding; reperfusion arrhythmias; cerebral edema. Coadministration with GPIIb/IIIa antagonists;  thrombolytics for left heart thrombus (e.g. mitral stenosis or atrial fibrillation). Avoid use of rigid catheters,  IM inj, and non-essential handling of patient. Do not initiate treatment later >4.5 hrs after symptoms onset.  Discontinue treatment with concomitant heparin therapy if serious bleeding occurs. Monitor BP and occurrences of angioedema during and up to 24 hrs after infusion. Give IV antihypertensive if >180  mmHg SBP or >105 mmHg DBP. Elderly >80 yrs. Childn &ge;16 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Intracranial, eye, hepatic, pericardial, respiratory tract, GI, retroperitoneal, urogenital, and catheter site hemorrhage, hematoma, embolism; ecchymosis; decreased BP, increased temperature; reperfusion arrhythmias."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Drugs affecting coagulation/platelet function (e.g. anticoagulants), ACE inhibitors."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Powder for solution for IV infusion 50 mg (P30,536.02)."
          }
        ],

        "description": "A rapid test based on unique and highly specific monoclonal antibodies that bind to the phosphorylated form of insulin-like growth factor binding protein-1 (phlGFBP-1). Reliable test for quickly and easily detecting premature rupture of fetal membranes in all patients.",
        "directions": "Take a vaginal fluid sample with polyester swab from the posterior fornix of the vagina or from the cervix if no fluid is visible, by leaving the swab in the vagina for 10-15 seconds. This allows the swab to absorb sufficient amount of specimen. Place the polyester swab in the specimen extraction solution provided and swirl it around vigorously for 10 seconds. After extraction, dip the yellow area of the dipstick into the solution and hold it there until the liquid front reaches the result area. Then remove the dipstick from the solution and place it in a horizontal position. A positive result can be seen if 2 lines, a control line and a test line, appear in the result area.             "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Thyroid disorders. IHD, arrhythmia or tachycardia, occlusive vascular disorder including arteriosclerosis, HTN or aneurysm. Anginal pain. DM, susceptibility to QT-interval prolongation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category C.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [

                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {

                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."

            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Tachycardia, palpitations, headaches, peripheral vasodilation. Fine skeletal muscle tremors, tolerance, hypersensitivity. Hypokalemia."

          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "For treatment and prophylaxis of hemorrhage associated with excessive fibrinolysis; prophylaxis of hereditary angioedema."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Hemorrhage (short-term use):</b> 0.5-1 g (or 10 mg/kg) thrice daily given via slow IV injection. Depending on the indication, tranexamic acid is given by continuous infusion at a rate of 25-50 mg/kg daily. <b>Childn:</b> 10 mg/kg IV, usually 2-3x daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Acute venous or arterial thrombosis. Fibrinolytic conditions following consumption coagulopathy except in those with predominant activation of the fibrinolytic system with acute severe bleeding. History of convulsions. Severe renal impairment. Administration via intrathecal, intraventricular, and intracerebral due to the risk of cerebral edema and convulsions."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with hematuria, disseminated intravascular coagulation, or history of thromboembolic diseases; receiving oral contraceptives. Risk for convulsion and/or visual disturbances (e.g. visual impairment, vision blurred, impaired color vision). Pregnancy (1<sup>st</sup> trimester) and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Dose-related GI disturbances, hypotension (after rapid IV dosage), and transient disturbances of color vision."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Estrogens. Medicinal products acting on hemostasis. Thrombolytic drugs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",

  {

      "success": true,

        "id": 3102,
        "brand_name": "Aspidon",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/DRXbowvu6TkZvLgOAbhgC7KzXdpaIl4PcTKS1bKIyrFwLtd7SS.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/U5ptcNAm4ZqyBiEkP7WT52yGurAmRaILlkdODISkbRKCVhHaWC.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/jRrgwSYQ07aD2zKSH0Pi6OHHX37L13wtNfAc0GwtZ5y4uOTOAM.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Risperidone",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Atypical Antipsychotics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "<b>1 mg</b>: Management of psychotic disorders and non-psychotic symptoms associated with dementia in the elderly. <b>2 mg</b>: Treatment of schizophrenia and for the short-term treatment of acute manic or mixed episodes associated with bipolar disorders."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>1 mg</b>: Schizophrenia – Adults: Initially 2 mg/day given once or in 2 doses, may be increased to 4 mg/day on the 2nd day; <b>Elderly and patients with renal and liver disease</b>: 0.5 mg twice daily, may be adjusted with 0.5 mg twice daily increments to 1-2 mg twice daily. <b>Bipolar mania – Adults</b>: Initially 2 mg once daily, may be adjusted in increments of 1 mg/day at intervals not &lt;24 hrs. Dose range: 1-6 mg/day; <b>Elderly and patients with renal and liver disease</b>: Initially 0.5 mg twice daily, may be adjusted with 0.5 mg twice daily increments to 1-2 mg twice daily. <b>2 mg: Schizophrenia – Adults</b>: Initially 2 mg/day given once or in 2 doses, may increase the dose in increments of 1-2 mg/day at 24-hr intervals or greater to 4-6 mg/day; <b>Adolescents</b>: Initially 0.5 mg once daily as single dose, may be adjusted at 24-hr intervals or greater in increments of 0.5-1 mg/day to 3 mg/day. <b>Bipolar mania – Adults</b>: Initially 2-3 mg/day, may be adjusted at 24-hr intervals or greater in increments of 1 mg/day. Dosing range: 1-6 mg/day; <b>Childn</b>: Initially 0.5 mg once daily as single dose, may be adjusted at 24-hr intervals or greater in increments of 0.5-1 mg/day to 1-2.5 mg/day; <b>Patients with severe renal (CrCl &lt;30 mL/min) or hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh 10-15 points)</b>: Initially 0.5 mg twice daily, may be increased in increments of 0.5 mg or less twice daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "May induce orthostatic hypotension associated with dizziness, tachycardia and syncope especially during the initial dose titration period. Patients with known CV disease e.g. MI, ischemia, heart failure or conduction abnormalities, cerebrovascular diseases and conditions which would predispose patients to hypotension. NMS; tardive dyskinesia; metabolic changes including hyperglycemia and DM, dyslipidemia and weight gain; hyperprolactinemia; history of seizures; esophageal dysmotility and aspiration; priapism; body temp disruption. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn &lt;15 yrs. Elderly with dementia or dementia-related psychosis. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Insomnia, agitation, anxiety and headache. Parkinsonism, akathisia, dystonia, tremor, sedation, dizziness, blurred vision, nausea, vomiting, upper abdominal pain, stomach discomfort, dyspepsia, diarrhea, salivary hypersecretion, constipation, dry mouth, increased appetite, increased weight, fatigue, rash, nasal congestion, URTI, nasopharyngitis and pharyngolaryngeal pain."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Fluoxetine, paroxetine, carbamazepine; centrally acting drugs and alcohol; drugs with hypotensive effects; levodopa and dopamine agonists; clozapine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 1 mg (P44.10), 2 mg (P110.27)."
          }
        ],

          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Primary prevention of thromboembolic disorders and cardiovascular (CV) events e.g. ischemic stroke, transient ischemic attack (TIA), prevention of recurrent myocardial infarction, unstable or chronic stable angina pectoris.           {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Ischemic stroke and TIA:</b> 50-325 mg once daily. <b>Prevention of recurrent MI:</b> 75-325 mg once daily. <b>Unstable and chronic stable angina pectoris:</b> 75-325 mg once daily. <b>Primary and secondary prevention of CV events in patients with DM:</b> 75-325 mg once daily. <b>CABG:</b> 325 mg daily starting 6 hrs post-op, then continue for 1 year post-op. <b>PTCA:</b> 325 mg 2 hrs pre-angioplasty, then 160-325 mg once daily maintenance dose. <b>Carotid endarterectomy:</b> 80 mg once daily to 650 mg twice daily pre-op. <b>Prevention of complications of pregnancy:</b> 80 mg daily from 13th to 26th weeks of gestation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with asthma, rhinitis, and nasal polyps, severe renal failure (GFR >10 mL/min) and hepatic insufficiency. Use in childn and teenagers with viral infections with or without fever. Pregnancy (3<sup>rd</sup> trimester)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "May cause GI bleeding. Avoid use 1 week before and during labor, delivery, and any surgical procedure. Alcohol use. Coagulation abnormalities. Childn and infants. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Fever, hypothermia, thirst. Hearing loss, tinnitus. Undesirable effects on CV, fluid and electrolyte, GI, hematologic, metabolic, musculoskeletal, nervous, reproductive, respiratory, and urogenital systems."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Acetazolamide, ACE inhibitors, anticoagulants, anticonvulsants, beta-blockers, diuretics, methotrexate, NSAIDs, oral hypoglycemic agents; probenecid and sulfinpyrazone."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Enteric-coated tablet 80 mg (P4.00)."
          }
        ],

Higher initial total daily dose (e.g., 1,000 mcg) may be considered. <b>Maintenance - Adults/elderly:</b> 500-4,000 mcg total daily dose, may be further increased in severe cases; <b>Childn &ge;6 months:</b> 250-2,000 mcg total daily dose."
          },
          {

          },

          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/p4nrkQPKlGbgjjzVlMzwfXCLsfa941yjLvCgt3nJs4frvHneZ3.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Ibuprofen",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Non-Steroidal Anti-inflammatory Drugs"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Non-Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Mild to moderate pain and inflammation in migraine, post-op pain, dental pain, musculoskeletal and joint disorders (e.g. ankylosing spondylitis, osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis (RA) including juvenile RA), peri-articular disorders (e.g. bursitis, tenosynovitis), soft tissue disorders (e.g. sprains and strains), fever."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Childn:</b> 5-10 mg/kg every 6-8 hrs. <b>Pain, or fever</b> - <b>100 mg/5 mL</b> - Childn 11 yrs: 3 tsp (15 mL); 9-10 yrs: 2&frac12; tsp (12.5 mL); 6-8 yrs: 2 tsp (10 mL); 4-5 yrs: 1&frac12; tsp (7.5 mL); 2-3 yrs: 1 tsp (5 mL). <b>200 mg/5 mL</b> - Childn 11 yrs: 1&frac12; tsp (7.5 mL); 4-10 yrs: 1 tsp (5 mL); 2-3 yrs: &frac12; tsp (2.5 mL). <b>Juvenile RA:</b> 7.5-12.5 mg/kg every 6 hrs. Shake well before use. Do not take >4x a day and not longer than 10 days. May be taken with food or milk."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Before or after heart surgery. History of stroke, heart attack, uncontrolled HTN, or CHF. Advanced kidney or liver disease. NSAID- or aspirin-induced bronchospasm, angioedema, nasal polyps."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Discontinue if allergic reaction occurs. History of stomach ulcer or bleeding problems. Concomitant use with anticoagulants, steroids, and other NSAIDs (e.g. aspirin, naproxen).",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Stomach ulceration and/or bleeding. Indigestion, heartburn, nausea, vomiting, anorexia, diarrhea, constipation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Anticoagulants (e.g. warfarin, dicoumarol), thrombolytic agents (e.g. streptokinase), salicylates, other NSAIDs (e.g. mefenamic acid, naproxen, diclofenac, ketoprofen), ACE inhibitors (e.g. captopril, enalapril, ramipril, imidapril, fosinopril, lisinopril), diuretics (e.g. furosemide, thiazide), aspirin, lithium."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Oral suspension 100 mg/5 mL x 60 mL (P77.00), 200 mg/5 mL x 60 mL (P99.00)."
          }
        ],

        "content": "Mycophenolate mofetil",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Immunosuppressants in Chemotherapy/Transplantation"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "In combination with ciclosporin and corticosteroids for the prophylaxis of acute transplant rejection in patients receiving allogeneic renal, cardiac, and hepatic transplants."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Renal transplant</b> – Adults and elderly: Initially 1 g twice daily within 72 hrs following transplantation. Childn 2-18 yrs: 600 mg/m<sup>2</sup> twice daily up to max 2 g daily. Severe chronic renal impairment (GFR < 25 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>): Avoid doses &gt;2 g/day. <b>Cardiac transplant</b> – Adults and elderly: 1.5 g twice daily within 5 days following transplantation. <b>Hepatic transplant</b> – Adults and elderly: 1.5 g twice daily for 4 days following transplantation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Increased risk of developing lymphomas and other malignancies particularly of the skin. Increased risk for opportunistic infections. Hypogammaglobulinemia in association with recurrent infections. Neutropenia. Pure red cell aplasia (PRCA). Avoid use with live attenuated vaccines. Patients with active serious digestive system disease. Avoid in patients with Lesch-Nyhan and Kelley-Seegmiller syndrome. Switching combination therapy from regimens containing immunosuppressants which interfere with mycophenolic acid enterohepatic recirculation. Concomitant use of azathioprine. Avoid blood donation during therapy or at least 6 weeks after discontinuation. Do not donate semen during therapy or for 90 days after discontinuation. Childn < 2 yrs. Women of childbearing potential should use effective contraception before, during, and for 6 weeks after treatment.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Sepsis, GI candidiasis, UTI, herpes simplex, herpes zoster, leucopenia, thrombocytopenia, anemia, vomiting, abdominal pain, diarrhea, nausea. Infections and infestations, neoplasms benign, malignant and unspecified, blood and lymphatic disorders, metabolism and nutrition disorders, psychiatric and nervous system disorders, tachycardia, hypotension, HTN, vasodilatation, pleural effusion, dyspnea, cough, GI and hepatobiliary disorders, skin hypertrophy, rash, acne, alopecia, arthralgia, renal impairment, edema, pyrexia, chills, pain, malaise, asthenia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Aciclovir, antacids and PPIs, cholestyramine, medicinal products that interfere with enterohepatic circulation, ciclosporin A, telmisartan, ganciclovir, rifampicin, sevelamer, norfloxacin, metronidazole, ciprofloxacin, amoxicillin plus clavulanic acid, tacrolimus, sirolimus, live vaccines, and azathioprine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 500 mg (P68.00)."
          }
        ],

          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Non-Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "For relief of mild to moderately severe pain of musculoskeletal origin e.g. myalgia, arthritis, rheumatism, sprain, strain, bursitis, tendonitis, backache, stiff neck; tension headache, dysmenorrhea, toothache and pain after tooth extraction and minor surgical operations. For fever reduction."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Adults and childn &gt;12 yrs: 1 cap every 6 hrs as needed. Max 6 tabs in 24-hr period. May be taken with food or milk."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "History of hypersensitivity to paracetamol, ibuprofen, aspirin or other NSAIDs. Concomitant use of paracetamol-containing products, aspirin or other NSAIDs. Patients with bronchospasm, angioedema, nasal polyps; stomach ulcers or other GI problems; severe cardiac, hepatic, and or renal disease (CrCl &lt;30 mL/min); SLE; dengue fever; dehydration due to vomiting, diarrhea, or lack of fluids; conditions associated with bleeding. Patients undergoing heart surgery. Pregnancy (last trimester) and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Do not use for  >10 days. Long-term use in patients with anemia. Risk for heart attack or stroke with long-term use. Concomitant use of anticoagulant or steroid medications; intake of alcohol. Patients with G6PD deficiency. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn &lt;12 yrs. Elderly &ge;60 yrs.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Minor allergic-type reactions (e.g. skin rashes), GI ulceration and/or bleeding, indigestion, heartburn, nausea, vomiting, anorexia, diarrhea, constipation, stomatitis, flatulence, bloating, abdominal pain, effects on kidney and liver."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Ciclosporin, tacrolimus. Phenothiazines. <b>Ibuprofen</b>: Aspirin; phenylbutazone, indomethacin, salicylates, other NSAIDS; aminoglycosides, quinolone antibiotics, zidovudine; antacids; ACE inhibitors; diuretics; anticoagulants and thrombolytic agents; cardiac glycosides; corticosteroids; SSRIs; <i>Ginkgo biloba</i>; lithium; methotrexate; sulfonylureas and insulin; probenecid. <b>Paracetamol</b>: Alcohol; chloramphenicol; isoniazid; metoclopramide, domperidone, cholestyramine; drugs that stimulate enzyme responsible for metabolism of paracetamol (e.g. anticonvulsants and oral contraceptives)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Capsule 200 mg/325 mg (P8.50)."
          }
        ],

            "content": "<b>Adults:</b> 25-75 g (125-375 mL) daily.           },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "HTN, severe anemia, or cardiac failure in the presence of normal or increased intravascular vol."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",

        "brand_shot": {

        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Human albumin",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Volume Expanders"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Restoration and maintenance of circulating blood volume in cases of volume deficiency where use of colloid is indicated."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Individualize concentration of albumin solution, dose, and infusion rate (max 1-2 mL/min) based on patient’s size, severity of trauma or illness, and on continuing fluid and protein losses. Administer by IV infusion, either undiluted or after dilution in isotonic solution (e.g. 5% glucose or normal saline)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Do not dilute with water for inj. Patients with renal and post-renal anuria, congestive cardiac failure, HTN, esophageal varices, pulmonary edema, hemorrhagic diathesis, severe anemia, control sodium diet. Transmitting infections. Measure adequacy of circulating volume not the plasma albumin levels in determining dose. Monitor arterial BP, pulse rate, central venous pressure, pulmonary artery wedge pressure, urine output, electrolyte, and hematocrit/Hgb, regularly upon administration. Assure adequate hydration when concentrated albumin is administered; adequate substitution of other blood constituents if comparatively large volumes are to be replaced. Hypervolemia. Discontinue when first clinical signs of CV overload, increased BP, increased venous pressure, or pulmonary edema occur. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity reactions, nausea, flush, urticaria, fever."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "High albumin bound drugs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Solution for IV infusion 250 g/L (25% w/v) (P7,219.51)."
          }
        ],

          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Local/Regional Anesthetics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "For procedures in which a rapid and short-acting topical ophthalmic anesthetic is indicated e.g. in suture removal from the cornea or conjunctiva, tonometry, gonioscopy, removal of corneal foreign bodies, conjunctival scraping, and other short corneal and conjunctival procedures."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Tonometry and other short-duration procedures:</b> Instill 1-2 drops prior to evaluation. <b>Minor surgical procedures:</b> Instill 1-2 drops every 5-10 mins for 1-3 doses. <b>Prolonged anesthesia:</b> Instill 1 or 2 drops in the eyes every 5-10 mins for 3-5 doses."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "For external use only. Prolonged use. Patients with cardiac disease or hyperthyroidism. Avoid direct contact with skin. Contains benzalkonium chloride. Do not touch or rub eyes or wear contact lens until effect wears off. May impair the ability to drive or operate machinery. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Transient stinging, burning, and conjunctival redness. Hypersensitivity. Syncope. Corneal erosion, corneal opacity, keratitis, blurred vision, photophobia, mydriasis, eye pain, irritation, and swelling, ocular discomfort, ocular hyperemia, increased lacrimation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Ophthalmic solution 5 mg/mL x 15 mL."
          }
        ],

            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Statins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "<b>20 mg</b>: Treatment of hyperlipidemia, including hypercholesterolemia and combined (mixed) hyperlipidemia (type IIa or IIb hyperlipoproteinemia), hypertriglyceridemia (type IV) and dysbetalipoproteinemia (type III). Adjunctive therapy in homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia and used for primary prophylaxis of cardiovascular (CV) events. <b>40 mg</b>: Prevention of CV disease. In patients with type 2 diabetes – reduce risk of myocardial infarction (MI) and stroke. In patients with coronary heart disease – reduce risk of non-fatal MI, fatal and non-fatal stroke, revascularization procedures, hospitalization for congestive heart failure, angina. Adjunct to diet in patients with primary hypercholesterolemia (heterozygous familial and non-familial) and mixed dyslipidemia (Fredrickson types IIa and IIb); patients with elevated serum triglyceride levels (Fredrickson type IV). Treatment of patients with primary dysbetalipoproteinemia (Fredrickson type III) who do not respond adequately to diet. Adjunct to other lipid-lowering treatments (e.g. LDL apheresis) in patients with homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia. Adjunct to diet in boys and postmenarchal girls (10-17 yrs) with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia if after adequate trial of diet therapy in the following findings are present – LDL-C remains &ge;190 mg/dL or &le;160 mg/dL), and there is a positive family history of premature CV disease, or &ge;2 CV disease risk factors are present in the child."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Initially 10-20 mg/day. For patients who require large reduction in LDL-C: Initially 40 mg. May be adjusted at intervals of 4 weeks up to max 80 mg/day. <b>Childn and adolescents (10-17 yrs) with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia</b>: Initially 10 mg/day, adjust according to response to max 20 mg/day. <b>Patients taking ciclosporin</b>: Max 10 mg/day; <b>clarithromycin</b>: Initially 10 mg. Max 20 mg/day; <b>itraconazole</b>: Initially 10 mg. Max 40 mg/day; <b>ritonavir-boosted lopinavir or ritonavir-boosted saquinavir</b>: Doses &gt;20 mg/day should be used with caution."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Active liver disease or unexplained persistently raised serum aminotransferase concentrations. Women of childbearing potential. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Predisposing factors for myopathy. Elderly &ge;65 yrs. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category X. <b>20 mg</b>: Effects on growth and sexual development of childn. Patients with porphyria. Fetal sterol synthesis.  <b>40 mg</b>: History of renal impairment. Patients with recent stroke or TIA. Patients with diffuse myalgias, muscle tenderness or weakness, and/or marked CPK elevation. Liver function abnormalities.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {

                  "title": "X",

                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "<b>20 mg</b>: GI disturbances. <b>40 mg</b>: Nasopharyngitis, arthralgia, diarrhea, pain in extremities, and UTI."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Ciclosporin, itraconazole, ketoconazole, HIV-protease inhibitors, nefazodone, amiodarone, and verapamil. Erythromycin and other macrolides. Rifampicin, oral anticoagulants, fibric acid derivatives (e.g. fibrates, gemfibrozil), nicotinic acid, and esomeprazole. Grapefruit juice. <b>20 mg</b>: CCBs and PPIs. <b>40 mg</b>: Digoxin, oral contraceptives (e.g. norethindrone and ethinyl estradiol), and colchicine."
          },

        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Statins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Adjunct to lifestyle changes for the reduction of elevated total cholesterol (total-C), LDL-C, triglycerides and apolipoprotein B, total-C/HDL-D ratio; for increasing HDL-C; in hyperlipidemic and dyslipidemic conditions including primary hypercholesterolemia (type IIa), combined (mixed) hyperlipidemia (type IIb), dysbetalipoproteinemia (type III), hypertriglyceridemia (type IV), familial hypercholesterolemia (homozygous and heterozygous). Reduce the risk of myocardial infarction (MI)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Primary hypercholesterolemia and combined (mixed) dyslipidemia including familial combined hyperlipidemia</b>: Initially 10-20 mg once daily; Patients requiring large reduction in LDL-C: 40 mg once daily. Dose range: 10-80 mg. Adjust dose at intervals of 2-4 weeks. Max 80 mg/day. <b>Severe dyslipidemias including homozygous and heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia and dysbetalipoproteinemia (type III)</b>: Up to 80 mg/day. <b>Heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia</b> – Childn 10-17 yrs: 10 mg/day. Max 20 mg/day, adjustment at intervals of &ge;4 weeks. <b>MI</b> - Primary prevention: 10 mg once daily. Secondary prevention: 10-80 mg once daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Active liver disease or unexplained persistent elevations of serum transaminases exceeding 3x ULN. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Predisposing factors for myopathy/rhabdomyolysis. Risk factor predisposing to the development of renal failure secondary to rhabdomyolysis. Recent stroke or TIA. Decrease in myocardial ubiquinone levels could lead to impaired cardiac function in CHF patients. Severe hypercholesterolemia. Perform liver function test before the initiation of treatment and periodically thereafter. Alcohol abuse or with history of liver disease. Renal insufficiency. Increase serum transaminase levels and serum glucose. Childn &lt;10 yrs. Elderly.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Diarrhea, dyspepsia, nausea, constipation, flatulence. Asthenia. Nasopharyngitis. Abnormal liver function test, increase blood creatine phosphokinase, hyperglycemia. Arthralgia, pain in extremities, musculoskeletal pain, muscle spasms, myalgia, joint swelling. Headache. Pharyngolaryngeal pain, epistaxis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Gemfibrozil, fenofibrate and other fibrates, niacin. Grapefruit juice, erythromycin, clarithromycin, ciclosporin, itraconazole, ketoconazole, protease inhibitors, antidepressants, nefazodone. Efavirenz, rifampicin. Bile acid sequestrants, digoxin, oral contraceptives and hormone replacement therapy, antacids, diltiazem, fusidic acid."
          },
          {
