  {
    "id": 129,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 129,
        "brand_name": "Aldara",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/6lGjt9uW6HCNGDcl3R16mvMcJWRLcVvn6b2P6VhbjjVtIvm1MR.png",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/6lGjt9uW6HCNGDcl3R16mvMcJWRLcVvn6b2P6VhbjjVtIvm1MR.png",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/M4Hn3k6C5bPyoU31YcQJNePwqfBtPmFzgW7fIdCYWmZ6RLbsM8.png"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Imiquimod",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Topical Antivirals"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of external genital and perianal warts (condylomata acuminata), and small superficial basal cell carcinomas (sBCCs) with max tumor diameter of 2.0 cm, located on the trunk (excluding anogenital skin, neck, or extremities (excluding hands and feet, when surgical methods are medically less appropriate."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>External genital/perianal warts</b>: Apply 3 times a week prior to normal sleeping hours. Leave on the skin for 6-10 hrs; Max duration of 16 weeks. Local skin reactions (erythema) at the treatment site are common. <b>sBCCs</b>: Apply 5 times a week for 6 weeks."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Do not use in immunosuppressed patients. Patients with preexisting autoimmune conditions. Do not use to treat urethral, intra-vaginal, cervical, rectal or intra-anal warts. May exacerbate inflammatory conditions of the skin. Avoid contact with eyes. Avoid sexual contact during treatment. Do not use an occlusive dressing on treated area. Minimize or avoid exposure to sunlight (including sunlamps). Patients with sunburn should fully recover prior to use. Childn. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category B.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Erythema, edema, induration, vesicles, erosion, ulceration, excoriation/flaking, scabbing, itching/pruritus, burning, pain, tenderness, irritation, rash, sensitivity, soreness, stinging sensation, influenza-like symptoms, fatigue, fever, headache, diarrhea, and myalgia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Cream 50 mg/g x 250 mg (P478.00)."
          }
        ],
        "company": {
          "id": 9,
          "name": "iNova Pharmaceuticals"
        },

    "id": 4429,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 4429,
        "brand_name": "Aldax",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/YZujO6mWDRYzPimKDjs6Jr2rgrTlPQh3kkPA7ZQEQJZhcsGiQV.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/rpqsWCOWsCZ9RIbuLUoXhL6c86NBFq6dtcqmCg2v0WxHMJ0qMh.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/LNb2linr9nh4EruiS4zZWIHGAc7c443TeaZILAXQPah8A2Cdlr.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Spironolactone",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Aldosterone Antagonists and Potassium-Sparing Diuretics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Management of primary hyperaldosteronism; edematous conditions for patients with congestive heart failure (CHF), liver cirrhosis accompanied by edema or ascites, nephrotic syndrome, essential hypertension (HTN), hypokalemia, and severe heart failure (NYHA class III-IV)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Primary hyperaldosteronism</b> - Long test: 400 mg daily for 3-4 weeks. Short test: 400 mg daily for 4 days. May administer 100-400 mg in preparation for surgery. <b>Edema in adults (CHF, liver cirrhosis, nephrotic syndrome):</b> Initially 100 mg daily in single or divided doses for 5 at least days. Dose may range from 25-200 mg daily. <b>Essential HTN:</b> Initially 50-100 mg daily in single or divided doses for at least 2 weeks. <b>Diuretic-induced hypokalemia:</b> 25-100 mg daily. <b>Severe heart failure</b> - Serum potassium &le;5.0 mEq/L and creatinine &le;2.5 mg/dL: 25 mg once daily, may increase to 50 mg once daily if tolerated, and decrease to 25 mg every other day for patients unable to tolerate."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Patients with anuria, acute renal insufficiency, renal impairment, or hyperkalemia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with hepatic impairment, severe heart failure. Observe for evidence of fluid or electrolyte imbalance. Monitor serum potassium levels. Delusional hyponatremia may occur in edematous patients in hot weather. May cause transient elevation of BUN in patients with preexisting renal impairment. Concomitant use with other potassium-sparing diuretics, oral potassium supplements, ACE inhibitors, NSAIDs (e.g. indomethacin), lithium. Childn. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "GI bleeding, ulceration, gastritis, diarrhea and cramping, nausea, vomiting; gynecomastia, erectile dysfunction, irregular menses or amenorrhea, post-menopausal bleeding; agranulocytosis; fever, urticaria, maculopapular or erythematous cutaneous eruptions, anaphylactic reactions, vasculitis; mental confusion, ataxia, headache, drowsiness, lethargy; renal dysfunction."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "ACE inhibitors, alcohol, barbiturates, or narcotics, corticosteroids, ACTH, pressor amines (e.g. norepinephrine), nondepolarizing skeletal muscle relaxants (e.g. tubocurarine), lithium NSAIDs, digoxin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 25 mg (P11.00), 50 mg (P19.00)."
          }
        ],

  {
    "id": 3571,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 3571,
        "brand_name": "Aldren 70",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/GvRrN5fJ6GJDoDmOWnPx6NrT1NBVeO9168gm97LYW33LCHfKVL.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/PM25hCAlQmeIYqXH1kLI3z9ajy0TYXG21JwIKdNM0gboIyxntc.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/o7aF5C4MSJJEzJIX0c6h9iBSVcgXk3oLdFm80zoCpf0rbDN8Ij.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Alendronic acid (as alendronate sodium)",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Bisphosphonates"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment and prevention of osteoporosis in postmenopausal women. Treatment to increase bone mass in men with osteoporosis. Treatment of glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis in men and women receiving glucocorticoids in a daily dosage equiv to &ge;7.5 mg prednisone and who have low bone mineral density; Paget’s disease of bone in men and women."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Osteoporosis in postmenopausal women</b>: 70 mg once weekly or 10 mg once daily. <b>To increase bone mass in men with osteoporosis</b>: 10 mg once daily. <b>Prevention of osteoporosis in postmenopausal women</b>: 35 mg once weekly or 5 mg once daily. <b>Glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis in men and women</b>: 5 mg once daily; for postmenopausal women not receiving estrogen: 10 mg once daily. <b>Paget’s disease of bone in men and women</b>: 40 mg once a day for 6 months. Must be taken at least 30 mins before 1<sup>st</sup> meal, beverage, or medication of the day; do not lie down for at least 30 mins after. Patients should receive calcium and vit D if dietary intake is inadequate."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Esophagus abnormalities which delay esophageal emptying e.g. stricture or achalasia. Inability to stand or sit upright for at least 30 mins. Hypocalcemia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with active upper GI problems (e.g. dysphagia, esophageal diseases, gastritis, duodenitis, or ulcers), disturbances of mineral metabolism, renal insufficiency (CrCl &lt;35 mL/min). May cause upper GI irritation. Concomitant use with glucocorticoids. Ensure adequate calcium and vit D intake in patients with Paget’s disease and/or taking glucocorticoids. Discontinue if dysphagia, odynophagia, retrosternal pain, and if new or worsening heartburn develops. Childn. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Abdominal pain, nausea, dyspepsia, constipation, diarrhea, flatulence, acid regurgitation, esophageal ulcer, vomiting, dysphagia, abdominal distention, gastritis, gastric ulcer, melena; musculoskeletal pain, muscle cramps; headache, dizziness; taste perversion."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Calcium supplements, antacids and some oral medications, aspirin-containing products, NSAIDs, IV ranitidine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 70 mg (P225.00)."
          }
        ],

          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/t0tIpX9FohGHB8bCATOeWWK2lp2odbo0ivnsD7ZNjWNz0zUJ2Y.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/YF3jdmIBUCkx6zUFD2HrJdk3u8NRHOKXb6d032oSJkRICT5B1Q.jpg"

        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Atorvastatin (as calcium), ezetimibe",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Lipid Modifying Agent Combination"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Adjunctive therapy to diet for the reduction of elevated total cholesterol, low-density lipoprotein (LDL) and apolipoprotein (Apo B) in patients with primary (heterozygous familial and non-familial) hypercholesterolemia. Reduction of elevated total cholesterol and LDL in patients with homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia as adjunct to other lipid-lowering treatments (e.g., LDL apheresis)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Initially 10/10 mg tab/day or 10/20 mg tab/day as single dose at any time of day, with or without food. <b>Patients requiring larger LDL-C (>55%) reduction:</b> Initially 10/40 mg tab/day. Assess lipid levels within &ge;2 weeks after initiation or upon titration of therapy. <b>Homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia:</b> 10/40 mg tab/day or 10/80 mg tab/day. <b>Patients taking clarithromycin, itraconazole or in patients with HIV taking 3 combinations (saquinavir + ritonavir, darunavir + ritonavir, fosamprenavir, or fosamprenavir + ritonavir):</b> 10/20 mg tab; <b>Nelfinavir or boceprevir:</b> 10/40 mg tab."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Active liver disease or unexplained persistent elevations of serum transaminases. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with HIV taking lopinavir plus ritonavir; history of hepatic disease, substantial alcohol consumption; recent stroke or TIA. Avoid concomitant cyclosporine, tipranavir + ritonavir, telaprevir, or gemfibrozil. Interrupt therapy if serious liver injury with hyperbilirubinemia or jaundice occurs. May increase HbA1c and fasting serum glucose levels. Temporary discontinue in patients with acute, serious conditions suggestive of myopathy or risk factor predisposed to renal failure secondary to rhabdomyolysis. Perform liver enzyme tests prior to initiation of therapy. Childn.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Myopathy, liver injury."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Fibric acid derivatives, niacin, cyclosporine, strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., clarithromycin, HIV protease inhibitors, itraconazole, rifampin), fenofibrates, digoxin, oral contraceptives, colchicine, cholestyramine, warfarin. Grapefruit juice."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 10 mg/10 mg (P26.34), 40 mg/10 mg (P33.93)."
          }
        ],

          },

            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of acute bronchospasm associated with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) e.g. chronic bronchitis and asthma in concomitant use with inhaled beta-agonists. Maintenance for bronchospasm associated with COPD e.g. chronic bronchitis and emphysema."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults (including elderly) and adolescents &ge;12 yrs - Acute attacks:</b> 1 vial, may repeat doses until patient is stable. Dilute 1 mL vial with normal saline soln up to a final vol of 2-4 mL or may be combined with fenoterol HBr nebulizer soln. Use open contents immediately. See product insert for handling instructions."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "For inhalation use only. Not for oral or parenteral. Do not allow the soln or mist into the eyes. May induce ocular complications. Discontinue if paradoxical bronchospasm occurs. May impair the ability to drive or operate machinery. Pregnancy and lactation.",

          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Headache, throat irritation, cough, dry mouth, GI motility disorders (e.g. constipation, diarrhea,  vomiting), nausea, and dizziness."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Other anticholinergic drugs; beta-adrenergics, xanthine preparations; beta-mimetics."

        "content": "Fenofibrate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Fibric Acid Derivatives & Related Agents"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "160 mg: As adjunct to diet and other non-pharmacological treatment of severe hypertriglyceridemia with or without low HDL-C; Mixed hyperlipidemia: (1) when a statin is contraindicated or not tolerated, (2) in patients at high cardiovascular risk in addition to a statin when triglycerides and HDL-C are not adequately controlled. 300 mg: Treatment of type IIa, type IIb, type III, type IV and type V hyperlipoproteinemias. Reduces elevated plasma concentrations of triglycerides by reducing the concentration of VLDL and cholesterol to a lesser extent but effect is variable."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "300 mg once daily with food, may be adjusted according to response between 200 and 400 mg daily; or 160 mg cap once daily. Patients taking 200 mg Fenofibrate may change to 160 mg micronized cap without dose adjustment."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with known photoallergy/phototoxic reaction during treatment with fibrates or ketoprofen; Severe renal dysfunction, including patients on dialysis, active liver disease, hepatic dysfunction, including primary biliary cirrhosis and unexplained persistent liver function abnormality, pre-existing gallbladder disease, chronic or acute pancreatitis with the exception of acute pancreatitis due to severe hypertriglyceridemia. Childn. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Monitor liver and renal function. Treat secondary causes of hypercholesterolemia before Fenofibrate therapy. Muscle toxicity, pancreatitis, cholelithiasis, renal impairment. Patients with predisposing factors for myopathy/rhabdomyolysis. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category C.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {

            "content": "GI disturbances e.g. abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea and flatulence. Hepatobiliary disorders: moderately elevated levels of serum transaminases."

        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Alendronic acid",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Bisphosphonates"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Osteoporosis in postmenopausal women and in men. Prevention of osteoporosis in postmenopausal women."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Treatment of osteoporosis in postmenopausal women and in men</b>: 1 tab once weekly. <b>Prevention of postmenopausal osteoporosis</b>: &frac12; tab once weekly."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Abnormalities of the esophagus, inability to stand or sit upright for at least 30 mins, renal impairment with CrCl &lt;35 mL/min, hypocalcemia. Infants and childn. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with active GI problems e.g. Barret’s esophagus, gastritis, duodenitis, ulcers; recent history (within the previous yr) of major GI disease e.g. peptic ulcer, active GI bleeding, or surgery of the upper GI other than pyloroplasty. Correct hypocalcemia and other disturbances before initiating alendronate therapy. Small, asymptomatic decreases in serum calcium and phosphate may occur, particularly in patients with Paget’s disease or patients receiving glucocorticoids. May cause ONJ, osteonecrosis of the external auditory canal, musculoskeletal pain, atypical subtrochanteric, diaphyseal femoral fractures, mild and transient decrease in serum calcium and phosphate especially in patients with Paget’s disease, atrial fibrillation, local irritation of the upper GI mucosa, esophageal events (e.g. esophagitis erosions and ulcerations, occasionally with bleeding and rarely followed by esophageal stricture or perforation); discontinue if dysphagia, odynophagia (pain on swallowing), worsening heartburn, retrosternal pain develops. Conjunctivitis, uveitis, episcleritis, and scleritis; discontinue if ocular inflammatory symptoms occurs. May impair ability to drive or operate machines. Childn. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category C.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "GI disorders; hypersensitivity reactions; metabolism and nutrition, nervous system, eye, ear and labyrinth, respiratory, thoracic, and mediastinal, skin and subcutaneous tissue, musculoskeletal and connective tissue disorders; fever, peripheral edema, myalgia, malaise; asymptomatic, mild, transient decreases in serum calcium and phosphate; elevated transaminases."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Antacids, mineral supplements and some osmotic laxatives containing aluminum, calcium, iron, or magnesium; IV ranitidine, HRT (e.g. estrogen and progestin), aspirin and other NSAIDs; herbal products."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 70 mg x 4s (P1,664.00)."
          }
        ],

          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults and childn &gt;16 yrs</b>: 1-2 tabs every 4-6 hrs as needed for pain relief. Max 8 tabs/day. <b>Elderly &gt;75 yrs</b>: Dose interval should not be less than 6 hrs. <b>Renal impairment (CrCl &lt;30 mL/min)</b>: Max 2 tabs every 12 hrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity.  Acute intoxication with alcohol, hypnotics, narcotics, centrally acting analgesics, opioids, or psychotropic drugs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Avoid abrupt discontinuation. Patients prone to suicide or addiction, with emotional disturbance or depression, taking tranquilizers, antidepressants, excessive amounts of alcohol; at risk for respiratory depression, have increased intracranial pressure or head trauma, are opioid-dependent, with severe acute abdominal conditions, severe liver impairment, renal impairment. Risk of misuse, abuse, diversion, and overdosage. Concomitant use with CNS depressants, MAOIs, SSRIs.  Elderly. Childn. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category C. <b>Paracetamol</b>: Increases risk for acute liver failure in patients with liver disease. <b>Tramadol</b>: Increases risk for seizure in patients taking SSRIs, TCAs, MAOIs, antipsychotics, other opioids, other drugs that reduce seizure threshold; with epilepsy, risk or history of seizures; administration of naloxone. May induce serotonin syndrome with concomitant use with serotonergic drugs, drugs that impair metabolism of serotonin or tramadol (e.g. CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 inhibitors). Concomitant use with alcohol, other opioids, and illicit drugs. May impair ability to drive and operate machines.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Asthenia, fatigue, hot flushes, chest pain, rigors, syncope, withdrawal syndrome; dyspnea, abnormal hepatic function, decreased weight, anemia, tinnitus, abnormal vision; GI, nervous, psychiatric, CV, urinary, dermatologic effects. <b>Tramadol</b>: Vasodilation, myocardial ischemia, orthostatic hypotension, allergic reactions (e.g. anaphylaxis, urticaria, SJS/TEN), pulmonary edema, cognitive dysfunction, difficulty concentrating, depression, suicidal tendency, hepatitis, liver failure."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Alcohol, CNS depressants, warfarin. <b>Tramadol</b>: Other opioids, carbamazepine, CYP3A4 inducers (e.g. rifampicin, St. John’s Wort) and inhibitors (e.g. ketoconazole, erythromycin), CYP2D6 inhibitors (e.g. amitriptyline, fluoxetine, paroxetine), digoxin, quinidine, serotonergic drugs (e.g. alpha 2-blockers, MAOIs, SSRIs, SNRIs, triptans, lithium). <b>Paracetamol</b>: INH, phenothiazines."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 37.5 mg/325 mg (P57.20)."
          }
        ],

          },

            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "90 mg once daily for the 1<sup>st</sup> 7 days, then increase to 180 mg. <b>Patients with severe impairments:</b> Reduce dose by 50% (renal) or 40% (hepatic)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Monitor for development of severe, life-threatening, and fatal pulmonary adverse reactions (including those with features consistent with ILD/pneumonitis), HTN, bradycardia, visual disturbances, elevation of CPK and pancreatic enzymes, hepatotoxicity, hyperglycemia. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn < 18 yrs. Elderly >85 yrs. Women of childbearing potential should use non-hormonal contraception during and for at least 4 months after treatment. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Pneumonia, URTI. Anemia; decreased lymphocyte, WBC, and neutrophil count; increased APTT. hyperglycemia, hyperinsulinemia, hypophosphatemia, hypomagnesemia, hypercalcemia, hyponatremia, hypokalemia, decreased appetite. Headache, peripheral neuropathy, dizziness. Visual disturbances. HTN. Cough, dyspnea. Increased lipase and amylase, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation, abdominal pain, stomatitis. Increased AST/ALT and alkaline phosphatase. Rash, pruritus. Increased CPK levels, myalgia, arthralgia; increased blood creatinine. Fatigue, edema, pyrexia. Decreased platelet count, insomnia, dysgeusia, memory impairment, bradycardia, QT prolongation, tachycardia, palpitations, dry mouth, dyspepsia, flatulence, increased lactate dehydrogenase, dry skin, photosensitivity, non-cardiac chest pain/discomfort, musculoskeletal stiffness/pain, increased cholesterol, decreased weight."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "CYP3A inducers, inhibitors, and substrates. P-gp, BCRP, OCT1, MATE1, and MATE2K substrates."
          },
          {

          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Severe hypotension, shock, high-grade aortic stenosis, and unstable heart failure after acute MI."

          },

            "content": "CYP3A4 inhibitors and inducers. Grapefruit juice. Dantrolene IV, and CCBs."
          },

  {
    "id": 3822,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 3822,
        "brand_name": "Aurantin",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Fosphenytoin sodium",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Hydantoins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Control of generalized convulsive status epilepticus, prevention and treatment of seizures occurring during neurosurgery."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults - Status epilepticus loading dose:</b> 15-20 mg PE (phenytoin sodium equivalent) per kg BW administered at 100-150 mg PE/min. Rate should not be >150 mg PE/min. <b>Non-emergent situation loading and maintenance dosing:</b> 10-20 mg PE/kg given IV or IM. Rate should not be >150 mg PE/min. <b>Maintenance dose for status epilepticus or non-emergent situation:</b> 4-6 mg PE/kg/day."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with sinus bradycardia, SA block, 2<sup>nd</sup> and 3<sup>rd</sup>-degree AV block, and Adams-Stokes syndrome. Concomitant use with delavirdine or to the class of non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NNRTIs)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Do not make any adjustment in the recommended doses when substituting fosphenytoin for phenytoin sodium. Do not confuse the amount of drug to be given in PE with the concentration of the drug in the vial. Risk of adverse CV reactions associated with rapid administration (>150 mg PE/min). Not to be used for absence (petit mal) seizures, seizures due to hypoglycemic or other metabolic causes. Patients with renal and/or hepatic disease, or with hypoalbuminemia. Potential to lower serum folate levels. May increase risk of suicidal ideation and/or behavior, all patients should be routinely evaluated for depression, anxiety, and suicidality. Hypotension may occur especially after IV administration at high doses and high rates of administration. Severe CV reactions (e.g. atrial and ventricular conduction depression and ventricular fibrillation). Patients with hypotension and severe myocardial insufficiency. Edema, discoloration, and pain distal to the site of injection (\"purple glove syndrome\"). May develop hypersensitivity syndrome or drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms. Patients at higher risk for developing hypersensitivity syndrome/drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (e.g. black patients, patients who have experienced syndrome in the past). Patients with family history of syndrome and immunosuppressed patients. Severe cutaneous adverse reactions (e.g. acute generalized exanthematous pustulosis, exfoliative dermatitis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, toxic epidermal necrolysis and drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms). Discontinue treatment if rash appears. If rash of a milder type (measles-like or scarlatiniform), therapy may be resumed after the rash has completely disappeared. Discontinue immediately if symptoms of angioedema (e.g. facial, perioral, or upper airway swelling) occur; acute hepatotoxicity. Impaired liver function, or those who are gravely ill may show early signs of toxicity. Hematopoietic complications (e.g. thrombocytopenia, leukopenia, granulocytopenia, agranulocytosis, and pancytopenia with or without bone marrow suppression). May develop lymphadenopathy (local or generalized), including benign lymph node hyperplasia, pseudolymphoma, lymphoma and Hodgkin's disease. May produce confusional states. Exacerbation of porphyria; hyperglycemia. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Pregnancy. Not recommended for breastfeeding women. Elderly.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "CV collapse and/or central nervous system depression. Nystagmus and dizziness; pruritus. Tinnitus, ear disorder, vertigo; visual impairment, vision blurred; nausea, dry mouth, vomiting; pain, asthenia, injection site pain, chills; paresthesia, somnolence, ataxia, headache, tremor, abnormal coordination, dysgeusia, stupor, dysarthria; euphoric mood; ecchymosis; hypotension, vasodilatation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Acute alcohol intake, azapropazone, phenylbutazone, salicylates, halothane, chloramphenicol, erythromycin, isoniazid, sulfadiazine, sulfamethizole, co-trimoxazole, sulfaphenazole, sulfisoxazole, sulfonamides, felbamate, oxcarbazepine, sodium valproate, succinimides, topiramate, amphotericin B, fluconazole, itraconazole, ketoconazole, miconazole, voriconazole, fluorouracil, capecitabine, chlordiazepoxide, diazepam, disulfiram, methylphenidate, trazodone, viloxazine, amiodarone, dicumarol, diltiazem, nifedipine, ticlopidine, cimetidine, fluvastatin, estrogens, tacrolimus, tolbutamide, omeprazole, fluoxetine, fluvoxamine, sertraline."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Solution for injection 75 mg/mL x 10 mL."
          }
        ],
        "company": {
          "id": 221,
          "name": "Zuellig Pharma Corp."
        },

        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Atorvastatin calcium",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Statins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Adjunct to diet for the treatment of elevated total cholesterol, LDL-C, apolipoprotein B and triglycerides and to increase HDL-C in patients with primary hypercholesterolemia (heterozygous familial and non-familial hypercholesterolemia), combined (mixed) hyperlipidemia (Fredrickson types IIa and IIb), elevated serum triglyceride levels (Fredrickson type IV), and dysbetalipoproteinemia (Fredrickson type III). To reduce total cholesterol and LDL-C in patients with homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia as adjunct to diet and other non-pharmacological measures. To prevent CV events in high risk adult patients."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Individualized dosing. <b>Usual dosage range:</b> 10-80 mg once a day, adjust dose at intervals of 4 weeks or more. <b>Primary hypercholesterolemia and combined (mixed) hyperlipidemia:</b> 10 mg once a day. <b>Homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia:</b> 10-80 mg once a day, as adjunct to other lipid-lowering treatments. <b>CV disease prevention:</b> 10 mg/day. <b>Concomitant use with hepatitis C antiviral agents (elbasvir/grazoprevir):</b> Should not exceed 20 mg/day."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Active liver disease, or unexplained persistent serum transaminase elevations >3x ULN. Pregnancy and lactation. Patients treated with hepatitis C antivirals glecaprevir/pibrentasvir."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Monitor liver function. Patients who are alcoholic and/or have history of liver disease. Predisposing factors to myopathy or rhabdomyolysis. Childn < 18.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Chest pain, face edema, fever, neck rigidity, malaise, photosensitivity reaction, and generalized edema. Adverse effects on digestive, respiratory, nervous, musculoskeletal, skin, and appendages, urogenital, CV, metabolic-nutritional, hemic and lymphatic systems. Amblyopia, tinnitus, dry eyes, refraction disorder, eye hemorrhage, deafness, glaucoma, parosmia, taste loss and perversion."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "CYP3A4 inhibitors and inducers, transport inhibitors (e.g. ciclosporin), gemfibrozil/fibric acid derivatives, ezetimibe, colestipol, fusidic acid, colchicine. Digoxin, oral contraceptives, warfarin, and niacin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 10 mg (P26.37), 20 mg (P31.05), 40 mg (P37.63), 80 mg (P35.83)."
          }
        ],

          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Proton-Pump Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Short-term treatment (7-10 days) of adult patients with gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and a history of erosive esophagitis. Treatment of pathological hypersecretory conditions including Zollinger-Ellison syndrome in adults."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>GERD associated with a history of erosive esophagitis</b>: 40 mg once daily by IV infusion for 7 to 10 days. <b>Pathological hypersecretion including Zollinger-Ellison syndrome</b>: 80 mg IV every 12 hrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to the formulation or any substituted benzimidazole."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity and severe skin reactions. Injection site reactions. <i>Clostridium difficile</i>-associated diarrhea. Bone fracture. Interference with urine screen for THC. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category B.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]

          },

            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Asthenia, fatigue, malaise. Anaphylaxis. Erythema multiforme, SJS, toxic epidermal necrolysis and angioedema. Rhabdomyolysis, bone fracture. Interstitial nephritis. Hepatocellular damage leading to jaundice and hepatic failure. Hallucinations, confusion, insomnia, somnolence. Hyponatremia, hypomagnesemia. <i>Clostridium difficile</i>-associated diarrhea.           {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Fourth Generation Cephalosporins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of the following infections caused by susceptible microorganisms: lower respiratory tract infections (LRTI) including moderate to severe pneumonia and bronchitis; uncomplicated and complicated urinary tract infections (UTIs) including pyelonephritis; skin and skin structure infections; complicated intraabdominal infections including peritonitis and biliary tract infections; septicemia. Empiric therapy for febrile neutropenia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "May be administered IV or IM. <b>Moderate to severe pneumonia -</b> Adults and childn >40 kg: 1-2 g; Childn < 40 kg: 50 mg/kg. All doses taken every 12 hrs for 10 days. <b>Uncomplicated or complicated UTIs including pyelonephritis and/or concurrent bacteremia -</b> Mild to moderate: Adults and childn >40 kg: 500 mg-1 g; Childn < 40 kg: 50 mg/kg. All doses taken every 12 hrs for 7-10 days; Severe: Adults and childn >40 kg: 2 g; Childn < 40 kg: < 50 mg/kg. All doses taken every 12 hrs for 7-10 days. <b>Complicated intra-abdominal infections (in combination with metronidazole) -</b> Adults and childn >40 kg: 2 g; Childn < 40 kg: 50 mg/kg. All doses taken every 12 hrs for 7-10 days. <b>Empiric therapy for febrile neutropenia -</b> Adults and childn >40 kg: 2 g; Childn &le;40 kg: 50 mg/kg. All doses taken every 8 hrs for 7 days or until resolution of neutropenia. In patients whose fever resolves but remain neutropenic for >7 days, the need for continued therapy should be re-evaluated. <b>Very severe or life-threatening infections -</b> Adults and childn >40 kg: 2 g; Childn &le;40 kg: 50 mg/kg. All doses taken every 8 hrs for 7-10- days. More severe infections may require longer treatment. <b>Renal impairment - CrCl 30-60 mL/min:</b> Mild to moderate UTI: 500 mg daily; Mild to moderate infections other than UTI: 1 g daily; Severe infections: 2 g every 24 hrs; Very severe or life-threatening infections: 2 g every 12 hrs; <b>11-29 mL/min:</b> Mild to moderate infections including UTI: 500 mg; Severe infections: 1 g; Very severe or life-threatening infections: 2 g. All doses administered every 24 hrs; <b>< 11 mL/min:</b> Mild to moderate infections including UTI: 250 mg; Severe infections: 500 mg; Very severe or life-threatening infections: 1 g. All doses administered every 24 hrs; <b>CAPD:</b> Mild to moderate UTI: 500 mg; Mild to moderate infections other than UTI: 1 g; Severe infections: 2 g; Very severe or life-threatening infections: 2 g. All doses administered every 48 hrs; <b>Hemodialysis:</b> 1 g on Day 1, then 500 mg every day for all infections except febrile neutropenia (1 g every 24 hrs). Dose should be administered after hemodialysis at the same time each day."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with renal or hepatic impairment; high risk of severe infections, underlying malignancy, severe or prolonged neutropenia; poor nutritional state; receiving protracted course of antimicrobials or previously stabilized on anticoagulants. CDAD, colitis; encephalopathy, myoclonus, seizures, renal failure; fall in prothrombin activity. Overgrowth of nonsusceptible organisms during prolonged use. Childn &le;16 yrs. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category B.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",

                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },

                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "GI disturbances (e.g. diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, oral moniliasis, colitis including pseudomembranous colitis, abdominal pain, constipation). Hypersensitivity reactions (e.g. local reactions including phlebitis, pain and/or inflammation; erythema, unspecified moniliasis, pruritus, urticaria, rash, anaphylaxis including anaphylactic shock)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Aminoglycosides, diuretics. False positive reaction in Benedict’s reagent and Clinitest."
          },

        "content": "Ursodeoxycholic acid",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Hepatic Protectors, Cholagogues & Cholelitholytics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Dissolution of cholesterol-rich gallstones in patients with functioning gallbladders. Primary biliary cirrhosis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Dissolution of cholesterol gallstones</b> - Patients &gt;100 kg BW: 5 tabs (equiv to 1,250 mg); 81-100 kg: 4 tabs (equiv to 1,000 mg); 61-80 kg: 3 tabs (equiv to 750 mg); Up to 60 kg: 2 tabs (equiv to 500 mg). Taken unchewed together with some liquid in the evening before going to bed. <b>Symptomatic treatment of primary biliary cirrhosis:</b> 12-16 mg/kg. Daily dose depends on BW and is between 3-7 tabs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Acute inflammations of gallbladder and biliary tract. Occlusion of biliary tract (choledochal or cystic duct obstruction). Frequent episodes of biliary colic. Radio-opaque calcified gallstones. Impaired contractility of gallbladder."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Monitor AST, ALT and gamma-GT every 4 weeks, thereafter every 3 months. Hepatic cirrhosis. Reduce dose if diarrhea occurs. Not recommended if gallbladder cannot be visualized on x-ray; in cases of calcified gallstones, impaired contractility of gallbladder, frequent episodes of biliary colic. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Pasty stools or diarrhea."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Cholestyramine, colestipol or antacids containing aluminum hydroxide and/or smectite (aluminum oxide). Ciclosporin, nitrendipine, dapsone. Estrogenic hormones and blood cholesterol-lowering substances (e.g. clofibrate)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 250 mg (P45.64), 500 mg (P71.93)."
          }
        ],

        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Azithromycin (as monohydrate)",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Macrolides"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of respiratory tract infections (including otitis media); skin and soft-tissue infections; and uncomplicated genital infections. Prophylaxis and as a component of regimens in the treatment of <i>Mycobacterium avium</i> complex (MAC)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults</b>: 500 mg as a single dose daily for 3 days. <b>Uncomplicated genital infections caused by <i>Chlamydia trachomatis</i> and for chancroid</b>: 1 g as a single dose. <b>Uncomplicated gonorrhoea</b>: 2 g single dose. <b>Treatment of granuloma inguinale</b>: Initially 1 g followed by 500 mg daily or 1 g once a week for at least 3 weeks. <b>Prophylaxis of disseminated MAC infections</b>: 1.2 g once weekly. <b>Mild or moderate typhoid caused by multidrug-resistant strains</b>: 500 mg once daily for 7 days."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with hepatic or renal impairment, known prolongation of the QT interval, history of torsades de pointes, congenital long QT syndrome, bradyarrhythmias or uncompensated heart failure, ongoing proarrhythmic condition. Patients on drugs known to prolong the QT interval. Elderly.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "GI disturbances. Headache, somnolence and taste disturbances. Pain and inflammation at the injection site of IV infusions. Risk of QT prolongation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Antacids containing aluminum or magnesium. Atorvastatin, lovastatin. Quinine, nelfinavir, ciclosporin and pimozide."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 500 mg x 3s (P287.56)."

          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of infections caused by susceptible organisms in  upper and lower respiratory tract infections; skin and soft tissue infections, acute otitis media. Uncomplicated genital infections due to <i>Chlamydia trachomatis</i> or non-multiresistant <i>Neisseria gonorrhoeae</i>, chancroid due to <i>Haemophilus ducreyi</i>. Prophylaxis against Mycobacterium avium intracellulare complex (MAC) infection either alone or in combination with rifabutin, and disseminated MAC (DMAC) in combination with ethambutol in patients with advanced HIV. Treatment of community-acquired pneumonia (CAP) caused by <i>Legionella pneumophila</i> and pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) caused by <i>Chlamydia trachomatis</i>, <i>Neiseria gonorrhea</i>, <i>Mycoplasma hominis</i> in patients who require initial IV therapy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "1 tab once a day as a single daily dose depending on the type of infection. Can be taken with or without food and swallowed whole. Childn >45 kg: Total dose of 1,200 mg."
          },

            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with significant hepatic diseases, renal impairment, diabetes. Prolonged cardiac repolarization and QT interval. Observe for signs of superinfection. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },

        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Second Generation Cephalosporins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of patients with mild to moderate infections caused by susceptible strains of microorganisms in the conditions: pharyngitis/tonsillitis; acute bacterial otitis media; acute bacterial maxillary sinusitis; acute bacterial exacerbation of chronic bronchitis and secondary bacterial infections of acute bronchitis, uncomplicated skin and skin structure infections, urinary tract infections (UTI), gonorrhea; early Lyme disease (erythema migrans)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults and adolescents &gt;13 yrs</b> – Pharyngitis/tonsillitis, acute bacterial maxillary sinusitis: 250 mg twice daily for 10 days. Secondary bacterial infections of acute bronchitis: 250 or 500 mg twice daily for 5-10 days. Uncomplicated UTI: 250 mg twice daily for 7-10 days. Acute bacterial exacerbations of chronic bronchitis, uncomplicated skin and skin structure infections: 250 or 500 mg twice daily for 10 days. Early Lyme disease: 500 mg twice daily for 20 days. Uncomplicated gonorrhea: 1 g once daily as single dose. <b>Childn (who can swallow tabs whole)</b> – Acute otitis media, acute bacterial maxillary sinusitis: 250 mg twice daily for 10 days. <b>Patients with renal impairment</b> – (CrCl 10- < 30 mL/min): Standard individual dose given every 24 hrs; < 10 mL/min (without hemodialysis): Standard individual dose given every 48 hrs; Hemodialysis: A single additional standard dose given at the end of each dialysis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Renal or hepatic impairment. Cross-hypersensitivity. Overgrowth of non-susceptible microorganism (<i>Candida</i>, Enterococci, <i>Clostridium difficile</i>). Superinfection. Discontinue use if CDAD is suspected or confirmed. Concurrent treatment of potent diuretics. Individuals with history of colitis. Monitor prothrombin time in patients at risk and administered exogenous Vitamin K. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category B.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Anaphylaxis, angioedema, pruritus, rash, serum sickness-like reaction, urticaria, drug fever. Pseudomembranous colitis. Hemolytic anemia, leukopenia, pancytopenia, thrombocytopenia, increased prothrombin time. Hepatitis, cholestasis, jaundice. Seizure, encephalopathy. Erythema multiforme, SJS, TEN. Renal dysfunction."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Probenecid, drugs that reduce gastric acidity, oral estrogen/progesterone contraceptives. False-positive reactions for glucose with copper reduction tests (Benedict’s or Fehling’s solution). False-negative result with ferricyanide test. Glucose oxidase or hexokinase method to determine blood/plasma glucose levels."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 500 mg (P46.30)."

            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Take 1 tab daily, beginning on the 1<sup>st</sup> day of menstrual bleeding. The interval for the next tab should be 24 hrs.         "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/wxxBspI3dBW0nhhMEFz3KBPoLN3agPGEASInWbXob5kfaaEkIc.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/6k5ZzomnKD3QqyQbMs0yEG2YKaBUYS513YLAz1MYR2aKLEVfFD.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/HDf7mlXezLEqiaIzoMv8z4uyEb2ajSBfBCNqaEfakG9BxPGbfy.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Atorvastatin",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Statins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Adjunct to diet for treatment of elevated total-C, LDL-C, apolipoprotein B, and triglycerides and to increase HDL-C in primary hypercholesterolemia, combined hyperlipidemia, elevated serum triglyceride levels, and dysbetalipoproteinemia not adequately controlled by diet. Reduction of total-C and LDL-C in homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia. Reduces risk of fatal CHD and non-fatal MI, stroke, revascularization procedures, and angina pectoris in patients without clinically evident CV disease, with or without dyslipidemia, but with multiple risk factors for CHD; non-fatal MI, fatal and non-fatal stroke, revascularization procedures, hospitalization for CHF, and angina in patients with CHD; CV disease in patients with diabetes with moderately decreased eGFR; major CV events (e.g., stroke) in patients with CHD and CKD not requiring dialysis. Reduces rate of GFR decline and CKD progression in patients with CHD and/or diabetes with microalbuminuria. Adjunct to diet to reduce total-C, LDL-C, and apolipoprotein B levels in childn 10–17 yrs with heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia and persistently elevated LDL-C (&ge;160 or &ge;190 mg/dL) despite adequate diet therapy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Primary hypercholesterolemia and combined hyperlipidemia:</b> 10 mg once daily. <b>Homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia:</b> 80 mg. <b>Severe dyslipidemia in childn &ge;10 yrs:</b> Initially 10 mg once daily, may be increased to 80 mg once daily. <b>In combination with cyclosporine, telaprevir, tipranavir/ritonavir, glecaprevir/pibrentasvir:</b> Max 10 mg."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Active liver disease or unexplained persistent serum transaminase elevations >3x ULN. Women of childbearing potential not using adequate contraception. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with heavy alcohol use and/or have history of liver disease; history of renal impairment. Myalgia, immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy, rhabdomyolysis with acute renal failure secondary to myoglobinuria, hemorrhagic stroke, increased HbA1c and fasting serum glucose levels. Perform liver function tests before initiation of therapy and periodically thereafter. Reduce dose or discontinue if ALT/AST persist >3x ULN. Discontinue if markedly elevated CPK levels occur, myopathy is diagnosed or suspected, or if risk factors for renal failure secondary to rhabdomyolysis are present.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nasopharyngitis, hyperglycemia, pharyngolaryngeal pain, epistaxis, diarrhea, dyspepsia, nausea, flatulence, arthralgia, pain in extremity, musculoskeletal pain, muscle spasms, myalgia, joint swelling, abnormal liver function test, increased blood creatine phosphokinase, nightmare, blurred vision, tinnitus, abdominal discomfort, eructation, hepatitis, cholestasis, urticaria, muscle fatigue, neck pain, malaise, pyrexia, positive WBC urine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Cyclosporine, fibric acid derivatives, lipid-modifying doses of niacin, CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., erythromycin/clarithromycin, protease inhibitors, diltiazem HCl, itraconazole, grapefruit juice) and inducers (e.g., efavirenz, rifampin), glecaprevir, pibrentasvir, letermovir, elbasvir, grazoprevir, antacids, colestipol, digoxin, oral contraceptives, colchicine, fusidic acid."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 20 mg (P15.00), 40 mg (P21.50)."
          }
        ],

          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/hCYF3taEfIPqi9YgaBRPu485Xh54dIWlD4LdnZTlemULAKZdaK.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/GGficlvJQNsyC1BwKKo80I3c3ftTds2HmfD0VeZZSsusKHm8Aa.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Azithromycin",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Macrolides"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of respiratory tract infection (including otitis media), skin and soft tissue infections and uncomplicated genital infections. Prophylaxis and as component regimens in the treatment of <i>Mycobacterium avium</i> complex (MAC). <b>Adults</b>: Acute bacterial exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, acute bacterial sinusitis, community-acquired pneumonia (CAP), uncomplicated skin and skin structure infections, urethritis and cervicitis, genital ulcer disease (chancroid) in men. <b>Childn</b>: Acute otitis media, CAP."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults</b>: 500 mg single dose for 3 days. Alternatively, an initial dose of 500 mg may be followed by 250 mg/day for a further 4 days. <b>Uncomplicated genital infections caused by <i>C. trachomatis</i> and for chancroid</b>: 1 g single dose. <b>Uncomplicated gonorrhea</b>: 2 g single dose. <b>Treatment of granuloma inguinale</b>: Initially 1 g followed by 500 mg daily or 1 g may be given once a week for at least 3 weeks until all lesions have completely healed. <b>Disseminated MAC infections – Prophylaxis</b>: 1.2 g once weekly. <b>Treatment or secondary prophylaxis</b>: 500 mg once daily should be given with other antimycobacterials.<b> Mild or moderate typhoid</b>: 500 mg once daily for 7 days."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to macrolide or ketolide antibiotics. Patients with history of cholestatic jaundice or hepatic dysfunction associated with prior azithromycin use."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Hepatoxicity. Discontinue if signs and symptoms of hepatitis occurs. Patients with cystic fibrosis, nosocomial acquired infections, known or suspected bacteremia, patients requiring hospitalization, elderly or debilitated patients, or patients with immunodeficiency or functional asplenia. Patients with <i>Clostridium difficile</i>-associated diarrhea and impaired hepatic function. Increased risk of prolonged cardiac repolarization and QT interval, developing cardiac arrhythmia and Torsades de Pointes. Exacerbation of myasthenia gravis and new onset of myasthenic syndrome. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category B.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea/loose stools, and abdominal pain."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Antacids containing aluminum or magnesium. Nelfinavir, oral anticoagulants, atorvastatin, carbamazepine, cetirizine, didanosine, efavirenz, fluconazole, indinavir, midazolam, rifabutin, sildenafil, theophylline (IV and oral), triazolam, trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole, zidovudine, digoxin, ergotamine, dihydroergotamine, terfenadine, ciclosporin, hexobarbital, and phenytoin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 500 mg (P65.00)."
          }

            "content": "Treatment of susceptible infections including gonorrhea, otitis media, pharyngitis, lower respiratory tract infections (e.g. bronchitis), and urinary tract infections."

            "content": "<b>Adults</b>: 400 mg once daily or 200 mg every 12 hrs. <b>Childn</b>: 8 mg/kg/day as single dose or as 4 mg/kg every 12 hrs. Childn &gt;12 yrs and weighing &gt;50 kg should not be treated with the recommended adult dose."

            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Previous, immediate and/or severe hypersensitivity to penicillin or other beta-lactam antibiotics."

            "content": "Superinfection, <i>Clostridium difficile</i>-associated diarrhea and colitis. Patients with history of GI disease (particularly colitis). Prolonged PT and PTT. Patients with CrCl &lt;20 mL/min. Childn &lt;6 months. Pregnancy and lactation.",

          },

          },

          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/pSJFYJ0ScfbxN0B1C89hxor8ZNl5eUfXZtk08J7aqu7lO1t68W.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Allopurinol",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Antigout Preparations"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of gout, primary or secondary to hyperuricemia associated with blood dyscrasias, primary or secondary uric acid nephropathy, recurrent uric acid formation. Prophylaxis to prevent tissue deposition, renal calculi, or uric acid nephropathy in patients with leukemia, lymphomas, and malignancies who are receiving cancer chemotherapy which results to elevation of serum uric acid levels."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults – Mild</b>: 100-200 mg; <b>Moderately severe</b>: 300-600 mg; <b>Severe</b>: 700-900 mg. All doses to be taken 3 times daily or as prescribed. <b>Childn &lt;15 yrs</b>: 100-400 mg daily. <b>Renal or hepatic impairment</b>: Reduce dose."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Patients with idiopathic hemochromatosis. Childn (except with hyperuricemia secondary to malignancy). Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Acute attacks of gout. Treatment should be stopped immediately if any skin reactions or other signs of hypersensitivity. Patients with HTN or cardiac insufficiency who may also have renal impairment.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Skin rash. SJS and toxic epidermal necrolysis. Fever, chills, lymphadenopathy, leucopenia or leukocytosis, eosinophilia, arthralgia, vasculitis. Hepatotoxicity, altered liver function. Hematological effects e.g. thrombocytopenia, aplastic anemia, agranulocytosis and hemolytic anemia. Paresthesia, peripheral neuropathy, alopecia, gynecomastia. Hypertension, taste disturbances, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, diarrhea, malaise, drowsiness, vertigo, and visual disturbances."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",

          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults:</b> 1,760 mg/day (11 mL twice daily). <b>Childn 2 months-12 yrs</b> - Mild to moderate infections (skin and soft tissue infections): 25 mg/3.6 mg/kg/day. More severe infections (otitis media, sinusitis, and LRTIs): 45 mg/6.4 mg/kg/day twice a day. <b>Renal impairment (GFR &gt;30 mL/min):</b> Reduce dose depending on the severity of the impairment and patient’s BW. To be taken at the start of meals."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. History of severe immediate hypersensitivity reaction (e.g. anaphylaxis) to other beta-lactams, history of jaundice/hepatic impairment. Suspected infected mononucleosis. Not be used to treat penicillin-resistant <i>S. pneumoniae</i>. Drugs that inhibit peristalsis in antibiotic-associated colitis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Impaired renal and hepatic function. Prolonged use. Convulsions may occur in patients with impaired renal function or receiving high doses. Concomitant use with allopurinol. Perform periodic assessments of renal, hepatic, and hematopoietic functions. May impair ability to drive or operate machines. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Diarrhea, nausea and vomiting. Mucocutaneous candidosis. Antibiotic-associated colitis. AGEP. False positive Coombs' test."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Allopurinol, oral anticoagulants, methotrexate, probenecid, mycophenolate mofetil."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Powder for oral suspension 457 mg/5 mL x 70 mL (P324.80)."
          }
        ],

    "id": 946,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 946,
        "brand_name": "Bactiv Tablet",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Co-amoxiclav",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Penicillins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Short-term treatment of bacterial infections when amoxicillin resistant beta-lactamase-producing strains are suspected as the cause at the following sites: upper respiratory tract infections (URTI) (including ear, nose and throat) e.g. sinusitis, otitis media, recurrent tonsillitis; lower respiratory tract infections (LRTI) e.g. acute exacerbations of chronic bronchitis, bronchopneumonia; genitourinary tract and abdominal infections e.g. cystitis, septic abortion, pelvic or puerperal sepsis and intra-abdominal sepsis; skin and soft tissue infections e.g. cellulitis, animal bites and severe dental abscess with spreading cellulitis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults</b>: One 625 mg tab every 12 hrs or one 375 mg tab every 8 hrs. <b>More severe infections and RTI</b>: 1 g tab every 12 hrs or one 625 mg tab every 8 hrs. <b>Renal impairment - GFR 10-30 mL/min</b>: 625 mg or 375 mg every 12 hrs depending on the severity of infection; <b>&lt;10 mL/min</b>: 625 mg or 375 mg every 24 hrs depending on the severity of infection. <b>Hemodialysis</b>: 625 mg or 375 mg every 24 hrs depending on the severity of infection and an additional dose both during and at the end of dialysis. <b>Childn weighing &ge;40 kg</b>: Adult dose."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to penicillin. Cross-sensitivity with other beta-lactam antibiotics e.g. cephalosporins. Previous history of co-amoxiclav or penicillin-associated jaundice or hepatic dysfunction."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with hepatic or renal impairment. Monitor hepatic function at regular intervals. Cholestatic jaundice. Maintain adequate fluid intake and urinary output in order to reduce the possibility of crystalluria. Serious and occasionally fatal hypersensitivity (anaphylactoid) reactions. Prolonged use may result to overgrowth of non-susceptible organisms. Patients on anti-coagulation therapy. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Diarrhea, indigestion, nausea, vomiting and mucocutaneous candidiasis; crystalluria; vaginal itching, soreness and discharge; moderate and asymptomatic rises in AST and/or ALT and ALP; urticarial and erythematous skin rashes."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Anticoagulants."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 625 mg (P43.75), 1 g (P66.25)."
          }
        ],
