          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of diabetes mellitus in adults, adolescents and childn &ge;2 yrs. Can be co-administered with oral antidiabetics for type 2 DM."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "SC inj once daily at same time each day. Individualized dosage. <b>Switch from other insulins:</b> Adjust dose and concomitant antidiabetic. <b>Switch from NPH insulin 2x daily:</b> Reduce daily dose by 20-30% during 1st weeks of therapy. <b>Switch from 300 units/mL insulin glargine:</b> Reduce dose by approx 20%."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Not for IV administration."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not insulin of choice for diabetic ketoacidosis. Transferring to another type or brand, changes in strength, origin and/or method of manufacture of insulin. Conditions that lessen or diminish hypoglycemic symptoms. Perform metabolic monitoring during switch and initial weeks after; intensified glucose monitoring in clinically relevant hypoglycemia or intercurrent illness. Combination with pioglitazone, especially in patients with risk factors for cardiac heart failure. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn < 2 yrs. Elderly &ge;65 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Hypoglycemia, lipohypertrophy, inj site reactions."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Oral antidiabetics, ACEIs, disopyramide, fibrates, fluoxetine, MAOIs, pentoxifylline, propoxyphene, salicylates, somatostatin analogues, sulfonamide antibiotics. Beta-blockers, clonidine, lithium salts, alcohol. Pentamidine. Guanethidine, reserpine."
          },

            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Adjunct to diet and exercise in non-insulin-dependent (type 2) diabetes mellitus (DM) sufficiently controlled by sulfonylurea or metformin therapy alone or at max tolerated dose."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Individualized dosage. Initiate at the lowest effective dose and increase the dose depending on patient’s blood glucose levels. Max daily dose: 8 mg glimepiride and 2,000 mg metformin. <b>Switching from combination therapy of glimepiride and metformin as separate tabs:</b> Administer based on dose currently being taken. All doses must be taken once daily before or with breakfast or 1<sup>st</sup> main meal. Tab should be swallowed whole, not crushed or chewed."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Type 1 DM, diabetic ketonemia, diabetic coma or precoma. Severe hepatic dysfunction or hemodialysis, serious metabolic complication. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with impaired renal function, clinical or laboratory evidence of hepatic disease. Excessive alcohol intake. May impair ability to drive or operate machines.             "pregnancy_risk": {

                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },

            "content": "Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain and anorexia. Taste disturbance or metallic taste, changes in BP."

          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "For hypertension, chronic stable and vasospastic (Prinzmetal’s) angina pectoris."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults - Hypertension and angina:</b> Initially 5 mg once daily, may be increased to max 10 mg. <b>Childn and adolescents 6-17 yrs - Hypertension:</b> Initially 2.5 mg once daily, up-titrated to 5 mg once daily if BP goal is not achieved after 4 weeks. <b>Hepatic impairment:</b> Start on lowest dose and titrated slowly."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Severe hypotension. Shock (e.g. cardiogenic shock). Obstruction of the outflow tract of the left ventricle (e.g. high grade aortic stenosis). Hemodynamically unstable heart failure after acute MI."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with hypertensive crisis, heart failure, or CHF. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Elderly. Childn < 6 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",

          },

            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Edema, somnolence, dizziness, headache, palpitations, flushing, abdominal pain, dyspnea, dyspepsia, altered bowel habits (e.g. diarrhea or constipation), nausea, ankle swelling, muscle cramps, fatigue, asthenia, visual disturbance (e.g. diplopia)."
          },
          {

        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Tibolone",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Estrogens"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Menopausal therapy in the treatment of menopausal vasomotor symptoms and prevention of postmenopausal osteoporosis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "1 tab daily. Start treatment 12 months after last menstrual bleed or immediately in case of surgical menopause."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Known, past, or suspected breast cancer. Known or suspected estrogen-dependent malignant tumors e.g. endometrial cancer. Undiagnosed genital bleeding. Untreated endometrial hyperplasia. Previous idiopathic or recurrent VTE (DVT, pulmonary embolism). Any history of arterial thromboembolic disease e.g. angina, MI, stroke, or TIA. Acute liver disease or any history of liver disease as long as liver function tests have failed to return to normal. Porphyria. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Leiomyoma (uterine fibroids) or endometriosis. Risk factors for or history of thromboembolic disorders, estrogen-dependent tumors (e.g. 1<sup>st</sup> degree hereditary for breast cancer). Liver disorders (e.g. liver adenoma). DM with or without vascular involvement. Cholelithiasis. Migraine or (severe) headache. SLE. History of endometrial hyperplasia. Epilepsy. Asthma. Otosclerosis. Discontinue if jaundice or deterioration of liver function, significant increase in BP, new onset of migraine-type headache occurs. Endometrial cancer. Cardiac or renal dysfunction. May cause breakthrough bleeding and spotting during the 1<sup>st</sup> month of treatment. Increased risk of endometrial hyperplasia and carcinoma when administered alone or for prolonged periods; probable dementia in women who start using continuous combined conjugated estrogen and MPA after 65 yrs old. Breast cancer. History of VTE (i.e. DVT or pulmonary embolism). CAD. Ischemic stroke. Ovarian cancer. Decrease in HDL-C, total triglycerides and lipoprotein levels; very minor decrease in thyroid binding globulin and total T4; decreased level of sex hormone-binding globulin. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category D.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {

                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },

                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },

            "content": "GI disorders, skin and subcutaneous tissue disorders, reproductive and breast disorders, CNS disorders, CV disorders; estrogen-dependent neoplasms, arthralgia, myalgia, increased weight, abnormal cervical smear, changes in liver function parameters; visual disturbances (e.g. blurred vision), edema, thromboembolism; gallbladder disease, probable dementia."

          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of psychoses, particularly schizophrenic disorders."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Acute psychotic episodes</b>: 400-800 mg/day, may be increased up to 1,200 mg/day. <b>Mixed positive and negative symptoms</b>: 400-800 mg/day. <b>Predominant negative symptoms</b>: 50-300 mg/day. Doses above 400 mg should be administered in 2 divided doses. <b>Renal insufficiency - CrCl 30-60 mL/min</b>: Reduce to &frac12; of dose; <b>10-30 mL/min</b>: Reduce to &frac13; of dose."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Concomitant prolactin-dependent tumors (e.g. pituitary gland prolactinomas and breast cancer), pheochromocytoma. In combination with Class Ia and III antiarrhythmic agents, sertindole, bepridil, cisapride, sultopride, thioridazine, IV erythromycin, IV vincamine, halofantrine, pentamidine, and sparfloxacin, levodopa. Childn &lt;15 yrs. Women of childbearing potential not using contraceptives. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis. Patients with stroke risk factors, history of epilepsy, DM or diabetes risk factors, preexisting bradycardia, hypokalemia, congenital or acquired long QT interval, thromboembolism risk factors, Parkinson’s disease, severe insufficiency, moderate or severe hepatic impairment. NMS, seizure, acute dystonia, EPS, tardive dyskinesia, may increase plasma prolactin, withdrawal symptoms. May impair the ability to drive or operate machines.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Hypotension, bradycardia, allergic reaction, angioedema, urticaria, weight gain, breast pain, nausea, vomiting, dry mouth, hepatic enzymes elevation, insomnia, agitation, somnolence, seizures."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Dopamine agonists, alcohol, bradycardia-inducing drugs (e.g. beta-blockers), hypokalemic diuretics, stimulant laxatives, IV amphotericin B, glucocorticoids, and tetracosactides, other antipsychotics, CNS depressants, antihypertensives and other hypotensive drugs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 200 mg (P100.94), 400 mg (P161.32)."
          }

          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/lWHSetQWUaqdc6J8fa6qceKia1pVpUvFVAO4y4ew9FmxpMpQzn.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/LNfqFOuCYatMz4FqEJBVPihdw6Q1hfDzSSMwdvDBQjrWqvzDte.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Amikacin sulfate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Aminoglycosides"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of bacterial septicemia including neonatal sepsis, respiratory tract infections, serious and complicated urinary tract infection (UTI); bone and joint, intraabdominal (including peritonitis), burns and post-op infections caused by susceptible microorganisms. Initial therapy in suspected G(-) infections."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "May be given IV or IM. <b>Adults, childn, and older infants:</b> 15 mg/kg as single dose or divided in 2-3 equal doses at equally divided intervals (i.e. 7.5 mg/kg every 12 hrs or 5 mg/kg every 8 hrs). For uncomplicated UTI: 500 mg once daily or 250 mg twice daily. <b>Neonates -</b> Loading dose: 10 mg/kg, followed by 7.5 mg/kg every 12 hrs; 0-7 days with BW < 2 kg: 7.5 mg/kg every 18-24 hrs for 7-10 days. <b>Renal impairment -</b> CrCl >80 mL/min: 15 mg/kg once daily; 60-80 mL/min: 12 mg/kg once daily; 40-60 mL/min: 7.5 mg/kg once daily; 30-40 mL/min: 4 mg/kg once daily; 20-30 mL/min: 7.5 mg/kg every other day; 10-20 mL/min: 4 mg/kg every other day; < 10 mL/min: 3 mg/kg every 3 days. Hemodialysis: Approx half the normal mg/kg after hemodialysis. Peritoneal dialysis: 7.5 mg/kg."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Should not be used >14 days. Patients with sulfite sensitivity; tinnitus, vertigo, subclinical high-frequency hearing loss, renal impairment; neuromuscular disorders (e.g. myasthenia gravis, parkinsonism). Concomitant use with other ototoxic or nephrotoxic drugs. Nephrotoxicity, ototoxicity, neurotoxicity. Observe for signs of 8<sup>th</sup> cranial nerve damage during therapy. Assess kidney function prior to therapy and daily during treatment. Overgrowth of non-susceptible organisms during prolonged use. Contains metabisulfite. Neonates. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Auditory, vestibular, and renal toxicity; neuromuscular blockade. Hearing loss, loss of balance. Acute muscular paralysis, apnea. Elevated serum creatinine, albuminuria, presence of casts, RBC and WBC in urine, azotemia, oliguria."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Neurotoxic, ototoxic, or nephrotoxic drugs. General anesthetics and neuromuscular blockers. Neomycin. Beta-lactam antibiotics or vancomycin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Solution for injection (IM/IV) 50 mg/mL x 2 mL (P236.32); 125 mg/mL x 2 mL (P502.84); 250 mg/mL x 2 mL (P814.07)."
          }

            "content": "Opiates & Antagonists"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Symptomatic treatment of moderate to severe acute and chronic pain."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults and adolescents &gt;12 yrs</b>: Initially 2 tabs. Additional doses may be taken at minimum 6 hrs intervals, not exceeding 8 tabs/day. <b>Moderate renal insufficiency (CrCl 10-30 mL/min)</b>: Increase dosing to 12-hrs intervals."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Acute intoxication with alcohol, hypnotic drugs, centrally acting analgesics, opioids or psychotropic drugs. Moderate hepatic failure. Severe respiratory depression. Patients with risk of consciousness disturbance due to head injury or encephalopathy; peptic ulcer or severe blood disorders; severe liver disease, renal disorder or severe renal disorder. Patients with aspirin asthma (induction of asthmatic attack caused by NSAIDs), uncontrolled epilepsy. Patients receiving MAOIs or within 2 weeks of withdrawal."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Do not withdraw abruptly. Hypersensitivity to opioids. Hepatic and renal disease. Moderate renal insufficiency (CrCl &lt;30 mL/min). Patients with biliary tract disorders, epilepsy, history of or at risk of seizure; increased intracranial pressure or head injury. Concurrent use with morphine. Patients receiving CNS depressants e.g. alcohol, opioids, anesthetics, hypnotics, phenothiazine, tranquilizers and sedatives. Drug dependence or abuse. May impair ability to drive and operate machinery. Childn &lt;12 yrs. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Anergia, fatigue, flushing, occasional chest pain, spasticity, syncope, withdrawal symptoms. Effects on the skin, circulatory, CNS and peripheral nervous, GI, psychiatric, and urinary systems."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "SSRIs, TCAs and other tricyclic compounds (e.g. cyclobenzaprine, promethazine), other opioids, MAOIs, neuroleptics, other drugs that reduce seizure threshold."
          },
          {

        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Parenteral Nutritional Products"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Parenteral nutrition for adults when oral or enteral nutrition is impossible, insufficient, or contraindicated."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Individualized dose. Max 400 mL/kg/day (equiv to 1.4 g amino acids/kg/day and 2.5 g glucose/kg/day). <b>Max infusion rate:</b> 2.9 mL/kg/hr (equiv to 0.10 g amino acids/kg/hr and 0.18 g glucose/kg/hr). <b>Max infusion time:</b> 24 hrs.           },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Inborn error of amino acid metabolism. Newborns or infants < 2 yrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with hepatic, renal, cardiac, or pulmonary disease; altered amino acid and glucose metabolism; lactic acidosis and increased serum osmolarity. Strict aseptic precautions. Do not exceed recommended infusion rate. Discontinue when signs or symptoms of anaphylactic reaction occur. Patients with DM, reduced kidney function, phenylketonuria; on controlled potassium and sodium diet. Pregnancy and lactation.",

          },

          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Antihistaminic/antiemetic - Adults and childn &ge;12 yrs</b>: 25-50 mg every 4-6 hrs. <b>Childn 6-&lt;12 yrs</b>: 12.5-25 mg every 4-6 hrs. <b>Antihistaminic - Childn 2-&lt;6 yrs</b>: 6.25 mg every 4 6 hrs. <b>Antitussive - Adults and childn &ge;12 yrs</b>: Up to 28 mg every 4 hrs. <b>Childn 6-&lt;12 yrs</b>: Up to 14 mg every 4 hrs. <b>Childn 4-&lt;6 yrs</b>: Up to 7 mg every 4 hrs. <b>Nighttime sleep aid - Adults and childn &ge;12 yrs</b>: 50 mg at bedtime."

        "content": "Fenofibrate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Fibric Acid Derivatives & Related Agents"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "To reduce LDL-C, total cholesterol, triglycerides, and apolipoprotein B, and to increase HDL-C. Management of hyperlipidemias including type IIa, IIb, III, IV, and V hyperlipoproteinemia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "200 mg once daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with severe renal impairment (CrCl < 15 mL/min) not undergoing dialysis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with severe hepatic impairment, significant liver disease, gallstones or gallbladder disorders, hypoalbuminemic states e.g. nephrotic syndrome; mild to moderate renal insufficiency; galactose intolerance, total lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Reversible elevations in serum creatinine. Monitor transaminase levels every 3 months during the first 12 months of treatment and thereafter. Risk for pancreatitis; muscle toxicity if used with another fibrate or HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor; myopathy if used with statins; cholestasis if used with raloxifene. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "GI disturbances e.g. anorexia, nausea, and gastric discomfort."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Drugs metabolized by CYP3A4, oral anticoagulants, tolbutamide and other antidiabetics, phenytoin, furosemide, bezafibrate, ciclosporin, raloxifene."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Capsule 200 mg (P23.00)."
          }

        "content": "Human rabies immunoglobulin",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Rabies Immunoglobulins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Post-exposure prophylaxis of rabies infection after exposure to scratches, bites or other injuries caused by suspected rabid animal; mucous membrane contamination with infectious tissue or saliva of suspected rabid animal; contact of mucous membranes or newly skin injury with rabies live attenuated vaccine e.g. vaccination baits."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "IM inj. <b>Rabies prophylaxis with simultaneous vaccination</b>: 20 IU/kg BW. May be administered in divided doses at different sites if a large total vol is required (&gt;2 mL for BW &le;20 kg or 5 mL for BW &gt;20 kg)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not for IV administration. Monitor patients for at least 20 mins after administration or longer term (at least 1 hr) in case of accidental IV inj. Vaccinations with live attenuated virus vaccines (e.g., rubella, mumps, and varicella vaccines) should be done at least 3 months. May interfere with some serological test for red cell allo-antibodies (e.g., Coombs’ test). May be given SC if IM is contraindicated. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Fall in BP, dyspnea, cutaneous reactions. Chills, fever, headache, malaise, nausea, vomiting, arthralgia and moderate backpain. Local pain, tenderness, or swelling."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Solution for injection (IM) 300 IU/2 mL in pre-filled syringe (P1,736.00)."

            "content": "Adults and adolescents: 1 tab daily. Dissolve in 200 mL glass of water."

          {
            "title": "Contraindications",

          },

          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/c12nuMc2lrLiM7sLB2yJNiHeeDq204IkhXkcWRRateDjfTvTcY.jpg"

        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Fenoterol HBr, ipratropium bromide monohydrate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Anticholinergic Anti-Asthmatic & COPD Agents"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Prevention and treatment of symptoms of chronic obstructive airway disorders with reversible airflow limitation, e.g. bronchial asthma and chronic bronchitis with or without emphysema."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults (including elderly) and adolescents >12 yrs - Acute episodes of bronchospasm:</b> 1 vial; 2  vials may be required in very severe cases. As needed only in bronchial asthma. Regular use in mild COPD. Use a nebulizing device with mouthpiece or well-fitting mask. Use open contents immediately.  See product insert for handling instructions."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy. Tachyarrhythmia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "For inhalation use only. Not for oral or parenteral. Do not allow product into the eyes. Patients predisposed to narrow-angle glaucoma; insufficiently controlled DM, recent MI, severe organic heart or vascular disorders, hyperthyroidism, phaeochromocytoma, or with pre-existing urinary outflow tract obstruction (e.g. prostatic hyperplasia or bladder-neck obstruction); underlying severe heart disease (e.g. IHD, arrhythmia or severe heart failure); cystic fibrosis. Increasing use of treatment beyond recommended dose for extended time. Acute, rapidly worsening dyspnea. Concomitant use with other sympathomimetic bronchodilators. May induce ocular complications, CV effects, hypokalemia. Discontinue if paradoxical bronchospasm occurs. May yield positive results in non-clinical substance abuse tests. May impair the ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn &le;12 yrs. Pregnancy (especially 1<sup>st</sup> trimester) and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Cough, dry mouth, headache, tremor, pharyngitis, nausea, dizziness, dysphonia, tachycardia,  palpitations, vomiting, increased SBP, nervousness."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Other beta-adrenergics, beta-mimetics, anticholinergics, xanthine derivatives (e.g. theophylline); beta blockers; corticosteroids, diuretics; digoxin; MAOIs, TCAs; halothane, trichloroethylene, enflurane."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Solution for inhalation 1.25 mg/500 mcg per 4 mL (P48.08)."

        "content": "Metronidazole",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Anti-protozoals"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Amebiasis, urogenital trichomoniasis, non-specific vaginitis, giardiasis. Curative treatment of medico-surgical infections due to susceptible anaerobic pathogens. Prophylaxis against infections caused by susceptible anaerobic pathogens in high-risk surgical contexts. Conversion from prophylactic to curative injectable treatment of infections due to susceptible anaerobic pathogens."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Amebiasis</b> - Adults: 1.5 g daily, in 3 divided doses; Childn: 30-40 mg/kg/day, in 3 divided doses. Treatment duration: 7 days. <b>Giardiasis</b> - Adults: 750 mg to 1 g daily; Childn 10-15 yrs: 500 mg/day; 5-10 yrs: 375 mg/day; 2-5 yrs: 250 mg/day. Treatment duration: 5 days. <b>Trichomoniasis in women (urethritis and vaginitis) and men (urethritis)</b>: 2 g as single dose or 500 mg/day in 2 divided doses for 10 days. <b>Non-specific vaginitis</b>: 500 mg twice daily for 7 days. <b>Anaerobic infections</b> - Adults: 1-1.5 g/day; Childn: 20-30 mg/kg/day. <b>Surgical chemoprophylaxis (in combination with a drug active against Enterobacteriaceae)</b>: 500 mg (adults) or 20-30 mg/kg/day (childn) every 8 hrs administered approx 48 hrs pre-op; the last dose must be at the latest 12 hrs pre-op."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with active or chronic severe peripheral & CNS diseases. Perform leukocyte count regularly. Patients with hepatic encephalopathy. Avoid alcohol consumption. May darken urine. May affect ability to drive or operate machinery. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "GI, immune system, nervous system, psychiatric, eyes, blood and lymphatic system, hepatobiliary, and skin and subcutaneous tissue disorders."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Disulfiram, alcohol, oral anticoagulants (warfarin), lithium, ciclosporin, phenytoin or phenobarbital, 5-fluorouracil, busulfan."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Oral suspension 250 mg/5 mL x 60 mL (P210.00)."
          }

  {

      "data": {
        "id": 4179,
        "brand_name": "Besartan",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/weTCWjudOkRSZPHzd72spR72b191VSj3ib2ak3vaYpQXtrwNR9.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/cNWFf6fKeooFzURiUpF2SEvgCGK4OEtrSCwIVIRYyOAps0ij3M.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/76qeWf1emU3Cnrc97jBjuChUla1WopshW5TaDd6j5kPJsrDcxD.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Losartan potassium",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Angiotensin II Receptor Blockers"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of essential HTN in adults and childn 6-18 yrs; renal disease in adults with HTN and T2DM with proteinuria &ge;0.5 g/day. Reduction in the risk of stroke in hypertensive adults with left ventricular hypertrophy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>HTN, hypertensive type II diabetics with proteinuria &ge;0.5 g/day:</b> Initial and maintenance dose of 50 mg once daily. May be increased to 100 mg once daily in the morning. <b>HF:</b> Initially 12.5 mg once daily, titrated at weekly intervals up to max 150 mg once daily. <b>Reduction in the risk of stroke in hypertensive adults with left ventricular hypertrophy:</b> Initially 50 mg once daily, added with low dose of HCTZ and/or dose is increased to 100 mg once daily. <b>Intravascular volume depletion:</b> Initially 25 once daily. <b>History of hepatic impairment:</b> Lower dose. <b>Childn 6-18 yrs with >20 to < 50 kg BW:</b> 25 mg once daily; <b>>50 kg:</b> 50 mg once daily, may be increased to max 100 mg once daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Severe hepatic impairment. Concomitant use with aliskiren-containing products in DM or renal impairment (GFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>). Pregnancy (2<sup>nd</sup> and 3<sup>rd</sup> trimesters)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with history of angioedema; recent kidney transplantation; HF and concomitant severe renal impairment, severe HF (NYHA class IV), HF and symptomatic life-threatening cardiac arrhythmias; aortic or mitral stenosis, or obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. Not recommended in primary hyperaldosteronism. Changes in renal function (e.g., renal failure) in RAAS-dependent patients (e.g., severe cardiac insufficiency or pre-existing renal dysfunction). Increased blood urea and serum creatinine in bilateral renal artery stenosis of the artery to a solitary kidney. MI or stroke in ischemic CV and cerebrovascular disease. Correct volume and/or sodium depletion and electrolyte imbalances before administration. Monitor plasma concentration of potassium and CrCl in patients with HF and CrCl 30-50 mL/min. Childn < 6 yrs; GFR < 30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>. Lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Anemia, dizziness, vertigo, orthostatic hypotension, renal impairment, renal failure, asthenia, fatigue, hyperkalemia, increased blood urea, serum creatinine, and serum potassium, hypoglycemia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Potassium-sparing diuretics, supplements and salt substitutes, ACE inhibitors, angiotensin II receptor blockers, aliskiren, TCA, antipsychotics, baclofen, amifostine, lithium, NSAIDs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 50 mg (P14.50)."
          }
        ],

        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Atorvastatin calcium",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Statins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Reduction of LDL-cholesterol, apolipoprotein B, and triglycerides and increase HDL-cholesterol in treatment of hyperlipidemia, including hypercholesterolemia and combined (mixed) hyperlipidemia (Type IIa or IIb hyperlipoproteinemias), hypertriglyceridemia (Type IV), and dysbetalipoproteinemia (Type III). Adjunct therapy in homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia with some LDL-receptor function."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Usual dose 10 to 20 mg once daily. <b>Require large LDL-cholesterol reduction:</b> Initially 40 mg daily, may be adjusted at intervals of 4 weeks up to max 80 mg daily. <b>Heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia - Childn and adolescents 10-17 yrs:</b> Initially 10 mg once daily, max 20 mg once daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Active liver disease or unexplained persistent serum transaminases elevations >3x ULN. Treated with hepatitis C antivirals glecaprevir/pibrentasvir. Women of childbearing potential not using appropriate contraceptives. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Perform liver function tests before treatment initiation and periodically thereafter and if signs or symptoms suggestive of liver injury develops. Patients with substantial amounts of alcohol consumption and/or have history of liver disease; predisposing factors to rhabdomyolysis. Administration of 80 mg in patients with prior hemorrhagic stroke or lacunar infarct. May cause myalgia, myositis, and myopathy that may progress to rhabdomyolysis. Do not measure CK levels following strenuous exercise or in any alternative cause of CK increase. Discontinue if muscular symptoms are severe and cause daily discomfort even if CK &le;5x ULN, if CK >10x ULN, or if rhabdomyolysis is diagnosed or suspected. Elderly >70 yrs.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nasopharyngitis, allergic reactions, hyperglycemia, headache, pharyngolaryngeal pain, epistaxis, constipation, flatulence, dyspepsia, nausea, diarrhea, myalgia, arthralgia, pain in extremity, muscle spasms, joint swelling, back pain."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., ciclosporin, erythromycin, telithromycin, clarithromycin, delavirdine, stiripentol, ketoconazole, voriconazole, itraconazole, posaconazole, HIV protease inhibitors, verapamil, diltiazem, amiodarone) and inducers (e.g., efavirenz, rifampin, St. John’s wort), fibric acid derivatives, boceprevir, telaprevir, elbasvir/grazoprevir, erythromycin, niacin, ezetimibe, fusidic acid, colestipol, colchicine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 20 mg (P18.00), 40 mg (P22.34)."
          }
        ],

        "brand_shot": {

          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/7EmbXtwL4Zuois5IlizcKFIysGSv46gPoYrGOZlrYOLIfFAbEa.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Carvedilol",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Beta Blockers (Antihypertensives)"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Management of hypertension (HTN) and angina pectoris. Adjunct to standard therapy in symptomatic heart failure."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>HTN - Initial dose</b>: 12.5 mg once daily, increase to 25 mg once daily after two days; <b>Alternative initial dose</b>: 6.25 mg twice daily, increase to 12.5 mg twice daily after 1-2 weeks. May be further increased at intervals of 2 weeks to 50 mg once daily or in divided doses at 2 weeks intervals; <b>Elderly</b>: 12.5 mg once daily. <b>Angina pectoris</b>: 12.5 mg twice daily, increase to 25 mg twice daily after two days. <b>Heart failure</b>: Initially 3.125 mg twice daily with food, double the dose to 6.25 mg twice daily after 2 weeks, then increase gradually to the max tolerated dose not &gt;25 mg twice daily. <b>Mild to moderate heart failure with BW &gt;85 kg</b>: 50 mg twice daily. <b>Severe heart failure or BW &lt;85 kg</b>: Max 25 mg twice daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Unstable/decompensated heart failure; liver dysfunction. Patients with 2<sup>nd</sup>- or 3<sup>rd</sup>-degree AV block (unless a permanent pacemaker is in place); severe bradycardia (&lt;50 bpm); sick sinus syndrome (including SA block); severe hypotension (systolic &lt;85 mmHg); cardiogenic shock and history of bronchospasm or asthma; metabolic acidosis; severe PAD."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Do not give to patients with bronchospasm or asthma or those with history of obstructive airways disease. 1<sup>st</sup>-degree AV block. Pheochromocytoma without concomitant alpha-adrenoceptor blocking therapy. Abrupt withdrawal may exacerbate angina. Reduced peripheral circulation can produce coldness of the extremities and may exacerbate PVD (e.g. Raynaud's syndrome). Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Heart failure, heart block, and bronchospasm; bradycardia and hypotension. Fatigue and coldness of the extremities."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "ACE inhibitors, CCBs, clonidine; aldesleukin, general anesthetics; NSAIDs; antiarrhythmics; digoxin; insulin and oral hypoglycemics; adrenaline (epinephrine); aluminum salts and bile acid-binding resins such as cholestyramine; barbiturates, rifampicin; cimetidine, erythromycin, fluvoxamine, hydralazine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 6.25 mg (P10.49), 25 mg (P15.74)."
          }
        ],

          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Non-Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Symptomatic treatment of conditions that cause inflammation or infection (viral, bacterial, or fungal) of the mouth or throat e.g., sore throat (pharyngitis), tonsillitis, oral thrush, gingivitis, periodontitis, oral ulcers, common colds, flu, and stomatitis. Oral mucositis. Protective measure in infection control against common cold, MERS, flu, pneumonia, hospital-acquired infections, and infections caused by antibiotic-resistant bacteria. Oral hygiene, before or after oral and dental surgery (e.g. tonsillectomy), and procedures. Remove plaques causing bacteria that can result in oral infection and bad breath. Degerming soak for dentures and toothbrushes."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults, childn >6 yrs:</b> Use undiluted or dilute with one part water. Rinse and gargle with 10 mL up to 4x a day for 30 secs for sore throat, oral hygiene, during outbreaks, before surgery and dental procedures; 2-3 mins each for ulcers, oral mucositis. Spit out after use. Do not swallow. For oral use only."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Radioactive iodine treatments. Concomitant use with mercury-containing products (e.g. thimerosal). Thyroid problem. Childn < 2 yrs old."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients who received radioactive iodine treatments within last 4 weeks. Allergic reactions that occur quickly. Childn 1-6 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Skin irritation, discoloration, redness, swelling, itching, dryness, small blisters. Tiredness, weakness, confusion, rapid shallow breathing, little or no urine, fluid retention, swelling of legs, ankle, and feet."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Hydrogen peroxide, silver taurolidine, octenidine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",

          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/FvtrCtrFyLMqMnUu9AVz8MgI2SIkMOWSsQ1RdPI733AlTGZGcu.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/ZsxbmOIe3biNPaQGKItUGacWPls6ipTOLjXpdcmPJvxrrE5lxD.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Metoprolol",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Beta Blockers (Antihypertensives)"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Hypertension (HTN) - Reduction of blood pressure and risk of cardiovascular and coronary mortality, including sudden death, and morbidity. Angina pectoris. Disturbance of cardiac rhythm including especially supraventricular tachycardia. Maintenance treatment after myocardial infarction (MI). Functional heart disorders with palpitations. Migraine prophylaxis. <b>25 mg tab:</b> Symptomatic mild to severe chronic heart failure and adjunct to other heart failure therapy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>HTN:</b> 50 mg once daily, could be increased to 100-200 mg once daily and/or combined with other hypertensive agents. <b>Angina pectoris:</b> 100-200 mg once daily, can be combined with other anti-anginal agents if needed. <b>Cardiac arrhythmias:</b> 100-200 mg once daily. <b>Maintenance treatment after MI:</b> 200 mg once daily. <b>Functional heart disorders with palpitations:</b> 100 mg once daily, can be increased to 200 mg. <b>Migraine prophylaxis:</b> 100-200 mg once daily. <b>Childn and adolescents >6 yrs:</b> 1 mg/kg, not exceeding 50 mg once daily. Can be increased to max daily dose 2 mg/kg/day. <b>25 mg tab - Chronic heart failure:</b> Individualized dosage. Initially 25 mg once daily during the first 2 weeks. Double the dose every 2<sup>nd</sup> weeks up to max 200 mg once daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. 2<sup>nd</sup> or 3<sup>rd</sup> degree AV block; patients with unstable decompensated cardiac heart failure (pulmonary edema, hypoperfusion or hypotension), and patients with continuous or intermittent inotropic therapy acting through beta-receptor agonism; clinically relevant sinus bradycardia, sick-sinus syndrome, cardiogenic shock; severe peripheral arterial circulatory disorder. Patients with suspected acute MI as long as the heart rate is < 45 bpm, the P-Q interval is >0.24 secs or the systolic BP is < 100 mmHg."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Do not give IV administration of verapamil-type CCBs. Patients with asthma. Risk of interfering with carbohydrate metabolism or masking hypoglycemia. May aggravate the symptoms of peripheral arterial circulatory disorders. Pheochromocytoma. Avoid abrupt withdrawal of beta-blockade is hazardous especially in high-risk patients. If there is a need to discontinue treatment, this should preferably be done gradually over at least 2 weeks when the dose is reduced by half in each step down to the final step when a whole 25 mg tab is reduced to a half-tab. The final dose should be taken for at least 4 days before discontinuation. If symptoms occur, a slower withdrawal rate is recommended. Avoid acute initiation of high-dose metoprolol to patients undergoing non-cardiac surgery. May impair ability to drive or use machines. Childn < 6 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Fatigue. Bradycardia, postural disorders (very rarely with syncope), cold hands and feet, palpitations; dizziness, headache; nausea, abdominal pain, diarrhea, constipation; Dyspnea on exertion."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Compounds metabolized by cytochrome P2D6 (e.g. antiarrhythmics, antihistamines, H<sub>2</sub>-receptor antagonists, antidepressants, antipsychotics, and COX2-inhibitors). Rifampicin, alcohol and hydralazine. Sympathetic ganglion-blocking agents, other beta-blockers (e.g. eye drops), or MAOIs. Clonidine. Verapamil and diltiazem. Antiarrhythmic agents (of the quinidine type and amiodarone). Digitalis glycoside. Inhalation anesthetics. Indomethacin or other prostaglandin synthetase inhibiting drugs. Adrenaline. Oral antidiabetics."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Controlled-release tablet 25 mg, 100 mg."
          }
        ],

        },

            "content": "For relief of clogged nose, runny nose, cough from postnasal drip, itchy and watery eyes, sneezing, headache, sore throat, body aches, and fever associated with the common cold, allergic rhinitis, sinusitis, flu, and other minor respiratory tract infections.             "content": "<b>Phenylephrine</b>: Tremor, restlessness, anxiety, insomnia/sleeplessness, nervousness, dizziness, increased BP, palpitation, arrhythmia, weakness, respiratory distress, pallor. <b>Chlorphenamine</b>: Sleepiness/drowsiness, insomnia/sleeplessness, nervousness, facial dyskinesia, faintness, headache, paresthesia, tremor, blurred vision, diplopia, visual disturbance, acute labyrinthitis, tinnitus, vertigo, chest tightness, increased or decreased BP, thickening of bronchial secretions, nasal stuffiness, wheezing, constipation, diarrhea, GI discomfort, nausea, vomiting, muscle weakness, difficulty urinating, early menses, impotence, chills, dryness of mouth, nose, and throat, irritability, sweating."

  {
    "id": 4310,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 4310,
        "brand_name": "Biomib",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/LTJrsbtvYOdRKFNVyYbcvpbA2ALzerxeENyHHGioyAf2xFOJOk.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/yYMaLol7K1SdvvhpIOARvhu9KIiurgtEI1REGN5kHJufOHQlEC.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/pAA2WGl57eO42nqYJPr8mlDIZZvqPV0Srg3jIzGJrnSSAWraLL.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Bortezomib",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Proteasome Inhibitor"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Monotherapy or in combination with pegylated liposomal doxorubicin or dexamethasone for the treatment of adults with progressive multiple myeloma who have received at least one prior therapy and who have already undergone or unsuitable for hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT). In combination with melphalan and prednisone for the treatment of adults with previously untreated multiple myeloma who are not eligible for high-dose chemotherapy with HSCT. In combination with dexamethasone, or with dexamethasone and thalidomide for the induction treatment of adults with previously untreated multiple myeloma who are eligible for high-dose chemotherapy with HSCT. In combination with rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, and prednisone for the treatment of adults with previously untreated mantle cell lymphoma who are unsuitable for HSCT."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>For the treatment of adults with progressive multiple myoma who have received at least one prior therapy - General dosing</b>: 1.3 mg/m<sup>2</sup> BSA via IV or SC twice weekly for 2 weeks (days 1, 4, 8, 11), followed by a 10-day rest period (days 12-21) in a 21-day treatment cycle. This 3-week period is considered a treatment cycle. <b>Monotherapy</b>: Two cycles of bortezomib after a complete response is confirmed; for patients responding to treatment but do not achieve complete remission: A total of 8 cycles therapy is recommended. <b>In combination with pegylated liposomal doxorubicin</b>: Follow general dosing recommendation. Recommended dose of pegylated liposomal doxorubicin: 30 mg/m<sup>2</sup> to be administered as a 1-hr IV infusion following bortezomib injection on day 4 of the treatment cycle. Up to 8 cycles of this combination therapy can be administered if patients have not progressed and can tolerate the treatment. Patients achieving a complete response can continue with the combination therapy for at least two cycles after the first evidence of complete response, even if this requires treatment for more than 8 cycles. Patients whose paraprotein levels continue to decrease after 8 cycles can still receive this combination therapy for as long as the patient can tolerate and respond with the treatment. <b>In combination with dexamethasone</b>: Follow general dosing recommendation. Dexamethasone 20 mg is administered orally at days 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 9, 11, and 12 of the bortezomib treatment cycle. Patients achieving a response or a stable disease after 4 cycles of this combination therapy may continue to be administered with the same combination for a max of 4 additional cycles. <b>For the treatment of adults with progressive multiple myeloma - In combination with melphalan and prednisone</b> - Administered IV or SC in combination with oral melphalan and oral prednisone; a 6-week period is a treatment cycle. For treatment cycles 1-4: Bortezomib 1.3 mg/m<sup>2</sup> for Day 1, 4, 8, 11, 22, 25, 29, 32, melphalan 9 mg/m<sup>2</sup> and prednisone 60 mg/m<sup>2</sup> for Day 1, 2, 3, 4. For treatment cycles 5-9: Bortezomib 1.3 mg/m<sup>2</sup> for Day 1, 8, 22, 29, melphalan 9 mg/m<sup>2</sup> and prednisone 60 mg/m<sup>2</sup> for Day 1, 2, 3, 4. Prior to initiating a treatment cycle, platelet counts (PC) should be &ge;70 x 10<sup>9</sup>/L and the absolute neutrophils count (ANC) should be &ge;1 x 10<sup>9</sup>/L; Non-hematological toxicities should have resolved to Grade 1 or baseline. <b>For previously untreated multiple myeloma patients eligible for hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (induction therapy) - In combination therapy with dexamethasone</b>: Bortezomib 1.3 mg/m<sup>2</sup> via IV or SC twice weekly for two weeks (i.e., on days 1, 4, 8, and 11), followed by a 10-day rest period (days 12-20) in a 21 days treatment cycle. This 3-week period is considered a treatment cycle. Dexamethasone 40 mg is administered orally on days 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 9, 10 and 11 of the bortezomib treatment cycle. Four treatment cycles of this combination therapy are administered. <b>In combination therapy with dexamethasone and thalidomide</b>: Bortezomib 1.3 mg/m<sup>2</sup> BSA via IV or SC twice weekly for two weeks (i.e., 1, 4, 8 and 11), followed by a 17-day rest period (days 12-28) in a 28-day treatment cycle. This four-week period is considered a treatment cycle. Dexamethasone 40 mg is orally administered on days 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 9, 10, and 11 of the bortezomib treatment cycle. Thalidomide 50 mg is orally administered daily on days 1 to 14 and if tolerated, the dose is increased to 100 mg on days 15 to 28. Thereafter, the dose may be further increased to 200 mg daily from cycle 2. Four treatment cycles of this combination are administered. It is recommended that patients with at least partial response should receive two additional cycles. When thalidomide is used, particular attention to pregnancy testing and prevention requirements is needed. Dosage adjustment for transplant eligible patients: Follow dosage adjustment guidelines described for monotherapy. <b>For patients with previously untreated mantle cell lymphoma (MCL) - Combination therapy with rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, and prednisone</b>: Bortezomib 1.3 mg/ m<sup>2</sup> via IV or SC twice weekly for two weeks (i.e., on days 1, 4, 8, and 11), followed by a 10-day rest period (days 12-21) in a 21-day treatment cycle. This 3-week period is considered a treatment cycle. It is recommended to administer 6 bortezomib treatment cycles. For patients with a response first documented at cycle 6, two additional bortezomib treatment cycles may be given. Prednisone is administered orally at 100 mg/m<sup>2</sup> on days 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 of each bortezomib treatment cycle. The medicinal products are administered on day 1 of each 3-week treatment cycle as IV infusion: rituximab at 375 mg/m<sup>2</sup>, cyclophosphamide at 750 mg/m<sup>2</sup>, doxorubicin at 50 mg/m<sup>2</sup>. Dose adjustment during treatment for patients with previously untreated MCL: Prior to initiating a new treatment cycle, PC should be &ge;100,000 cells/mcL (&ge;75,000 cells/mcL in patients with bone marrow filtration or splenic sequestration), and the ANC should be &ge;1,500 cells/mcL, hemoglobin &ge;8 g/dL, non-hematological toxicities should have resolved to Grade 1 or baseline. <b>Moderate to severe hepatic impairment</b>: Reduced starting dose of 0.7 mg/m<sup>2</sup> per injection during first treatment cycle. A subsequent dose escalation to 1 mg/m<sup>2</sup> or further dose reduction to 0.5 mg/m<sup>2</sup> may be considered, depending on patient’s tolerability. At least 72 hrs should elapse between consecutive doses of bortezomib."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to bortezomib, boron, mannitol, or any component in the product. Intrathecal administration. Patients with acute diffuse infiltrative pulmonary and pericardial disease. Pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Has a narrow therapeutic window. Risk for hematologic toxicities (neutropenia, anemia, thrombocytopenia); posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES); progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy; peripheral and autonomic neuropathy; dehydration; herpes zoster reactivation. Patients with moderate to severe thrombocytopenia; pulmonary disorders; renal and hepatic impairment. Patients at risk for bleeding, infections, CHF, cardiogenic shock, QT-prolongation. May impair ability to drive and use machines. Childn &lt;18 yrs. Lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nausea, diarrhea, constipation, vomiting, fatigue, asthenia, pyrexia, headache, paresthesia, decreased appetite, dyspnea, rash, herpes zoster, myalgia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. ketoconazole, ritonavir). CYP3A4 inducers (e.g. rifampicin, St. John’s wort, carbamazepine, phenytoin, phenobarbital. Oral antidiabetic agents. Melphalan-prednisone. Drugs associated with peripheral neuropathy or decrease in BP (e.g. amiodarone, anti-viral, INH, nitrofurantoin, statins)."
          },

          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Initial treatment of advanced epithelial ovarian cancer in established combinations with other approved chemotherapeutic agents. Palliative treatment of epithelial ovarian cancer, refractory to standard chemotherapy with or without cisplatin. Treatment of small cell lung carcinoma (SCLC)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Monotherapy - Initial dosing</b> - Previously treated recurrent ovarian carcinoma: 360 mg/m<sup>2</sup>. Previously treated or have poor performance status: 300-320 mg/m<sup>2</sup>. Previously untreated: 400 mg/m<sup>2</sup>. Administer by IV infusion over 15-60 mins on day 1, every 4 weeks. <b>Combination therapy with cyclophosphamide - Initial dosing</b> - Treatment of advanced ovarian cancer for previously untreated patients: 300 mg/m<sup>2</sup>; cyclophosphamide dose: 600 mg/m<sup>2</sup>. Administer by IV infusion over 15-60 mins on day 1, every 4 weeks for 6 cycles. <b>Dosage adjustments based on hematologic nadir from prior course</b> - Platelets &gt;100,000 cells/m<sup>2</sup> and neutrophils &gt;2,000 cells/m<sup>2</sup>: 125%. Platelets &gt;50,000-100,000 cells/m<sup>2</sup> and neutrophils 500-2,000 cells/m<sup>2</sup>: 100% from prior course. Platelets &lt;50,000 cells/m<sup>2</sup> and neutrophils &lt;500 cells/m<sup>2</sup>: 75% from prior course. <b>Renal impairment</b> - CrCl 41-59 mL/min: 250 mg/m<sup>2</sup>; 16-40 mL/min: 200 mg/m<sup>2</sup>. Do not repeat intermittent courses until neutrophil count is at least 2,000 cells/mm<sup>3</sup> and platelet count is at least 100,000 cells/mm<sup>3</sup>."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to carboplatin, cisplatin or other platinum-containing compounds, mannitol. Pre-existing severe renal impairment (CrCl &lt;30 mL/min) without risk-benefit ratio assessment; severe myelosuppression; significant bleeding, bleeding tumors. Concomitant use with yellow fever vaccine. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Do not use needles or IV sets containing aluminum parts. Patients at risk for myelosuppression.         "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Beta Blockers (Antihypertensives)"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of hypertension (HTN), stable chronic angina, and stable chronic heart failure (CHF) with reduced systolic left ventricular function in adults in ACE inhibitors, and diuretics, and optionally cardiac glycoside."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Treatment of HTN and chronic stable angina pectoris</b>: Initially 5 mg/day. Usual dose 10 mg/day. Max 20 mg/day. <b>Severe renal impairment (CrCl &lt;20 mL/min)</b>: Max 10 mg/day. <b>Treatment of stable CHF</b>: Start up titration with 1.25 mg/day for 1 week; if well-tolerated, increase to 2.5 mg/day for another week; if well-tolerated, increase to 3.75 mg/day for another week; if well-tolerated, increase to 5 mg/day for another 4 weeks; if well-tolerated, increase 7.5 mg/day for further 4 weeks; if well-tolerated, increase to 10 mg/day for maintenance therapy. Max 10 mg/day. Take in the morning with food. Do not chew."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. CHF patients with: acute heart failure or during episodes of heart decompensation requiring IV inotropic therapy, cardiogenic shock 2<sup>nd</sup>or 3<sup>rd</sup> degree AV block (without pacemaker); sick sinus syndrome, SA block, symptomatic bradycardia/hypotension, severe bronchial asthma or severe COPD, late stages of PAOD and Raynaud’s syndrome, untreated pheochromocytoma, metabolic acidosis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with HTN or angina pectoris and accompanying heart failure. DM, strict fasting ongoing desensitization therapy, 1<sup>st</sup> degree AV block, Prinzmetal angina, PAOD, ongoing desensitization or general anesthesia, bronchial asthma or other COPD, psoriasis or history of psoriasis, pheochromocytoma. May mask symptoms of thyrotoxicosis and hypoglycemia. Avoid abrupt withdrawal. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Dizziness, headache; GI complaints (e.g. nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation). Feeling of coldness or numbness in the extremities, hypotension; fatigue."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Class I antiarrhythmic drugs e.g. quinidine, disopyramide, lidocaine, flecainide, propafenone. calcium antagonist e.g. felodipine, amlodipine; class III antiarrhythmic drugs e.g. amiodarone; centrally acting antihypertensives e.g. clonidine, methyldopa, moxonidine, rilmenidine; topical beta-blockers e.g. eye drops for glaucoma treatment; parasympathetic drugs; insulin and oral antidiabetic drugs; anesthetic agents; digitalis glycosides; NSAIDs; beta sympathomimetic drugs e.g. isoprenaline, dobutamine; sympathomimetics e.g. noradrenaline, adrenaline; TCA, barbiturates, phenothiazines; mefloquine, MAOIs (except MAO-B inhibitors), rifampicin, and ergotamine derivatives."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 2.5 mg (P18.00), 5 mg (P26.00)."
          }

        "id": 4983,
        "brand_name": "Boramir",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/9knFVOS9eKNVyF8l6ajQnWy5HtXfcLZCTfd8DoZWI66GQYcju9.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/ddWBx2TGcYki3Aq8qt1BsfkIGCxULnHXYHx4JUJhDgyDbQsTZl.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/ETqq3kfKnoZHvRVbFoDieaDsH0tLSE0CpjZ1NYtsRrFk7QXUpF.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Bortezomib",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Proteasome Inhibitor"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Monotherapy or in combination with pegylated liposomal doxorubicin or dexamethasone for the treatment of adult patients with progressive multiple myeloma who have received at least 1 prior therapy and who have undergone or are unsuitable for hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. In combination with melphalan and prednisone indicated for the treatment of adult patients with previously untreated multiple myeloma who are not eligible for high-dose chemotherapy with hematopoietic stem cell transplantation.  In combination with dexamethasone, or with dexamethasone and thalidomide indicated for the induction treatment of adult patients with previously untreated multiple myeloma who are eligible for high-dose chemotherapy with hematopoietic stem cell transplantation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "IV/SC. Administered as a 3-5 secs IV bolus through a peripheral or central IV catheter followed by a flush with NaCl 9 mg/mL (0.9%) soln for inj. At least 72 hrs should elapse between consecutive doses. <b>Monotherapy:</b> 1.3 mg/m<sup>2</sup> BSA twice weekly for 2 weeks on days 1, 4, 8 and 11 in a 21-day treatment cycle. After confirmation of complete response: 2 cycles. Patients who do not achieve a complete remission receive a total of 8 cycles. At least 72 hours should elapse between consecutive doses. <b>Dose adjustment during treatment and re-initiation of treatment for monotherapy:</b> Re-initiated at 25% reduced dose (1.3 mg/m<sup>2</sup> reduced to 1.5 mg/m<sup>2</sup>; 1.0 mg/m<sup>2</sup> reduced to 0.7 mg/m<sup>2</sup>). <b>Combination therapy with pegylated liposomal doxorubicin:</b> 1.3 mg/m<sup>2</sup> BSA twice weekly for 2 weeks on days 1, 4, 8, and 11 in a 21-day treatment cycle. At least 72 hrs should elapse between consecutive doses. Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin is administered 30 mg/m<sup>2</sup> on day 4 of treatment cycle as 1-hr IV infusion administered after the bortezomib inj. May be administer up to 8 cycles as long as patients have not progressed and tolerate the treatment. <b>Combination with dexamethasone:</b> 1.3 mg/m<sup>2</sup> BSA twice weekly for 2 weeks on days 1, 4, 8, and 11 in a 21-day treatment. At least 72 hrs should elapse between consecutive doses. Dexamethasone is administered orally at 20 days on days 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 9, 11, and 12 of the bortezomib treatment cycle, patients achieving a response or a stable disease after 4 cycles of this combination therapy can continue to receive the same combination for a maximum of 4 additional cycles. <b>Combination therapy with melphalan and prednisone:</b> 6-week period treatment cycle. Cycles 1-4: Bortezomib administered twice weekly on days 1, 4, 8, 11, 22, 25, 29, and 32. Cycles 5-9: Bortezomib is administered once weekly on days 1, 8, 22 and 29. At least 72 hrs elapse between consecutive doses of Bortezomib. Melphan and prednisone both given orally on days 1, 2, 3 and 4 of the 1<sup>st</sup> week of each bortezomib treatment cycle. <b>Untreated multiple myeloma patients eligible for hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (induction therapy) – Combination therapy with dexamethasone:</b> 1.3 mg/m<sup>2</sup>  BSA twice weekly for 2 weeks on days 1, 4, 8, and 11 in 21-day treatment cycle. At least 72 hrs should elapse between consecutive doses + dexamethasone 40 mg orally on days 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 9, 10 and 11 of bortezomib treatment cycle for 4 treatment cycles; <b>Combination therapy with dexamethasone and thalidomide:</b> 1.3 mg/m<sup>2</sup> BSA twice weekly for 2 weeks on days 1, 4, 8, and 11 in a 28-day treatment cycle. At least 72 hrs should elapse between consecutive doses of bortezomib + dexamethasone 40 mg orally on days 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 9, 10 and 11 of bortezomib treatment cycle + thalidomide 50 mg orally on days 1-14 may be increased to 100 mg on days 15-28, may further increased to 200 mg daily from cycle 2 if tolerated. <b>Hepatic impairment (moderate and severe):</b> 0.7 mg/m<sup>2</sup> in the 1st treatment cycle. Consider dose escalation to 1.0 mg/m<sup>2</sup> or further dose reduction to 0.5 mg/m<sup>2</sup> in subsequent cycles based on patient’s tolerability."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to active substance, boron. Acute diffuse infiltrative pulmonary and pericardial disease."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Should not be administered intrathecally. Monitor patients who experience constipation. Hematological toxicity, HZV virus reactivation, HBV reactivation and infection, progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy, peripheral neuropathy, seizures, hypotension, posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome, heart failure, ECG investigations, pulmonary disorders, renal, and hepatic impairment, tumor lysis syndrome. Childn. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nausea, diarrhea, constipation, vomiting, fatigue, pyrexia, thrombocytopenia, anemia, neutropenia, peripheral neuropathy, headache, paresthesia, decreased appetite, dyspnea, rash, herpes zosters, myalgia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Potent CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. ketoconazole, ritonavir). Strong CYP3A4 inducers (e.g. rifampicin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, phenobarbital, St. John’s Wort)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Lyophilized powder for soln for inj 3.5 mg (IV/SC) (P12,000.00)."
          }
        ],

        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Bortezomib",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Proteasome Inhibitor"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of patients with multiple myeloma or mantle cell lymphoma (MCL) who have received at least 1 prior therapy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "IV/SC. Initially 1.3 mg/m<sup>2</sup> as a 3-5 secs IV bolus at a concentration of 1 mg/mL or SC at 2.5 mg/mL. Administer within 8 hrs of preparation. Prior to initiation of any cycle, platelet count of at least 70 x 10<sup>9</sup>/L and ANC of at least 1.0 x 10<sup>9</sup>/L. <b>Previously untreated multiple myeloma (in combination with oral melphalan and prednisone):</b> Administered for nine 6-week treatment cycles. <b>Cycles 1-4:</b> 2x weekly on days 1, 4, 8, 11, 22, 25, 29, and 32; <b>Cycles 5-9:</b> Once weekly on days 1, 8, 22, and 29. <b>Relapsed multiple myeloma and MCL:</b> 2x weekly for 2 weeks on days 1, 4, 8, and 11, followed by a 10-day rest period (days 12-21). <b>Extended therapy of >8 cycles:</b> Once weekly for 4 weeks (days 1, 8, 15, and 22), followed by a 13-day rest period (days 23-35). At least 72 hrs should elapse between consecutive doses. <b>Moderate or severe hepatic impairment:</b> Reduce to 0.7 mg/m<sup>2</sup> in cycle 1, increased to 1 mg/m<sup>2</sup> or further reduced to 0.5 mg/m<sup>2</sup> based on patient tolerability. See complete product insert for dose modifications during toxicity and preparation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to bortezomib, boron, or mannitol. Not suitable for intrathecal administration."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with numbness, pain or burning feet or hands or signs of severe neuropathy; history of syncope, dehydration, receiving drugs associated with hypotension; risk factors or existing heart disease; hepatic impairment; high tumor burden; diabetes. May induce peripheral neuropathy (predominantly sensory); acute development or exacerbation of CHF, new onset of decreased LVEF; ARDS, acute diffuse infiltrative pulmonary diseases of unknown etiology, pulmonary HTN; GI toxicities; thrombocytopenia/neutropenia; GI and intracerebral hemorrhage; JC virus infection; tumor lysis syndrome; hepatotoxicity; hypoglycemia or hyperglycemia in receiving oral hypoglycemics. Monitor CBC during treatment, platelets prior to each dose, and blood glucose levels. Discontinue treatment when posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome and progressive multifocal encephalopathy develops. Childn. Elderly. Women of childbearing potential. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category D.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
