          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/3Fz6RLwNAhWfZyyCcqEmpiOR8KIT3mw93W7HABzvowRWyB0IXX.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Bortezomib",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Proteasome Inhibitor"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Monotherapy or in combination with pegylated liposomal doxorubicin or dexamethasone for the treatment of adults with progressive multiple myeloma who have received at least 1 prior therapy and have undergone or are unsuitable for hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. In combination with melphalan and prednisone for the treatment of adults with previously untreated multiple myeloma who are not eligible for high-dose chemotherapy with hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. In combination with dexamethasone and thalidone for the induction treatment of adults with previously untreated multiple myeloma who are eligible for high-dose chemotherapy with hematopoietic stem cell transplantation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "IV/SC. <b>Progressive multiple myeloma (patients who have received at least 1 prior therapy)</b> - <b>Monotherapy:</b> 1.3 mg/m<sup>2</sup> twice weekly for 2 weeks on days 1, 4, 8 and 11 in a 21-day treatment cycle. After confirmation of complete response: 2 cycles. Patients who do not achieve a complete remission: Receive a total of 8 cycles. At least 72 hrs should relapse between consecutive doses. Adjust dose if toxicity develops. <b>Combination with pegylated liposomal doxorubicin:</b> 1.3 mg/m<sup>2</sup> BSA twice weekly for 2 weeks on days 1, 4, 8, and 11 in a 21-day treatment cycle. At least 72 hrs should elapse between consecutive doses. Pegylated liposomal doxorubicin 30 mg/m<sup>2</sup> on day 4 of treatment cycle as 1-hr IV infusion after bortezomib injection. May administer up to 8 cycles as long as patient has not progressed and tolerate treatment; <b>Combination with dexamethasone:</b> 1.3 mg/m<sup>2</sup> BSA twice weekly for 2 weeks on days 1, 4, 8, and 11 in a 21-day treatment cycle. At least 72 hrs should elapse between consecutive doses. Dexamethasone 20 mg orally on days 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 9, 11, and 12 of the bortezomib for injection treatment cycle, patients achieving a response or a stable disease after 4 cycles of this combination therapy can continue to receive the same combination for max 4 additional cycles. <b>Previously untreated multiple myeloma patients not eligible for hematopoietic stem cell transplantation</b> - <b>Combination with melphalan and prednisone:</b> 6-week period treatment cycle. Cycles 1-4: Bortezomib administered twice weekly on days 1, 4, 8, 11, 22, 25, 29, and 32. Cycles 5-9: Bortezomib administered once weekly on days 1, 8, 22 and 29. At least 72 hrs should elapse between consecutive doses of bortezomib injection. Melphalan and prednisone orally on days 1, 2, 3 and 4 of the 1<sup>st</sup> week of each bortezomib injection treatment cycle. <b>Previously untreated multiple myeloma patients eligible for hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (induction therapy)</b> - <b>Combination therapy with dexamethasone:</b> Bortezomib 1.3 mg/m<sup>2</sup> BSA twice weekly for 2 weeks on days 1, 4, 8, and 11 in a 21-day treatment cycle. At least 72 hrs should elapse between consecutive doses + dexamethasone 40 mg orally on days 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 9, 10, and 11 of the bortezomib injection treatment cycle for 4 treatment cycles; <b>Combination therapy with dexamethasone and thalidomide:</b> Bortezomib 1.3 mg/m<sup>2</sup> BSA twice weekly for 2 weeks on days 1, 4, 8, and 11 in a 28-day treatment cycle. At least 72 hrs should elapse between consecutive doses of bortezomib injection + dexamethasone 40 mg orally on days 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 9, 10, and 11 of the bortezomib injection treatment cycle + thalidomide 50 mg orally daily on days 1-14, may be increased to 100 mg on days 15-28, and may be further increased to 200 mg daily from cycle 2 as tolerated. <b>Hepatic impairment (moderate or severe):</b> 0.7 mg/m<sup>2</sup>/injection on 1<sup>st</sup> treatment cycle and subsequent escalation to 1 mg/m<sup>2</sup> or further dose reduction to 0.5 mg/m<sup>2</sup>."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Acute diffuse infiltrative pulmonary and pericardial disease."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Should not be administered intrathecally. GI and hematological toxicity, HZV reactivation, progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy, peripheral neuropathy, seizures, hypotension, posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome, heart failure, ECG investigations, pulmonary disorders, renal and hepatic impairment, tumor lysis syndrome. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Thrombocytopenia, neutropenia, anemia, leukopenia, lymphopenia. Herpes zoster, pneumonia, herpes simplex, fungal infection. Decreased appetite, dehydration, hypokalemia, hyponatremia, abnormal blood glucose, hypocalcemia, enzyme abnormality. Mood disorders and disturbances, anxiety, sleep disorders and disturbances. Neuropathies, peripheral sensory neuropathy, dysesthesia, neuralgia. Motor neuropathy, loss of consciousness, dizziness, dysgeusia, lethargy, headache. Eye hemorrhage, eyelid infection, eye inflammation, dysacu phlebitis, flushing, hematoma."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Ketoconazole, ritonavir, rifampicin, omeprazole, carbamazepine, phenytoin, phenobarbital, St. John's Wort, oral hypoglycemics."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Powder for solution for injection (IV/SC) 3.5 mg."
          }

          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Rinse mouth with water after inhaling dose, do not swallow. Avoid abrupt discontinuation. Not for acute episodes of bronchospasm i.e. as a rescue therapy. May induce paradoxical bronchospasm, CV effects (e.g. cardiac arrhythmias), systemic corticosteroid effects (e.g. Cushing's syndrome, Cushingoid features, adrenal suppression, decrease in bone mineral density, cataract, glaucoma), visual disturbances, pneumonia in COPD patients, hypokalemia (especially in patients with severe COPD), increase in plasma glucose.           "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/LvZTA7SVzKOdnmXH3H087SR8T7JCVXWewBCdmwr8tZvOorLWpv.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/bKXnXc5VC88fgLiaTo0cEasFz4r5bSI1hnHITRp7L0KQMNebis.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/ae5OM0Y6SgsDLa4r2grKL8phWmY18Lbb2C5Qk5jtr6zYUwKXak.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Sugammadex sodium",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Anesthetic Adjuvants"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Reversal of neuromuscular blockade induced by rocuronium or vecuronium. <b>Childn and adolescents:</b> Only recommended for routine reversal of rocuronium-induced blockade."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Routine reversal:</b> 4 mg/kg if recovery has reached at least 1-2 post-tetanic counts (PTC); 2 mg/kg if spontaneous recovery has occurred up to the reappearance of T<sub>2</sub> following rocuronium or vecuronium-induced blockade. <b>Immediate reversal of rocuronium-induced blockade:</b> 16 mg/kg, administered 3 mins after bolus dose of rocuronium bromide 1.2 mg/kg. All doses administered as single IV bolus injection, given rapidly within 10 secs. <b>Routine reversal - Childn and adolescent >2 yrs:</b> 4 mg/kg if recovery peaked 1-2 PTC; 2 mg/kg or at reappearance of T<sub>2</sub>. <b>Re-administration of rocuronium or vecuronium after sugammadex:</b> 2 mg/kg or 4 mg/kg sugammadex at routine reversal required at least 5 mins waiting time for 1.2 mg/kg rocuronium; 2 mg/kg or 4 mg/kg sugammadex at routine reversal requires at least 4 hrs waiting for 0.6 mg/kg rocuronium or 0.1 mg/kg vecuronium to be administered. 16 mg/kg sugammadex at immediate reversal requires at least 24 hrs waiting time for 0.6 mg/kg rocuronium or 0.1 mg/kg vecuronium to be administered."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Severe renal impairment, including those requiring dialysis (CrCl < 30 mL/min). Reversal of block induced by nonsteroidal neuromuscular blocking agents and steroidal neuromuscular blocking agents other than rocuronium and vecuronium. Immediate reversal in childn and adolescents. Infants."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Monitor respiratory function during recovery. Monitor coagulation parameters in patients with known coagulopathies or taking anticoagulants. Recurrence of neuromuscular blockade. If rocuronium re-administration is required, 24-hr waiting time is recommended. Occurrence of light anesthesia, in rare instances marked bradycardia. Use in ICU. Not to be used for reversal of block induced by nonsteroidal neuromuscular blockers (e.g. succinylcholine, benzylisoquinolinium compounds) other than rocuronium. Severe renal impairment. Delayed recovery time in CV disease, elderly, or edematous state. Hepatic impairment. Patients on controlled sodium diet. History of pulmonary complications. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Airway complications (e.g. bucking against the endotracheal tube, coughing, mild bucking, arousal reaction, coughing, contra breath). Anesthetic complications (e.g. limb or body movement, coughing, grimacing, or sucking on the endotracheal tube). Procedural complications (e.g. coughing, tachycardia, bradycardia, movement, and increased heart rate). Recurrence of neuromuscular blockade. Hypersensitivity reactions (e.g. flushing, urticaria, erythematous rash, hypotension, tachycardia, swelling of tongue or pharynx, bronchospasm, pulmonary obstructive events)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Toremifene, flucloxacillin, fusidic acid, hormonal contraceptives."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Solution for injection (IV) 100 mg/mL x 2 mL (P6,108.90/vial)."
          }
        ],

        "id": 1198,

        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/jLGBXUJo0OtwNeM1MXVGeDNMQ7gFpd4pIpVYrHLHXcJ13eqoxT.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/XGReEk53w7gpG1OyPf0faYeZz6B6LyKTRe3otyS2AnQy8LNbgu.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/xaBWkFZPU0UiMXcVvYLN75M2N5e8cf19gKVBBiWhSLBGER2jhF.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Ticagrelor",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Antiplatelets"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "<b>60 mg:</b> Prevention of thrombotic events (cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction (MI), and stroke) in patients with history of MI (&ge;1 yr ago), high risk of developing a thrombotic event; coronary artery disease (CAD) and type 2 diabetes mellitus (DM) who have undergone percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). <b>90 mg:</b> Prevention of thrombotic events in patients with acute coronary syndromes (ACS) (unstable angina, ST-elevation myocardial infarction [STEMI]) including patients managed medically and with PCI or coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). Prevention of stroke in patients with acute ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack (TIA)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>History of MI (&ge;1 yr ago) and CAD with type 2 DM (have undergone PCI):</b> 60 mg 2x daily. Long-term treatment is recommended. <b>ACS:</b> Initially 180 mg (2 tabs of 90 mg) once daily, then 90 mg 2x daily for &ge;1 yr unless discontinued. After 1 yr, continue with 60 mg 2x daily without interruption. <b>Acute ischemic stroke or TIA:</b> Initially 180 mg (2 tabs of 90 mg) once daily, then 90 mg 2x daily for 30 days. Use with maintenance dose of aspirin 75-150 mg daily for ACS, acute ischemic stroke, or TIA. 60 mg 2x daily may be started regardless of previous antiplatelet regimen and if lapse in therapy occurred or not. Discontinue current antiplatelet therapy before initiating treatment with low-dose aspirin at the next scheduled dose. <b>Switching from other antiplatelet:</b> Administer first dose 24 hrs after last dose of other antiplatelet. Tabs may be crushed, mixed in half a glass of water, and drunk immediately for patients unable to swallow tabs whole. Mixture can also be administered via a nasogastric tube."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Active pathological bleeding. History of intracranial hemorrhage. Severe hepatic impairment."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with moderate or severe hepatic impairment; increased risk of bleeding (e.g. with propensity to bleed, co-administration with drugs that increase risk of bleeding (e.g. NSAIDs, oral anticoagulants, and/or fibrinolytics) within 24 hrs of treatment; therapy of >1 yr in patients with prior ischemic stroke; increased risk of bradycardic events (e.g. patients without peacemaker who have sick sinus syndrome, 2<sup>nd</sup> or 3<sup>rd</sup> degree of AV block, bradycardic-related syncope, ACS, where ischemia and concomitant drugs reducing heart rate or affecting cardiac conduction). May induce bradyarrhythmic events; dyspnea; central sleep apnea (e.g. Cheyne-Stokes respiration); thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura; false negative results in platelet function test for heparin-induced thrombocytopenia. Premature discontinuation can increase risk of CV death, MI, or stroke due to underlying disease. Platelet transfusion and desmopressin are not effective in managing bleeding. Antifibrinolytic (e.g. aminocaproic acid or tranexamic acid) and/or recombinant factor VIIa therapy may augment hemostasis. Avoid co-administration with >300 mg aspirin or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. ketoconazole, clarithromycin, nefazodone, ritonavir, atazanavir). Discontinue 5 days prior to elective surgery where antiplatelet effect is not desired. Childn < 18 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Blood disorder bleedings; hyperuricemia; dyspnea; gout; dizziness, syncope; vertigo; hypotension; respiratory system bleedings; GI hemorrhage, diarrhea, nausea; subcutaneous or dermal bleedings, pruritus; urinary tract bleeding; increased blood creatinine; post-procedural hemorrhage, traumatic bleedings."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. ketoconazole, clarithromycin, nefazodone, ritonavir, atazanavir), CYP3A inducers (e.g. rifampin, phenytoin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital), cyclosporin, morphine, digoxin. Platelet function test for HIT."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated 60 mg (P80.00), 90 mg (P84.00)."
          }
        ],

          "name": "AstraZeneca Pharmaceuticals (Phils.), Inc."
        },

  {
    "id": 4994,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 4994,
        "brand_name": "Budesma",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/A6xLgneH25nD4oHMh9dVcyt5I03uYK9RvRK5VnRMsE2fsve3jq.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/WSkWxtjOxXCE95dl7CjoTezWUXNsurDoi9heavHEV3GcWfZlRh.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/qOS3Qd1qnoqUHWdfKKUDoq2YJjf3n1ZbXvR6pxBx4KAHwWrZWM.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Budesonide",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Inhaled Corticosteroids"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Management of bronchial asthma; seasonal allergic and allergic/non-allergic perennial rhinitis. Treatment and prevention of nasal polyps after polypectomy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Individualized dosage. <b>Severe asthma:</b> Divide total daily dose to be taken twice daily; <b>Elderly and adults:</b> 200-1,600 mcg daily as initial treatment, for severe asthma, and while reducing or discontinuing oral glucocorticoids; <b>Childn >12 yrs:</b> 200-800 mcg daily for less severe cases, may be increased to max 1,600 mcg daily during periods of severe asthma; <b>&le;12 yrs:</b> 200-800 mcg daily, may be increased to max 800 mcg daily during periods of severe asthma. <b>Mild to moderate asthma - Elderly, adults, childn >12 yrs:</b> 200-400 mcg for patients who have not previously received inhaled glucocorticoids. Max 800 mcg twice daily for patients already controlled on inhaled steroids; <b>Childn &le;12 yrs:</b> 200-400 mcg twice daily. Transfer patient to once daily dose taken at the same time each evening with same equiv total daily dose. <b>Increased frequency of bronchodilator use or persistent respiratory symptoms:</b> Administer dose twice daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Primary treatment of status asthmaticus or other acute episodes/exacerbations of asthma or in patients with moderate to severe bronchiectasis. Untreated active or quiescent pulmonary TB and untreated fungal, bacterial, or systemic viral infections."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not a treatment for acute asthmatic attack. Patients with excessive mucus secretion, on alternate-day prednisone regimens, hypothyroidism, cirrhosis. Concomitant aspirin in hypoprothrombinemia. Advise patient to rinse their mouth with water and spit out or brush their teeth after inhalation. May increase susceptibility to infections (e.g., Chickenpox, measles); risk of adrenal insufficiency and unmasking of allergic conditions when patients are transferred from systemic to inhalation therapy; pharyngeal and laryngeal candidiasis; pulmonary infiltrates with eosinophils. Immediately resume previously effective dosages of systemic steroids during periods of stress or severe asthmatic attack in patients withdrawn from systemic corticosteroids. Perform routine tests of hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal-axis (HPA) function and hematological status periodically during long-term therapy. Discontinue slowly if systemic effects occur. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category B. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Ocular complications, reduced bone density, suppression of HPA responsiveness to stress, inhibition of growth velocity in childn, exacerbation of glaucoma, osteoporosis, fractures."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Systemic steroids, aspirin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Metered dose inhalation 200 mcg (P750.00)."
          }
        ],
        "company": {
          "id": 1345,

        },

          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Non-Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of gastrointestinal (GI) spasm, spasm and dyskinesia of biliary system, and genitourinary spasm."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Adults and childn >6 yrs: 1-2 tabs 3-5x daily. Swallow whole with adequate fluid."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with myasthenia gravis, mechanical stenosis in the GIT, paralytic or obstructive ileus, megacolon."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients prone to narrow-angle glaucoma; with intestinal or urinary outlet obstructions, tachyarrhythmia; fructose intolerance. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Anaphylactic shock and reactions, dyspnea, skin reactions (e.g. urticaria, rash, erythema, pruritus); tachycardia, GI disorders, dry mouth; dyshidrosis; urinary retention."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "TCAs, tetracyclic antidepressants, antihistamines, antipsychotics, quinidine, amantadine, disopyramide, other anticholinergics (e.g. tiotropium, ipratropium, atropine-like compounds). Dopamine antagonists (e.g. metoclopramide). Beta-adrenergic drugs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 10 mg (P34.00)."

        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Spasmolytics/Antispasmodics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Non-Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Relief of pain of stronger abdominal cramps including menstrual cramps and urinary tract spasms."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Adults: 1-2 tabs thrice daily for &le;3 days. Max 6 tabs/day. Swallow whole; do not chew."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with myasthenia gravis, mechanical stenosis in GIT, paralytical or obstructive ileus, megacolon, severe hepatocellular insufficiency (Child-Pugh C)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Should not be taken for >3 days. Patients with G6PD deficiency, hepatic (e.g. due to chronic alcohol abuse, hepatitis) and renal impairment, Gilbert’s syndrome, hepatocellular insufficiency (Child-Pugh A/B); prone to narrow-angle glaucoma, intestinal or urinary outlet obstructions, tachyarrhythmia; on a controlled sodium diet. Childn < 10 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Pancytopenia, agranulocytosis, thrombocytopenia, leukopenia; skin reactions, abnormal sweating, pruritus, urticaria, nausea, erythema, decreased BP including shock, anaphylactic shock and reactions, drug eruption, dyspnea, angioedema, rash, exanthema; tachycardia; bronchospasms; dry mouth; increased transaminases; urinary retention."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Hypnotics and antiepileptics (e.g. glutethimide, phenobarbital, phenytoin, carbamazepine), rifampicin; potentially hepatotoxic substances and alcohol; TCAs, tetracyclic antidepressants, antihistamines, antipsychotics, quinidine, amantadine, disopyramide, other anticholinergics (e.g. tiotropium, ipratropium, atropine-like compounds); dopamine antagonists (e.g. metoclopramide); beta-adrenergic drugs. <b>Paracetamol:</b> Oral anticoagulants; zidovudine; probenecid; cholestyramine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 10 mg/500 mg (P41.00)."
          }

    "id": 4578,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 4578,
        "brand_name": "Caliberi",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/nuZIYG6X6cGohN7l0WvkW8ALc6euY6LNJvvjCMqpo3AVfqiEd8.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/NAfcUXmLPNhQ8aBWUfALXUT7o0W9LxJYk2ENJ5rDLm7qEldpU0.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/5slpwxz5X68Dz7T0koHy67COtAmLCcD6q85cNNU7o8BcyrpgoM.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Tadalafil",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Drugs Used in Erectile Dysfunction"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Management of benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), erectile dysfunction, and pulmonary hypertension (HTN)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>BPH:</b> 5 mg once daily; With finasteride: 5 mg once daily for up to 26 weeks. <b>Erectile dysfunction:</b> 2.5 mg once daily, may increase to 5 mg once daily or 10 mg prior to sexual activity, may increase to 20 mg or decrease to 5 mg depending on efficacy and tolerability. Max frequency is once daily. <b>Pulmonary HTN:</b> 40 mg once daily with or without food. <b>Hepatic impairment</b> - Mild to moderate (Child-Pugh Class A or B): Max 10 mg. <b>Renal impairment</b> - Moderate (CrCl 31-50 mL/min): Initially 5 mg not more than once daily. Max 10 mg in 48 hrs. <b>Patients taking potent CYP3A4 inhibitors:</b> Max 10 mg once every 72 hrs when used as needed or max 2.5 mg when used regularly. Film should be placed on the tongue and dissolved."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients using nitrates. Concomitant administration with guanylate cyclase stimulator (e.g. riociguat)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with underlying CV disease, severely impaired autonomic control of BP or left ventricular outflow obstruction (e.g. aortic stenosis, idiopathic hypertrophic subaortic stenosis), veno-occlusive disease, angina occurring during sexual intercourse or unstable angina, uncontrolled arrhythmias, hypotension (BP &lt;90/50 mmHg), uncontrolled HTN, heart failure (NYHA Class &ge;2) in the last 6 months, or MI within the last 90 days; bleeding disorders or active peptic ulceration; hereditary degenerative retinal disorders (e.g. retinitis pigmentosa); conditions that predispose to priapism (e.g. sickle cell anemia, multiple myeloma, leukemia) or with anatomical deformation of penis (e.g. angulation, cavernosal fibrosis, or Peyronie’s disease). Severe hepatic (Child-Pugh Class C) and renal impairment (CrCl &lt;30 mL/min or on hemodialysis). Stroke within the last 6 months. Discontinue when sudden vision or hearing loss occurs. Concomitant use with ritonavir, potent CYP3A inhibitors or inducers, other PDE5 inhibitors, and alpha-blockers.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Flushing, hypersensitivity reactions, rash; indigestion, nausea, dyspepsia, abdominal pain, vomiting, GERD; backache, myalgia; headache, dizziness; nasopharyngitis, RTI, nasal congestion, dyspnea, epistaxis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Nitrates, alpha-blockers, antihypertensives (e.g. amlodipine, ARBs, bendrofluazide, enalapril, metoprolol), alcohol. Potent CYP3A inhibitors (e.g. itraconazole, ketoconazole) or inducers (e.g. rifampin), other PDE5 inhibitors."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Orodispersible film 5 mg (P149.25), 20 mg (P417.00)."
          }
        ],
        "company": {
          "id": 10,
          "name": "Abbott Laboratories"
        },

          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/aLIHPfoisrUWfprlCnJuxd4s88k2mBF1umY3DaY8ZXrNiCQCpq.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Paracetamol",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Paracetamol & Other Para-Aminophenol Derivatives"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Non-Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Relief of mild to moderate fever and pain, headache, migraine, muscle ache, sore throat, musculoskeletal pain, pain after dental procedure/tooth extraction, toothache, fever and pain associated with vaccination/immunization, earache/otalgia, respiratory tract infections including cold and flu."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Based on recommended dosage of 10-15 mg/kg. <b>Susp - 250 mg/5 mL</b> - Childn 10-12 yrs (32-42 kg): 9 mL;  8-9 yrs (26-31 kg): 7 mL; 6-7 yrs (20-25 kg): 6 mL. <b>120 mg/5 mL</b> - Childn (2-6 yrs) weighing 21-24 kg: 13 mL; 16-20 kg: 10 mL;  12-15 kg: 7.5 mL; 8-11 kg: 5 mL. <b>Drops 100 mg/mL</b> - Childn 12-24 months (10-15 kg): 1.5 mL; 4-12 months (7-9 kg): 1 mL; 2-3 months (5-6 kg): 0.75 mL; 1 month (4 kg): 0.5 mL. All doses taken every 4-6 hrs. Do not take >4 doses in any 24-hr period. Max duration of continued use without medical advice: 3 days. Shake well before use."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Overdosing may cause serious harm to liver. Childn with liver or kidney impairment. Underweight or malnourished childn. Severe infection or glutathione-depleted states e.g. sepsis may increase the risk of metabolic acidosis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with liver or kidney impairment.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Thrombocytopenia, anaphylaxis, cutaneous hypersensitivity reactions (e.g. skin rashes, angioedema and SJS), bronchospasm, in patients sensitive to aspirin and other NSAIDs, hepatic dysfunction and liver toxicity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Warfarin and other coumarins, other paracetamol-containing medications."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Oral suspension 120 mg/5 mL x 60 mL (P94.50), 100 mL (P133.00); 250 mg/5 mL x 60 mL (P143.00), 100 mL (P199.58). Oral drops 100 mg/mL x 15 mL (P63.25)."
          }
        ],

        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,

          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Potassium citrate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Urinary Alkalinizers"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Management of renal tubular acidosis with calcium stones, hypocitraturic calcium oxalate nephrolithiasis of any etiology, and uric acid lithiasis with or without calcium stones."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Severe hypocitraturia (urinary citrate &lt;150 mg/day)</b>: 60 mEq/day (20 mEq 3x a day or 15 mEq 4x a day with meals or within 30 mins after meals or bedtime snack). <b>Mild to moderate hypocitraturia (&gt;150 mg/day)</b>: 30 mEq/day (10 mEq 3x a day with meals)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Patients with hyperkalemia (or conditions predisposing to hyperkalemia e.g. chronic renal failure, uncontrolled DM, acute dehydration, strenuous physical exercise in unconditioned individuals, adrenal insufficiency, extensive tissue breakdown, or administration of potassium-sparing agents), delayed gastric emptying, esophageal compression, intestinal obstruction or stricture or taking anticholinergic medication, PUD, renal insufficiency (GFR &lt;0.7 mL/kg/min)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with impaired mechanisms for excreting potassium. Avoid use in patients with chronic renal failure, severe myocardial damage, or heart failure. Use of potassium-sparing diuretics. Childn. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category C.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Minor GI complaints e.g. abdominal discomfort, vomiting, diarrhea, loose bowel movements, or nausea."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Extended-release tablet 1,080 g (equiv. to 10 mEq), 1.620 g (equiv to 15 mEq)."
          }
        ],
        "company": {

        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Bicalutamide",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Hormones and Antagonists in Chemotherapy"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "As part of combination therapy for treatment of advanced prostate cancer in combination with LHRH analogue therapy or surgical castration. Monotherapy (with 3 tabs of bicalutamide 50 mg): either alone or as adjuvant to radical prostatectomy or radiotherapy in patients with locally advanced prostate cancer at high-risk disease progression."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adult males including elderly</b> - <b>Combination therapy:</b> 50 mg tab once daily. May be started either 3 days before or at the same time as commencing treatment with an LHRH analogue, or at the same time as surgical castration. <b>Monotherapy:</b> 150 mg (3 tabs) once daily. Taken continuously for at least 2 yrs or until disease progression."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Coadministration with terfenadine, astemizole, or cisapride. Females and childn. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with moderate to severe hepatic impairment. Periodic liver function testing. Discontinue if severe hepatic changes and hepatic failure are observed. Monitor blood glucose when in combination with LHRH agonists. May prolong QT interval. History of or risk factors for QT prolongation or in patients receiving concomitant products that prolong QT interval. Coadministration of coumarin anticoagulants. May cause morphological changes in spermatozoa. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Anemia, decreased appetite, decreased libido, depression, dizziness, somnolence, MI, cardiac failure (combination therapy), hot flush, abdominal pain, constipation, dyspepsia, flatulence, nausea, hepatotoxicity, jaundice, hypertransaminasemia, rash, alopecia, hirsutism/hair re-growth, dry skin, pruritus, hematuria, gynecomastia, breast tenderness, erectile dysfunction, asthenia, chest pain, edema, and increased weight."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Midazolam, ciclosporin, CCBs, cimetidine, ketoconazole, warfarin and other coumarin anticoagulants, quinidine, disopyramide, amiodarone, sotalol, dofetilide, ibutilide, methadone, moxifloxacin, antipsychotics."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 50 mg (P161.00)."
          }
        ],

          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/xD73WLvF4Nmbi78jSqa5agUkwvTnWtLBgjTo4frBVL9T5j4N2b.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Candesartan cilexetil",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Angiotensin II Receptor Blockers"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Hypertension (HTN), may be used alone or in combination with other antihypertensives. To reduce cardiovascular death and heart failure hospitalizations in patients with impaired left ventricular systolic function (LVEF &le;40%)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>HTN - Monotherapy:</b> Initially 16 mg once daily. Total daily dose range: 8-32 mg once or in 2 divided doses. <b>Patients with intravascular vol depletion:</b> Initially 4 mg once daily. <b>Elderly:</b> Lower dose should be considered. <b>Renal impairment</b> - Mild: 4 mg once daily; Moderate: 2 mg once daily. <b>Hepatic impairment</b> - Mild to moderate: 2 mg once daily. <b>Heart failure:</b> Initially 4 mg once daily; target dose is 32 mg once daily, which is achieved by doubling the dose at approx 2-week intervals, as tolerated by the patient."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Severe hepatic impairment and/or cholestasis. Concomitant use with aliskiren in patients with DM or renal impairment (GFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>). Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Fetal toxicity. Hypotension in patients with heart failure or intravascular vol depletion. Patients taking other agents that affect RAAS, potassium-sparing diuretics, potassium supplements, salt substitutes containing potassium and other drugs that may increase serum potassium. Patients with renal artery stenosis, renal disease; suffering from aortic and mitral valve stenosis or obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy; undergoing anesthesia or surgery; on hemodialysis; primary hyperaldosteronism; ischemic cardiopathy or ischemic cerebrovascular disease. May impair ability to drive or operate machine. Childn < 18 yrs. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category D.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Back pain, dizziness, URTI, pharyngitis, rhinitis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Potassium-sparing diuretics, potassium supplements or salts, lithium, NSAIDs (i.e. COX2 inhibitors), other antihypertensive agents."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 8 mg (P22.00), 16 mg (P36.00)."
          }
        ],

        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Clotrimazole, beclomethasone dipropionate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Topical Antifungals w/ Anti-Inflammatories"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of fungal infections of the skin accompanied by eczematous features of tinea capitis, tinea corporis, tinea barbae, tinea cruris, tinea manum, tinea unguium, tinea pedis, tinea versicolor, vulvo-vaginal candidiasis, candidal nappy rash, candidal paronychia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Rub onto affected areas 2-3 times daily. In hairy sites, part hair before application to allow direct contact of cream or soln with lesions."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Skin TB, herpes simplex, chicken pox, measles, vaccinia, syphilitic skin lesions."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "May increase systemic absorption when used over large skin areas with or without occlusive dressing. Pregnancy. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category C for beclometasone; Category B for clotrimazole.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",

                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."

                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Miliaria, folliculitis or pyoderma under occlusive dressing. Localized atrophy and striae."
          },

  {
    "id": 1356,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 1356,
        "brand_name": "Canditral",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/LoAmcZ2ys2KuNlPZfwFNkUSAnjahIEWnF4DaXzZuXbBCZcCjrr.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/LoAmcZ2ys2KuNlPZfwFNkUSAnjahIEWnF4DaXzZuXbBCZcCjrr.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/dNbsxKqRFM9AlC5LjWLyLfOl4BBIe5h7YRuILfNYHp5jTHKWVJ.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Itraconazole",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Antifungals"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of fungal infections in immunocompromised and non-immunocompromised patients: blastomycosis, histoplasmosis, aspergillosis, tinea versicolor, tinea corporis, tinea cruris, dermatomycosis of palms and soles (tinea manuum, tinea pedis). Treatment of fungal infections in non-immunocompromised patients: onchomycosis of the toenail due to dermatophytes (tinea unguium)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Blastomycosis, histoplasmosis</b>: 200 mg (2 caps) once daily, may be increased by 100 mg increments up to max 400 mg daily. Doses &gt;200 mg/day should be given in 2 divided doses. <b>Aspergillosis</b>: 200-400 mg. <b>Life-threatening situations</b>: Loading dose of 200 mg (2 caps) 3x daily be given for the first 3 days of treatment. Duration of treatment: Minimum of 3 months until active fungal infection have subsided. <b>Onychomycosis - Toenails with or without finger involvement</b>: 200 mg (2 caps) once daily for 12 consecutive weeks. <b>Fingernails only</b>: 2 treatment pulses, each consisting of 200 mg (2 caps) twice daily for 1 week. Pulses are separated by a 3-week period without itraconazole. <b>Tinea versicolor</b>: 2 caps once daily for 7 days. <b>Tinea corporis, tinea cruris</b>: 1 cap once daily for 2 weeks. <b>Dermatomycosis of palms and soles (tinea manus, tinea pedis)</b>: 1 cap once daily for 4 weeks. Optimal healing: 2-4 weeks after withdrawing itraconazole in cases of mycoses of the skin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with ventricular dysfunction e.g. CHF or history of CHF. Concomitant use of methadone, disopyramide, dofetilide, dronedarone, quinidine, ergot alkaloids, irinotecan, lurasidone, oral midazolam, pimozide, triazolam, felodipine, nisoldipine, ranolazine, eplerenone, cisapride, lovastatin, simvastatin, colchicine. Pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Renal and hepatic impairment. Perform liver function testing and discontinue treatment if patients develop signs of liver dysfunction. Transient or permanent hearing loss. Should not be used interchangeably with itraconazole oral solution.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain, anorexia. Edema, fatigue, fever, malaise. Rash, pruritus. Headache, dizziness. Decreased libido, somnolence. HTN, hypokalemia, albuminuria, abnormal hepatic function, impotence."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Methadone, disopyramide, dofetilide, dronedarone, quinidine, ergot alkaloids, irinotecan, lurasidone, oral midazolam, pimozide, triazolam, felodipine, nisoldipine, ranolazine, eplerenone, cisapride, lovastatin, simvastatin, colchicine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Capsule 100 mg (P91.82)."
          }
        ],
        "company": {

        },

            "content": "Apply thinly 2-3 times daily. Continue treatment according to the indications specified even if symptoms disappear - Dermatomycoses: 3-4 weeks. Erythrasma: 2-4 weeks. <i>Pityriasis versicolor</i>: 1-3 weeks. <i>Candida</i> vulvitis and <i>Candida</i> balanitis: 1-2 weeks."

          },

            "content": "Avoid contact with eyes. Do not swallow. Cream may reduce the effectiveness and safety of latex products. Childn &lt;2 yrs. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category B.",

          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "IV infusion. <b>As substitute for oral nicardipine therapy</b>: 0.5 mg/hr IV infusion rate (oral 20 mg every 8 hrs); 1.2 mg/hr IV infusion rate (oral 30 mg every 8 hrs); 2.2 mg/hr IV infusion rate (oral 40 mg every 8 hrs). <b>Initiation therapy in drug-free patient</b>: 0.1 mg/mL by slow continuous infusion. <b>For gradual reduction in BP</b>: Initially 5 mg/hr, may be increased by 2.5 mg/hr every 15 mins up to max of 15 mg/hr, until desired BP reduction is achieved. <b>For more rapid BP reduction</b>: Initially 2.5 mg/hr every 5 mins up to max of 15 mg/hr, until desired BP is achieved.   {
    "id": 1035,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 1035,
        "brand_name": "Carvid",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Carvedilol",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Beta Blockers (Antihypertensives)"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Management of hypertension (HTN), alone or in combination with other antihypertensives; left ventricular dysfunction after myocardial infarction (MI). Prophylaxis for angina pectoris. Treatment of symptomatic, stable, chronic heart failure in combination with diuretics, ACE inhibitors, and digitalis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Individualized dosing. <b>HTN:</b> Initially 12.5 mg once a day or in 2 divided doses, then 25 mg once a day or in 2 divided doses, thereafter; dose may be increased at intervals of at least 2 weeks to max 50 mg once a day or in 2 divided doses. <b>Angina pectoris:</b> 12.5 mg twice daily for the first 2 days, followed by 25 mg twice daily; dose may be increased at intervals of at least 2 weeks to max 50 mg twice daily. <b>Elderly:</b> Max 50 mg/day in 2 divided doses. <b>Symptomatic, stable chronic heart failure:</b> 3.125 mg twice daily for 2 weeks; if tolerated increase to 6.25 mg twice daily, then 12.5 mg twice daily, then max 25 mg twice daily at intervals not less than 2 weeks. Mild to moderate heart failure in patients >85 kg: Max 50 mg twice daily. Mild to moderate heart failure in patients < 85 kg or patients with severe heart failure: Max 25 mg twice daily. <b>Left ventricular dysfunction following MI:</b> Initially 6.25 mg, then increase to 6.25 mg twice daily and maintain for 3-10 days. If tolerated, increase to 12.5 mg twice daily, then max 25 mg twice daily, at intervals of 3-10 days. Decrease dose to 3.125 mg twice daily if not tolerated. Start carvedilol between day 3 and day 21 after MI as patients should receive an ACE inhibitor for at  least 48 hrs, given at stable dose during at least the preceding 24 hrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Unstable/decompensated heart failure, hepatic impairment, marked fluid retention or overload requiring IV inotropic support, 2<sup>nd</sup> or 3<sup>rd</sup> degree AV block (unless a permanent pacemaker is in place), severe bradycardia, sick sinus syndrome, severe hypotension, cardiogenic shock, metabolic acidosis. History of bronchospasm, asthma, or other obstructive lung disorders."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Avoid abrupt discontinuation. May mask manifestations of hypoglycemia and hyperthyroidism i.e. tachycardia. Use with caution during anesthesia and major surgery; in combination with digitalis glycosides. Patients with bronchospastic disease, pheochromocytoma, PVD, Prinzmetal’s variant angina, Raynaud’s phenomenon, history of anaphylaxis and psoriasis. Decrease of lacrimation; wearing of contact lenses. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category C.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Asthenia, allergy, fatigue, fever, hypovolemia, malaise, edema, flu syndrome, pain in extremities. Undesirable effects on CV, GI, hematologic, metabolic and nutritional, musculoskeletal, nervous, male reproductive, respiratory, skin, appendages, and urogenital systems. Abnormal or blurred vision, eye irritation, tinnitus, decreased lacrimation and hearing. Latent DM and inhibition of blood glucose counterregulation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "CYP2D6 inhibitors, MAOIs, reserpine, clonidine, ciclosporin, digoxin, rifampicin, CCBs, insulin, oral hypoglycemics, amiodarone, anesthesia, and other antihypertensives."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 6.25 mg (P11.34), 25 mg (P19.07)."
          }
        ],

  {
    "id": 4803,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 4803,
        "brand_name": "Catania Max",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/S91238ZOdBkNytBK9FqxFgETDY8OfX2crfrlzSVNjRjd4MKVfi.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/X3384z4otFyDrAA6IAZEAq90ONO2hy9gKCneGss6vXPdfns2H3.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/tH5zablpxQ62rQN3VKeVr0YN0nECYXho6eM7JXcknrmHYCGY8Y.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Dapagliflozin propanediol monohydrate, metformin HCl",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults and childn &ge;10 yrs with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). It also reduces the risk of: (1) heart failure hospitalization in adults with T2DM and multiple cardiovascular (CV) risk factors or established cardiovascular diseases (CVD). (2) CV death and hospitalization in adults with heart failure (NYHA Class I-IV) and reduced ejection fraction. (3) end-stage kidney disease, CV death, sustained decline in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), and hospitalization in adults with chronic kidney disease (CKD) at risk progression."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Starting dose: 5 mg once daily, then 10 mg once daily. Max dose: 10 mg dapagliflozin and 2,000 mg metformin. Taken with food."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. End-stage renal disease, dialysis patients, or severe renal impairment (eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>). Diabetic ketoacidosis and other forms of acute or chronic metabolic acidosis, with or without coma."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Lactic acidosis, diabetic ketoacidosis in patients with type 1 DM and other ketoacidosis, volume depletion, urosepsis and pyelonephritis, hypoglycemia when used with insulin and insulin secretagogues, Fournier’s gangrene, vit B<sub>12</sub>deficiency, genital mycotic infections.   {
    "id": 2808,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 2808,
        "brand_name": "Caxeta 500",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Capecitabine",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Pyrimidine Analogs & Antagonists"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Monotherapy for the treatment of patients with locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer after failure of taxanes and an anthracycline-containing chemotherapy regimen or for whom further anthracycline is not indicated. In combination with docetaxel, treatment for locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer after failure of cytotoxic chemotherapy. Adjuvant treatment of patients with colon cancer. Treatment of patients with metastatic colorectal cancer. 1<sup>st</sup>-line treatment of patients with advanced esophagogastric cancer. In combination with oxaliplatin, adjuvant treatment following complete resection of stage II and stage III gastric adenocarcinoma."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Monotherapy in colon, colorectal and breast cancer:</b> 1,250 mg/m<sup>2</sup> 2x daily for 2 weeks followed by a 7-day rest period. <b>Combination therapy for breast cancer:</b> 1,250 mg/m<sup>2</sup> 2x daily for 2 weeks followed by a 7-day rest period, combined with docetaxel at 75 mg/m<sup>2</sup> as a 1 hr IV infusion every 3 weeks. <b>Combination therapy (except irinotecan) for colon, colorectal, gastric cancer and esophagogastric cancer:</b> 800-1000 mg/m<sup>2</sup> 2x daily for 2 weeks followed by a 7-day rest period, or to 625 mg/m<sup>2</sup> 2x daily when administered continuously; <b>Combination therapy with irinotecan:</b> 800 mg/m<sup>2</sup> 2x daily for 2 weeks followed by a 7-day rest period, combined with irinotecan 200 mg/m<sup>2</sup> on day 1 of each 3-week cycle. 6 months adjuvant treatment for stage III colon cancer. Start premedication in combination therapy prior to docetaxel, cisplatin, or oxaliplatin. Should be swallowed with water within 30 mins after meal. <b>Patients with moderate renal impairment (CrCl 30-50 mL/min):</b> Dose reduction to 75% of 1250 mg/m<sup>2</sup>. See product insert for dose reductions based on BSA and toxicity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with history of hypersensitivity to fluorouracil; known dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase deficiency; severe renal impairment (CrCl < 30 mL/min). Concomitant use with sorivudine or its chemically related analogues (e.g.brivudine). Neutrophil counts < 1.5 x 10<sup>9</sup>/L and/or thrombocyte < 100 x 10<sup>9</sup>/L. Pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with renal and hepatic impairment; severe diarrhea; anorexia, asthenia, nausea, vomiting; history of CAD. Avoid and manage dehydration. May induce SJS and TEN; Grade 1-3 hand-foot syndrome; hyperbilirubinemia. Concomitant use of vit B<sub>6</sub> for symptomatic or secondary prophylactic treatment for hand-foot syndrome and oral coumarin anticoagulant. Discontinue treatment if CrCl decreases to < 30 mL/min, bilirubin >3 x ULN or AST and ALT >2.5 x ULN. Childn. Elderly &ge;60 yrs. Women of childbearing potential. Lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category D.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Anorexia, dehydration, decreased appetite. Paresthesia, dysgeusia, headache, dizziness (excluding vertigo). Lacrimation increased, conjunctivitis. Diarrhea, vomiting, nausea, stomatitis, abdominal pain, constipation, dyspepsia. Palmar-plantar erythro-dysesthesia syndrome, dermatitis, rash, alopecia, erythema, dry skin. Fatigue, lethargy, pyrexia, weakness, asthenia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Coumarin anticoagulants, CYP450 2C9 substrates, phenytoin, antacid, leucovorin, sorivudine and analogues, oxaliplatin, bevacizumab."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 500 mg (P13,839.29)."
          }
        ],

Prolonged use may induce tolerance. May alter excretion of other drugs. Concomitant intake of caffeine, tea, zinc, phosphorus, calcium (dairy), or phytates (e.g. bran, brown bread). May interfere with the laboratory tests of paracetamol, AST, bilirubin, carbamazepine, creatinine, glucose, lactate dehydrogenase, stool guaiac, theophylline, and uric acid. <b>Syr/Drops:</b> Concomitant use with other vitamin-mineral supplements.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "<b>Chewable tab - Vitamin C:</b> Antacids, aspirin, disulfiram, fluphenazine, mexiletine, paracetamol, estrogen-containing oral contraceptives, warfarin; <b>Zinc:</b> Biphosphonates (e.g. alendronate, etidronate, risedronate), antihyperlipidemics, copper or iron, penicillamine, quinolones, tetracycline."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Chewable tablet 100 mg/10 mg (P6.50). Syrup 100 mg/10 mg per 5 mL x 60 mL (P86.00), 120 mL (P159.25), 250 mL (P302.25). Oral drops 40 mg/5 mg per mL x 15 mL (P92.25), 30 mL (P161.50)."
          }
        ],

          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Recommended dose 25-50 mg/kg body weight/day in 4 divided doses; may be increased to 50-100 mg/kg body weight/day in 4 divided doses for severe infections and otitis media. <b>Oral drops</b> - <b>Infant 0-3 months</b>: 0.5 mL; <b>4-6 months</b>: 0.75-1 mL; <b>7-12 months:</b> 1 mL. <b>Suspension 125 mg/5 mL</b> - <b>Children 1-2 years</b>: 5 mL; <b>3-6 years</b>: 5-10 mL; <b>7-12 years</b>: 10-15 mL. <b>Suspension 250 mg/5 mL</b> - <b>1-2 years</b>: 2.5 mL; <b>3-6 years</b>: 2.5-5 mL; <b>7-12 years</b>: 5-10 mL. All doses to be taken every 6 hours. Duration of treatment: Mild infections 5 days, moderate infections minimum of 7 days, serious or extensive infections and for prevention of recurrence rheumatic fever 10 days."
          },
          {

          },
          {

            "content": "<b>Adults</b>: 400 mg once daily or 200 mg every 12 hrs. <b>Uncomplicated cervical/urethral gonococcal infections</b>: 400 mg as single dose. <b>Childn</b>: 8 mg/kg/day or 4 mg/kg every 12 hrs. <b>Typhoid</b>: 15-20 mg/kg/day as single dose or divided into 2 equal doses every 12 hrs for 7-14 days. <b>Infections due to <i>S. pyogenes</i></b>: Therapeutic dosage should be given at least 10 days."

        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Cefuroxime axetil",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Second Generation Cephalosporins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Indicated for bronchitis, otitis media, pharyngitis, sinusitis, skin and soft tissue infections. <b>Tab:</b> Treatment of acute streptococcal tonsilitis, cystitis, pyelonephritis, early Lyme disease. <b>Susp:</b> Treatment of susceptible including bone and joint infections, and lower respiratory tract infection (LRTI), gonorrhea, meningitis, peritonitis, and urinary tract infection (UTI). Prophylaxis for surgical infection."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Tab: Adult and adolescents</b> – Acute sinusitis: 250 mg or 500 mg every 12 hrs; Acute otitis media: 500 mg every 12 hrs; Acute tonsillopharyngitis, bacterial exacerbations of chronic bronchitis, secondary bacterial infections of acute bronchitis, uncomplicated skin and skin structure infection, uncomplicated UTI including pyelonephritis: 250 mg or 500 mg every 12 hrs; Uncomplicated gonorrhea: 1 g once as a single dose; Early Lyme disease: 500 mg every 12 hrs or as prescribed. Duration of treatment: 10 days. <b>Susp: Adults</b> - UTI: 125 mg every 12 hrs; Most infections, mild to moderate LRTIs e.g. bronchitis, pyelonephritis: 250 mg every 12 hrs; More severe LRTIs, pneumonia: 500 mg every 12 hrs; Uncomplicated gonorrhea: 1 g once as a single dose. <b>Childn 3 months-12 yrs</b> - Pharyngitis, tonsillitis: 20 mg/kg/day. Max 500 mg/day; Acute bacterial otitis media, mild to moderate acute bacterial maxillary sinusitis, impetigo: 30 mg/kg/day. Max 1 g/day. All doses to be given in 2 divided doses. Duration of treatment: 10 days."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to cephalosporins, penicillins, monobactams, and carbapenems."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Pregnancy and lactation. <b>Tab:</b> Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction. Prolonged use may result in the overgrowth of other non-susceptible microorganisms. <b>Susp:</b> Renal impairment.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "GI disturbances, including diarrhea, nausea and vomiting. <b>Tab:</b> <i>Candida overgrowth</i>, eosinophilia, headache, dizziness, abdominal pain, transient increases of hepatic enzyme levels."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Probenecid. Drugs which reduce gastric acidity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 500 mg (P22.75). Powder for suspension 250 mg/5 mL x 70 mL (P492.80)."
          }
        ],

          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of infections caused by susceptible organisms e.g. Lyme disease, bone and joint infections, bronchitis and other lower respiratory tract infection, gonorrhea, meningitis, otitis media, peritonitis, pharyngitis, sinusitis, skin and soft tissue, urinary tract infections (UTI) and for surgical infection prophylaxis. Active against <i>Haemophilus influenzae</i>."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Tab - Adults &ge;13 yrs</b> - Pharyngitis/tonsilitis, acute bacterial maxillary sinusitis: 250 mg every 12 hrs for 10 days. Acute bacterial exacerbation of chronic bronchitis: 250-500 mg every 12 hrs for 10 days or 500-750 mg every 8 hrs. Uncomplicated skin and skin structure infections: 250-500 mg every 12 hrs for 10 days. Uncomplicated UTI: 250 mg every 12 hrs for 7-10 days. Uncomplicated gonorrhea: 1,000 mg once. <b>Childn</b> - Acute otitis media, acute bacterial maxillary sinusitis: 250 mg every 12 hrs for 10 days. <b>Susp - Childn 3 months-12 yrs</b> - Pharyngitis/tonsillitis: 20 mg/kg/day divided twice a day for 10 days. Max 500 mg/day. Acute otitis media, acute bacterial maxillary sinusitis and impetigo: 30 mg/kg/day divided twice a day for 10 days. Max 1 g/day. To be taken with food."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "<i>Clostridium difficile</i>-associated diarrhea. May result in overgrowth of non-susceptible microorganisms (prolonged use). Concurrent use with potent diuretics. History of colitis. Fall in prothrombin activity especially in patients with renal and hepatic impairment or poor nutritional state.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity reactions. <i>Candida</i> growth, eosinophilia, bleeding disorders, headache, dizziness, GI disturbances, and transient increase in hepatic enzyme levels."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Diuretics, anticoagulants. Probenecid."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 500 mg. Granules for suspension 250 mg/5 mL x 50 mL (P445.76)."
          }
