  {
    "id": 2106,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 2106,
        "brand_name": "Celabin",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/EQpZXHKXeWcAf1ExNXyqaB56a6f46n7X0xRuNd4Ua7lymXN37W.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/RBnpbELHCrU4jYHIhLEs81QItCEjXqvijgcZgc45xli9gDzdo8.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/I5hDnGw0yUgJQF2z3Y6ajvFQnYW04JEf3RnZGEKCaPm0Cpb56U.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Capecitabine",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Pyrimidine Analogs & Antagonists"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "First-line treatment of metastatic colorectal cancer or as adjuvant treatment of patients following surgery of stage III (Dukes’ stage C) colon cancer when treatment with fluoropyrimidine therapy alone is preferred. In combination with oxaliplatin for metastatic colorectal cancer following failure of irinotecan-containing combination chemotherapy. As monotherapy or in combination with docetaxel for locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer resistant to paclitaxel or anthracycline-containing regimen or after failure or prior anthracycline-containing chemotherapy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Metastatic/adjuvant colorectal cancer and metastatic breast cancer</b>: 1,250 mg/m<sup>2</sup> twice daily for 2 weeks, followed by 1 week rest period, for 8 cycles. <b>Combination with oxaliplatin for metastatic colorectal cancer</b>: 1,000 mg/m<sup>2</sup> twice daily for 2 weeks followed by 1 week rest period; capecitabine 1<sup>st</sup> dose is given on the evening of day 1 and last dose is given on the morning of day 15. Oxaliplatin 130 mg/m<sup>2</sup> is administered as IV infusion over 2 hrs to be given as a 3-weekly schedule. Premedicate with antiemetic prior to oxaliplatin administration. <b>Combination with docetaxel for metastatic breast cancer</b>: 1,250 mg/m<sup>2</sup> twice daily for 2 weeks followed by 1 week rest period. Docetaxel 75 mg/m<sup>2</sup> is administered as 1-hr IV infusion on the first day of each 3-week cycle. Premedication prior to docetaxel administration. <b>Renal impairment (CrCl 30-50 mL/min)</b>: Reduce to 75% of dose. Swallowed whole with water within 30 mins after a meal."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to capecitabine, 5-fluorouracil, or fluoropyrimidine. Patients with known dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase deficiency. Patients with severe renal (CrCl &lt;30 mL/min) and hepatic impairment; severe leucopenia, neutropenia, or thrombocytopenia. Patients on treatment with sorivudine or related analogues (e.g. brivudine). Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Concurrent use of oral coumarin-derivative anticoagulant. Patients with or at risk for diarrhea, dehydration, hypocalcemia or hypercalcemia, or other electrolyte disturbances; CAD, nervous system disease, DM, or ophthalmologic complications. Patients with galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, or glucose-galactose malabsorption. May impair ability to drive and operate machines. Fertility impairment. Elderly. Childn. Women of childbearing potential. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category D.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, stomatitis, hand-and-foot syndrome, fatigue, asthenia, anorexia, cardiotoxicity, increased renal dysfunction, thrombosis, or embolism."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Coumarin-derivative anticoagulants, phenytoin, leucovorin, folinic acid, antacids containing aluminum and magnesium, allopurinol, interferon alpha, oxaliplatin, radiotherapy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 500 mg (P8,687.45)."
          }
        ],
        "company": {
          "id": 3399,
          "name": "Bio-Onco, Inc."
        },

      "data": {

        "brand_name": "Celebrex",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/SGxzrj5IMsgSwKlITg3DMZRpOoX2SFHldgXVVAxKnqzwnNCLMB.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/h8pDRgEMUcwvQ9zAvF6Hi12V42gssdlQ5KwFjNdW4TQcFZwc2o.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/gAIIJvDfPnCaRfeKWfVTwWYK2euBaaaN9kl4JC86vbT4VL09HV.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Celecoxib",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "COX-2 Specific Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Symptomatic treatment of osteoarthritis (OA) and rheumatoid arthritis (RA). For relief of signs and symptoms of ankylosing spondylitis (AS). Management of acute pain. Treatment of primary dysmenorrhea. For acute and chronic low back pain."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Symptomatic treatment of OA</b>: 200 mg as single dose or 100 mg twice per day. <b>Symptomatic treatment of RA</b>: 100 mg or 200 mg twice per day. <b>AS</b>: 200 mg as single dose or 100 mg twice per day. Max 400 mg daily. <b>Management of acute pain</b>: Initially 400 mg followed by an additional 200 mg if needed on 1<sup>st</sup> day, then 200 mg twice daily or 400 mg once daily on subsequent days. <b>Treatment of primary dysmenorrhea</b>: Initially 400 mg followed by an additional 200 mg if needed on 1<sup>st</sup> day, then 200 mg twice daily on subsequent days. For patients with swallowing difficulties, caps can be opened and emptied onto a tsp of applesauce, rice gruel, yogurt, or mashed bananas."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to celecoxib or sulfonamide. Patients with history of aspirin- or NSAID-induced asthma, urticarial or allergic-type reactions. Treatment of peri-op pain in the setting of CABG surgery."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with IHD and those with risk factors for heart disease; HTN; hyperlipidemia; diabetes; smoking and PAD; hepatic impairment. Increased risk for serious CV thrombotic events, MI and stroke. Onset of new HTN or worsening of pre-existing HTN. Fluid retention and edema. Upper and lower GI perforations, ulcers or bleeds. Renal toxicity. Anaphylactoid reactions. Serious skin reactions including exfoliative dermatitis, SJS and toxic epidermal necrosis. Co-administration of oral anticoagulants and fluconazole or other CYP2C9 inhibitor. Elderly. Pregnancy (3<sup>rd</sup> trimester) and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Bronchitis, sinusitis, URTI; UTI; insomnia; dizziness; HTN; cough; vomiting, abdominal pain, diarrhea, dyspepsia, flatulence; pruritus, rash; peripheral edema."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Oral anticoagulants including warfarin/coumarin-type and novel oral anticoagulants. CYP2C9 inhibitors, CYP2C9 inducers (e.g. rifampicin, carbamazepine and barbiturates), lithium, ACE inhibitors, ARBs, diuretics and beta-blockers, ciclosporin, fluconazole and ketoconazole, dextromethorphan and metoprolol."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Capsule 100 mg (P46.87), 200 mg (P66.28), 400 mg (P85.20)."
          }

  {
    "id": 3578,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 3578,
        "brand_name": "Celetor-200",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/dJ6L2OWIgqtN1TCWnrKdm9crl6YqOLTaKg24CuteT8AgHdoGp1.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/0tMYTERihHszIKbEgQ9kv8tjgPuWU50R9WiSv12uZpPXt0ZOTv.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/So0zRScNlMnRYeEHJX1CYA6T0W4M5scG3XcUT73ojBbOsunW7s.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Celecoxib",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "COX-2 Specific Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Symptomatic relief in the treatment of osteoarthritis (OA), rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and ankylosing spondylitis in adults. Management of acute pain and treatment of primary dysmenorrhea."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults and elderly &gt;65 yrs (&ge;50 kg BW)</b>: Initially 200 mg/day, increased to 200 mg twice daily if needed. <b>OA</b>: 200 mg once daily or in 2 divided doses, may be increased to 200 mg twice daily. <b>RA</b>: Initially 200 mg in 2 divided doses, may be increased to 200 mg twice daily if needed. <b>Ankylosing spondylitis</b>: 200 mg once daily or in 2 divided doses, may be increased to 400 mg once daily or in 2 divided doses in patients with insufficient relief from symptoms. Max 400 mg. <b>Acute pain and primary dysmenorrhea</b>: Initially 400 mg followed by 200 mg if necessary, on the 1<sup>st</sup> day, then 200 mg twice daily thereafter. Taken with or without food. Entire content of caps can be added to applesauce, rice gruel, yogurt, or mashed banana for patients with difficulty swallowing."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to NSAIDs and sulfonamides. History of CVA, MI, CHF (NYHA II-IV), CABG, uncontrolled HTN. Patients who experienced asthma, acute rhinitis, nasal polyps, angioneurotic edema, urticaria, or other allergic-type reactions after taking aspirin or other NSAIDs including COX2 inhibitors. Treatment of peri-op pain in CABG. Pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "IHD, HTN, DM, PAD, hyperlipidemia. Smokers, poor CYP2C9 metabolizers. Not a substitute for aspirin for prophylaxis of CV thromboembolic disease. Concomitant use of other NSAIDs or aspirin, glucocorticoids, alcohol or patients with history of GI disease (e.g. ulceration and GI bleeding). History of cardiac failure, left ventricular dysfunction, pre-existing edema, diuretic use, risk of hypovolemia, dehydration. Patients with mild or moderate renal impairment, liver impairment and dehydration. May impair ability to drive and operate machinery. Not indicated for use in childn. Elderly with &lt;50 kg BW. Lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "HTN. Sinusitis, URTI, pharyngitis; UTI; hypersensitivity; insomnia; dizziness, hypertonia, headache; MI; rhinitis, cough, dyspnea; nausea, abdominal pain, diarrhea, dyspepsia, flatulence, vomiting, dysphagia; rash, pruritus; arthralgia; influenza-like illness, edema, peripheral/fluid retention; accidental injury."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Warfarin or other oral anticoagulant; aspirin, ACE inhibitors, ARBs, diuretics, beta-blockers; ciclosporin, tacrolimus; TCAs, SSRIs, neuroleptics, anti-arrhythmics; dextromethorphan and metoprolol; lithium; fluconazole."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Capsule 200 mg (P24.25)."
          }
        ],
        "company": {
          "id": 1246,
          "name": "Torrent Pharma Philippines, Inc."
        },

    "id": 4967,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 4967,
        "brand_name": "Celevid",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/McsILDgZ2disJdctUGJ097Kuh7tFdsbW2qlAGJae2rnZfYvQck.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/84m47V25Fuz1c6t5iI9hsyyaFruWr7u9WQtWHnmgdOZ6JRK059.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/Wauhvob9llTjbIExgHAl9sjIhiaO9oLSpMPGH1VtgruhNkVj3g.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Celecoxib",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Non-Steroidal Anti-inflammatory Drugs"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Symptomatic treatment of osteoarthritis (OA) and rheumatoid arthritis (RA). Relief of signs and symptoms of ankylosing spondylitis (AS). Management of acute pain in adults, acute and chronic low back pain.  Treatment of primary dysmenorrhea."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>OA:</b> 200 mg as single dose or 100 mg twice per day. <b>RA:</b> 100 mg or 200 mg twice per day. <b>AS:</b> 200 mg administered as single dose or as 100 mg twice per day. Max dose 400 mg/day. <b>Acute pain in adults and dysmenorrhea:</b> 400 mg, initially followed by an additional 200 mg dose if needed on the 1st day then 200 mg twice daily as needed. <b>Chronic low back pain:</b> 200 mg or 400 mg daily, administered 200 mg single dose or 100 or 200 mg twice/day."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with known sulfonamide hypersensitivity, active peptic ulceration or GI bleeding, asthma urticaria or allergic-type reaction after taking ASA or NSAIDs, including other COX-2 inhibitors. Peri-op pain of CABG surgery. Congestive heart failure (NYHA II-IV). Established ischemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease and/or cerebrovascular disease."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Upper and lower GI complications, concomitant NSAID use. Increased risk of serious CV thrombotic events, MI, and stroke. Patients with pre-existing CHF or HTN, with compromised cardiac function, pre-existing edema, or other conditions pre-disposing to, or worsened by, fluid retention, renal toxicity, dehydration, severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh class B). CYP2D6 inhibitors, CYP2C9 poor metabolizers. Serious skin reactions (e.g. exfoliative dermatitis, SJS and toxic epidermal necrolysis). Concurrent therapy with warfarin. Patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Elderly. May affect the ability of driving or operating machinery. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Bronchitis, sinusitis, URTI, UTI; Insomnia, dizziness, hypertension, cough, vomiting, abdominal pain, diarrhea, dyspepsia, flatulence; Pruritus, rash, edema peripheral."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "CYP2C9 inhibitors, CYP2C9 inducers (e.g. rifampicin, carbamazepine, barbiturates), fluconazole, ketoconazole, ACE inhibitors, ARBs, diuretics, beta-blockers, cyclosporine, dextromethorphan, metoprolol, lithium, aspirin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Capsule 200 mg (P15.00)."
          }
        ],

          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Ear Anti-Infectives & Antiseptics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "For the treatment of infections caused by susceptible isolates of the designated microorganisms in specific conditions: Otitis externa in adults and childn >6 months due to <i>Escherichia coli, Pseudomonas aeruginosa</i>, and <i>Staphylococcus aureus</i>; Chronic suppurative otitis media in patients >12 yrs with perforated tympanic membranes due to <i>Proteus mirabilis, P. aeruginosa, S. aureus</i>; Acute otitis media in childn >1 yr with tympanostomy tubes due to <i>Haemophilus influenzae, Moraxella catarrhalis, P. aerugunosa, S. aureus</i>, and <i>Streptococcus pneumoniae</i>."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Otitis externa</b> - Patients >13 yrs: 10 drops instilled into the affected ear once daily for 7 days; Childn 6 months-13 yrs: 5 drops instilled into the affected ear once daily for 7 days;  <b>Acute otitis media in childn with tympanostomy tubes</b> - Childn 1-12 yrs: 5 drops instilled into the affected ear twice daily for 10 days. <b>Chronic suppurative otitis media with perforated tympanic membranes - >12 yrs:</b> 10 drops instilled into the affected ear twice daily for 14 days. Soln should be warmed by holding it in the hand for 1 or 2 mins. The patient should lie with the affected ear upwards and then drops should be instilled. The tragus should be pumped 4x by pushing inwards to facilitate penetration of drops into the middle ear. The position should be maintained for 5 mins."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to ofloxacin, other quinolones, or any of the components in this medication."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not for ophthalmic use or injection. Avoid contaminating applicator tip. Discontinue use if allergic reaction is suspected. Overgrowth of nonsusceptible organisms e.g. fungi during prolonged use. If infection does not improve after 1 week, cultures should be obtained to guide further treatment. Further evaluation is recommended if otorrhea persists after a full course of therapy, or if two or more episodes occur within 6 months. Childn < 6 months. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category C.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",

                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nausea, seborrhea, transient loss of hearing, tinnitus, otitis externa, otitis media, tremor, HTN, and fungal infection. Dermatitis, eczema, erythematous rash, follicular rash, hypoaesthesia, dyspepsia, hot flushes, flushing and otorrhagia. Taste perversion, earache, pruritus, paraesthesia, rash, dizziness. Vomiting, dry mouth, headache, vertigo, fever. Application site reaction, urticaria, abdominal pain, dysaesthesia, hyperkinesia, halitosis, inflammation, pain, insomnia, coughing, pharyngitis, rhinitis, sinusitis, and tachycardia."

          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/RltFLBa3UEmxW8Qk3mpp9QRidG1yKWyvQTb6RivEb6sFiNEoGE.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Cefepime HCl",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Fourth Generation Cephalosporins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of infections due to susceptible organisms: Lower respiratory tract (LRTI) including nosocomial and community-acquired pneumonia, acute bacterial exacerbation of chronic and acute bronchitis, complicated and uncomplicated urinary tract (UTI), intra-abdominal including peritonitis and biliary tract infections; LRTI (pneumonia), UTI, skin and skin structure in childn &ge;2 months; empiric treatment in febrile neutropenia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Deep IM injection or IV infusion over at least 30 mins. <b>Adults</b> - <b>Mild to moderate infections:</b> 1-2 g daily in 2 divided doses; <b>Severe infections:</b> 4 g daily in 2 divided doses; <b>Febrile neutropenia:</b> 6 g daily in 3 divided doses. <b>Childn &gt;2 months weighing 40 kg:</b> 50 mg/kg twice daily (thrice daily for febrile neutropenia). <b>Renal impairment</b> - Maintenance dose - CrCl 30-60 mL/min: 0.5-2 g every 24 hrs (2 g every 24 hrs for febrile neutropenia); 11-29 mL/min: 0.5-1 g every 24 hrs (2 g every 24 hrs for febrile neutropenia); &le;10 mL/min: 250-500 mg every 24 hrs (1 g every 24 hrs for febrile neutropenia). Hemodialysis: 1 g on 1st day, followed by 500 mg daily (1 g daily for febrile neutropenia); <b>CAPD:</b> Normal doses at intervals of 48 hrs (2 g every 48 hrs for febrile neutropenia)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with impaired renal function (CrCl &le;60 mL/min), allergy to drugs. Pseudomembranous colitis, overgrowth of nonsusceptible organisms, superinfection. Coadministration of nephrotoxic drugs. Childn. Elderly.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },

          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/tZUKpPrMhUhkTTOWuollOyx3lN7fjzwpel98fjjnGlh4NiAJxJ.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Desogestrel",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Progestogens (Progestins)"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Oral contraception."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "1 tab daily for 28 days starting from the 1<sup>st</sup> day of menstrual bleeding."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Thrombosis, jaundice or severe liver disease, cancer sensitive to sex-steroids, unexplained vaginal bleeding. Known or suspected pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Breast and liver cancer, thrombosis, diabetes, epilepsy, tuberculosis, high blood pressure, chloasma. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category X.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Bleeding irregularities, acne, mood changes, breast pain, decreased libido, headache, nausea, irregular or no menstruation and weight increase, contact lens intolerance, vomiting, alopecia, dysmenorrhea, ovarian cyst, fatigue, rash, urticaria, erythema nodosum. Breast discharge. Hypersensitivity reactions (including angioedema and anaphylaxis). Venous and arterial thromboembolic disorders and hormone-dependent tumors have been reported in women using combined oral contraceptives."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Medicinal or herbal products that induce microsomal enzymes, specifically CYP450 enzymes including phenytoin, phenobarbital, primidone, bosentan, carbamazepine, rifampicin, and possibly also oxcarbazepine, rifabutin, topiramate, felbamate, griseofulvin, some HIV-protease inhibitors (e.g. ritonavir, nelfinavir) and non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (e.g. efavirenz, nevirapine), and products containing St. John's wort. HCV medicinal products (e.g. boceprevir, telaprevir). Strong (e.g. ketoconazole, itraconazole, clarithromycin) or moderate (e.g. fluconazole, diltiazem, erythromycin) CYP3A4 inhibitors. Medical charcoal. Ciclosporin. Lamotrigine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 75 mcg x 28s (P561.52)."
          }
        ],

            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Carbonic Anhydrase Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Management of glaucoma, epilepsy, congestive heart failure (CHF), and drug-induced edema."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Chronic simple glaucoma</b>: 250 mg-1 g every 24 hrs given in divided doses. <b>Secondary glaucoma, pre-op treatment of some cases of acute congestive glaucoma</b>: 250 mg every 4 hrs. In some acute cases, initially 500 mg then 125-250 mg every 4 hrs. <b>Epilepsy</b>: 8-30 mg/kg in divided doses. Max 375-1,000 mg daily. <b>CHF</b>: 250-375 mg once daily in the morning. <b>Drug-induced edema</b>: 250-375 mg once daily for 1-2 days, alternating with a day of rest."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Depressed sodium and/or potassium blood serum levels, marked kidney or liver disease, suprarenal gland failure, hyperchloremic acidosis, cirrhosis. Long-term administration in patients with chronic non-congestive angle-closure glaucoma."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Pulmonary obstruction or emphysema where alveolar ventilation may be impaired. Rapid ascent to high altitude. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Paresthesia, loss of appetite, tinnitus. Taste alteration, GI disturbances, polyuria, drowsiness, and confusion acidosis (long-term therapy), and transient myopia. Urticaria, melena, hematuria, glycosuria, hepatic insufficiency, flaccid paralysis, photosensitivity, convulsion. Sulfonamide-type reactions."
          },

        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Ethinylestradiol, levonorgestrel, ferrous fumarate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Estrogens w/ Progestogens &/or Related Agents"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Contraception and treatment of menstrual disorders e.g. dysmenorrhea, premenstrual syndrome and menorrhagia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Take 1 tab daily, within the first 5 days of menstrual bleeding. Start with the pill marked number '1' and follow the arrows indicated on the pack. The interval between 2 pills should be 24 hrs. Should be taken at the same time every day preferably taken after meals or at bedtime. A pack is good for 28 days. Start a new pack after taking the last pinkish-brown pill of the pack."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Liver disorders, clotting disorders, breast and cervical cancer, sickle-cell anemia, hormone-active tumors, hyperlipidemia, severe CV diseases, previous or existing thromboembolic diseases and idiopathic jaundice. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "DM, high BP, varicose veins, multiple sclerosis, epilepsy, migraine, ophthalmological problems, tetany.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Headache, gastric upsets, nausea, vomiting, abdominal cramps, changes in appetite, breast tenderness, change in weight and libido, depressive moods or interference with liver functions."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Analgesics, anti-migraine and tranquilizer. Ampicillin, chloramphenicol, neomycin, penicillin V, nitrofurantoin, sulfonamides, tetracycline and isoniazid. Clarithromycin, erythromycin, itraconazole, ketoconazole, ritonavir, grapefruit juice. Carbamazepine, oxcarbazepine, felbamate, topiramate, phenytoin. Griseofulvin, troglitazone, phenylbutazone, rifampicin and troleandomycin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "<b>Each blister pack - 21 beige tablet:</b> Ethinylestradiol 30 mcg, levonorgestrel 150 mcg; <b>7 pinkish-brown tablet:</b> Ferrous fumarate 75 mg (equiv to 24.75 mg elemental iron) x 28s."

  {
    "id": 4452,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 4452,
        "brand_name": "Chemodox",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Doxorubicin",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Anthracycline Antibiotics in Chemotherapy"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Management of Kaposi’s sarcoma (KS) in patients with AIDS. Treatment of metastatic breast and ovarian cancers; multiple myeloma with bortezomib."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "IV infusion. <b>Breast or ovarian cancer:</b> 50 mg/m<sup>2</sup> at an initial rate of 1 mg/min once every 4 weeks, can be increased to complete administration over 1 hr if no infusion-related reactions are observed; if infusion-related reaction occurs: 5% of the total dose slowly over the 1<sup>st</sup> 15 mins, may be doubled for the next 15 mins if tolerated without reaction, then completed over the next hr for a total infusion time of 90 mins. A minimum of 4 courses is recommended. Concomitant or pretreatment with antiemetics. <b>AIDS-KS:</b> 20 mg/m<sup>2</sup> over 30 mins once every 3 weeks when tolerated. Should not be administered as bolus injection or undiluted soln. If any signs or symptoms of extravasation are observed, terminate immediately and restart in another vein. Apply ice over the extravasation site for approx 30 mins to alleviate local reaction. <b>Multiple myeloma:</b> 30 mg/m over 60 mins on day 4 after bortezomib of each 21-day cycle for 8 cycles or until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. <b>Hepatic impairment - Bilirubin 1.2-3.0 mg/dL:</b> Reduce dose by 25%; <b>>3.0 mg/dL:</b> Reduce dose by 50%. Increase to full dose for cycle 2 if the first dose is tolerated without an increase in serum bilirubin or liver enzymes. If reduced by 50%, increase to 75% for cycle 2, can be increased to full dose for subsequent cycles. See product insert for dose modifications during toxicity and preparation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not suitable for IM or SC administration. Should not be used interchangeably with other formulations of doxorubicin. Patients with hepatic impairment; previous or concomitant therapy with other anthracyclines or related compounds; history of CV disease; AIDS-KS with baseline myelosuppression. Concomitant use with other anthracyclines or drugs that can cause bone marrow suppression. Cardiac toxicity at dose 450 mg/min<sup>2</sup> prior mediastinal irradiation or those receiving concurrent cyclophosphamide therapy; CHF due to cardiomyopathy; acute infusion-related reactions; serious, life-threatening or fatal allergic/anaphylactoid-like infusion reactions; hematologic toxicities; radiation-induced toxicity. Monitor ECG frequently; if reduction of the QRS complex or cardiomyopathy occurs, consider endomyocardial biopsy. Perform echocardiography or multigated angiography prior to initiation and during therapy. Monitor WBC, neutrophil, platelet count, and Hgb/Hct. Evaluate hepatic function prior to administration; left ventricular function before each added administration that exceeds lifetime cumulative anthracycline 450 mg/min<sup>2</sup>. Discontinue treatment if sepsis occurs. Childn < 18 yrs. Elderly. Women of childbearing potential. Pregnancy.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Hematological adverse effects (e.g. leukopenia, neutropenia, anemia, thrombocytopenia), palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia, stomatitis, nausea, asthenia, vomiting, rash, alopecia, constipation, anorexia, mucous membrane disorder, diarrhea, abdominal pain, paresthesia, pain, fever, pharyngitis, dry skin, headache, dyspepsia, somnolence, skin discoloration; alopecia, increased alkaline phosphatase, vomiting, stomatitis, oral moniliasis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Antineoplastics (e.g. cyclophosphamide, 6-mercaptopurine), cytotoxic (especially myelotoxic) agents."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Liposomal concentrate solution for IV infusion 2 mg/mL (P25,000.00)."
          }

      "success": true,

        "id": 4199,

        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/I3QrlpZOOr2iPazeaCeWD2OpYbEk9E6Ixb576uRWHKQ0UaaftH.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/7Yu18zqQQFbdV24iQ4ycfi5AxVbYp21XNVQE7l4Rz27FN9OOy3.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/2SpZS7oerJLCUnhbfK9kwrKtwQj2WOkhpeY8MFr8saJA7Iyo2o.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Simvastatin",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Statins"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of hypercholesterolemia, homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia or combined (mixed) hyperlipidemia in patients who have not responded adequately to diet and other appropriate measures. Prevention of CV events in atherosclerotic CV disease or DM."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults - Homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia:</b> 40 mg once daily or 80 mg/day; <b>Prevention of CV events, hyperlipidemias:</b> 20-40 mg once daily. <b>Patients requiring only moderate LDL-cholesterol reduction:</b> Initially 10 mg once daily; >45% LDL-cholesterol reduction: Initially 40 mg once daily. <b>Existing or at high risk for CHD:</b> Initially 40 mg once daily. Hypertriglyceridemia: Initially 10 or 20 mg once daily. <b>Childn 10-17 yrs (females >1 yr postmenarche) - Heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia:</b> 10 mg once daily. <b>Severe renal impairment (CrCl < 10 mL/min):</b> Initially 5 mg/day. <b>Concomitant amiodarone, verapamil diltiazem:</b> Max 10 mg daily; Amlodipine, ranolazine: Max 20 mg daily. Taken in the evening."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Active liver disease. Unexplained persistent serum transaminases elevations. Concomitant administration with itraconazole, ketoconazole, posaconazole, erythromycin, clarithromycin, telithromycin, HIV protease inhibitors, nefazodone, gemfibrozil, cyclosporine, danazol. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Do not start at 80 mg. Exclude secondary causes of hyperlipidemia before therapy. Patients with renal insufficiency, heavy ethanol consumption, history of liver disease. Avoid initiation in patients on cyclosporine or danazol unless tolerance to &ge;5 mg/day has been established. Discontinue if pain on the calf muscle, back, or body occurs or if transaminase levels increase >3x ULN. Temporarily discontinue for elective surgical procedures or in acute/serious medical or surgical conditions that may increase risk of rhabdomyolysis. Risk of rhabdomyolysis with acute renal failure. May increase risk of high blood sugar level. Perform liver function test 6 weeks before treatment and 12 months thereafter. Childn < 10 yrs or premenarcheal girls. Elderly. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category X.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Constipation, flatulence, dyspepsia, increased transaminases, CPK elevation, URTI."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Digoxin, warfarin, itraconazole, ketoconazole, posaconazole, erythromycin, clarithromycin, HIV protease inhibitors, nefazodone, verapamil, diltiazem, gemfibrozil, nicotinic acid, cyclosporine, amiodarone, colchicines, danazol, dasatinib, dronedarone, eltrombopag, fenofibrate, fenofibric acid, fusidic acid, imatinib, niacin, niacinamide, quinine, ranolazine, rifamycin derivatives, antacids, bosentan, CYP3A4 inducers and inhibitors, deferasirox, etravirine, phenytoin, St. John’s wort. Alcohol, grapefruit juice, red yeast rice."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 20 mg (P19.65), 40 mg (P30.36)."
          }
        ],
        "company": {

          },

            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Prevention and treatment of mild to moderate dehydration. Provides zinc that reduces the rates of diarrhea."

            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Dissolve 1 sachet in 250 mL of freshly boiled and cooled water. Adults and adolescents: 1,000 mL; childn: 500 mL; infants up to 2 yrs: 250 mL. For each large watery stool in infants and childn: 50-100 mL of prepared soln. Give as needed to prevent dehydration. Consume within 24 hrs after preparation. Taken with or without food."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {

        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Tadalafil",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Drugs Used in Erectile Dysfunction"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of erectile dysfunction (ED). <b>5 mg FC tab</b>: Treatment of signs and symptoms of benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>ED</b>: 5 mg once daily at approx. same time every day. Alternatively, 10 mg once a day, given prior to anticipated sexual activity, may be increased to 20 mg or decreased to 5 mg. <b>BPH</b>: 5 mg once daily at approx. same time every day. In combination with finasteride: 5 mg once daily for 26 weeks. <b>Renal impairment</b> – CrCl 30-50 mL/min: 5 mg/day. Max 10 mg, not more than once every 48 hrs; &gt;30 mL/min or on hemodialysis: 5 mg, not more than once in every 72 hrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Any form of organic nitrates. Severe hepatic impairment (Child Pugh Class C). Concomitant guanylate cyclase (GC) stimulators."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Mild or moderate hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh Class A or B). Renal impairment (CrCl < 30 mL/min) or on hemodialysis. Patients with left ventricular outflow obstruction; CV disease e.g. MI, unstable angina or angina occurring during sexual intercourse, heart failure NYHA class 2 or greater last 6 months, uncontrolled arrhythmias, hypotension (< 90/50 mmHg), or uncontrolled HTN, stroke (within last 6 months); conditions that may predispose to priapism, anatomical deformation of the penis. Sudden loss of vision in one or both eyes. Patients with underlying non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION). Individuals with \"crowded\" optic discs. Concomitant use of alpha-blockers, antihypertensives, CYP3A4 inhibitors. Childn.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Headache, dyspepsia, nasopharyngitis, back pain, URTI, flushing, myalgia, cough, diarrhea, nasal congestion, pain in extremity, GERD, abdominal pain."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Alpha blockers (doxazosin, tamsulosin, alfuzosin), antihypertensives (amlodipine, ARBs, enalapril, metoprolol), antacids (magnesium hydroxide/aluminum hydroxide). Ketoconazole, erythromycin, itraconazole, grapefruit juice. Ritonavir, rifampicin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, phenobarbital."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 5 mg, 20 mg."
          }
        ],

            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Quinolones"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of bacterial exacerbations in bronchitis, bacterial prostatitis, acute sinusitis, typhoid fever, lower respiratory tract infections (LRTI)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults and elderly - Inhalational anthrax</b>: 500 mg every 12 hrs for 60 days. <b>Bone and joint infections</b> - Mild to moderate: 500 mg every 12 hrs for at least 4-6 weeks; <b>Severe or complicated</b>: 750 mg every 12 hrs for at least 4-6 weeks. <b>Mild to moderate infectious diarrhea</b>: 500 mg 12 for 5-7 days. <b>Endocervical and urethral gonorrhea</b>: 250 mg as a single dose. <b>Intra-abdominal infections</b>: 500 mg every 12 hrs for 7-14 days in combination with oral metronidazole. <b>LRTI, skin, and soft skin tissue infection</b> - Mild to moderate: 500 every 12 hrs for least 7-14 days; Severe or complicated: 750 mg every 12 hrs for 7-14 days. <b>Mild to moderate chronic prostatitis</b>: 500 mg every 12 hrs for 28 days. <b>Mild to moderate sinusitis or typhoid fever</b>: 500 mg every 12 hrs for 10 days. <b>UTI</b> - Acute complicated: 100 mg 12 hrs for 3 days; Mild to moderate: 250 mg 12 days 7-14 days; Severe or complicated: 500 mg every 12 for 7-14 days. Max 1.5 g daily. <b>Childn &le;18 yrs</b>: Given only when alternative therapy could not be used. <b>Inhalational anthrax</b>: 15 mg/kg every 12 hrs for 60 days. Max 500 mg mg/dose. <b>Other infections</b>: 10-15 mg/kg twice daily, up to 1.5 g/day."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. History of tendinitis or tendon rupture. Hepatic and renal impairment."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with epilepsy, or history of CNS disorders. Elderly. Childn and adolescents &le;18 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Dizziness or lightheadedness, drowsiness, nausea, vomiting, headache, nervousness, insomnia, mild abdominal or stomach pain or discomfort, mild diarrhea."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Aminophylline, oxtriphylline, theophylline, magnesium and aluminum antacids, ferrous sulfate, zinc, sucralfate, phenytoin, ciclosporin, didanosine, warfarin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 500 mg (P35.00)."
          }
        ],

        "content": "Cilostazol",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Antiplatelets"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of ischemic symptoms including ulcer, pain, and coldness of extremities, in chronic arterial occlusion. Prevention of reoccurrence of cerebral infarction (excluding cardiogenic cerebral embolism)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "200 mg every 24 hrs, taken at least 30 mins before or 2 hrs after meals."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with known predisposition to bleeding (e.g. active peptic ulceration, recent (within 6 months), hemorrhagic stroke, proliferative diabetic retinopathy, poorly controlled HTN). Patients with CHF. Women of childbearing potential. Pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients using anticoagulants, prostaglandin E1 or derivatives. Severe renal impairment (CrCl &le;25 mL/min). Moderate or severe hepatic impairment. Patients with history of ventricular tachycardia, ventricular fibrillation or multifocal ventricular ectopics, prolongation of QT interval; menstruation, predisposition to bleeding e.g. active peptic ulceration, recent hemorrhagic stroke (within 6 months), proliferative diabetic retinopathy, poorly controlled HTN. Elderly. Lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Arrhythmia e.g. arterial fibrillation, ventricular tachycardia, premature ventricular contraction, decline in BP. Tremor, dizziness. Anemia, ecchymosis, iron deficiency anemia, polycythemia, purpura. Increased creatinine, gout, hyperlipemia, hyperuricemia. Arthralgia, bone pain, bursitis. Anxiety, insomnia, neuralgia. DM, asthma, epistaxis, hemoptysis, pneumonia, sinusitis. Dry skin, furunculosis, skin hypertrophy, urticaria. Amblyopia, blindness, conjunctivitis, diplopia, ear pain, eye hemorrhage, retinal hemorrhage, tinnitus. Albuminuria, cystitis, urinary frequency, vaginal hemorrhage, vaginitis. Pyrexia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Warfarin, aspirin, ticlodipine, urokinase, alteplase. Alprostadil, rimaprodex, alphadex. Erythromycin, cimetidine, grapefruit juice, diltiazem, omeprazole."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Controlled-release tablet 200 mg."
          }
        ],

          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Childn and adolescents."
          },

            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Severe and persistent diarrhea during or after treatment may mask symptoms of pseudomembranous colitis. Patients with epilepsy and history of CNS disorders. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category C.",

    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 3838,
        "brand_name": "Cirok IV",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/sTWJi8ic6uQkiXnGhA8bzSVy8fxYbvHUbXLbi8NEl7NhCMyPiO.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/IqYqwEAJsCsVc4YjSZQiHMt5L0TGAxEiZXiBq55GFIPn0KONPZ.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/SzCYwAzcKJE9IW3385ZQAX8eOTv8C24NYzYupCuxkqHQgH8gcf.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Ciprofloxacin",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Quinolones"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "<b>Adults</b>: Treatment of lower respiratory tract infections (LRTI) due to G(-) bacteria e.g. exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), broncho-pulmonary infections in cystic fibrosis or in bronchiectasis, pneumonia; URTI e.g. chronic suppurative otitis media; acute exacerbation of chronic sinusitis; urinary tract infections (UTI); genital tract infections e.g. epididymo-orchitis, pelvic inflammatory disease (PID); infections of the GIT (e.g. traveler’s diarrhea); intra-abdominal infections; infections of the skin and soft tissue; malignant external otitis; infections of bone and joints; inhalation anthrax (post-exposure prophylaxis and curative treatment). Management of neutropenic patients with fever due to bacterial infection. <b>Childn and adolescents</b>: Broncho-pulmonary infections in cystic fibrosis; complicated UTI and pyelonephritis; inhalation anthrax (post-exposure prophylaxis and curative treatment)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults – LRTI, URTI</b>: 400 mg 2-3x daily for 7-14 days. <b>Malignant external otitis</b>: 400 mg 3x daily for 28 days up to 3 months. <b>UTI – Complicated and uncomplicated pyelonephritis</b>: 400 mg 2-3x daily for 7-21 days. <b>Prostatitis</b>: 400 mg 2-3x daily for 2-4 weeks (acute). <b>Epididymo-orchitis and PID</b>: 400 mg 2-3x daily for at least 14 days. <b>GIT and intra-abdominal infections – Diarrhea caused by <i>Shigella</i> spp. and severe traveler’s diarrhea</b>: 400 mg twice daily for 1 day. <b>By <i>Shigella dysenteriae</i></b>: 400 mg twice daily for 5 days. <b>By <i>Vibrio cholerae</i></b>: 400 mg twice daily for 3 days. <b>Typhoid fever</b>: 400 mg twice daily for 7 days. <b>Intra-abdominal infections due to G(-)</b>: 400 mg 2-3x daily for 5-14 days. <b>Infections of the skin and soft tissue</b>: 400 mg 2-3x daily for 7-14 days. <b>Bone and joint infections</b>: 400 mg 2-3x daily for max 3 months. <b>Neutropenic patients with fever suspected to be due to bacterial infections</b>: 400 mg 2-3x daily continued over the entire period of neutropenia. <b>Inhalation anthrax post-exposure prophylaxis</b>: 400 mg twice daily for 60 days (from <i>B. anthracis</i> exposure). <b>Childn – Cystic fibrosis</b>: 10 mg/kg BW thrice daily for 10-14 days. Max 400 mg. <b>Complicated UTI and pyelonephritis</b>: 6-10 mg/kg thrice daily for 10-21 days. Max 400 mg. <b>Inhalation anthrax post-exposure prophylaxis</b>: 10-15 mg/kg twice daily for 60 days (from <i>B. anthracis</i> exposure). Max 400 mg. <b>Renal impairment</b> – CrCl 30-60 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>: 200-400 mg every 12 hrs. &lt;30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>: 200-400 mg every 24 hrs. <b>Hemodialysis, peritoneal dialysis</b>: 200-400 mg every 24 hrs (after dialysis)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Concomitant administration of tizanidine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not suited for treatment of severe and mixed infections with G(+) and anaerobic pathogens, streptococcal infections (e.g. <i>S. pneumoniae</i>). Patients with history of tendon disease/disorder related to quinolone treatment; myasthenia gravis. Patients with family history of aneurysm disease, or diagnosed with pre-existing aortic aneurysm and/or dissection (e.g. Marfan syndrome, vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, Takayasu arteritis, giant cell arteritis, Behcet’s disease, HTN, known atherosclerosis). Avoid direct exposure to either extensive sunlight or UV irradiation during treatment. Patients with known risk factors for prolongation of QT interval. Concomitant use of drugs known to prolong QT interval e.g. Class IA and III anti-arrhythmic, TCAs, macrolides, antipsychotics). Uncorrected electrolyte imbalance (e.g. hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia), cardiac disease (e.g. heart failure, MI, bradycardia). May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, transient increase in transaminases, rash, injection and infusion site reactions."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Drugs known to prolong QT interval, probenecid, tizanidine, methotrexate, theophylline, caffeine or pentoxifylline (oxpentifylline), phenytoin, ciclosporin, vit K antagonists, ropinirole, lidocaine, clozapine, sildenafil, zolpidem."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Solution for IV infusion 2 mg/mL x 100 mL."
          }
        ],

          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",

          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "<b>Adults</b>: Lower respiratory tract infections (LRTI) e.g. exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, broncho-pulmonary infections in cystic fibrosis or in bronchiectasis, pneumonia; URTI e.g. chronic suppurative otitis media, acute exacerbation of chronic sinusitis; urinary tract infections (UTI), genital tract infections; gonococcal urethritis and cervicitis, epididymo-orchitis, and pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) including cases due to <i>Neisseria gonorrhea</i>; gastrointestinal (GI) infections, intra-abdominal infections, infections of skin and soft tissue, malignant external otitis, infections of bones and joints. Treatment and prophylaxis of infections in neutropenic patients. Prophylaxis of invasive <i>N. meningitides</i> infections. Post-exposure and curative treatment of inhalation anthrax. Management of neutropenic patients with fever suspected due to bacterial infection. <b>Childn</b>: Bronchopulmonary infections in cystic fibrosis and/or severe infections in childn and adolescents."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults – LRTI</b>: 500-750 mg twice daily for 7-14 days. <b>URTI</b>: 500-750 mg twice daily for 7-14 days. <b>Malignant external otitis</b>: 750 mg twice daily for 7-14 days. <b>Uncomplicated cystitis</b>: 250-500 mg twice daily for 3 days; in premenopausal women: 500 mg as single dose. <b>Complicated cystitis, uncomplicated pyelonephritis</b>: 500 mg twice daily for 7 days. <b>Complicated pyelonephritis</b>: 500-750 mg twice daily for at least 10 days; can be continued for longer than 21 days. <b>Prostatitis</b>: 500-750 mg twice daily for 2-4 weeks for acute and 4-6 weeks for chronic. <b>Gonococcal urethritis and cervicitis</b>: 500 mg as single dose for 1 day. <b>Epididymo-orchitis and PID</b>: 500-750 mg twice daily for at least 14 days. <b>Diarrhea caused by bacterial pathogens (including <i>Shigella</i> spp.)</b>: 500 mg twice daily for 1 day; if caused by <i>Shigella dysenteriae</i> type 1:  500 mg twice daily for 5 days; if caused by <i>Vibrio cholera</i>: 500 mg twice daily for 3 days. <b>Typhoid fever</b>: 500 mg twice daily for 7 days. <b>Intra-abdominal infections due to G(-) bacteria</b>: 500-750 mg twice daily for 5-14 days. <b>Infections of skin and soft tissue</b>: 500-750 mg twice daily for 7-14 days. <b>Bone and joint infections</b>: 500-750 mg twice daily for max of 3 months. <b>Treatment of infections or prophylaxis of infections in neutropenic patients</b>: 500-750 mg twice daily. Continue therapy over entire period of neutropenia. <b>Prophylaxis of invasive infections due to <i>N. meningitides</i></b>: 500 mg given as single dose for 1 day. <b>Childn – Cystic fibrosis</b>: 20 mg/kg BW twice daily for 10-14 days. Max 750 mg/dose. <b>Complicated UTI, pyelonephritis</b>: 10-20 mg/kg BW twice daily for 10-21 days. Max 750 mg/dose. <b>Inhalational anthrax post-exposure prophylaxis and as curative treatment by oral route</b>: 10-15 mg/kg BW twice daily for 60 days from confirmation of <i>Bacillus anthracis</i> exposure. Max 500 mg/dose. <b>Other severe infections</b>: 20 mg/kg BW twice daily. Max 750 mg/dose. <b>Renal impairment</b> – CrCl 30-60 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>: 250-500 mg every 12 hrs. &lt;30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>: 250-500 mg every 24 hrs. Patients on hemodialysis: 250-500 mg every 24 hrs (after dialysis). Patients on peritoneal dialysis: 250-500 mg every 24 hrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Concomitant use of tizanidine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Hypoglycemia. Not suited for severe infections and mixed infections due to G (+) and anaerobic pathogens; streptococcal infections. Visual impairment. Avoid direct exposure to either extensive sunlight or UV irradiation during treatment. Patients with G6PD; history of tendon disease, myasthenia gravis; CNS disorders which may be predisposed to seizure; known risk factors for prolongation of QT intervals e.g. congenital long QT syndrome, concomitant use of drugs known to prolong QT intervals, uncorrected electrolyte imbalance, cardiac disease. Patients with DM. Concomitant use of methotrexate. Coadministration of multivalent cation-containing products, dairy and mineral-fortified drinks. May impair ability to drive and operate machinery. Childn. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nausea, diarrhea."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Class IA and III anti-arrhythmics, TCAs, macrolides, antipsychotics. Probenecid, omeprazole. Tizanidine, methotrexate, xanthine derivatives, phenytoin, ciclosporin, vit K antagonists, zolpidem, ropinirole, lozapine, sevelamer, sildenafil. False negative bacteriological test results for <i>M. tuberculosis</i>."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 500 mg."
          }

  {
    "id": 1411,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 1411,
        "brand_name": "Citagem",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/PGg0dRxJCnQDixfuRL60MQ11wl1afGqMhTYxtv8BbN9Gv7acFN.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/V2COnyHIjn90PKWip99xtucajBstK60tFKaP9d0XJPxLYf6JnT.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/bIHoEHO8SxAFkBkIQSPYF4nQLdVM5C41CuizBLpVq1fmpCVO4p.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Gemcitabine HCl",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Pyrimidine Analogs & Antagonists"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of recurrent epithelial ovarian carcinoma in patients who have relapsed at least 6 months following platinum-based therapy in combination with carboplatin. 1<sup>st</sup> line treatment in patients with unresectable, locally recurrent or metastatic breast cancer who have relapsed following adjuvant or neoadjuvant chemotherapy in combination with paclitaxel; inoperable, locally advanced (stage IIIA or IIIB) or metastatic (stage IV) non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) alone or in combination with cisplatin; locally advanced or (non-resectable stage II or III) or metastatic (stage IV) adenocarcinoma of the pancreas. 1<sup>st</sup> or 2<sup>nd</sup> line therapy in 5-fluorouracil refractory pancreatic cancer. Treatment of advanced transitional cell bladder cancer in combination with cisplatin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "IV infusion over 30 mins but not more than 60 mins and not more frequent than once a week. <b>Adults - Ovarian cancer</b>: Gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m2 on days 1 and 8 of each 21-day cycle; carboplatin should be administered after, on day 1 consistent with a target AUC of 4 mg/mL/min. <b>Breast cancer</b>: Gemcitabine 1,250 mg/m<sup>2</sup> on days 1 and 8 of each 21-day cycle; paclitaxel 175 mg/m<sup>2</sup> administered on day 1 over approximately 3 hrs as IV infusion before the administration of gemcitabine. <b>NSCLC – Monotherapy</b>: 1,000 mg/m<sup>2</sup> repeated once a week for 3 weeks, followed by a 1-week rest period. The 4-week cycle is then repeated. <b>Combination therapy - 3-week schedule</b>: Gemcitabine 1,250 mg/m<sup>2</sup> on days 1 and 8 of each 21-day cycle; cisplatin 100 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV administered on day 1 after gemcitabine infusion. <b>4-week schedule</b>: Gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m<sup>2</sup> on days 1, 8, and 15 of each 21-day cycle; cisplatin 100 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV administered on day 1 after gemcitabine infusion. <b>Pancreatic cancer</b>: 1,000 mg/m<sup>2</sup> repeated once a week for up to 7 weeks, followed by a 1-week rest period. Subsequent cycles should consist of injection once a week for 3 consecutive weeks out of every 4 weeks. <b>Bladder cancer – Monotherapy</b>: 1,250 mg/m<sup>2</sup> on days 1, 8, and 15 of each 28-day cycle. This 4-week cycle is then repeated. <b>Combination therapy</b>: Gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m<sup>2</sup> on days 1, 8 and 15 of each 28-day cycle; cisplatin 70 mg/m<sup>2</sup> administered on day 1 following gemcitabine or day 2 of each 28-day cycle. This 4-week cycle is then repeated."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with compromised bone marrow reserve due to prior irradiation or chemotherapy; recovering bone marrow function; history of CV diseases.           {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Constipation: Regulation of the physiological rhythm of the colon. Where a soft stool is considered of medical benefit (hemorrhoids, post colonic/anal surgery). Hepatic encephalopathy: Treatment and prevention of hepatic coma or pre-coma. For bowel cleansing in preparation for colonoscopy (adults). As a prebiotic, which helps create and maintain a healthy intestinal balance and stimulates the intestinal absorption of minerals e.g. calcium and magnesium (adults)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Constipation</b> - Adults: 15-45 mL initial dose, 15-30 mL maintenance dose. Childn 7-14 yrs: 15 mL initial dose, 10-15 mL maintenance dose; 1-6 yrs: 5-10 mL. Infants: Up to 5 mL. As single dose or in divided doses. <b>Hepatic encephalopathy:</b> Initial dose 30-45 mL 3-4x daily; maintenance dose adjusted individually to obtain soft feces. <b>Bowel cleansing:</b> A course of treatment consists of taking 10 mg of bisacodyl in the evening before colonoscopy. <b>Prebiotic:</b> 7.5-15 mL daily (5-10 g/day)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Galactosemia, bowel obstruction. For bowel cleansing, should not be used for unconscious patients or those with impaired consciousness and patients prone to aspiration or regurgitation."

  {
    "id": 2827,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 2827,
        "brand_name": "Duphaston",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/rXXO6pULxYRcaSrfo8GV2QDDxfYPVqICvd6jWOn18nKsSxZMPW.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/v5xKnnxwoO7oigG1mtybG3ipqu0asWtoJA1jRT5iSJjIUAoVzF.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/O24UXOssvWamRZSS9PIxtvFy0tbkEOd90Ts99MKCtLOq0rJ0k2.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Dydrogesterone",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Progestogens (Progestins)"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Threatened and habitual miscarriage, dysmenorrhea, endometriosis, secondary amenorrhea, irregular cycles, dysfunctional uterine bleeding, pre-menstrual syndrome (PMS), infertility due to luteal insufficiency. Luteal support as part of an Assisted Reproductive Technology (ART) treatment. Hormone replacement therapy (HRT) for women with disorders due to natural or surgical-induced menopause with an intact uterus."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Threatened miscarriage:</b> 40 mg at once, then 20 or 30 mg daily until symptoms remit. <b>Habitual miscarriage:</b> 10 mg twice daily until the 12<sup>th</sup> week of pregnancy. <b>Dysmenorrhea:</b> 10 or 20 mg daily from day 5-25 of the cycle. <b>Endometriosis:</b> 10-30 mg daily from day 5-25 of the cycle or continuously. <b>Secondary amenorrhea:</b> 10 or 20 mg daily for 14 days during the 2<sup>nd</sup> half of the theoretical menstrual cycle. <b>Irregular cycles:</b> 10 or 20 mg daily starting with the 2<sup>nd</sup> half of the menstrual cycle until the 1<sup>st</sup> day of the next cycle. <b>Dysfunctional uterine bleeding</b> - To arrest bleeding: 20 or 30 mg daily for up to 10 days. To prevent bleeding: 10 or 20 mg during the 2<sup>nd</sup> half of the menstrual cycle. <b>PMS:</b> 10 mg twice daily starting with the 2<sup>nd</sup> half of the menstrual cycle until the 1<sup>st</sup> day of the next cycle. <b>Infertility due to luteal insufficiency:</b> 10 or 20 mg daily starting with the 2<sup>nd</sup> half of the menstrual cycle until the 1<sup>st</sup> day of the next cycle. <b>Luteal support as part of ART treatment:</b> 1 tab of 10 mg thrice daily (30 mg daily) starting at the day of oocyte retrieval and continuing for 10 weeks if pregnancy is confirmed. <b>HRT</b> - Continuous sequential therapy: An estrogen is dosed continuously and 1 tab of 10 mg dydrogesterone is added for the last 14 days of every 28-day cycle. Cyclic therapy: When an estrogen is dosed cyclically with a treatment-free interval, usually 21 days on and 7 days off. 1 tab of 10 mg dydrogesterone is added for the last 12-14 days of estrogen therapy. Depending on the clinical response, the dosage can subsequently be adjusted to 20 mg/day."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Known or suspected progestogen-dependent neoplasms, undiagnosed vaginal bleeding. Treatment for luteal support as part of an ART treatment should be discontinued upon diagnosis of abortion or miscarriage. Use in combination with estrogen. Lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Breakthrough bleeding or spotting. Porphyria, depression, abnormal liver function values caused by acute or chronic liver disease. Perform a complete personal and family medical history before initiating HRT. Risk of endometrial hyperplasia, carcinoma, breast and ovarian cancer, VTE, CAD, and ischemic stroke. Patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, the Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. May impair ability to drive or operate machines.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Vaginal hemorrhage, migraines or headache, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, menstrual disorders, and breast pain or tenderness."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Anticonvulsants (e.g. phenobarbital, phenytoin, carbamazepine), anti-infectives (e.g. rifampicin, rifabutin, nevirapine, efavirenz), herbal preparations containing (e.g. St. John’s wort, sage, ginkgo biloba), ritonavir, and nelfinavir."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 10 mg (P89.50)."
          }
        ],
        "company": {
          "id": 10,

        },

        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Beta Blockers (Antihypertensives)"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "HTN, angina pectoris, cardiac arrhythmias, and MI (early and late intervention)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>HTN:</b> 50 mg daily, max 100 mg. Give doses >100 mg daily in divided doses. <b>Angina pectoris:</b> 50 mg daily, may be increased to 100 mg daily as single or divided dose. <b>Cardiac arrhythmias:</b> 50-100 mg daily. <b>MI:</b> Initially controlled by IV, followed by 50 mg orally after 15 mins. Followed by further 50 mg orally 12 hrs after IV dose and then 12 hrs later by 100 mg orally once daily. Late intervention after acute MI: 100 mg daily for long-term prophylaxis. <b>Elderly, CrCl < 35 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>:</b> Lower dose."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Asthma. HF. 2<sup>nd</sup> or 3<sup>rd</sup> degree heart block. Poor cardiac reserve."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Avoid abrupt withdrawal. May increase the number and duration of angina attacks in Prinzmetal’s angina; aggravate less severe peripheral arterial circulatory disturbances; mask hypoglycemia and symptoms or signs of thyrotoxicosis. Angioedema and urticaria. Patients with poor cardiac reserve; 1st degree heart block; history of anaphylactic reaction; CrCl < 35 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>. Discontinue if bradycardia and/or hypotension requiring treatment occur. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Bradycardia, HF, bronchospasm, peripheral vasoconstriction, GI and sleep disturbances, fatigue."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Adrenaline, clonidine, digoxin, insulin, acarbose, gliclazide, metformin, ibuprofen, ketoprofen, mefenamic acid, verapamil, diltiazem, nifedipine, alfuzosin, doxazosin, prazosin, terazosin, quinidine, St. John’s Wort, fenoterol, formoterol, salmeterol, aluminum, calcium or magnesium-containing antacids, warfarin, chlorpromazine, methyldopa, glycopyrrolate."
          },

            "content": "Urinary Alkalinizers"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Management of renal tubular acidosis with calcium stones, hypocitraturic calcium oxalate nephrolithiasis of any etiology and uric acid lithiasis with or without calcium stones."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Severe hypocitraturia (urinary citrate &lt;150 mg/day)</b>: 60 mEq/day (20 mEq thrice daily or 15 mEq/day with meals or within 30 mins after meals or bedtime snack). <b>Mild to moderate hypocitraturia (>150 mg/day)</b>: 30 mEq/day (10 mEq thrice daily with meals). Do not crush, chew or suck tab."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Patients with hyperkalemia or conditions predisposing hyperkalemia e.g. chronic renal failure, uncontrolled DM, acute dehydration, strenuous physical exercise in unconditioned individuals, adrenal insufficiency, extensive tissue breakdown, PUD, renal insufficiency (GFR &lt;0.7 mL/kg/min). Concomitant use with potassium-sparing agents e.g. triamterene, spironolactone or amiloride. Patients whom there is cause for arrest or delay in tab passage through GIT e.g. delayed gastric emptying, esophageal compression, intestinal obstruction or stricture or those taking anticholinergic medication."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Measure urinary citrate and pH every 4 months. Patients with chronic renal failure, severe myocardial damage or heart failure.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Minor GI complaints e.g. abdominal discomfort, vomiting, diarrhea, loose bowel movement or nausea."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Triamterene, spironolactone or amiloride."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Extended-release tablet 1,080 mg (equiv to 10 mEq) (P16.00)."
