          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/ybXK2fursBvNPpk5hlDjBfy61KwgTJA4Ibgb8XENBUGU1tsPaU.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Dydrogesterone",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Progestogens (Progestins)"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Management of conditions associated with progesterone insufficiency: dysmenorrhea, endometriosis, infertility, irregular menstrual cycles, and pre-menstrual syndrome (PMS). Management of dysfunctional bleeding or secondary amenorrhea, or in association with estrogen in hormone replacement therapy (HRT)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Dysfunctional uterine bleeding</b> - To arrest bleeding episode: 10 mg twice daily for 5-7 days. For continuous treatment: 10 mg twice daily from day 11-25 of the cycle. <b>Secondary amenorrhea, irregular cycles</b>: 10 mg twice daily from day 11-25. <b>PMS</b>: 10 mg twice daily from day 12-26 of the cycle. <b>Endometriosis, dysmenorrhea</b>: 10 mg twice daily from day 5-25 of the cycle. <b>Infertility due to luteal insufficiency</b>: 10 mg twice daily from day 11-25 of the cycle. Treatment should be maintained for at least 3 consecutive cycles. <b>HRT</b>: 10 mg daily for the 14 days of each 28-day estrogen treatment cycle, may be increased to 10 mg twice daily if either early withdrawal bleeding occurs or if endometrial biopsy reveals inadequate progestational response."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Known or suspected sex hormone dependent malignancies. Vaginal bleeding. Presence of serious liver disorders."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Exclude organic cause of dysfunctional uterine bleeding. Breakthrough bleeding and spotting may occur. Consider discontinuation if exceptionally severe headache, migraine, symptoms that may indicate cerebral ischemia; marked increase in BP; or VTE occurs. Patient with history of depression, rare hereditary conditions e.g. galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Migraine, headache, nausea. Disturbed menstruation, painful/sensitive breast."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Phenobarbital, phenytoin, carbamazepine. Rifampicin, rifabutin, nevirapine, efavirenz. St. John’s wort, valerian root, sage and ginkgo biloba."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 10 mg."
          }
        ],

            "content": "Treatment of asymptomatic and symptomatic trichomoniasis, infections due to susceptible anaerobic bacteria, intestinal and hepatic amebiasis and giardiasis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Trichomoniasis</b> - </b>Adults:</b> 2 g single dose, or 800 mg in the morning and 1.2 g in the evening for 2 days, or 600 mg-1 g daily in 2 or 3 divided doses for 7 days. <b>Anaerobic bacterial infections:</b> 800 mg followed by 400 mg every 8 hrs for 7 days. <b>Amebiasis</b> - <b>Adults:</b> 400-800 mg thrice daily for 5-10 days, or 1.5-2.5 g single dose for 2-3 days; <b>Childn 7-10 yrs:</b> &frac12;; 3-7 yrs: &frac13;; 1-3 yrs: &frac14; of the total adult daily dose; alternatively, 35-50 mg/kg in divided doses. <b>Giardiasis</b> - <b>Adults:</b> 2 g once daily for 3 days, or 400 mg thrice daily for 5 days, or 500 mg twice daily for 7-10 days; <b>Childn:</b> 15 mg/kg/day in divided doses."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Blood dyscrasia. Pregnancy (1<sup>st</sup> trimester)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Monitor for neurological signs, <i>Candida</i> overgrowth. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "GI disturbances, nausea, metallic taste, vomiting, diarrhea or constipation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Disulfiram, warfarin, phenytoin, lithium, ciclosporin, fluorouracil, phenobarbital, cimetidine. Alcohol."

          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with ileus, intestinal obstruction, acute abdominal conditions (including appendicitis and acute IBD), severe abdominal pain associated with nausea and vomiting; severe dehydration."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not for prolonged use. Patients with galactose intolerance (e.g. galactosemia), fructose intolerance. Hematochezia; dizziness and/or syncope. Childn &le;10 yrs with chronic or persistent constipation. Pregnancy.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Abdominal pain, diarrhea."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Diuretics, adrenocorticosteroids, other laxatives."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Enteric-coated tablet 5 mg."
          }
        ],

        "brand_shot": {

          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/LJhycJzejpvmx9oEYZdIr3WhrrPZ48sePvdA6XhgnuWLs9Hm4U.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/NWMYm2WUjIxxAzKmvlQETUjL85UCogovyPejwM5HMMPhlbynxt.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Carvedilol",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Beta Blockers (Antihypertensives)"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Essential HTN. Chronic stable angina pectoris. Adjunctive treatment of moderate to severe stable CHF."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Essential HTN - Adults:</b> Initially 12.5 mg once daily for first two days, continued at 25 mg/day; <b>Elderly:</b> 12.5 mg once daily as initial and maintenance dose. May be further increased gradually at intervals of &ge;2 weeks. Max 25 mg as single dose and max 50 mg daily. <b>Chronic stable angina pectoris -  Adults and elderly:</b> 12.5 mg twice daily for first two days, continued at 25 mg twice daily (max dose for elderly). May be further increased gradually at intervals of &ge;2 weeks (adults). <b>HF:</b> 3.125 mg twice daily for 2 weeks, may be increased slowly with intervals of not < 2 weeks up to 6.25 mg twice daily, then up to 12.5 mg twice daily, and finally up to 25 mg twice daily. Max 25 mg twice daily for BW < 85 kg; 50 mg twice daily for BW >85 kg if HF is not severe. Taken with food in patients with HF."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. HF (NYHA Class IV) with marked fluid retention or overload requiring IV inotropic. COPD with bronchial obstruction. Clinically significant hepatic dysfunction. Bronchial asthma. 2<sup>nd</sup> or 3<sup>rd</sup> degree AV block. Severe bradycardia (< 50 bpm). Sick sinus syndrome (including sinoatrial block). Cardiogenic shock. Severe hypotension (< 85 mmHg SBP). Prinzmetal’s angina. Untreated pheochromocytoma. Metabolic acidosis. Severe peripheral arterial circulatory disturbance. Concomitant IV verapamil or diltiazem. Rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, fructose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption, sucrase-isomaltase insufficiency. Lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Avoid abrupt withdrawal. CHF treated with digitalis; suspected Prinzmetal’s angina; COPD with risk of bronchospasms not treated with oral or inhalation drug; wearing contact lenses; history of serious hypersensitivity and undergoing desensitization therapy; psoriasis; peripheral vascular diseases; Raynaud’s syndrome; poor metabolizers of debrisoquine; pheochromocytoma; 1<sup>st</sup> degree AV block; use of anesthetics. Monitor patients with severe HF, salt and vol-depleted, elderly, or low basic BP for 2 hrs after treatment initiation or dose increase. Hypotension. Worsening of HF or fluid retention. May mask symptoms and signs of acute hypoglycemia and thyrotoxicosis. Bradycardia. Impaired blood glucose control in DM and HF. Manage symptoms due to worsening HF or hypotension due to vasodilation before dose increase. Reduce dose or discontinue therapy if significant worsening renal function occurs. Do not administer in labile or secondary HTN, orthostasis, acute inflammatory heart disease, concomitant alpha 1-receptor antagonist and alpha 2-receptor agonist. Childn < 18 yrs. Elderly. Pregnancy.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Dizziness, headache, cardiac failure, hypotension, asthenia, bronchitis, pneumonia, URTI, UTI, anemia, increased weight, hypercholesterolemia, hyperglycemia/hypoglycemia (in pre-existing DM), depression, depressed mood, visual impairment, decreased lacrimation, eye irritation, bradycardia, edema, hypervolemia, fluid overload, orthostatic hypotension, peripheral circulation disturbances (cold extremities, peripheral vascular disease, exacerbation of intermittent claudication and Raynauld’s phenomenon) dyspnea, pulmonary edema, asthma, pain in extremities, renal failure and function abnormalities in diffuse vascular and/or underlying renal insufficiency, pain."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Diltiazem, cimetidine, antiarrhythmics, dihydropyridines, nitrates, cardiac glycosides, other antihypertensives, antidiabetics, clonidine, inhalational anesthetics, NSAIDs, estrogens, corticosteroids, CYP450 inducers (e.g., rifampicin, barbiturates) and inhibitors (e.g., cimetidine, ketoconazole, fluoxetine haloperidol, verapamil, erythromycin), alpha- and beta-sympathomimetics, ergotamine, neuromuscular blockers."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 6.25 mg (P7.00), 25 mg (P16.00)."
          }
        ],

  {
    "id": 435,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 435,
        "brand_name": "Dynastat",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Parecoxib",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "COX-2 Specific Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "For short-term treatment of acute pain and post-op pain i.e. oral surgery, abdominal hysterectomy, myomectomy, total knee replacement, total hip arthroplasty, laparoscopic cholecystectomy, inguinal hernia repair, and other general surgery e.g. diagnostic laparoscopy, gastrectomy, hernioplasty, appendectomy, hemithyroidectomy and splenectomy. May be used pre-op to prevent or reduce post-op pain and it can reduce opioid requirements used concomitantly."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Management of acute pain:</b> Single or initial dose of 40 mg slow IM or IV bolus, followed by 20 mg or 40 mg every 6-12 hrs. Max 80 mg/day. <b>Prevention or reduction of post-op pain:</b> 40 mg IM or IV 30-45 mins prior to surgical incision. Continue medication post-op for adequate analgesic effect. <b>Elderly weighing < 50 kg:</b> Reduce initial dose by 50%. Max 40 mg/day. <b>Patients with severe renal impairment (CrCl < 30 mL/min) or who may be predisposed to fluid retention:</b> Lowest recommended dose and patient's kidney function closely monitored. <b>Patients with moderate hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh B), and concurrently taking fluconazole:</b> Lowest recommended dose."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to sulfonamides, previous allergic drug reaction especially cutaneous reactions (e.g., SJS, TEN, erythema multiforme). History of CVA, MI, CABG, uncontrolled HTN, CHF (NYHA II-IV). Active peptic ulceration or GI bleeding. Patients who experienced bronchospasm, acute rhinitis, nasal polyps, bronchial asthma, angioneurotic edema, urticaria or other allergic-type reactions after taking aspirin or NSAIDs. Severe hepatic dysfunction. IBD, treatment of post-op pain immediately following CABG surgery. Established IHD, PAD and/or cerebrovascular disease. Pregnancy (3<sup>rd</sup> trimester) and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Increased risk of CV and thrombotic adverse events on long term treatment. Not recommended in patients with severe hepatic impairment. Upper GI perforations, ulcers, or bleeding; severe hypotension. Patients with CV disease, concomitantly using aspirin, corticosteroids, SSRIs, other antiplatelet drugs or NSAIDs, ingesting alcohol, with history of, or active GI diseases; concomitant use of anticoagulants; HTN; compromised cardiac function, pre-existing edema, or other condition predisposing to, or worsened by fluid retention in diuretic treatment or at risk of hypovolemia. Closely monitor BP during initiation and throughout the course of therapy; renal function in patients with advanced renal disease. Rehydrate patients with dehydration prior to treatment. Discontinue treatment at 1<sup>st</sup> appearance of skin rash, mucosal lesion or any sign of hypersensitivity. May impair diagnostic signs in detecting infections (e.g., fever). Female fertility. Elderly. Childn < 18 yrs.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nausea, abdominal pain, constipation, dyspepsia, vomiting, peripheral edema, alveolar osteitis (dry socket), dizziness, insomnia, oliguria, increased sweating, pruritis, hypotension."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Fluconazole, ketoconazole, ACE inhibitors, ARBs, beta-blockers, diuretics, ciclosporin, methotrexate lithium."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Lyophilized powder for injection (IM/IV) 40 mg."
          }
        ],
        "company": {
          "id": 221,
          "name": "Zuellig Pharma Corp."
        },

      "data": {
        "id": 4501,

        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Etoricoxib",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "COX-2 Specific Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Symptomatic relief of osteoarthritis (OA), rheumatoid arthritis (RA), ankylosing spondylitis, pain and signs of inflammation associated with acute gouty arthritis. Short-term treatment of moderate pain associated with dental surgery."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>OA:</b> 30 mg once daily, may be increased to max 60 mg once daily. <b>RA and ankylosing spondylitis:</b> 60 mg once daily, may be increased to max 90 mg once daily. Down-titrate to 60 mg once daily when patient is stabilized. <b>Acute gouty arthritis:</b> 120 mg once daily for max 8 days. <b>Post-op dental surgery pain:</b> 90 mg once daily for max 3 days. <b>Hepatic impairment</b> - Mild (Child-Pugh score 5-6): Max 60 mg; Moderate (Child-Pugh score 7-9): Max 30 mg."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. CVA, MI, CABG, uncontrolled HTN (BP &gt;140/90 mmHg), CHF NYHA II-IV. Active peptic ulceration or GI bleeding, severe hepatic (Child-Pugh score &ge;10) and renal (CrCl &lt;30 mL/min) impairment, IBD, IHD, PAD, and CVD. Patients experiencing bronchospasm, acute rhinitis, nasal polyps, angioneurotic edema, urticaria, or allergic-type reactions after taking aspirin or NSAIDs. Childn and adolescents &lt;16 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "History of GI disease (e.g. ulceration or bleeding), cardiac failure, left ventricular dysfunction, pre-existing edema. Concomitant use with other NSAIDs or aspirin, warfarin or other anticoagulants. Patients with osteoarthritis, HTN, hyperlipidemia, DM, impaired renal function, uncompensated heart failure or cirrhosis, dehydration; smoking. Monitor BP within 2 weeks after initiation of therapy and periodically thereafter. Discontinue if persistently abnormal liver function tests are detected; at 1<sup>st</sup> sign of rash.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Alveolar osteitis, edema, fluid retention, dizziness, headache, palpitations, arrhythmia, HTN, bronchospasm, constipation, flatulence, gastritis, heartburn or acid reflux, diarrhea, dyspepsia or epigastric discomfort, nausea, vomiting, esophagitis, oral ulcer, increased ALT and AST, ecchymosis, asthenia or fatigue, flu-like disease."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Oral anticoagulants, diuretics, ACE inhibitors, ARBs, aspirin, ciclosporin, tacrolimus, lithium, methotrexate, oral contraceptives, HRT, digoxin, salbutamol, minoxidil, rifampicin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 90 mg, 120 mg."
          }
        ],

        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Calcium 125 mg, magnesium 100 mg, ascorbic acid 85 mg, vit E 44.70 mg, iron 27 mg, nicotinamide 18 mg, zinc 11 mg, vit B <sub>5</sub> 6.52 mg, B<sub>6</sub> 2.31 mg, manganese 2 mg, vit B<sub>1</sub> 1.73 mg, B<sub>2</sub> 1.40 mg, copper 1 mg, biotin 0.03 mg, vit D<sub>3</sub> 1,000 IU, vit B<sub>9</sub> 451 mcg, iodide 220 mcg, selenium 50 mcg, vit B<sub>12</sub> 2.60 mcg",

            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Vitamins & Minerals, Maternal"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Non-Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Indicated for adult women and adolescent girls who are planning a pregnancy or who are pregnant. Prevention and treatment of vitamin and mineral deficiencies in preparation for pregnancy, and during pregnancy; iron and folate anemia. Reduction of the risk of first occurrence neural tube defects and other congenital abnormalities."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "1 tab daily with glass of water preferably with a meal. In case of morning sickness, recommended to be taken at noon or in the evening. To be taken at least 1 month before conception (when planning a pregnancy) and throughout the pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Severe impaired renal function, existing hypervitaminosis D, hypercalcemia, severe hypercalciuria, iron or copper metabolism disorders."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Recommended dosage must not exceed. Patients receiving other single vitamins or multivitamins preparation. Patients with nephrolithiasis or urolithiasis.",

          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "GI and abdominal pain, constipation, diarrhea, nausea and vomiting. Darkening of stool. Allergic or anaphylactic reaction, exanthema, slightly yellow urine."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Antacids, gastric acid suppressive medications, fluoroquinolones, bisphosphonates, levodopa, levothyroxine, penicillamine, tetracycline, trientine."

          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Relief of inflammatory and pruritic manifestations of corticosteroid-responsive dermatoses, e.g. psoriasis, atopic dermatitis, irritant and/or allergic contact dermatitis. Lotion may be applied to scalp lesions."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Apply to affected areas once a day. Massage gently and thoroughly until medication disappears."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not for ophthalmic use. Discontinue if sensitization or irritation develops. Use appropriate antifungal or antibacterial agent in the presence of infection. Treatment of extensive body areas. Use of occlusion. Infants. Childn. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category C.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Pruritus, application site reactions, bacterial infections, folliculitis, furunculosis, acneiform eruptions, signs of skin atrophy, burning, irritation, dryness, hypertrichosis, hypopigmentation, perioral dermatitis, maceration of skin, secondary infection, striae, miliaria, blurred vision."
          },

            "title": "Packaging",

          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone Agonists"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Palliative treatment of advanced prostate cancer."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Single SC injection. 7.5 mg (every month); 22.5 mg (every 3 months); 45 mg (every 6 months). See package insert for mixing and administration procedure."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to leuprorelin acetate or other GnRH agonist analogs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "QTc prolonging drugs. Use of bupropion and SSRIs. Patients with metastatic vertebral lesions and/or with urinary tract obstruction, congenital long QT syndrome, CHF, frequent electrolyte abnormalities, history of seizures, epilepsy, cerebrovascular disorders, CNS anomalies or tumors. Increased risk of convulsions, developing DM or hyperglycemia, MI, sudden cardiac death, or stroke in men. May cause transient increase in serum concentrations of testosterone during the 1st week of treatment resulting in bone pain, neuropathy, hematuria or bladder outlet obstruction. Monitor serum glucose, glycosylated Hgb (HbA1c), testosterone, and prostate-specific antigen. Childn. Pregnancy and lactation. Infertility.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Malaise, fatigue, weakness; dizziness; hot flashes/sweats; urinary frequency, nocturia; nausea, gastroenteritis/colitis; pruritus, clamminess, night sweats, alopecia; arthralgia, myalgia, pain in limb; testicular atrophy, gynecomastia, testicular pain; decreased libido; transient burning/ stinging, pain, erythema, bruising, erythema, induration in injection site; decreased bone density in men."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Diagnostic tests of pituitary gonadotropic and gonadal functions."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Lyophilized powder for suspension for injection (SC) 7.5 mg, 22.5 mg, 45 mg."
          }

        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/ejQZGFyDJ8X4eszmhSe4Q75mHj4GLcunhqDGQaOWRn8DIZuADT.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/yrYx4vNSQFBdPablzUMhglcGjsTXhBVfgz0hNmb2JkuHrGxX6H.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/LnM0IBydmNS9yQSogfQ4RBHvPfawJSgIYvnj4HtDHlVGYqE8cP.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Escitalopram",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitors (SSRIs)"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of major depressive episodes (MDE), panic disorder with or without agoraphobia, social anxiety disorder (SAD), generalized anxiety disorder (GAD), and obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "All doses taken once daily. <b>MDE, GAD, OCD:</b> Initially 10 mg, may be increased to max 20 mg. <b>Panic disorder with or without agoraphobia:</b> Initially 5 mg during the 1<sup>st</sup> week, then increased to 10 mg and may be further increased up to max 20 mg. <b>SAD:</b> 10 mg, may be decreased to 5 mg or increased to max 20 mg. <b>Elderly >65 yrs:</b> Reduce initial dose by half. A lower max dose should be considered. <b>Mild to moderate hepatic impairment, poor metabolizers of CYP2C19:</b> Initially 5 mg during the 1<sup>st</sup> 2 weeks, may be increased to 10 mg; <b>Severe hepatic impairment:</b> Titrate dose. <b>Treatment duration -</b> MDE: Usually 2-4 weeks to obtain a response, then at least 6 months after symptoms resolve. <b>Panic disorder with or without agoraphobia:</b> Max effectiveness after 3 months. <b>SAD:</b> 2-4 weeks to obtain symptom relief, 12 weeks to consolidate response, and 6 months to prevent relapse. <b>OCD:</b> Until patient is symptom-free. Taken with or without food."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Concomitant use with MAOIs (e.g. moclobemide and linezolid). Pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Avoid abrupt withdrawal. Patients with severe renal (CrCl < 30 mL/min) and hepatic impairment, unstable or controlled epilepsy, history of mania/hypomania, diabetes, CHD. Concomitant use with oral anticoagulants, atypical antipsychotics, phenothiazines, TCAs, aspirin, NSAIDs, ticlopidine, dipyridamole; electroconvulsive therapy; sumatriptan or other triptans, tramadol, tryptophan; St. John’s Wort. Increased anxiety symptoms at the beginning of treatment in some patients with panic disorder; suicidal thoughts, self-harm, and suicide (suicide-related events) in patients with depression; akathisia; hyponatremia; cutaneous bleeding abnormalities (e.g. ecchymoses, purpura) in patients with known bleeding tendencies. Discontinue if seizure develops or if there is an increase in seizure frequency. Gradually taper dose upon discontinuation. Elderly with SAD. Lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Decreased/Increased appetite, increased weight; anxiety, restlessness, abnormal dreams, decreased libido, anorgasmia; insomnia, somnolence, dizziness, paresthesia, tremor; sinusitis, yawning; diarrhea, constipation, vomiting, dry mouth; increased sweating; arthralgia, myalgia; ejaculation disorder, impotence; fatigue, pyrexia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "MAOIs, tramadol, sumatriptan and other triptans, TCAs, SSRIs, phenothiazines, thioxanthenes, mefloquine, bupropion, lithium, tryptophan, St. John’s Wort, oral anticoagulants, NSAIDs, alcohol."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 5 mg (P9.00), 10 mg (P16.00)."
          }
        ],

          },

            "content": "Rx"

            "content": "Relief of severe symptoms of atopic dermatitis, angioedema, urticaria, seasonal and perennial allergic rhinitis, food and drug allergic reactions, allergic contact dermatitis, seborrheic dermatitis, neurodermatitis, allergic asthma, ocular allergic manifestations (e.g. conjunctivitis and iridocyclitis), allergic reaction to insect stings."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults and childn &ge;12 yrs</b>: 1 tab twice daily. Adjust dose in cases of remission or exacerbation of diseases, surgery, infection, or injury."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Systemic fungal infections. Vaccination against smallpox and other immunization procedures."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with severe liver impairment. Consider dietary restriction and potassium supplementation in cases of BP elevation, salt and water retention, and increased potassium or calcium excretion. Discontinue approx 48 hrs prior to skin testing procedures. Enhanced corticosteroid effect in patients with hypothyroidism or cirrhosis. Corneal perforations may develop in patients with ocular herpes simplex. Existing emotional instability or psychotic tendencies may be aggravated. Nonspecific ulcerative colitis, impending perforation, abscesses or other pyogenic infections, TB, diverticulitis, fresh intestinal anastomoses, active or latent peptic ulcer, renal insufficiency, HTN, osteoporosis, myasthenia gravis, visual disturbance. Infants and childn. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category B for loratadine; Category C but D in 1<sup>st</sup> trimester for betamethasone.",

        "content": "Gadoteric acid",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Radiopharmaceuticals"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Lesions or stenoses of non-coronary arteries (MR angiography) in adults. Used for lesions of brain, spine and surrounding tissues; whole body MRI in adults and childn 0-18 yrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults – MRI of brain and spine</b>: 0.1 mmol/kg BW (0.2 mL/kg BW). <b>In patients with brain tumors</b>: Administer an additional 0.2 mmol/kg BW (0.4 mL/kg BW). <b>Whole body MRI (including lesions of the liver, kidneys, pancreas, lungs, heart, breast, and musculoskeletal system)</b>: 0.1 mmol/kg BW (0.2 mL/kg BW). <b>For angiography</b>: 0.1 mmol/kg BW (0.2 mL/kg BW). <b>In exceptional circumstances (e.g. failure to gain satisfactory images of an extensive vascular territory)</b>: Administer a 2<sup>nd</sup> consecutive injection of 0.1 mmol/kg (0.2 mL/kg BW). <b>Childn – Encephalic and spinal MRI, whole body MRI</b>: Max 0.1 mmol/kg BW. Refrain from eating for 2 hrs prior to investigation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Childn &lt;6 months."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "For IV injection only. Not to be administered by subarachnoid (or epidural) injection. History of allergy (e.g. fish, seafood allergy, hay fever, hives), sensitivity to contrast media and bronchial asthma. Patients who have experienced reaction during previous administration of gadolinium-containing MRI contrast agent. Patients with asthma; severe renal impairment (GFR &lt;30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>); in peri-op liver transplantation period; hepatic impairment; taking beta-blockers. Patients with low threshold for seizures, severe CV disease. Do not use in patients with pacemakers, vascular clips, infusion pumps, nerve stimulators, cochlear implants, or suspected intracorporeal metallic foreign bodies particularly in the eyes. Neonates and infants up to 1 yr. Elderly &gt;65 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Paresthesia, headache. Nausea, vomiting, pruritus, erythema, rash, felling hot/cold, injection site pain."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Beta-blockers, vasoactive substances, ACE inhibitors, ARBs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Solution for injection (IV) 0.5 mmol/mL x 10 mL."
          }
        ],

Protozoal infection including toxoplasmosis and for eradication of <i>Helicobacter pylori</i>-associated peptic ulcer disease (PUD)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Tab</b> - <b>Adults:</b> 250 mg twice a day, may be increased to 500 mg twice a day, if necessary, in severe infections; Duration of treatment: 7-14 days. <b>Prophylaxis and treatment of disseminated infection due to MAC</b> - <b>Adults:</b> 500 mg twice a day; <b>Childn:</b> 7.5 mg/kg twice a day up to 500 mg twice a day; may be given in combination with other antimycobacterials. <b>Leprosy:</b> 500 mg daily as part of an alternative multidrug therapy regimen. <b>Eradication of <i>H. pylori</i>-associated PUD:</b> 500 mg twice daily with other antibacterial and either a PPI or H2-receptor antagonist for 7-14 days. <b>Susp</b> - Duration of treatment: 5-10 days depending on the pathogen involved and severity of condition; <b>Childn weighing 30-40 kg (approx 10-12 yrs):</b> 10 mL; <b>20-29 kg (approx 7-9 yrs):</b> 7.5 mL; <b>12-19 kg (approx 3-6 yrs):</b> 5 mL; <b>8-11 kg (approx 1-2 yrs):</b> 2.5 mL; <b>&lt;8 kg:</b> Dosed on a per kg basis (approx 7.5 mg/kg daily). <b>Severe renal impairment (CrCl &lt;30 mL/min):</b> Reduce dose."
          },

            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Concomitant use with astemizole, cisapride, or terfenadine. Pregnancy and lactation."

        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/2baYh7xx35PbBh8DB6O4aT4waeE1b8XOow4X5oXqNjT879A0wo.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/p6S9kocUmgCjTgLynK7hBqsJaRP0NKsAJ0PxZEeuQ0DgU5AjKg.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/zjfh40t9wq9MEvgOAWK59Bz8KTHNesl9bOWFw3LTLuoxXzjDWI.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Apixaban",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Anticoagulants"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Prevention of venous thromboembolic events (VTE) in adults who have undergone elective hip or knee replacement surgery; of stroke and systemic embolism in adults with non-valvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF) with one or more risk factors e.g. prior stroke, transient ischemic attack (TIA), &ge;75 yrs, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, symptomatic heart failure (NYHA Class &ge;II). Treatment of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE), and prevention of recurrent DVT and PE in adults."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Prevention of VTE - Elective hip or knee replacement surgery</b>: 2.5 mg twice daily, should be taken 12-24 hrs after surgery. Duration of treatment - Hip replacement surgery: 32-38 days; Knee replacement surgery: 10-14 days. <b>Prevention of stroke and systemic embolism in patients with NVAF</b>: 5 mg twice daily and 2.5 mg twice daily in patients with at least 2 of the following characteristics: &ge;80 yrs, BW &le;60 kg, serum creatinine &ge;1.5 mg/dL (133 micromole/L). Severe renal impairment (CrCl 15-29 mL/min): 2.5 mg twice daily. <b>Treatment of DVT and PE</b>: 10 mg twice daily for 7 days, followed by 5 mg twice daily. <b>Prevention of recurrent DVT and PE</b>: 2.5 mg twice daily after 6 months of treatment for DVT or PE. <b>Switching treatment - Vit K antagonist (VKA) to apixaban</b>: Discontinue VKA, initiate apixaban tabs when INR is &lt;2; <b>Apixaban to VKA therapy</b>: Co-administration of apixaban tabs and VKA therapy until the INR is &ge;2. <b>Patients undergoing cardioversion but not previously treated with anticoagulants and initiating treatment with apixaban</b>: 5 mg twice daily for at least 2.5 days (5 single doses) before cardioversion, reduce to 2.5 mg twice daily if patient meets the criteria for dose reduction. If cardioversion is required before 5 doses of apixaban can be administered, give 10 mg loading dose, followed by 5 mg twice daily, reduce to 5 mg loading dose, then 2.5 mg twice daily if patient meets the criteria for dose reduction. Administer loading dose 2 hrs prior to cardioversion."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Active clinically significant bleeding. Hepatic disease associated with coagulopathy and clinically relevant bleeding risk. Lesion or condition if considered a significant risk factor for major bleeding. Concomitant use with other anticoagulant agents."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with conditions with increased risk of hemorrhage, prosthetic heart valves, history of thrombosis diagnosed with antiphospholipid syndrome; triple positive results for lupus anticoagulant, anticardiolipin antibodies and anti-beta 2-glycoprotein I antibodies; pulmonary embolism and are hemodynamically unstable; active cancer; severe renal impairment; low BW &lt;60 kg; hepatic impairment and elevated liver enzymes; undergoing hip fracture surgery; rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Spinal/epidural anesthesia or puncture. Concomitant use with antiplatelets, SSRIs, SNRIs, NSAIDs (e.g. aspirin), other platelet aggregation inhibitors (following surgery), thrombolytic agents (for treatment of acute ischemic stroke), CYP3A4 and P-gp inhibitors and inducers. Discontinue at least 48 hrs prior to elective surgery or invasive procedures with moderate or high risk of bleeding and 24 hrs prior to invasive procedures with a low risk of bleeding. Discontinuing therapy may increase risk of thrombosis. Elderly. Childn &lt;18 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Anemia, hemorrhage, hematoma, nausea, confusion. <b>Treatment of DVT and PE and prevention of recurrent DVT and PE</b>: Thrombocytopenia, epistaxis, increased GGT and ALT, skin rash, hematuria. <b>Prevention of stroke and systemic embolism in adult patients with NVAF</b>: Epistaxis, increased GGT, hematuria."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "CYP3A4 and P-gp inhibitors (e.g. azole-antimycotics, HIV protease inhibitors, diltiazem, naproxen, clarithromycin, amiodarone, fluconazole, verapamil, quinidine) and inducers (e.g. rifampicin, phenytoin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital, St. John’s wort), anticoagulants, platelet aggregation inhibitors, SSRIs or SNRIs, NSAIDs, P2Y12 inhibitors (e.g. aspirin), thrombolytic agents, GPIIb/IIIa receptor antagonists, thienopyridines (e.g. clopidogrel), dipyridamole, dextran, sulfinpyrazone, activated charcoal; clotting tests."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 2.5 mg (P49.50), 5 mg (P54.50)."
          }
        ],

          "id": 1583,

        },

          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/OElSytqFskwNbuGnMdsj70WOsfJDKqa8ESZ56N1AzGOu2Ij0o3.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/a5CUgFxVRa1L6sBXKWQ8dOgQV57whlenxUsyppFSfucdm9pdRL.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/cqqSY2E61WQ4Kl4p41FeyHZE0H3JWmsX6dVLeLONarKLRpEbOh.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Quetiapine",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Atypical Antipsychotics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, moderate to severe manic episodes in bipolar disorder, major depressive episodes in bipolar disorder. For the prevention of recurrence of manic or depressed episodes in patients with bipolar disorder who previously responded to quetiapine treatment."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adult – Schizophrenia</b>: Total daily dose for the 1<sup>st</sup> 4 days of therapy is 50 mg on day 1, 100 mg on day 2, 200 mg on day 3, and 300 mg on day 4. All administered twice daily. From day 4 onwards, titrate dose to the usual effective dose range of 300-450 mg/day, may be adjusted within the dose range of 150-750 mg/day depending on clinical response and tolerability. <b>Moderate to severe manic episodes in bipolar disorder</b>: Total daily dose for the 1<sup>st</sup> 4 days of therapy is 100 mg on day 1, 200 mg on day 2, 300 mg on day 3, and 400 mg on day 4. All administered twice daily. Adjust dose to 800 mg/day by Day 6 and no increments of no greater than 200 mg/day. <b>Major depressive episodes in bipolar disorder</b>: Total daily dose for the 1st 4 days of therapy is 50 mg on day 1, 100 mg on day 2, 200 mg on day 3, and 300 mg on day 4. Dose is adjusted depending on clinical response and tolerability of the individual patient, within the range of 200 to 800 mg/day. Recommended daily dose is 300 mg; usual effective dose is 400-800 mg/day. All administered once daily at bedtime. <b>Prevention of recurrence of manic, mixed or depressive episodes in bipolar disorder</b>: 300-800 mg/day administered twice daily. <b>Hepatic impairment</b>: Initially 25 mg/day, may be increased daily in increments of 25-50 mg/day."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Concomitant administration of cytochrome P450 3A4 inhibitors, e.g. HIV-protease inhibitors, azole-antifungal agents, erythromycin, clarithromycin and nefazodone."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Risk for suicide/suicidal thoughts or clinical worsening; severe neutropenia and agranulocytosis; weight gain; hyperglycemia and/or development or exacerbation of diabetes associated with ketoacidosis or coma; increased triglycerides, LDL-C and total cholesterol; decreased HDL; QT prolongation; cardiomyopathy and myocarditis; dysphagia; constipation and intestinal obstruction; venous thromboembolism; pancreatitis. Patients with dementia-related psychosis, Parkinson’s disease. Childn. Elderly. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Somnolence, dizziness, headache, dry mouth, withdrawal (discontinuation) symptoms, elevations in serum triglyceride levels, elevations in total cholesterol (predominantly LDL-C), decreases in HDL-C, weight gain, decreased hemoglobin and EPS."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Centrally-acting drugs, alcohol, carbamazepine, phenytoin, lithium, valproate. False positive results in enzyme immunoassays for methadone and tricyclic antidepressants."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 100 mg (P35.00), 300 mg (P48.00)."
          }
        ],

        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/EecanImLsaHANqYuRQ0Je2lMc22gBqSrLmalUh9uRl6BDHMmpV.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/dV6t4whwntr4zek2b9BcWXY4ObfN2v6i5ut4up0d9dtOQvHi55.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/DTc2ZNLAZU13I1DKSZmG3gpESeKDo3N3PFRJ8wR2DExC0NPa3m.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Telmisartan",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Angiotensin II Receptor Blockers"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of essential hypertension (HTN) in adults. Reduction of cardiovascular (CV) morbidity with manifest atherothrombotic CV disease (e.g. history of CHD, stroke, peripheral arterial disease) or type 2 diabetes mellitus with documented target organ damage."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Essential HTN:</b> 40 mg once daily, may be increased to max 80 mg once daily if target BP is not achieved. Some may already benefit from 20 mg once daily. May be used in combination with thiazide diuretics (e.g. HCTZ). The max effect is attained 4-8 weeks after start of treatment. <b>CV morbidity reduction:</b> 80 mg once daily. <b>Severe renal impairment, on hemodialysis:</b> Initially 20 mg. <b>Mild to moderate hepatic impairment:</b> Max 40 mg once daily. Take with or without food."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with cholestasis, severe hepatic impairment and biliary obstructive disorders. Pregnancy (2<sup>nd</sup> and 3<sup>rd</sup> trimesters)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with mild to moderate hepatic impairment; bilateral renal artery stenosis or stenosis of the artery to a single functioning kidney, recent kidney transplantation; vol/sodium depletion; primary aldosteronism; aortic and mitral stenosis, obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy; diabetes treated with insulin or antidiabetics; fructose intolerance; ischemic cardiopathy or CV disease. Dual blockade of RAAS with concomitant use of products that affect this system. Patients at risk for hyperkalemia.  Correct volume and sodium depletion prior to initiation of treatment. Monitor BP closely when initiating therapy for CV morbidity reduction; potassium and creatinine serum levels in patients with renal impairment. May impair ability to drive or operate machines. Black hypertensive patients. Childn < 18 yrs. Women of childbearing potential. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Sepsis. Hypotension. Abnormal hepatic function or liver disorder. Interstitial lung disease."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Salt substitutes containing potassium, potassium-sparing diuretics or supplements, ACE inhibitors, ARBs, heparin, cyclosporin, tacrolimus, trimethoprim, lithium. NSAIDs (e.g. aspirin, COX-2 inhibitors), thiazide or loop diuretics, other antihypertensives, corticosteroids."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 40 mg (P13.00), 80 mg (P22.00)."
          }
        ],

  {

    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 2822,
        "brand_name": "Encorate Chrono 500",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Sodium valproate, valproic acid",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Fatty Acid Derivatives"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of generalized, partial or other epilepsy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults:</b> Initially 600 mg daily, increased by 200 mg at 3-day intervals, usually within 1,000-2,000 mg daily (20-30 mg/kg BW), until control is achieved. May be further increased to 2,500 mg daily. <b>Childn >20 kg:</b> Initially 400 mg/day with spaced increases, usually within 20-30 mg/kg BW daily. <b>Combined therapy:</b> Taper dose of anticonvulsants slowly and initiate treatment gradually."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Active liver disease. Personal or family history of severe dysfunction, especially drug-related. Urea cycle disorder. Porphyria. Mitochondrial disorders caused by mutations in the nuclear gene encoding mitochondrial polymerase (POLF) and childn < 2 yrs suspected with POLG-related disorder. Concomitant use with salicylates in childn < 3 yrs. Lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with history, at risk, or present hepatic insufficiency, combination anticonvulsant therapy in severe seizures and neurological impairment, SLE, underlying carnitine palmitoyltransferase type II deficiency. Severe liver damage, aggravated convulsions, suicidal ideation and behaviors, weight gain. False positive in urine testing for DM. Discontinue if abnormally low prothrombin rate or pancreatitis is confirmed. Not recommended with carbapenems and alcohol. Assess liver function prior and periodically during 1<sup>st</sup> 6 months of therapy; blood tests prior therapy or before surgery due to spontaneous bruising or bleeding. May impair ability to drive and operate machinery. Reproductive effects on females. May impair men's fertility. Female childn. Women of childbearing potential. Pregnancy.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nausea, tremor, gastralgia, diarrhea, liver injury, EPS, stupor, somnolence, convulsion, memory impairment, headache, nystagmus, confusional state, aggression, agitation, attention disturbance, hyponatremia, anemia, thrombocytopenia, hypersensitivity, transient and/or dose related alopecia, dysmenorrhea, hemorrhage, deafness, weight gain."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Antipsychotics, MAOIs, antidepressants, benzodiazepines, phenobarbital, primidone, phenytoin, carbamazepine, lamotrigine, felbamate, zidovudine, nimodipine, vit K dependent anticoagulants, mefloquine, chloroquine, aspirin, cimetidine, erythromycin, cholestyramine, rifampicin, topiramate."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Controlled-release tablet 333 mg/145 mg (P32.20)."
          }
        ],

        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Antiplatelets"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Prevention of thrombotic events in patients with acute coronary syndromes unstable angina, non-ST elevation myocardial infarction, or ST elevation myocardial infarction, including medically managed patients and those managed with percutaneous coronary intervention or coronary artery bypass grafting."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Initially single 180 mg loading dose, then continued at 90 mg twice daily. After one yr, may be continued with 60 mg twice daily without interruption. Take with daily low maintenance dose of 75-150 mg acetyl-salicylic acid. Tab can be crushed to fine powder and mixed with half glass of water and drunk immediately. Mixture can also be administered via nasogastric tube."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Active pathological bleeding. History of intracranial hemorrhage. Severe hepatic impairment."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Avoid premature discontinuation. Patients with moderate hepatic impairment; increased risk for bleeding or bradycardic events; requiring surgery. Co-administration with NSAIDs, oral anticoagulants, fibrinolytics, antifibrinolytics, or recombinant factor VIIa. Dyspnea, thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura. False negative result in platelet function test for heparin-induced thrombocytopenia. Discontinue 5 days prior to elective surgery. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Blood disorders, respiratory system, urinary tract, subcutaneous/dermal, or traumatic bleeding; hyperuricemia, dyspnea, gout, dizziness, syncope, vertigo, hypotension, respiratory system bleedings, GI hemorrhage, diarrhea, nausea, pruritus, urinary tract bleeding, increased blood creatinine, post-procedural hemorrhage."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole, clarithromycin, nefazodone, ritonavir, atazanavir), inducers (e.g., rifampin), cyclosporine, morphine, simvastatin, digoxin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 90 mg."
          }

          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/8F0tsD1pFXiMrV5SKxAa4d2RVLUlt4ZZkQLDM77qAOG0tGBXGw.jpg",

        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Lincosamides"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of serious infections caused by susceptible G(+) organisms, staphylococci (both penicillinase and non-penicillinase), streptococci (except <i>Streptococcus faecalis</i>) and pneumococci. Management of serious infections caused by susceptible anaerobic pathogens."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults – Serious infections</b>: 600 mg-1.2 g/day in 2, 3, or 4 equal doses. <b>More severe infections</b>: 1.2-2.7 g/day in 2, 3, or 4 equal doses. <b>Life-threatening situations</b>: 4.8 g daily. Maybe administered as single rapid infusion for 1<sup>st</sup> dose followed by continuous infusion. Administration of >600 mg single IM injection or >1.2 g single 1 hr infusion is not recommended. <b>Childn >1 month – Serious infections</b>: 15-25 mg/kg/day in 3 or 4 equal doses. <b>More severe infections</b>: 25-40 mg/kg/day in 3 or 4 equal doses."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Renal or hepatic impairment. Superinfection with prolonged use. Periodic liver and kidney function tests carried out during prolonged therapy. Atopic individuals. Patients with history of GI disease especially colitis. Neonates and infants. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, diarrhea. Transient neutropenia (leucopenia), eosinophilia, agranulocytosis, thrombocytopenia. Pruritus, vaginitis. Maculopapular rash, urticaria, mild to moderate morbilliform-like skin rashes. Jaundice, abnormalities in liver functions."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Neuromuscular blocking agents. Erythromycin. Ampicillin, phenytoin, barbiturates, aminophylline, calcium gluconate, magnesium sulfate."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Solution for injection (IV/IM) 150 mg/mL x 2 mL, 4 mL."
          }

            "content": "GI disease, especially colitis. Periodic liver and kidney function tests should be carried out during prolonged therapy. Monitor neonates and infants. Superinfection. Contains benzyl alcohol. Used only in the treatment of serious infections. Elderly. Lactation.",

    "id": 4232,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 4232,
        "brand_name": "Clipax",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Paclitaxel",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Taxanes"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "<b>Ovarian carcinoma</b>: 1<sup>st</sup>-line chemotherapy: Treatment of patients with advanced carcinoma of the ovary or with residual disease (>1 cm) after initial laparotomy, in combination with cisplatin; 2<sup>nd</sup>-line: Treatment of metastatic carcinoma of the ovary after failure of standard, platinum-containing therapy. <b>Breast carcinoma</b>: Treatment of node-positive breast carcinoma following anthracycline and cyclophosphamide (AC) therapy; initial treatment of locally-advanced or metastatic breast cancer either in combination with an anthracycline therapy is suitable, or in combination with trastuzumab, in patients who over-express HER-2 at a 3+ level as determined by immunohistochemistry and for whom an anthracycline is not suitable; as a single agent, treatment of metastatic carcinoma of the breast in patients who have failed, or are not candidates for standard, anthracycline-containing therapy. <b>Advanced non-small cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC)</b>: Treatment of NSCLC in combination with cisplatin, in patients who are not candidates for potentially curative surgery and/or radiation therapy. <b>AIDS-related Kaposi’s sarcoma (KS)</b>: Treatment of advanced AIDS-related KS who have failed prior liposomal anthracycline therapy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Premedication prior to paclitaxel administration</b>: Oral dexamethasone 20 mg approx 12 and 6 hrs before or IV dexamethasone 20 mg for 30-60 mins before; diphenhydramine 50 mg IV for 30-60 mins (8-20 mg for KS patients) before; cimetidine 300 mg IV or ranitidine 50 mg IV for 30-60 mins before. <b>Ovarian carcinoma</b> - <b>1<sup>st</sup>-line chemotherapy</b>: Paclitaxel 175 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV over 3 hrs, followed by cisplatin 75 mg/m<sup>2</sup> every 3 weeks or paclitaxel 135 mg/m<sup>2</sup> in a 24-hr infusion, followed by cisplatin 75 mg/m<sup>2</sup> with 3-week intervals between courses; <b>2<sup>nd</sup>-line</b>: Paclitaxel 175 mg/m<sup>2</sup> over 3 hrs, with 3-week intervals between courses. <b>Breast carcinoma</b> - <b>Adjuvant chemotherapy</b>: Paclitaxel 175 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV over 3 hrs every 3 weeks for 4 courses, following AC therapy. <b>1<sup>st</sup>-line</b> - <b>In combination with doxorubicin</b> (50 mg/m<sup>2</sup>): Paclitaxel 220 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV over 3 hrs, with 3-week intervals between courses. Administer paclitaxel 24 hrs after doxorubicin; <b>In combination with trastuzumab</b> (4 mg/kg loading dose then 2 mg/kg weekly): Paclitaxel 175 mg/m<sup>2</sup> IV over 3 hrs, with 3-week intervals between courses. Paclitaxel infusion may be started the day following the 1<sup>st</sup> dose of trastuzumab or immediately after the subsequent doses of trastuzumab if the preceding dose of trastuzumab was well tolerated. <b>2<sup>nd</sup>-line</b>: Paclitaxel 175 mg/m<sup>2</sup> over 3 hrs, with 3-week intervals between courses. <b>Treatment of advanced NSCLC</b>: Paclitaxel 175 mg/m<sup>2</sup> over 3 hrs, followed by cisplatin 80 mg/m<sup>2</sup> with 3-week intervals between courses. <b>Treatment of AIDS-related KS</b>: Paclitaxel 100 mg/m<sup>2</sup> administered as 3-hr IV infusion every 2 weeks. Patients experiencing severe neutropenia or severe peripheral neuropathy: Dose reduction of 20% for subsequent courses and 25% for KS patients."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to paclitaxel or polyoxyethylated castor oil. Patients with baseline neutrophils < 1,500/mm<sup>3</sup> (< 1,000/mm<sup>3</sup> for KS patients) and those suffering from uncontrolled infections. Lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Risk for extravasation, bone marrow suppression, grade 3-4 myelosuppression (patients with hepatic impairment), severe cardiac conduction abnormalities, and interstitial pneumonitis. Patients must be pretreated with corticosteroids, antihistamines, and H2-antagonists before paclitaxel treatment. Patients should not be treated with paclitaxel until neutrophil counts recover to &ge;1,500 cells/mm<sup>3</sup> (&ge;1,000/mm<sup>3</sup> for KS patients), and platelet counts recover to &ge;100,000 platelets/mm<sup>3</sup> (&ge;75,000/mm<sup>3</sup> for KS patients). Give before cisplatin when used in combination. Radiation of the lung. Severe hepatic impairment. Patients of fertile age and their partners should use contraception for at least 6 months after treatment. Possibility of infertility in males. Childn < 18 yrs. Pregnancy.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Bone marrow suppression. Infections (mainly UTI and URTI), myelosuppression, neutropenia, anemia, thrombocytopenia, leukopenia, bleeding, minor hypersensitivity reactions (mainly flushing and rash), peripheral neuropathy, bradycardia, hypotension, diarrhea, vomiting, nausea, mucosal inflammation, alopecia, and transient nail and skin changes, arthralgia, myalgia, injection site reactions, severe elevation in AST and alkaline phosphatase."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "CYP2C8 or CYP3A4 inhibitors (e.g. ketoconazole and other imidazole antifungals, erythromycin, fluoxetine, gemfibrozil, clopidogrel, cimetidine, ritonavir, saquinavir, indinavir, and nelfinavir). CYP2C8 or CYP3A4 inducers (e.g. rifampicin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, efavirenz, nevirapine). Protease inhibitors."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Concentrate for solution for injection (IV) 6 mg/mL x 5 mL (P2,500.00). Concentrate solution for IV infusion 6 mg/mL x 16.7 mL (P6,500.00)."
          }
        ],

        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Clonidine HCl",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Centrally-Acting Antihypertensives"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of hypertension (HTN). May be used alone or concomitantly with other antihypertensives."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Individualized dosing. <b>Mild to moderate HTN:</b> 75-150 mcg twice daily, in the morning and at bedtime. May be increased in increments of 100 mcg/day. Maintenance dose: 200-600 mcg/day given in 2 divided doses. Max 2,400 mcg/day in 2-3 divided doses. <b>Severe HTN:</b> Increase initial dose to 300 mcg thrice daily. Max 900 mcg/day."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Severe bradyarrhythmia from sick sinus syndrome or 2<sup>nd</sup> or 3<sup>rd</sup> degree AV block."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Avoid abrupt withdrawal; when discontinuing therapy, dose should be reduced gradually over 2-4 days to avoid withdrawal symptoms. Peri-op use; therapy should not be interrupted, continue oral clonidine within 4 hrs before surgery. Patients with severe coronary insufficiency, recent MI, conduction disturbances, mild to moderate bradyarrhythmia, cerebrovascular disease, cerebral or peripheral perfusion disorders, polyneuropathy, depression, chronic renal failure, Reynaud’s disease, thromboangiitis obliterans or constipation. May cause decreased lacrimation and dryness of eyes. Off-label use for ADHD, concomitantly with methylphenidate. May impair ability to drive or operate machine. Childn. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category C.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Undesirable effects on CV, dermatologic, GI, genitourinary, hematologic, hepatic, hematologic, metabolic, musculoskeletal, and nervous systems"
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "NSAIDs. CNS depressants e.g. opiates or other analgesics, barbiturates or other sedatives, anesthetics, or alcohol. Psychotherapeutic agents and TCAs. Beta-blockers. Calcium agonists, cardiac glycosides, haloperidol, alpha2-receptor blockers, and other hypotensive agents."
          },
          {

            "content": "Tablet 75 mcg (P21.99), 150 mcg (P35.49)."

            "content": "Rx, Exempt Dangerous Drug"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of all types of epilepsy and seizures, myoclonus and associated abnormal movements, panic disorders and status epilepticus."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Epilepsy - Adults</b>: Initially 1.5 mg/day given in 3 divided doses, may be increased in increments of 0.5 mg every 3 days until seizures are adequately controlled. <b>Childn 10-16 yrs</b>: Initially 1-1.5 mg/day in 2-3 divided doses, may be increased by 0.25-0.5 mg every 3<sup>rd</sup> day until 3-6 mg/day maintenance dose is reached. Max 0.2 mg/kg BW/day. &gt;10 yrs (&gt;30 kg BW): Initially 0.01-0.03 mg/kg daily given in 2-3 divided doses, may be increased in not more than 0.25-0.5 mg every 3<sup>rd</sup> day until maintenance dose (approx 0.1 mg/kg) has been reached. <b>Elderly</b>: Initially 0.5 mg/day. <b>Panic disorder - Adults</b>: 250 mcg twice daily, may be increased after 3 days to total 1 mg daily. Max 4 mg/day."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with acute or severe pulmonary insufficiency, preexisting myasthenia gravis, CNS depression or coma, respiratory depression, sleep apnea."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Avoid abrupt withdrawal. Risk of dependence. Renal and hepatic impairment. Suicidal ideation and behavior. Patients with history of depression or suicide attempts; chronic pulmonary insufficiency, preexisting disease of the liver or respiratory system (e.g. COPD); history of alcohol or drug abuse. Patients undergoing treatment with centrally acting medications or anticonvulsants. Concomitant use of alcohol and/or CNS depressants. Patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency, glucose-galactose malabsorption. Elderly or debilitated patients. May impair ability to drive and operate machinery. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Drowsiness; sedation, fatigue, muscle weakness, ataxia, somnolence, slowed reaction, muscular hypotonia, dizziness."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Carbamazepine, phenobarbital or phenytoin; alcohol."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 500 mcg (P8.85), 2 mg (P11.80)."

          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/5lxZWOyEI1xPSDFxrZQ3qclCPeebluCT96OqAlU4k4ZDI9d67t.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/uIVf6qu35Stz1MuU6njBSJk301YziKGnMtC4NZzUIujDM9SZb0.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Clozapine",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Atypical Antipsychotics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment-resistant schizophrenia, serious psychosis with tardive dyskinesia, negative symptom schizophrenia, schizo-affective disorder, severely manic bipolar I disorder and borderline personality disorder."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults:</b> 12.5 mg once or twice daily on the 1<sup>st</sup> day, followed by 25 mg once or twice daily on the 2<sup>nd</sup> day, may be increased gradually in steps of 25-50 mg to achieve 300 mg daily dose within 14-21 days. Subsequent increases in steps of 50-100 mg may be made once or twice daily. Max 900 mg/day; Maintenance dose: Gradually reduce to 200-450 mg daily in divided doses, larger portion may be given at night; If dose is &le;200 mg may be given as single dose in the evening. Withdrawal: Gradually over 1-2 weeks. <b>Elderly:</b> Initially 12.5 mg on the 1<sup>st</sup> day and subsequent dose increments should be restricted to 25 mg; <b>Restarting treatment after &gt;2 days interval:</b> 12.5 mg once or twice daily on the 1<sup>st</sup> day, may be increased more quickly when the 1<sup>st</sup> starting dose is well tolerated."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Myeloproliferative disorder, uncontrolled epilepsy, or history of clozapine-induced agranulocytosis or granulocytopenia. Severe CNS depression or comatose states, bone marrow suppression. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Agranulocytosis, seizures or other predisposing factors. May impair ability to drive or operate machines.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Agranulocytosis, seizure, CV effects, fever. Drowsiness, dizziness, hypersalivation, dry mouth, tachycardia, sedation. Constipation, headache, nausea, changes in eyesight."
          },

        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Leuprorelin acetate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone Agonists"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Management of endometriosis including pain relief and reduction of endometriotic lesions. In combination with norethindrone acetate 5 mg daily for initial management of endometriosis and management of recurrence of symptoms. Concomitantly with iron therapy for the pre-operative hematologic improvement of patients with anemia caused by uterine leiomyomata."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Endometriosis</b> - Duration of treatment: 6 months. Consider retreatment with a 6-month course if symptoms recur after a course of therapy. <b>Uterine leiomyomata (fibroids)</b> – Duration of therapy: 3 months."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to GnRH, GnRH agonist analogs or leuprorelin acetate. Undiagnosed abnormal vaginal bleeding. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Discontinue treatment if there is a sudden, partial or complete loss of vision, or sudden onset of proptosis, diplopia or migraine. Thrombophlebitis and pulmonary embolism. Assessment and management of risk factors for CV disease prior to initiation of add-back therapy; women with risk factors including lipid abnormalities or cigarette smoking. May experience breakthrough bleeding in patients missing successive doses. Development or worsening of depression and the occurrence of memory disorders. May result loss in bone density over the course of treatment; major risk factors e.g. chronic alcohol and/or tobacco use, strong family history of osteoporosis, chronic use of drugs that can reduce bone mass (e.g. anticonvulsants, corticosteroids). Discontinue if severe depression occurs. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category X.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Asthenia, general pain, headache; hot flushes/sweats; nausea/vomiting, GI disturbances; edema, weight gain/loss; acne, hirsutism; joint disorder, myalgia; decreased libido, depression/emotional lability, dizziness, nervousness, neuromuscular blockers, paresthesias; skin reactions; breast changes/tenderness/pain, vaginitis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Diagnostic tests of pituitary gonadotropic and gonadal functions."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
