  {
    "id": 3621,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 3621,
        "brand_name": "Endogen HP",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Urofollitropin",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone Agonists"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Ovulation induction and multiple follicular development (controlled ovarian stimulation) during ART cycles in patients previously received pituitary suppression administered in conjunction HCG."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Infertile patients with oligo-anovulation</b>: Individualized dosage. <b>Patients who received GnRH agonist or antagonist pituitary suppression</b>: Initially 150 IU daily SC or IM for the first 5 days of treatment. Adjust dose not more frequently than once every 2 days and not exceeding >75-150 IU/adjustment. If response is appropriate, administer HCG 7,500 IU one day after last dose of urofollitropin or the follicle attains a size &gt;18 mm. Max 450 IU/day and not beyond 12 days. Patients undergoing in vitro fertilization and donor egg patients who received GnRH agonist or antagonist pituitary suppression: Initially 225 IU daily SC for the first 5 days of treatment. Adjust dose not more frequently than once every 2 days and not exceeding >75-150 IU/adjustment. Max 450 IU/day and 12 days. Once adequate follicular development is evident, highly purified human chorionic gonadotropin 7,500 IU should be administered."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Women with high FSH level indicating primary ovarian failure; uncontrolled thyroid and adrenal dysfunction, organic intracranial lesion e.g. pituitary tumor; presence of any cause on infertility other than anovulation; abnormal bleeding of undetermined origin, ovarian cysts or enlargement not due to PCOS. Pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity/anaphylactic reactions. Mild to moderate uncomplicated ovarian enlargement accompanied by abdominal distension and/or pain. Discontinue treatment if severe ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome occurs. Multiple pregnancies. Perform gynecologic and endocrine evaluation before instituting treatment. Careful examination should be made to rule out the presence of early pregnancy. Cervical dilation and curettage should always be done for diagnosis before starting therapy in patients in late reproductive life who have greater predilection to endometrial carcinoma as well as higher incidence of anovulatory disorders. Evaluation of the husband’s fertility potential should be included in the workup. Elderly. Lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain; headache, pain, malaise; ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome in susceptible individuals."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Lyophilized powder for IM/SC injection 75 IU."
          }
        ],

            "content": "Uterotonics"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of postpartum hemorrhage (PPH), especially due to uterine atony, which has not responded to conventional methods of management. Prophylaxis in patients with grandmultiparity, pre-eclampsia, rapid or prolonged labor, previous uterine surgery, placental abnormalities, history of PPH and retained placenta and overdistention of uterus."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Prophylactic treatment for the control of PPH</b>: 125-250 mcg via IM injection at the delivery of anterior shoulder of fetus. <b>For refractory PPH</b>: 250 mcg via deep IM injection at about 90 mins interval. Interval may be reduced if necessary but should not be &lt;15 mins. Total dose should not exceed 2,000 mcg."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Acute PID. Patients with active cardiac, pulmonary, renal or hepatic disease. Patients having chorioamnionitis during labor."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with history of asthma, hypotension, HTN, anemia, jaundice, DM, epilepsy, compromised or scarred uterus; CV, renal, or hepatic disease.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Contractile effect on smooth muscle includes vomiting and diarrhea. Hyperpyrexia and flushing."
          },

            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Herpes Simplex Infections (including Genital Herpes):</b> 200 mg 5x daily for 5-10 days. <b>With Impaired Absorption:</b> 400 mg 5x daily for 5 days. <b>Recurrent Herpes Simplex in Immunocompetent Patients: </b>800 mg daily in 2-4 divided doses; dosage reduction in 400-600 mg daily. <b>Prophylaxis of Herpes Simplex:</b> 200-400 mg four times daily. <b>Episodic Treatment of Recurrences:</b> 200 mg 5x for 5 days; preferably initiated during prodromal period. <b>Chickenpox:</b> 800 mg 4-5x for 5-7 days. <b>Herpes Zoster:</b> 800 mg 5x daily 7-10 days. <b>Children (under 2 years):</b> 200 mg 4x daily. <b>2-5 years:</b> 400 mg 4x daily. <b>6 years and over:</b> 800 mg 4x daily."

            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Topical anesthesia and local vasoconstriction prior to endoscopy of the upper airways. Preparation of nasal mucosa for surgery. Aid in the treatment of acute nose bleeds and removal of foreign bodies from the nose. Topical anesthesia of the pharynx prior to direct or indirect laryngoscopy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "For nasal and pharyngeal administration. <b>Adults:</b> 5 squirts per nostril, administered once only or may be repeated as directed by the physician."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Childn. Pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with hepatic insufficiency, renal impairment, hyperthyroidism and CV disease (e.g. HTN, severe bradycardia, conduction disturbances or severe digitalis intoxication), existing neurological disorders, cuts or sores in areas of the nose or throat. May interfere with swallowing and may enhance the danger of aspiration of food or drinks. Increase risk of trauma from hot drinks or biting. Risk of inducing closed-angle glaucoma.             "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Transient bitter taste in the mouth, headache, drowsiness, lightheadedness, confusion, blurred vision, twitching, convulsions, sensations of hot or cold, slow heartbeat, fast heart rate with or without palpitations.           },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Propranolol, cimetidine, antiarrhythmic drugs, suxamethonium, phenytoin, TCAs, MAOIs, phenothiazines and butyrophenones."

        "brand_shot": {

          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/xZfF3UDZxgltyR4vmAeyifEYSZEqap7MhFTPExTpiDu3vJ6k87.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/yFF7fT8gAgJPqK51oZnyxSilWIEkSrPpT47u3sg5ahQmuZpu7E.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Sitagliptin phosphate monohydrate, metformin HCl",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Dipeptidyl Peptidase-4 (DPP-4) Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "For adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus, as adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in patients inadequately controlled on their max tolerated dose of metformin alone or those already being treated with combination of sitagliptin and metformin as separate tabs; as triple combination with sulfonylurea or PPAR-gamma agonist as adjunct to diet and exercise in patients inadequately controlled on their max tolerated dose of metformin and a sulfonylurea or PPAR-gamma agonist; as add-on to insulin as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control when diet and exercise plus stable dose of insulin and metformin alone do not provide adequate glycemic control."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Individualized dosage. Max for sitagliptin: 100 mg/day. <b>Patients not adequately controlled on metformin alone</b>: Initially, 50 mg twice daily plus dose of metformin already being taken. <b>Switching from sitagliptin and metformin combination as separate tabs</b>: Initiate at the dose already being taken. <b>Patients inadequately controlled on dual combination therapy with max tolerated dose of metformin and a sulfonylurea or a PPAR-gamma agonist or insulin</b>: 50 mg sitagliptin twice daily plus dose of metformin already being taken. Consider lower dose for sulfonylurea and insulin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Diabetic ketoacidosis or pre-coma. Moderate and severe renal impairment (CrCl &lt;6 mL/min). Acute conditions that can alter renal function e.g. dehydration, severe infection, shock. IV administration of iodinated contrast agents. Acute or chronic disease which may cause tissue hypoxia e.g. cardiac or respiratory failure, recent MI, hepatic impairment. Acute alcohol intoxication, alcoholism. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not for type 1 DM and treatment of diabetic ketoacidosis. Patients with impaired renal function. May induce pancreatitis, lactic acidosis, hypoglycemia (when used with a sulfonylurea or insulin). Discontinue prior to, or at the time of, imaging procedure and resume at least 48 hrs after, once renal function is stable.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Hypoglycemia, nausea, flatulence, vomiting."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Alcohol, iodinated contrast agents; NSAIDs (e.g. COX2 inhibitors), ACE inhibitors, ARBs, diuretics (e.g. loop diuretics), OCT2/MATE inhibitors (e.g. ranolazine, vandetanib, dolutegravir, cimetidine), glucocorticoids, beta2-agonists."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 50 mg/1,000 mg (P20.00)."

  {
    "id": 4558,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 4558,
        "brand_name": "Colstim",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/Ja85HBzZuIPzA4lI3DeOmbtmxKkJTHNDjC23YNBzVAZr2AntZV.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/u4ejxWnKG428xNoDRS8SN8qa9hIgLTVD3x2nhUoFfQo7wtdiAt.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/9xM4OGsoJIxFWemzKtd18YnYJH2LkECzihTi7CFVgSSpHZN61I.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Filgrastim",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Immunological Chemotherapeutic Agents"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Reduction in duration of neutropenia in bone marrow transplant (BMT) and in patients receiving cytotoxic therapy. Mobilization of peripheral blood progenitor cells (PBPCs) in patients undergoing myelosuppressive therapy followed by autologous PBPC transplantation or in normal donors prior to allogeneic PBPC transplantation. Treatment of severe congenital, cyclic, or idiopathic neutropenia; persistent neutropenia in patients with advanced HIV infection."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Cytotoxic therapy</b>: 0.5 MIU (5 mcg/kg/day) as single SC injection or IV infusion for 15-30 mins daily up to 2 weeks until absolute neutrophil count (ANC) has reached 10,000/mm<sup>3</sup> following expected neutrophil nadir; may be increased by 0.5 MIU/kg/day depending on duration and severity of ANC nadir. Administer at least 24 hrs after cytotoxic therapy. <b>Following BMT</b>: 1 MIU (10 mcg/kg/day) IV infusion for 4 or 24 hrs, or continuous 24-hr SC infusion; 1<sup>st</sup> dose is administered at least 24 hrs after cytotoxic chemotherapy and bone marrow infusion. <b>Mobilization of PBPC</b>: 1 MIU (10 mcg/kg/day) SC, as bolus or continuous infusion, at least 4 days before 1<sup>st</sup> leukapheresis until last leukapheresis. <b>Congenital neutropenia</b>: 0.6 MIU (6 mcg/kg) SC twice daily. <b>Idiopathic or cyclic neutropenia</b>: 0.5 MIU (5 mcg/kg) SC daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Cross-reactivity with endogenous G-CSF and other <i>E. coli</i>-derived proteins. Patients with myelodysplasia, acute myelogenous leukemia, chronic myelogenous leukemia; pre-malignant myeloid conditions; high-dose chemotherapy; sepsis; sickle cell disease (i.e. homozygous sickle cell anemia, sickle cell-Hgb C disease, sickle cell beta+-thalassemia). May induce splenic rupture, alveolar hemorrhage manifesting as pulmonary infiltrates, hemoptysis, allergic-type reactions; mild to moderate cutaneous vasculitis in patients with SCN. Perform CBC and platelet counts regularly. Rule out any conditions causing neutropenia, other than SCN, prior to treatment of SCN. Discontinue if ANC &gt;10,000/mm<sup>3</sup> or if ARDS develops. Childn. Elderly &lt;65 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Medullary and musculoskeletal bone pain. Transient decrease in BP."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Myelosuppressive cytotoxic drugs, drugs which may potentiate neutrophil release (e.g. lithium), bone scan. <b>IV incompatibilities</b>: Saline solns."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Solution for injection (IV/SC) 300 mcg/mL in pre-filled syringe (P2,625.00)."
          }
        ],

          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/Wm1kD6vOnA0kBtjCl6VJohRCgbJ2fqVyUHaR81Ge486s9cYlkI.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Lipid 20% emulsion, amino acids 11.3% with electrolytes, glucose 19%",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Parenteral Nutritional Products"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "For adults and childn &gt;2 yrs when oral or enteral nutrition is impossible, insufficient or contraindicated."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "IV infusion into central vein only. <b>Adults and childn &gt;10 yrs - Nitrogen requirement</b>: Nitrogen requirements for maintenance of body protein mass depend on the patient’s condition (e.g. nutritional state and degree of catabolic stress). <b>Normal nutrition state</b>: 0.1-0.15 g nitrogen/kg BW/day. <b>Moderate to high metabolic stress with or without malnutrition</b>: 0.15-0.3 nitrogen/kg BW/day (1-2 amino acid/kg/day); 2-6 g for glucose and 1-2 g for fat. Dose range of 0.1-0.2 g nitrogen/kg BW/day (0.7-1.3 g amino acid/kg/day) corresponds to 19-38 mL/kg/day of Combiflex Lipid Central. <b>Total energy requirement</b>: Depends on the patient's clinical condition and is often between 20-30 kcal/kg BW/day. For obese patients, dose should be based on the estimated ideal weight. <b>Childn (2-10 yrs)</b>: 12.5-25 mL/kg (corresponding to 0.49-0.98 g lipid, 0.41-0.83 g amino acids, and 0.1.2-2.4 g glucose per kg/day) and increased by 10-15 mL/kg/day up to max 40 mL/kg/day (1.3 g amino acids [0.21 g nitrogen] and 31 kcal nonprotein energy [3.9 g glucose and 1.6 g lipid] per kg/day). <b>Infusion rate</b>: Should not exceed 2.6 mL/kg/hr (corresponding to 0.25 g glucose, 0.09 g amino acids, and 0.1 g lipid per kg BW) over 12-24 hrs. Max infusion rates - Glucose: 0.25 g/kg/hr; Amino acid: 0.1 g/kg/hr; Lipid: 0.15 g/kg/hr."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity to egg, soya or peanut protein or to any of the active substances or excipients. Severe hyperlipidemia. Severe liver insufficiency. Severe blood coagulation disorders. Inborn errors of amino acid metabolism. Severe renal insufficiency without access to hemofiltration or dialysis. Acute shock. Hyperglycemia (requiring &gt;6 U insulin/hr). Elevated serum levels of any of the included electrolytes. Hemophagocytic syndrome. General contraindication to infusion therapy (e.g. acute pulmonary edema, hyperhydration and decompensated cardiac insufficiency and hypotonic dehydration). Unstable conditions (e.g. severe PTSD, uncompensated diabetes, acute MI, metabolic acidosis, severe sepsis and hyperosmolar coma). Infants &lt;2 yrs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Monitor lipid elimination. Disturbance of the electrolytes and fluid balance (e.g. abnormally high or low serum levels of the electrolytes) should be corrected before starting the infusion. Impaired lipid metabolism due to renal insufficiency, uncompensated DM, pancreatitis, impaired liver function, hypothyroidism (with hypertriglyceridemia) or sepsis. Risk of infection with the use of any central vein. Monitoring serum glucose, electrolytes and osmolarity as well as fluid balance, acid-base status, and liver enzyme tests. CBC and coagulation should be monitored if given in long periods. In patients with renal insufficiency, control phosphate and potassium intake. Any signs or symptoms of anaphylactic reactions (e.g. fever, shivering, rash or dyspnea). May interfere with certain laboratory measurements (e.g. bilirubin, lactate dehydrogenase, oxygen saturation, hemoglobin). In malnourished patients, may precipitate fluid shifts resulting in pulmonary edema and CHF. Should not be given together with blood or blood products in the same infusion set. Thrombophlebitis in peripheral vein infusion. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Rise in body temp. Shivering, chills and nausea/vomiting. Transient increases in liver enzymes."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Emulsion for IV infusion in 3-Chamber bag 1,540 mL (P6,157.00), 2,053 mL (P6,808.00)."
          }
        ],

  {
    "id": 1824,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 1824,
        "brand_name": "Entresto",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": null,
          "medium": null,
          "small": null
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Sacubitril, valsartan",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Angiotensin Receptor Neprilysin Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "To reduce risk of cardiovascular death and hospitalization for heart failure in adult patients with chronic heart failure especially in patients with left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) below normal. Administered in place of an ACE inhibitor or ARBs."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Initially 100 mg twice daily. Double the dose at 2-4 weeks to target dose of 200 mg twice daily as tolerated. <b>Patients not currently on ACE inhibitors or ARBs or previously taking low doses of these agents:</b> Start at 50 mg twice daily and slow dose titration (doubling every 3-4 weeks). <b>Patients with moderate to severe renal impairment (eGFR 30-60 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>) and moderate hepatic impairment:</b> Initially 50 mg twice daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Concomitant use with an ACE inhibitor (do not start Entresto for at least 36 hrs after discontinuing ACE inhibitor therapy) or ARBs. History of angioedema related to ACE inhibitor or ARBs therapy, hereditary or idiopathic angioedema. Concomitant use with aliskiren in patients with DM or with renal impairment (eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>). Severe hepatic impairment, biliary cirrhosis and cholestasis. Pregnancy (2<sup>nd</sup> and 3<sup>rd</sup> trimester)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Sodium and/or sodium depletion should be corrected before treatment. Hypotension, impaired renal function, hyperkalemia, angioedema. Patients with renal artery stenosis, CHF NYHA class IV, hepatic impairment. Not suitable with B-type natriuretic peptide as biomarker for heart failure. Psychiatric disorders (e.g. hallucination paranoia, and sleep disorders). May impair ability to drive and operate machinery.  Childn < 18 yrs. Pregnancy (1<sup>st</sup> trimester) and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Hyperkalemia, hypotension, renal impairment,  cough, dizziness, diarrhea, anemia, fatigue, renal failure, hypokalemia, headache, syncope, asthenia, nausea, orthostatic hypotension, gastritis, vertigo, hypoglycemia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 substrates (e.g. statins), PDE5 inhibitors (e.g. sildenafil), lithium, furosemide, metformin, potassium-sparing diuretics including mineralocorticoid antagonists (e.g. spironolactone, triamterene, amiloride), potassium supplements, or salt substitutes containing potassium, NSAIDs including COX-2 inhibitors, nitrates, inhibitors of OATP1B1, OATP1B3, OAT3 (e.g. rifampin, ciclosporin) or multidrug resistance-associated protein (e.g. ritonavir)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 50 mg (P157.50), 100 mg (P157.50), 200 mg (P157.50)."
          }
        ],
        "company": {

          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/v6AbCth4MwntgM4bVEMp4Gaowjpr4qufDrc40uqNRvBYHajlv7.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/Iis2WLBkyapxVrDQrMstixWgmeYkVM9Xv44VT9mKk50gC2C1pO.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Vedolizumab",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Integrin Receptor Antagonists"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of adults with moderate to severe active ulcerative colitis or Crohn’s disease who have had an inadequate response with, lost response to, or were intolerant to either conventional therapy or a TNF-alpha antagonist."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "300 mg IV infusion at 0, 2, and 6 weeks, then every 8 weeks thereafter. Discontinue therapy if no evidence of therapeutic benefit is observed by week 10 in patients with ulcerative colitis and by week 14 in patients with Crohn’s disease. Reduce or discontinue corticosteroids in patients who have responded to treatment. <b>Retreatment (therapy interruption extending to 1 yr or need to restart):</b> Consider dosing every 4 weeks."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Active severe infections (e.g. TB, sepsis, CMV, listeriosis) and opportunistic infections (e.g. PML)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Monitor patients during and after infusion. Infusion-related reactions. Patients with controlled chronic severe infection, history of recurring severe infections, and those with prior and concurrent use of biological products and live and oral vaccines. Increased risk of malignancy. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn < 18 yrs. Women of childbearing potential should use adequate contraception. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Nasopharyngitis, headache, arthralgia. Bronchitis, gastroenteritis, URTI, influenza, sinusitis, pharyngitis, paresthesia, HTN, oropharyngeal pain, nasal congestion, cough, anal abscess or fissure, nausea, dyspepsia, constipation, abdominal distension, flatulence, hemorrhoids, rash, pruritus, eczema, erythema, night sweats, acne, muscle spasms or weakness, back pain, fatigue, pain in extremity, pyrexia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Live vaccines particularly live oral ones."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Powder for concentrate for solution for IV infusion 300 mg (P83,853.38)."
          }
        ],

            "content": "Management of reversible bronchospasm associated with obstructive airway diseases in patients who require more than a single bronchodilator."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Adults, elderly, adolescents >12 yrs:</b> 1 vial. <b>Childn 2-12 yrs:</b> 3 drops/kg/dose (max 2,500 mcg salbutamol). Use an intermittent positive pressure ventilator or nebulizing device with mouthpiece or well-fitting mask. Use open contents immediately. See product insert for handling instructions."

        "content": "Losartan potassium, hydrochlorothiazide",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Angiotensin II Receptor Blockers"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of hypertension."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "50 mg/12.5 mg once daily, may be increased to max 100 mg/25 mg."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Therapy-resistant hypokalemia or hypercalcemia. Severe hepatic impairment. Cholestasis. Biliary obstructive disorders. Refractory hyponatremia. Symptomatic hyperuricemia/gout. Severe renal impairment (CrCl < 30 mL/min). Anuria. Concomitant use with aliskiren in patients with DM or renal impairment (GFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>). Pregnancy."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Fetal toxicity. History of angioedema; recent kidney transplantation; aortic or mitral stenosis or obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy; renal or hepatic disease. Hypokalemia, delusional hyponatremia, hypomagnesemia, hypersensitivity, SLE, hyperglycemia, hyperuricemia. May impair glucose tolerance. May decrease urinary calcium excretion and increase cholesterol and triglyceride levels. Risk of MI or stroke in ischemic cardiopathy or cerebrovascular disease. Severe arterial hypotension in heart failure. Not recommended in primary hyperaldosteronism. Correct hypotension and electrolyte/fluid imbalance before therapy. Monitor serum potassium levels in type 2 DM with nephropathy; renal function periodically in RAAS-dependent; serum electrolytes regularly. Increased BUN and serum creatinine in bilateral renal artery stenosis or stenosis of the artery to a single functioning kidney. Discontinue before parathyroid testing and immediately if acute myopia and secondary angle-closure glaucoma occur. Black population. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category D. Lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Dizziness, URTI, nasal congestion, back pain."
          },
          {

            "content": "Lithium, NSAIDs. <b>Losartan:</b> Potassium-sparing diuretics/supplements/salt substitutes, aliskiren, ACE inhibitors, TCAs, antipsychotics, baclofen, amifostine, rifampicin, fluconazole. <b>HCTZ:</b> Alcohol, barbiturates, narcotics, amantadine, aminoglycoside antibiotics, anticholinergic agents, antidiabetic agents, diazoxide, antigout agents, calcium salts, carbamazepine, cardiac glycosides, cholestyramine, colestipol resins, corticosteroids, ACTH, parenteral amphotericin B, stimulant laxatives, glycyrrhizin, cytotoxic agents, ciclosporin, pressor amines, nondepolarizing skeletal muscle relaxants, iodinated contrast media."

    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 50,
        "brand_name": "Concore",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/gXfX16pMx3Qa5PQkXJWcq7foYGaRjZKoKLfNXZUKMAeqM3hp5t.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/0pzuW42XrCN8Ks7ps5H63qDffgxe6sYTccegcDvoejtnojZ44D.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/IAvF5OOY7zorvxY8KWBAa1KiUnWzjBQ9ftTh6U8Abcw4yyYJHx.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Bisoprolol fumarate",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Beta Blockers (Antihypertensives)"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of stable chronic heart failure (CHF) with reduced systolic left ventricular function in addition to ACE inhibitors and diuretics, and optionally cardiac glycosides. <b>5 and 10 mg:</b> Treatment of hypertension (HTN), coronary heart disease (angina pectoris)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>HTN or angina pectoris:</b> Initially 5 mg once daily. If necessary, increase to 10 mg once daily. Max 20 mg once daily. <b>Patients with severe renal impairment (CrCl < 20 mL/min):</b> Do not exceed 10 mg/day. <b>Stable CHF:</b> Initially 1.25 mg once daily. May be increased to 2.5 mg, 3.75 mg, 5 mg, 7.5 mg and 10 mg once daily in intervals of 2 weeks or longer depending on individual tolerance. Max 10 mg once daily."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Acute heart failure or during episodes of heart failure decompensation requiring IV inotropic therapy, cardiogenic shock, 2<sup>nd</sup> or 3<sup>rd</sup> degree AV block without a pacemaker, sick sinus syndrome, SA block, symptomatic bradycardia, symptomatic hypotension, severe bronchial asthma, severe forms of PAOD or Raynaud’s syndrome, pheochromocytoma, metabolic acidosis."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Avoid abrupt withdrawal. Patients with heart failure, DM with extremely fluctuating blood glucose levels: Symptoms of markedly reduced blood glucose (hypoglycemia) e.g. tachycardia, palpitations or sweating can be masked, strict fasting, ongoing desensitization therapy, mild disturbances of AV conduction (1<sup>st</sup> degree AV block), Prinzmetal angina, PAOD, psoriasis or history of psoriasis; with pheochromocytoma. Increase sensitivity to allergens and severity of anaphylactic reactions. May mask symptoms of thyrotoxicosis. Administer only after alpha-receptor blockade in pheochromocytoma patients. If necessary to withdraw bisoprolol before surgery, it should be done gradually and completed about 48 hrs before anesthesia. Avoided in patients with obstructive airways diseases. No therapeutic experience in patients with type 1 DM, severely impaired renal or hepatic function, restrictive cardiomyopathy, congenital heart disease, hemodynamically significant organic valvular disease, or MI within the last 3 months. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Childn. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "<b>Patients with CHF:</b> Bradycardia, asthenia, fatigue. Worsening of pre-existing heart failure. Dizziness, headache. Nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation. Feeling of coldness or numbness in the extremities, hypotension."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Calcium antagonists, class I and III antiarrhythmic agents, rifampicin, insulin or hypoglycemic agents, anesthetic agents. Centrally acting antihypertensive drugs, cardiac glycosides, NSAIDs, mefloquine, MAOIs (except MAO-B), beta-sympathomimetics, sympathomimetic drugs that activate both alpha & beta-adrenoceptors topical beta blockers, parasympathomimetic drugs, non-selective beta-blockers, and ergotamine derivatives, antihypertensive agents, other drugs with BP lowering potential (e.g. TCA, barbiturates, phenothiazines)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 2.5 mg, 5 mg, 10 mg."
          }
        ],

  {

        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Tab: Valproic acid (equiv divalproex sodium). Syr: Valproic acid",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Fatty Acid Derivatives"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "<b>Tab:</b> For the treatment of primary generalized seizures, has notable benefit absence and myoclonic seizures, also used for partial seizures. Treatment for the acute manic phase of bipolar disorder and for the prophylaxis of migraine. <b>Syr:</b> Monotherapy and adjunctive therapy in the treatment of patients with complex partial seizures that occur either in isolation or in association with other types of seizures. Sole and adjunctive therapy in the treatment of simple and complex absence seizures, and adjunctively in patients with multiple seizure types that include absence seizures."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Tab- Mania:</b> Initial dose is 25 mg/kg/day, increasing at 1-week intervals by 5-10 mg/kg/day to achieve optimal clinical response. Max dose: 60 mg/kg/day. <b>Absence Seizures:</b> Initial dose is 15 mg/kg/day, increasing 1-week interval by 5-10 mg/kg/day until seizure control or limiting side effects. Max dose: 60 mg/kg/day. <b>Migraine:</b> The starting dose is 500 mg/day for 1 week, thereafter increasing to 1000 mg/day. <b>Syr:</b> <b>Complex partial seizure</b>: Adults and childn &ge;10 yrs - Monotherapy (Initial therapy): 10-15 mg/kg/day, increased by 5-10 mg/kg/week. Conversion to monotherapy: 10-15 mg/kg/day, increased by 5-10 mg/kg/week. Adjunctive therapy: 10-15 mg/kg/day, increased by 5-10 mg/kg/week. <b>Simple and complex absence seizures</b>: Initially 15 mg/kg/day, increase at 1 week intervals by 5-10 mg/kg/day. Max: 60 mg/kg/day. If total daily dose exceeds 250 mg, give in divided doses. <b>Elderly</b>: Reduced initial dose."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with hepatic disease or significant hepatic dysfunction; mitochondrial disorders caused by mutations in mitochondrial DNA polymerase gamma (POLG), and childn &lt;2 yrs suspected with POLG-related disorder; known urea cycle disorders; porphyria. Not for use in prophylaxis of migraine headaches in pregnant women."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with history of hepatic disease, on multiple anticonvulsants, congenital metabolic disorders, severe seizure disorders accompany by mental retardation, and organic brain disease, DM, rare hereditary problems of fructose intolerance, glucose-galactose malabsorption or sucrose-isomaltase insufficiency. Increased risk of developing fatal hepatotoxicity in childn &lt;2 yrs. Cases of life-threatening pancreatitis. Hyperammonemic encephalopathy in patients with urea cycle disorders. Suicidal behavior and ideation. Somnolence in elderly patients with dementia. Thrombocytopenia. Hyperammonemia. Hypothermia. Brain atrophy. False interpretation of the urine ketone test. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Women of childbearing potential. Contains sucrose. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category D.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "GI disturbances, Headache, weight gain or loss, rashes. <b>Tab:</b> Increased appetite, reversible prolongation of bleeding time, thrombocytopenia. Leucopenia and bone marrow suppression, ataxia, tremor, sedation, lethargy, confusion. Acne, toxic epidermal necrolysis, SJS, liver dysfunction, Fanconi's syndrome. Congenital malformations in infants born to women who received valproate during pregnancy.  <b>Syr:</b> Asthenia, fever, back or chest pain, malaise, chills, neck pain or rigidity, face edema, tachycardia, HTN, palpitation, hypotension, postural hypotension, vasodilation, thrombocytopenia, ecchymosis, petechiae, peripheral edema, ALT and/or AST increased, myalgia, twitching, arthralgia, leg cramps, myasthenia, arthrosis, nervous system disorders, respiratory disorders, pruritus, dry skin, alopecia, furunculosis, maculopapular rash, seborrhea, tinnitus, taste perversion, abnormal vision, deafness, otitis media, conjunctivitis, dry eyes, eye pain, urinary incontinence or frequency, vaginitis, dysmenorrhea, dysuria, cystitis, metrorrhagia and vaginal hemorrhage."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Antidepressants. <b>Tab:</b> Erythromycin, antacids (e.g. aluminum and magnesium hydroxide). <b>Syr:</b> Ritonavir, phenytoin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital, aspirin, carbapenem antibiotics, felbamate, rifampin, chlorpromazine, amitriptyline, nortriptyline, clonazepam, diazepam, ethosuximide, lamotrigine, primidone, tolbutamide, topiramate, warfarin, zidovudine, lorazepam."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Extended-release tablet 250 mg, 500 mg. Syrup 250 mg/5 mL x 100 mL (P352.80)."
          }
        ],

          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Symptomatic treatment of chronic stable angina pectoris in adults with coronary artery disease with normal sinus rhythm and heart rate &ge;70 bpm; in adults unable to tolerate or contraindicated with the use of beta-blockers; in combination with beta-blockers in patients inadequately controlled with an optimal beta-blocker dose.           },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "Initially 5 mg twice daily, may be increased if tolerated. Maintenance dose: 7.5 mg twice daily. <b>Elderly:</b> 2.5 mg twice daily. All doses taken in the morning and evening."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with pretreatment resting heart rate < 70 bpm; cardiogenic shock; heart rhythm disorder; MI; severe hypotension; unstable angina; heart failure which has recently become worse; pacemaker dependence; severe hepatic impairment. Concomitant use with antifungals, macrolides, anti-HIV agents, nefazodone, diltiazem, or verapamil. Childn < 18 yrs. Women of childbearing potential. Pregnancy and lactation."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with sustained atrial fibrillation or long QT syndrome; suffering from tiredness, dizziness, or shortness of breath; recent stroke; mild to moderate hypotension; uncontrolled BP especially after a change in antihypertensive therapy; severe heart failure or bundle brand block; chronic eye retinal disease; moderate liver and severe renal impairment; lactose intolerance. Concomitant use with grapefruit juice. May impair ability to drive or operate machines.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Luminous visual phenomena. Bradycardia, irregular rapid heart contraction, abnormal perception of heart beat, uncontrolled BP, headache, dizziness, blurred vision."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Fluconazole, rifampicin, barbiturates, phenytoin, St. John’s Wort, QT-prolonging agents (e.g. quinidine, disopyramide, ibutilide, sotalol, amiodarone; bepridil; anxiolytics, antipsychotics; anti-malarial agents; IV erythromycin; pentamidine; cisapride), potassium-depleting diuretics (e.g. furosemide, hydrochlorothiazide, indapamide)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 5 mg x 56s (P1,305.36), 7.5 mg x 56s (P1,317.12)."
          }
        ],

        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "Antiplatelets"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Alternative to aspirin as prophylaxis in patients with atherosclerosis at risk of thromboembolic disorders e.g. myocardial infarction (MI), peripheral arterial disease, stroke."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Thromboembolic disorders:</b> 75 mg once daily. <b>Acute coronary syndrome (unstable angina/non-Q wave MI):</b> 300 mg as a single loading dose then continue at 75 mg once daily in combination with aspirin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with an increased risk of bleeding e.g. due to PUD, trauma, surgery."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients who have lesions with a susceptibility to bleed. Patients with hepatic and renal impairment. Pregnancy and lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a>:</b> Category B.",
            "pregnancy_risk": {
              "header": "Pregnancy Risk Category by the US FDA:",
              "categories": [
                {
                  "title": "A",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans do not show any evidence that the product poses a risk to the baby in the womb."
                },
                {
                  "title": "B",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals do not show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. Otherwise, animal studies show a risk but studies on humans do not show any."
                },
                {
                  "title": "C",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals show a risk to the baby, but there are not enough compelling studies in humans. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "D",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in humans show a risk to the baby. However, the product may be used in pregnant women in certain situations despite the potential risks."
                },
                {
                  "title": "X",
                  "content": "Adequate and compelling studies in animals or humans show a risk to the baby in the womb. Also, use or experience in humans shows a risk. The danger of using the product in pregnant women clearly outweighs its benefits."
                }
              ]
            }
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "GI hemorrhage and events e.g. abdominal pain, dyspepsia, gastritis, constipation, and diarrhea."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "NSAIDs. Phenytoin, tamoxifen, tolbutamide, warfarin, torsemide, and fluvastatin."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Film-coated tablet 75 mg (P30.24)."
          }

            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"

          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of chronic hepatitis C virus infection in adults."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Patients without cirrhosis and patients with compensated cirrhosis:</b> 1 tab once daily for 12 weeks. Addition of ribavirin may be considered for genotype 3 infected patients with compensated cirrhosis. <b>Patients with decompensated cirrhosis:</b> 1 tab once daily + ribavirin for 12 weeks. <b>Ribavirin dosing guide - Child-Pugh-Turcotte (CPT) Class B cirrhosis pre-transplant:</b> 1,000 mg/day for patients < 75 kg and 1,200 mg for those weighing &ge;75 kg. <b>CPT Class C cirrhosis pre-transplant or CPT Class B or C post-transplant:</b> Starting dose of 600 mg, which can be titrated up to a max of 1,000 mg for patients weighing &lt;75 kg and 1,200 mg for patients weighing &ge;75 kg if well tolerated. If the starting dose is not well tolerated, the dose should be reduced as clinically indicated based on Hgb levels."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Co-administration with potent P-gp or potent CYP450 inducers."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Should not be administered concurrently with other medicinal products containing sofosbuvir. Concomitant use with amiodarone or other medicinal products that lower heart rate. HCV/HBV (hepatitis virus) co-infection. Patients who have previously failed therapy with an NS5A-containing regimen. Severe renal impairment (eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>) and ESRD requiring hemodialysis. Concomitant use with moderate P-gp inducers and/or moderate CYP inducers (e.g. efavirenz, modafinil, oxcarbazepine or rifapentine). Co-administration of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir with the fixed-dose combination tab containing elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir disoproxil fumarate or tenofovir disoproxil fumarate given in conjunction with a boosted HIV protease inhibitor (e.g. atazanavir or darunavir). Diabetes. CPT class C cirrhosis. Liver transplant patients. Pregnancy and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Headache, fatigue, nausea. Rash, angioedema. Liver disease or known toxicity profile of ribavirin in patients receiving treatment in combination with ribavirin. Renal impairment.  Bradycardia and heart block in combination with amiodarone."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "Acid-reducing agents (e.g. PPIs), antiarrhythmics (e.g. amiodarone, digoxin), anticoagulants (e.g. dabigatran, vit K antagonists), anticonvulsants (e.g. phenytoin. phenobarbital, carbamazepine, oxcarzepine), antimycobacterials (e.g. rifampicin, rifabutin, rifapentine), HIV antiviral agents (reverse transcriptase inhibitors e.g. tenofovir disoproxil fumarate, efavirenz/emtricitabine/tenofovir disoproxil fumarate, sofosbuvir/velpatasvir). St. John's wort, HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors (e.g. rosuvastatin)."
          },

            "content": "<b>Epilepsy – Adults</b>: 25 mg once daily for 1 week, increased thereafter by increments of 25-50 mg at intervals of 1-2 weeks. Monotherapy: 100-400 mg daily; <b>Childn 2-16 yrs – Adjunctive therapy</b>: 25 mg nightly for the 1<sup>st</sup> week, increased at intervals of 1-2 weeks by increments of 1-3 mg/kg/day. Dose of &gt;25 mg should be taken in 2 divided doses. Usual dose: 100 mg. <b>Patients with renal impairment (CrCl &lt;70 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>)</b>: &frac12; of adult dose. <b>Patients undergoing hemodialysis</b>: &frac12; of the daily dose given in divided doses."

          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Control of hyperphosphatemia in adults receiving hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis and chronic kidney disease (CKD) not on dialysis with serum phosphorus &gt;1.78 mmol/L."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>Starting dose</b> - Serum phosphorus >2.42 mmol/L (7.5 mg/dL): 4.8 g/day; 1.78-2.42 mmol/L (5.5-7.5 mg/dL): 2.4 g/day. <b>Titration and maintenance</b>: 0.8 g thrice daily (2.4 g/day) increments every 2-4 weeks. Tabs should be swallowed whole, not crushed, chewed, or broken."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Hypophosphatemia, bowel obstruction. Patients with rare hereditary problems of galactose intolerance, total lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Patients with CKD not on dialysis with serum phosphorus &lt;1.78 mmol/L, dysphagia, swallowing disorders, severe GI motility disorders, active IBD, major GI tract surgery, hypothyroidism, and secondary hyperparathyroidism. Fat-soluble vitamins and folic acid. Monitor serum calcium and bicarbonate levels. Patients on peritoneal dialysis. Childn &lt;18 yrs. Pregnancy and lactation.",

            "content": "Nausea, vomiting, upper abdominal pain, constipation, diarrhea, dyspepsia, flatulence, abdominal pain."

            "content": "Ciprofloxacin, ciclosporin, mycophenolate mofetil, tacrolimus, levothyroxine, antiarrhythmics, anti-seizure, digoxin, warfarin, enalapril, metoprolol, PPIs."

    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 1027,
        "brand_name": "Coveram",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/37Ll6ku3ksLTfmuQpdJquhFwrIg5xfvTdBhvezZK2Q2g0dyCVB.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/yV7iUETfZ9ztz28sW7dw0GY5uKG0AubHPiMnAorUQWTSkytjtN.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/nB2WQTeB5P3FQ3h7t2QfZHiLkzDTvfQ7ky15WuaXpwQY2FhJCz.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Perindopril, amlodipine",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "ACE Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Substitution therapy for essential hypertension and/or stable coronary artery disease in patients already controlled with perindopril and amlodipine given concurrently at the same dose level."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "1 tab/day, preferably in the morning before meals."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Patients with history of ACE inhibitor-associated angioedema, hereditary or idiopathic angioedema, significant bilateral renal artery stenosis or stenosis of the artery to a single functioning kidney, or those receiving extracorporeal treatments leading to contact of blood with negatively charged surfaces. Concomitant use with aliskiren in patients with DM or renal impairment (GFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m<sup>2</sup>), and sacubitril/valsartan (therapy must not be initiated until after 36 hrs of last dose). Severe hypotension, shock including cardiogenic shock, obstruction of the outflow tract of the left ventricle (e.g. high-grade aortic stenosis), hemodynamically unstable heart failure after acute MI. Pregnancy (2<sup>nd</sup> and 3<sup>rd</sup> trimesters)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Precautions",
            "content": "Not for initial therapy. Patients with renal/hepatic impairment and failure, heart failure, malignant hyperthermia; galactose intolerance, glucose-galactose malabsorption, total lactase deficiency; collagen vascular disease, undergoing immunosuppressant therapy, treated with allopurinol or procainamide, or combination of these factors; primary hyperaldosteronism, diabetes, mitral valve stenosis, obstruction in the outflow of the left ventricle (e.g. aortic stenosis, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy); at high risk of symptomatic hypotension; receiving desensitization treatment (e.g. hymenoptera venom). LDL-apheresis with dextran. Neutropenia/agranulocytosis, thrombocytopenia, anemia, hyperkalemia. Non-productive, persistent cough. Monitor BP, renal function, and serum potassium before and during treatment. Discontinue treatment 1 day prior to surgery. May impair ability to drive or operate machinery. Black patients. Childn and adolescents. Elderly. Pregnancy (1<sup>st</sup> trimester) and lactation.",
            "pregnancy_risk": null
          },
          {
            "title": "Side Effects",
            "content": "Edema, somnolence, dizziness, headache, dysgeusia, paresthesia, visual impairment (including diplopia), tinnitus, vertigo, palpitations, flushing, hypotension, dyspnea, cough, abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, dyspepsia, change of bowel habit, diarrhea, constipation, pruritus, rash, exanthema, joint swelling, muscle spasms, fatigue, asthenia."
          },
          {
            "title": "Drug Interactions",
            "content": "mTOR inhibitors (e.g. sirolimus, everolimus, temsirolimus), baclofen, beta-blockers and vasodilators, nitroglycerin and other nitrates, corticosteroids, tetracosactide, alpha-blockers, amifostine, TCAs, antipsychotics, anesthetics. <b>Perindopril:</b> ACE inhibitors, ARBs, racecadotril, gliptins, aliskiren, potassium salts, potassium-sparing diuretics (e.g. spironolactone, triamterene, amiloride, eplerenone), heparin, immunosuppressants (e.g. ciclosporin, tacrolimus), trimethoprim and co-trimoxazole, estramustine, lithium, antidiabetics (e.g. insulins, oral hypoglycemics), non-potassium-sparing diuretics, racecadotril, NSAIDs (e.g. aspirin &ge;3 g daily), sympathomimetics, injectable gold (sodium aurothiomalate). <b>Amlodipine:</b> IV Dantrolene, CYP3A4 inducers and inhibitors, tacrolimus, simvastatin, grapefruit or grapefruit juice."
          },
          {
            "title": "Packaging",
            "content": "Tablet 5 mg/5 mg x 30s (P841.80), 5 mg/10 mg x 30s (P945.90), 10 mg/5 mg x 30s (P1,137.90), 10 mg/10 mg x 30s (P991.20)."
          }
        ],

  {
    "id": 39,
    "detail": {
      "success": true,
      "data": {
        "id": 39,
        "brand_name": "Coversyl",
        "brand_suffix": null,
        "brand_shot": {
          "original": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/GZXk4RyI1cJ5SGKWTOJ3xb7rMjkNAWOwmjznKOXAqLmovRXP4p.jpg",
          "medium": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/shQA7c6fXC3ZOd9wz6qHMYlH41iUkKM0jlWqRHITW10eNiJble.jpg",
          "small": "https://d1c0x5rkl7k63i.cloudfront.net/upload/drug/brand/image/tDupgRTWBzFa4Un7dXCuzMFRvv4GXykXmn8CM5M4EeocNPv8DH.jpg"
        },
        "brand_status": 1,
        "content": "Perindopril",
        "brand_info": [
          {
            "title": "Therapeutic class",
            "content": "ACE Inhibitors"
          },
          {
            "title": "Regulatory Classification",
            "content": "Rx"
          },
          {
            "title": "Indications",
            "content": "Treatment of arterial hypertension (HTN) and congestive heart failure. Prevention of stroke recurrence in combination with indapamide in patients with history of cerebrovascular disease. Reduction of risk of cardiovascular events in patients with stable coronary artery disease (CAD)."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>HTN:</b> As monotherapy or in combination with other antihypertensives. Initially 5 mg/day in the morning. Patients with strongly activated RAAS (renovascular HTN, salt and/or vol depletion, cardiac decompensation, or severe HTN): Initially 2.5 mg. May increase to 10 mg/day after 1 month. <b>Concomitant treatment with diuretics:</b> Discontinue diuretic 2-3 days before start of Coversyl. If not possible, initiate Coversyl at 2.5 mg, monitor renal function and serum potassium, and adjust subsequent dose according to blood pressure response. <b>Elderly:</b> Initially 2.5 mg. May increase to 5 mg after 1 month, then 10 mg if necessary depending on renal function. <b>Symptomatic heart failure:</b> Initially 2.5 mg/day in the morning, may increase to 5 mg/day after 2 weeks if tolerated. Adjust dose based on clinical response. <b>Stable CAD:</b> Initially 5 mg/day for 2 weeks, then increase to 10 mg/day if tolerated depending on renal function. Elderly: 2.5 mg/day for 1 week, then 5 mg/day the next week, before increasing to 10 mg/day if well tolerated depending on renal function. <b>Renal impairment -</b> CrCl &ge;60 mL/min: 5 mg/day; 30-60 mL/min: 2.5 mg/day; 15-30 mL/min: 2.5 mg every other day; < 15 mL/min: 2.5 mg on the day of dialysis. Take after dialysis on hemodialysis patients. Take in the morning before a meal."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity.             "content": "Hypertension (HTN). Reduction in the risk of cardiovascular (CV) morbidity and mortality in hypertensive patients with left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH). Renal protection in Type 2 diabetic patients with proteinuria."
          },
          {
            "title": "Dose",
            "content": "<b>HTN</b>: Initially 50 mg once daily, may be increased to 100 mg once daily. Max effect is attained 3-6 weeks after initiation of therapy. <b>Patients with intravascular vol depletion</b>: Initially 25 mg once daily. Lower dosage in patients with a history of hepatic impairment. <b>Reduction in the risk of CV morbidity and mortality in hypertensive patients with LVH</b>: Initially 50 mg once daily, add a low-dose HCTZ and/or increase the dose of losartan potassium to 100 mg once daily based on BP response. <b>Renal protection in type 2 DM patients with proteinuria</b>: Initially 50 mg once daily, may be increased to 100 mg once daily based on BP response."
          },
          {
            "title": "Contraindications",
            "content": "Hypersensitivity. Concomitant use with aliskiren in patients with DM. Pregnancy."

Neonates with history of in utero exposure to losartan. Lactation. <b><a href=\"#\" id=\"has_preg_risk\">Pregnancy Risk</a></b>: Category C but D in 2<sup>nd</sup> and 3<sup>rd</sup> trimesters.",
